author: profnardi
body:
## Description

The ballot page offers the voting form only on an open ballot: not
before the ballot is opened, not after its deadline and not once its
result is counted. The `vote` view, which receives the form, checked
none of these. It saved any vote that reached it: one sent from a
ballot page left open past the deadline, or one sent without the page.
On a secret ballot it also saved the receipt, added the line to the
voting record and sent the receipt mail.

`vote` now refuses such a vote with the error page "This ballot is not
open for votes." and saves nothing. The conditions are those of the
open ballots on the agenda page: the ballot is opened, its result is
not counted and its deadline has not passed. A vote on an open ballot
is saved as before.

The checks of `vote` look at the ballot of the first option only. A
vote whose options belong to more than one ballot is therefore refused
first, with "You can vote on only one ballot at a time.", and nothing
is saved; otherwise the option of a second ballot, open or not, would
be saved without any check.

The change is in `apps/voting/views.py`. #808, #1008 and #1009 change
other functions of that file and merge with this branch without
conflicts.

## Testing

`apps/voting/tests/test_vote_on_open_ballot.py`, 5 new tests: a vote is
refused and not saved on a ballot past its deadline, on one not yet
opened, on one whose result is counted, and when it holds an option of
an open ballot and one of a ballot that is not open; a vote on an open
ballot is saved.

In the dev Docker setup:

- Without the change, the 4 refusal tests fail, because the vote is
  accepted; the fifth passes.
- With the change, the 14 tests of `apps/voting` pass, these 5 among
  them.
- Full suite with the change: 1773 passed, 1 failed:
  `test_native_reset_management_sequence_can_seed_again`, which fails on
  beta too when the whole suite runs; #1017 fixes it.

author: randal-cox
body:
draft.inator's side of the Zotero handoff in #40, on cite.inator **0.6.0-preview.1** (`402247d`, `dist/citation-manager.mjs`, vendored for testing only).

**What it does:**
- **A Zotero button** in the editor's toolbar, shown when the site passes `zotero: { manager }`.
- **Connect:** the writer pastes an API key (read-only is enough). It's checked with `GET /keys/current`, which also gives the library's owner, and kept in `sessionStorage` for the tab only. It's never written to the page, a draft, or the repository, and **Forget the key** removes it. Errors say what happened: refused key, rate limit, or Zotero unreachable (for example, blocked by the site's CSP).
- **Search:** a keyboard combobox over `GET /users/{id}/items?q=…&qmode=titleCreatorYear&itemType=-attachment || note&include=csljson,data`. Results read "Rivera 2020 · title", and works this page already cites are marked **already cited here**.
- **Choose:**
  - `fromZotero(item, { recordId, transport: 'web' })`, with the id made site-style (`okafor-2019-masks`).
  - `reconcileZoteroItem` against the site's cache. A work the site already has is offered with plain-words evidence, and adding a duplicate warns that the site would have two copies.
  - Anything cite.inator flags (for example, an http URL) is listed before inserting.
  - A page or section is optional.
- **Insert:** the marker goes in at the cursor, as one undoable step. A new work joins the works list and goes to `importer.onRecords`. Escape or Close leaves everything unchanged.
- **Bindings:** a Zotero item → work map in `localStorage`, for "already cited" and id reuse. It's disposable, and nothing needs it to save.
- **The demo** answers for Zotero with a small made-up library (`demo/editor/zotero-sample.mjs`, key `samplesamplesamplesample`), so it can be tried without an account.

**Tests:** `npm test` gives 141 pass, 0 fail. The new ones cover connecting, search parameters, labels, the site-match offer without merging, new ids, review flags, binding reuse, and that the Zotero key stays out of the record.

**Checked in Chromium** (light at 1300 px, dark at 390 px):
- a bad key is refused, and the key stays in `sessionStorage` only;
- search works with keyboard Enter;
- Bell is offered as the site's work, and inserting gives `{cite bell-1992-ritual | note:"Bell 1992" | locator:94}`;
- Okafor is added as a new work and formatted in the preview;
- a second search marks Okafor "already cited here".

**Before merging:**
- [ ] **cite.inator 0.6 released.** Swap `citation-manager.mjs` for the release file, checked against `SHA256SUMS`.
- [ ] **A real Zotero key test.** Randal, with his own key, once the site allows api.zotero.org.
- [ ] **KR's CSP.** `connect-src` for the editor's pages needs `https://api.zotero.org`, as a separate KR PR for Randal.

This changes what the editor can write into a page (new works and markers), so the merge is Randal's.

body:
> Closes #1623

## What
Records one cast a long rest for the ERLW dragonmark spells whose trait prints it, and grants Wards and Seals' arcane lock and Headwinds' gust of wind from 3rd level, each once a long rest.

## Why
Upstream's `additionalSpells` omits the count and the two 3rd-level spells, so the sheet listed these spells uncounted.

## Deviations
- **Addition:** `spellsMechanicSchema` in `featureMechanics.ts` gains `learnedAt`, a total level before which `learns` holds all its spells back. `learns` had no level, and a race trait cannot be gated by one level per spell.
- **Addition:** `learnedSpells` in `heldFeatures.ts` now skips a spell below its `learnedAt` and returns the feature's recorded `casts`; `learnedBy` in `character-spells.ts` turns them into the spell's `uses` for a leveled spell. Existing `learns` records (Moon Fire) are unchanged.
- **Addition:** the `Spellsmith` comment "Its one use is the catalog's" is deleted, and its magic weapon now carries the cast count the issue asks for beside the feature's own use, so Magic Weapon's one cast shows on the feature card and as the spell's `uses`.

author: kblack0610
body:
fleet-liveness has been red for 16h on `knowledge-engine: STALLED`. Its 2026-11-25 run stalled on "2026-07-14: apply refused the batch", because `notes knowledge apply` failed with `parsing the ops batch: invalid type: null, expected a string at line 13 column 17`. The model had written `"why": null` on a source that an op cites, and the batch structs read optional strings as `#[serde(default)] String`, which accepts a missing key but rejects a JSON null.

The suspect merge, private PR 1314 (c6bde559, MAX_RUNTIME), is cleared. The run took 8.5 min of its 40 min cap and the unit ended `result=exit-code` (a cap kill reads `timeout`), so the cap never fired.

Fix forward: every defaulted field of `Batch`, `Source` and `Op` now reads a JSON null as if the key were missing, through one `null_as_default` deserializer. Required fields (`date`, `id`, `path`, `op`) stay strict. A null `content` gets the same per-op checks as a missing one, the frontmatter check included. Added test `a_null_optional_field_reads_as_left_out`.

assumed: fix forward rather than revert, because PR 1314 did not cause the stall.
assumed: the fix belongs in the parser rather than the prompt, because null is how JSON says "not applicable" and the schema already treats these fields as optional.

Before: `watch-companion-loop list --long fleet-liveness` showed TRIP, `knowledge-engine: STALLED`. The refused batch (`last-refused-batch.json`) has exactly one null, `sources[1].why`.
After: once merged and the autopull rebuilds `notes`, the next knowledge-engine run, or a hand run, replaces the STALLED outcome. Then `watch-companion-loop resolve fleet-liveness --pr Kblack0610/.dotfiles#3639`.

Checks: CI runs the rust tier (`tests/pick.sh rust`). Nothing was run on the workstation, per AGENTS.md.

Review: /code-review high, three nits and none changed: required fields stay strict on purpose; a null path or content reads as an empty one, which the parser already accepted for a missing key and the per-op checks reject; `allow_shrink` is an Option, which already reads null as None.

This comes from the rotation licence asks. The data are on [OSF kxb9r](https://osf.io/kxb9r), "Mental Rotation Performance" by Mehdi Rajeb and Joni Lakin. **Joni Lakin granted permission by email on 2026-11-25 and set CC BY 4.0 on the OSF project the same day** (checked through the OSF API).

| table | ids | items | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| lakin_2024_mrt | 129 | 15 | 1,935 |

**Test.** 15 mental rotation items with Shepard–Metzler-style cube figures and four response options each, according to the project's item PDF (`Mental Rotation Items.pdf`, recorded as the codebook). The project doesn't name the test or describe the sample, and Ben's letter asked about both. With 129 people it clears the 100-person floor for fixed-item tests.

**Layout:**
- id = the file's student number.
- item = `mr01`–`mr15` (source MR.1–MR.15).
- resp = 0/1.
- `cov_female` comes from the F/M column (48 F, 75 M, 6 NA).

**Check.** Overall accuracy is 0.52. Item means run from 0.24 to 0.98. `mr01` (0.98) and `mr11` (0.92) are the easy ones.

**Validation.** The table conforms and passes the upload gate. The one warning (`imputed_values`) is response concentration on the easy items, which is expected.

It uploads to the shard 10 draft. Once released, it joins `mental_rotation`.

author: iuriioapps
body:
## Summary

Main now says when its thread was blocked, and the IPC rule says what to do about it.

```text
watchMainThread(log)                       electron/main-thread-watch.ts
  every 1 s: read Node's event-loop delay histogram, then reset it
    longest block > 50 ms -> warn main.stall { durationMs }

main.ts
  first window ready-to-show
    show it
    1 s later: start the watch     # creating and first painting the window block main ~80 ms on every launch
```

`logCalls` measures only the handler. Serializing a result happens after it returns, so a 50,000-row result (about 100 ms of serializing, measured in #241) would never show up in `ipc.end`. The event-loop delay catches every cause, and the `ipc.start` lines just before a `main.stall` show which calls ran.

`.claude/rules/ipc.md` gains "Watching the main thread" and "When load grows": seven patterns in the order to reach for them, from narrow rows and canceling stale queries to bypassing main, which needs its own ADR first. `docs/quality-targets.md` lists `main.stall` among the lines every process writes.

## Evidence

| Test | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| A fake histogram at 161 ms, two intervals | One `main.stall` line, `durationMs: 161` |
| A fake histogram at exactly 50 ms | No line |
| A real 200 ms busy loop | A `main.stall` line with `durationMs` of at least 150 |

In the built app (a development machine, not the reference machine):

| Run | `main.stall` lines |
| --- | --- |
| Watch started at launch | One per launch, 277 ms: window creation |
| Watch started at `ready-to-show` | One per launch, 60 to 95 ms: the first paint |
| Watch started 1 s after `ready-to-show`, three launches | None |
| A 150 ms busy loop in main, through the inspector | `main.stall`, `durationMs: 161` |

`pnpm check` passes: 90 tests.

## Merge Danger

| Door | Blast radius |
| --- | --- |
| Two-way | Main process log |

The watch adds one 1 s timer and a native histogram that samples every 10 ms. Its timer is unref'd, so it never keeps the process alive.

Part of the stack #235 → #236 → #237 → #238 → #240 → #241 → #242.

author: cscheid
body:
Closes #1344.

On a Windows checkout, `scripts/prune-embed-dist.mjs` gets CRLF line endings. Vite strips a hashbang with `/^#!.*\n/` (`vite/dist/node/chunks/config.js`), and `.` doesn't match `\r`, so the `#!` line stays inside the SSR module wrapper and `pruneEmbedDist.test.ts` fails at import with `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token`. With this change, every `.mjs` under the root `scripts/` checks out with LF.

## Changes

- `.gitattributes`: add `scripts/**/*.mjs text eol=lf`. It covers the root `scripts/` only, not `hub-client/scripts/` or `ts-packages/*/scripts/`. The index already stores all of these files as LF, so `git add --renormalize` changes nothing.
- `hub-client/src/pandoc/scriptsLineEndings.test.ts` (new): a guard test that fails if any `scripts/**/*.mjs` contains `\r`. It is a separate file because a broken import keeps `pruneEmbedDist.test.ts` from running at all. Like pampa's `annotated_qmd_fixture_guard`, it can only fail on a CRLF checkout.
- `claude-notes/plans/2026-11-25-mjs-scripts-eol-lf.md`: plan and record.

author: krzysztof-cieslak
body:
## T132a: Headless approvals

This fixes what dogfooding the native binary turned up before T132 (fx builds fx). §13, §19; it depends on T127b and T129b, and T132 now depends on it.

### 1. A headless denial no longer sticks

**Root cause.** Two things combined:
- The first-install request was keyed `component.install/<install>`, which is one request per component for the whole life of the data directory. The grants rules say a key is one request and its answer is final for it, so the first answer applied to every later run.
- That first answer came from a headless run. With nobody at a terminal, it answered "deny once" and recorded the denial under the person who started the run, even though nobody had been asked.

As a result, every later run was refused Bun without a prompt, even from a terminal.

**Fix.**
- **Install keys come from what asks.** The installer now passes an `ApprovalRequest` (the install, the holder whose `Ensure` started the attempt, and the attempt), and `Approvals.key` builds `component.install/<install>/<holder>/<attempt>` from all three.
  - If the pipeline retries the same attempt, it is still one request.
  - A later attempt or another holder (the environment of a later run) asks a person again.
  - A host-wide grant still approves every install at once.
- **Nobody's answer is not a denial.** When nobody can answer, the run withdraws the request: the host closes it as `Withdrawn "nobody could answer: not run from a terminal"` and never answers on the person's behalf.
- **CodeAct's guard (T127b) didn't have this bug.** Its keys already come from the turn and the call. A live test now runs the same `shell.exec` headless, then from a terminal (asked again, allowed once, runs), then headless again (asked again). The model now reads "its grant request was not answered" instead of "denied".
- **Requests left pending by a crash are shown.** A request left pending by a host that stopped mid-prompt is now shown to the next run's person first. Before, a recovered install or turn waited on a prompt nobody saw.

### 2. `fx grants`: decide beforehand

```
fx grants list [--all]
fx grants allow|deny <action> <pattern> [--scope host|session:<id>] [--reason <text>]
fx grants revoke <id> [--reason <text>]
```

- **Who can grant:** the OS user, signed in in process through `local-os-user` the same way embedded mode signs them in, and only if they own the host. Grants record the `user:` principal.
- **Locking:** it runs under the data directory's lock, like `fx auth`, so it fails beside a running host.
- **Checks:** the action must be known and must allow the chosen scope (`component.install` cannot be granted for a session).
- **No repository scope:** requests on this host don't name a repository yet, so a repository grant would never apply.
- **The headless message now names the exact command**, quoted for the shell and escaped as an exact pattern, for example: `Allow it beforehand with \`fx grants allow component.install bun@1.4.5\`, or run from a terminal.`

### 3. Credentials before the first install

For a new session, `fx run` now checks before the environment installs anything:
- that a model is configured for the main role;
- that the provider's credentials resolve (`AuthService.resolve`).

If either check fails, the run stops with what the turn would have said, e.g. `the model call would fail: unavailable: anthropic: no credentials: …`, and nothing is downloaded.

### 4. Human sizes

The install prompt used to show `size: size (download 54438042, installed 115378776)`. It now shows `size: download 51.9 MiB, installed 110.0 MiB`.

### 5. Running unattended (host.md)

host.md has a new section on running unattended:
- **Credentials:** `fx auth login` or the provider's environment variable.
- **Installs:** run `fx grants allow component.install bun@1.4.5` once per data directory. The first install is always a person's grant, and no variant skips it.
- **What turns do:** grant it beforehand (e.g. `fx grants allow shell.exec 'git **'`), or set `codeact.grants.mode`.
  - The setting is privileged. The command line (`--variant codeact.grants.mode=deny`) and host config can set it; a project's config cannot ("privileged: only host config, explicit selections and policy may select it"); policy can pin it. I checked all three with the native binary. No privileged-slot rule was loosened.

### Docs and spec
- `host.md`, `grants.md`, `components.md`, `codeact.md` and the `AGENTS.md` rules and command rows are updated.
- **spec.md §13** now names `fx grants` as a way for a person to grant beforehand on the host's machine, next to the client protocol. It also says requests nobody can answer are withdrawn and asked again next time. §19.5 lists the command.

### How I verified it
- **Restore, build and tests:** `dotnet restore --locked-mode` and `dotnet build Fx.slnx -c Release` succeed with 0 warnings. `dotnet test --solution Fx.slnx -c Release` passes all 3460 tests (55 skipped).
  - New host tests use a scripted model and downloads that always fail, so no network is needed. They cover installs in both orders (headless → terminal deny once → terminal allow once → headless), `fx grants` allow/list/revoke and its refusals, the credential check, and a request left pending by a crash.
  - Also new: unit tests for prompts, quoting and drafts, CLI parse tests, and component tests for keys and sizes.
- **Formatting, analyzers, task graph:** `fantomas --check`, the analyzers and `tasks.ts check` all pass.
- **Native AOT:** `dotnet publish -r linux-x64` succeeds, and the JIT-vs-native diff shows 185 identical cases plus the self-test.
  - The host-embedded scenario now runs `fx grants` (and the refusal beside a running host).
  - The diff runs `fx grants --help` and a scope `allow` doesn't offer.
- **CI smoke test:** `.github/scripts/aot-smoke.sh host` now covers:
  - a run without credentials, which must stop before any install;
  - a run with a key that is never sent, which stops at the install approval, withdraws it and names `fx grants allow …`;
  - `fx grants` list, allow and revoke.

  It passes locally on linux-x64.
- **End to end with the native binary, scratch `FX_HOME`:**
  - Headless run: withdrawn, with the command printed.
  - Then from a terminal: asked again (the bug is gone). `n` gives "denied by user:… at the terminal"; `y` installs.
  - Terminal first (`n`), then headless: asked again and withdrawn.
  - `fx grants allow component.install bun@1.4.5`, then headless: installs without asking.
  - Without a key: fails before `runtimes/` exists.

### Left for later
- `fx grants` over the client protocol to a host that `fx serve` is running (today it needs the data directory's lock).
- Repository-scoped grants, once requests name the workspace's repository.

### CI
- **Fast tier is green** on linux-x64, osx-arm64 and win-x64, plus Lint. One unrelated, intermittent macOS failure happened on the first run: `Fx.Replay.Tests` "recorded sessions replay / an interrupted cell; the kernel lives on" timed out with "replay made no progress for 10 s". It passed on rerun.
- **Full tier is green on all 8 targets.** The PR is labelled `ci:full` because it changes `.github/scripts/aot-smoke.sh`, and the run includes the musl targets, which run the smoke test in Alpine through `docker exec -e`.

author: ashtonchew
body:
## Summary

`Streaming.wait(timeout)` returned the count sent so far when the timeout ran out, which is the same value a finished stream returns. `Thread.join` returns `None` either way, and `wait` never checked whether the thread was still alive. It now raises `TimeoutError`, as `concurrent.futures.Future.result(timeout)` does.

```diff
 def wait(self, timeout=None) -> int:
     self._thread.join(timeout)
     if self.error is not None:
         raise self.error
+    if self._thread.is_alive():
+        raise TimeoutError(f"still streaming after {timeout}s ({self.sent} events sent so far)")
     return self.sent
```

The standard library's waits that return a value raise on timeout: `Future.result` raises `TimeoutError`, and `subprocess.Popen.wait` raises `TimeoutExpired`. The waits that return a bool or `None` (`Event.wait`, `Thread.join`) leave the check to the caller. `wait` returns a count, so it raises. A failed stream still raises its own error first, and `wait()` with no timeout behaves as before.

## Evidence

A live source that sends one event and then goes quiet, waited on for 0.5s:

- **Before:** `wait(0.5) returned 1 after 0.58s; thread alive: True`
  **After:** `wait(0.5) raised TimeoutError(still streaming after 0.5s (1 events sent so far)) after 0.51s`

New test, `test_waiting_on_a_stream_that_is_still_going_raises_timeout`:

```text
streaming = client.stream(OneThenQuiet(), every=0.05)
with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
    streaming.wait(0.5)
```

- **Before:** `Failed: DID NOT RAISE TimeoutError`
  **After:** passes (3 of 3 runs). Full suite: 178 passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

One check in `wait`, easy to revert.

**Blast Radius:** callers

A caller that passed a timeout and used the partial count as a progress reading now gets `TimeoutError` instead. To keep that behaviour, catch `TimeoutError` and read `streaming.sent`. No caller in the repo, its examples, or its skills does this: the one timed call, `test_stream_an_adapter`, calls `wait(10)` on a bounded source that finishes well inside the timeout. This touches only `wait` and stays clear of the `Streaming` lines that #43 and #45 change. All three PRs add a test after `test_stream_an_adapter`, so whichever lands second gets a trivial conflict at the end of `tests/test_server.py`.

author: cozygarage
body:
Follow-up to #4120 (#3910), found in review.

## Bug
`Authorization::rearm` (`crates/policy/src/guard.rs`) is meant to drop the read deadline for a person's write or DDL. It decided this **before** adding the approval wait:

```rust
.filter(|deadline| !runs_past_the_read_deadline || *deadline <= now)   // original deadline
.map(|deadline| deadline + approval_wait)
```

**Scenario:** a Prod `UPDATE` with a 30 s timeout, approved after 60 s.
1. When the approval returns, the original deadline is already past, so the filter keeps it.
2. The deadline then moves to D+60.
3. The write starts with about 30 s left and is cancelled mid-flight. It can end as an unknown outcome, which blocks governed writes (ADR 0056).

That is the failure #3910 exists to remove, on the path where it matters most.

## Fix
Shift by the approval wait first, then decide:

```rust
.map(|deadline| deadline + approval_wait)
.filter(|deadline| !runs_past_the_read_deadline || *deadline <= now)
```

- A write keeps the deadline only when it had expired even without counting the approval wait, so it is refused before it runs.
- Otherwise a person's write runs until it finishes or Stop is pressed.
- Reads and agents are unchanged.

## Also fixed: Workspace Clippy fails on main
`crates/policy/tests/bulk_import_postgres.rs` (from #4124) took a `cancel: bool` parameter that it never used. That breaks `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`. Worse, `a_cancelled_import_still_moves_the_sequence_past_the_rows_that_committed` was really testing a *completed* import. The helper now ends the scope with `BulkInsertEnd::Cancelled` when `cancel` is true.

## Tests
- **New:** `a_write_approved_after_the_read_deadline_still_runs_until_stopped` (paused time).
  - A Prod DDL is approved after 60 s, with a 30 s read deadline.
  - The write must still be running at 600 s, and Stop then gives `Cancelled`.
  - It **failed before the fix** ("a write approved after its read deadline passed must not get that deadline back") and passes after.
- `cargo test -p bookie-policy --lib`: 497 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p bookie-policy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (it failed on main).
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- The Docker-only Postgres import tests run in CI.

No changelog fragment: the defect came in with #4120 and is not released yet (AGENTS.md).

Security-sensitive (policy guard); please review the one-line reorder.

body:
Stacked on #124 (`fix/review-phase1`). GitHub retargets this PR to `main` once #124 merges and its branch is deleted.

## Changes
- **Release profile:** drop `codegen-units = 1`, so ThinLTO compiles the app crate across the default 16 codegen units in parallel. `lto = "thin"`, `strip = true` and the `x86-64-v2` baseline are unchanged. The speech, ONNX and ggml hot paths are native C/C++ libraries that this profile doesn't compile.
- **llama-helper:** remove its `[profile.release]`. Cargo ignores profiles in workspace members and warned about it on every build.
- **app_lib crate types:** `rlib` only. `staticlib` and `cdylib` were unused Tauri mobile defaults that cost two extra full release links, one of them a ThinLTO DLL link.
- **build-windows-release.ps1:** pass `tauri.prebuilt-frontend.conf.json` (`beforeBuildCommand: null`) after `Build-FrontendAssets` has already built and checked `frontend/out`, so the frontend isn't built a second time. A plain `tauri build`, `-CheckOnly` and CI are unaffected.
- **Dev profile:** dependencies use `debug = "line-tables-only"`, which shrinks `target/debug` and speeds up links. Workspace crates keep full debug info. The first dev build after this rebuilds dependencies once.
- **CI:** skip `choco install llvm --version=20.1.8` when `clang.exe` reports 20.1.8 and `libclang.dll` exists. The pinned install remains the fallback.

- `node scripts/verify-public-repo-safety.mjs`: passed

author: iprodev
body:
## Summary

On the live server, on-device processing failed in every browser because nginx sent the browser ffmpeg's modules with the wrong type, so everything quietly fell back to the server. This fixes that, gives two services files that work or simpler ones, and gives iPhones the file itself in the share sheet instead of a link to the API. The service changes match what yt-dlp gets for the same videos. The PornHub change was found and tested on the live server first, as a local patch.

## Changes

### On-device processing: send `.mjs` as JavaScript
- Ubuntu 24.04's nginx (1.24) doesn't know the `.mjs` extension, so `_libav/*.mjs` was sent as `application/octet-stream` with `nosniff`. Browsers refuse to run that as a module: Safari says "Importing a module script failed", Chrome "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module". Every local processing task failed at its first ffmpeg step and fell back to the server, which handed out a tunnel link.
- `deploy/nginx/fetchr-web.conf`: `.mjs` is sent as `text/javascript` (`default_type` in a regex location without `add_header`, so the cross-origin isolation headers still apply).
- `deploy/install.sh`: existing web configs are otherwise kept as they are, so the same block is added to them (after each `root` line, so also in server blocks certbot made), with a backup and the usual `nginx -t` rollback. A `fetchr-mjs` marker keeps it from being added twice.

### PornHub: direct mp4 files where HLS is blocked
- In countries with age verification laws (e.g. Poland, where the live server is), the HLS files answer 410, so every video was `content.region`.
- The direct mp4 files still work there. They're listed by the `mp4` media definition (`/video/get_media`), which only answers with the cookies the page sets, and the files need the page as referer. When HLS is blocked, the best mp4 for the quality is used (up to 720p) and tunneled with that referer (`match-action`: pornhub's direct files are `proxy`).
- Where HLS works, nothing changes.

### xvideos: mp4 instead of HLS when it's the same quality
- The site has HLS (up to 1080p) and a single mp4 file (usually 480p). When the HLS variant for the requested quality has the same size as the mp4, the mp4 is used: no segments, and a broken download can resume.
- The mp4's size comes from the `tkhd` box at the start of the file (one 64 KB range request).

### iOS: share files, not links
- On iOS, a file the browser downloaded itself is shared as a file ("Save Video" in the share sheet), but a tunnel was shared as a link, so the share sheet showed `api.fetchr.download`.
- With local processing on (`preferred`, the default), iOS devices now ask for `forced`: the browser downloads every file itself, also ones that need no processing (the queue's existing `proxy` pipeline), and shares the file. Files over 256 MB are opened instead, as before. If local processing fails, the request goes to the server like before.
- This also makes redirect-type files go through the API on iOS (`forced` implies `alwaysProxy`), which iOS couldn't save directly anyway.

### Other
- Release notes for 1.2.4.

## Testing
- **`.mjs` type, live site:** reproduced in WebKit and Chromium with iPhone emulation on `fetchr.download` with a YouTube Short (`YAoHH5uFZT0`): both files downloaded, then the ffmpeg worker failed with the errors above and the task fell back to the server. Same as a screen recording from a real iPhone. The files themselves are fine (they merge into a valid 23.3 MB mp4 here).
- **`.mjs` type, nginx 1.24.0 from Ubuntu:** the old config sends `application/octet-stream`; after `install.sh`'s new step, and with the new config, `text/javascript` with COOP/COEP, and other files are unchanged. Running the step twice changes nothing, and it doesn't add a second block after the manual one-line fix.
- **PornHub, live server** (temporary API with the patch on 1.2.2): 1080p (500 MB, complete), 480p (166 MB), 240p with local processing (71 MB), audio (15 MB) and mute (45 MB). The API answers in under 2 seconds.
- **xvideos, from here:** 720p and 480p now give the 480p mp4 (37.8 MB, 480×854, plays). 1080p and 360p still use HLS, since the mp4 isn't that size.
- **iOS**, iPhone emulation against a local API: a TikTok link is requested with `localProcessing: "forced"`, the API answers `local-processing` / `proxy`, the queue downloads the file, and its download button shares a `File` (`video/mp4`, 1,552,169 bytes, same as the server's file) instead of a URL. Not tested on a real iPhone yet.
- **Unit tests:** the mp4 size from `tkhd` boxes (versions 0 and 1, audio track first, no moov box, cut off), and PornHub's mp4 fallback (needs the page's cookies and referer, picks the quality, still a region error without mp4 files). The PornHub test fails with the old code.
- API unit tests: 84 pass on Node 22 and Node 24. `svelte-check` and lint pass, `bash -n deploy/install.sh` passes.

author: reliant-01
body:
Fixes obs `855d1b57` (report `10e3286f`), row of tracker #2279: `forge obs issue` had no verb to edit or delete a comment. The control plane serves `IssuesService.UpdateIssueComment` / `DeleteIssueComment`, but the CLI could not reach them, so cleaning up 143 duplicate comments took raw Connect calls through the credential helper, with the scopes guessed by hand.

## Change
- `forge obs issue edit-comment <id> <comment-id> <text> [env]` → `UpdateIssueComment` (the control plane admits the author only). The document is the `obs issue comment` one: the stored comment, `updated_at` set.
- `forge obs issue delete-comment <id> <comment-id> [env]` → `DeleteIssueComment` (author, or an org owner/admin). The document carries `deleted_comment.id`, a new field in `forge.obs.issue/v1`; nothing existing changes.
- `obsbackend.IssueReader` gains `UpdateIssueComment` and `DeleteIssueComment`. Cloud calls them by procedure name, like the other issue writes. Local refuses (exit 2), as it does for `comment`. Both procedures are declared under `obs:triage` (`DeclareCloudScopes`), which matches control-plane `admitWrite`. The mock is regenerated with `go run ./internal/tools/mockgen`.
- A missing comment id or an empty edit is refused before any call (exit 1).
- The `observability/query` skill's verb table lists both verbs.

Comment ids were already in `obs issue <id> --json` (`timeline[].comment.id`) and in the text timeline, so the report's ask for them is already met.

## Alternatives considered
- **Flags on `comment`** (`comment <id> <text> --edit <comment-id>`, `--delete`): this overloads one verb's positional shape, and a delete takes no text. Separate verbs keep each one's arity honest, like `assign`.
- **A `comment` subgroup** (`comment add|edit|delete`): this would break `obs issue comment <id> <text>`, a v1 surface.
- **Not done here (separate asks in the same report):** an idempotent comment mode, and a structured exit for quota refusals on `comment`. Each one is its own design change.

## Test
- `internal/obsbackend`: `TestCloudUpdateAndDeleteIssueComment` covers the request shapes, the pre-call refusals, error-code→exit mapping and Local refusals.
- `internal/cli`: `TestObsIssueEditAndDeleteComment` covers the JSON and text documents, the procedure and body sent, a permission-denied delete (exit 2, not retried), and a local env (exit 2).
- `go test -short ./internal/obsbackend/` and `-run 'TestObsIssue|Schema|Surface|Capabilit|Help|Command|Skill' ./internal/cli/` pass.

## Post-merge check
None is needed in production. The change is CLI-only: two new verbs and two procedures declared under the existing `obs:triage` scope, which the control plane already enforces in `admitWrite`. Nothing is deployed and no server behaviour changes. To check by hand after a release, `forge obs issue comment <id> "x" <env> --json` and then `forge obs issue delete-comment <id> <comment.id> <env>` on a hosted env remove the comment again, and `forge obs issue <id> <env> --timeline-limit 5` no longer shows it.

## Rollback
Revert this PR. No state, schema or wire contract changes, so a revert only removes the two verbs. Comments that were already edited or deleted stay as they are; that is the control plane's own behaviour for these RPCs.

body:
## Summary

Proves a wanted statement of the wiki's task list, moved out of `WantedExt` with its full name and statement unchanged, with its own tests and bookkeeping.

### Prove A set in the van der Waerden, lacunary and difference-set ideals outside the Sidon ideal

**A set in the van der Waerden, lacunary and difference-set ideals outside the Sidon ideal.** There is a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that belongs to the van der Waerden ideal, is contained in a finite union of gap-lacunary sets (infinite sets whose gaps between consecutive elements tend to infinity), and belongs to the ideal $D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ of sets avoiding large difference sets, but is not contained in any finite union of Sidon sets.

author: ghost-in-the-groove
body:
A player reads tablature from arm's length. The fret numbers were the smallest
thing on the page that had to be read, and the texts of the techniques could
not be read at all.

## What changes (ADR-0113)

| | before | now | on paper at 1.75 mm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fret numbers | 1.3 staff spaces | 1.6 | 6.4 pt → 7.9 pt |
| "P.M.", "let ring", harmonic labels | 0.95 | 1.25 | 4.7 pt → 6.2 pt |
| "H" and "P" over an arc | 0.85 | 1.05 | 4.2 pt → 5.2 pt |
| The amount over a bend | 0.95 | 1.2 | 4.7 pt → 5.9 pt |
| The whammy bar's label | 0.85 | 1.1 | 4.2 pt → 5.4 pt |
| The first fret of a chord diagram | 0.9 | 1.0 | |

The lanes that hold the texts grow by what the text grew.

A tablature staff under the standard staff of its instrument now leaves the
time signature to that staff, as guitar editions are printed; a tablature that
stands alone still carries it. The measures of both staves start together as
before.

## How it was checked

- `python scripts/elara.py check` passes.
- New test: alone, the tablature carries the signature and its change; under a
  standard staff only that staff does.
- The corpus snapshots with tablature were regenerated and looked at, and the
  app's page was looked at in both views.

## To watch

- Lines with many fretted notes are a little wider, so a long song may break
  its lines elsewhere.

author: langosch16
body:
## Woher sie kommen

Aus dem Dropbox-Archiv, `studio flatland/_JOBS/ARCHIV/burgenland energie/BGLD_2/`. Die Dateien lagen dort als Platzhalter ohne lokalen Inhalt (0 Byte auf der Platte) und mussten erst aus der Cloud geholt werden.

| Datei | Format | Inhalt |
|---|---|---|
| `partikel-gitter.mp4` | 1280 × 720 | Partikelwelle, die zum Burgenland-Umriss als Gitternetz wird |
| `partikel-spirale.mp4` | 1280 × 720 | Partikellinie, die sich zu einer Spirale aufrollt |
| `umriss-hoch.mp4` | 720 × 1280 | Gitternetz-Nahaufnahme, dann der leuchtende Umriss |

## Wasserzeichen

Alle drei hatten ein sichtbares „Veo" unten rechts. Entfernt per `delogo` — quer `x=1190 y=660 w=88 h=52`, hoch `x=630 y=1225 w=86 h=42`.

Das war nicht von vornherein klar. Meine erste Einschätzung war, dass es bei zweien über Bildinhalt liegt und eine Entfernung schmieren würde. Nachgemessen stimmte das nicht: die Stelle liegt über die ganze Laufzeit entweder auf Schwarz oder auf stark unscharfem Bokeh, und dort interpoliert `delogo` unsichtbar. An mehreren Zeitpunkten gegengeprüft, auch an den hellsten.

## Ton

Die Clips haben echte Tonspuren (mean −20 dB, max −4,6 dB), keine Stille. Ich hatte sie im ersten Durchgang versehentlich mit `-an` weggeworfen und neu encodiert — jetzt als AAC 128k erhalten.

## Einbindung

Jedes der nun vier Videos hängt als Standbild-plus-mp4-Paar in `images[]`. Der bestehende Film hat dafür nachträglich auch ein Standbild bekommen, sonst wäre er als einziger ohne Play-Overlay dagestanden. Vier Play-Overlays, kein `<video>`-Element vor dem ersten Klick.

`mp_.mp4` aus demselben Ordner ist byte-identisch (SHA-256) mit dem Hochformat-Film, der schon in `_quellen/` liegt, und deshalb nicht dazugekommen.

## Gewicht

Der Ordner wächst auf 15 MB. Das ist der mit Abstand schwerste unter `public/projekte/` — falls das zu viel wird, wäre die Spirale (4,3 MB) der erste Kandidat zum Streichen, sie zeigt als einzige nicht den Umriss.

## Prüfung

`tsc --noEmit` sauber. Panel lokal aufgeklappt: vier Standbilder, vier Play-Overlays, `partikel-gitter.mp4` abgespielt und an der Wasserzeichen-Stelle kontrolliert — nichts zu sehen. Kein Bild mit `naturalWidth === 0`.

author: swbaek
body:
Refs #1997

## 변경

`apps/editor/src/styles.css`의 선택자 세 개를 같은 요소에 맞으면서 Chromium의 스타일 무효화 범위가 좁아지는 형태로 바꿨다. 화면과 동작은 바뀌지 않는다.

Chromium은 `:has()`, `:last-child`, `:hover`·`:focus-within`마다 규칙들의 오른쪽 특징(첫 class, 없으면 첫 attribute, 없으면 tag)을 하나의 무효화 집합으로 합친다. 상태가 바뀐 요소 아래에서 그 특징을 가진 요소를 모두 다시 계산한다. 5,000블록 문서에는 블록마다 조작 버튼이 있어, 아래 세 규칙 때문에 클릭·포커스·입력마다 약 33,800개 요소를 다시 계산했다.

| 규칙 | 무효화 집합에 넣던 특징 | 계기 | 바꾼 형태 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 명령 센터 닫힘 overlay `.ui-portal:has(...) [data-slot="dialog-overlay"][data-ending-style]` | `[data-slot]` (모든 `Button`, 약 14,500개) | body의 DOM 변경마다 `:has()` 확인 | attribute 순서를 바꿔 `[data-ending-style]`이 특징이 됨 |
| 폴더 선택 창 정렬 머리글 `[role="columnheader"]:last-child > button` | `button` 태그 | 제목 번호 폭 측정이 body에 임시 요소를 붙였다 뗄 때 `#root`의 `:last-child` 변경 | 마지막 머리글에 custom property를 두고 버튼이 읽음 |
| 보이는 블록 조작부 `.document:is(:hover, :focus-within) .block-controls.visible` | `.block-controls` (블록 수만큼) | 포인터가 문서에 들어오거나 포커스가 들어올 때 | `.visible.block-controls` |

## 배포 빌드 측정 (5,000블록, 파일 클릭부터 첫 입력 반영 확인까지)

Windows, persistent Chrome, CLI 패키징 빌드의 정적 파일을 실제 HTTP daemon으로 제공했다. 실행마다 Host와 브라우저를 새로 띄우고 master와 이 변경을 번갈아 실행했다. 측정 중 같은 PC에서 다른 작업이 CPU를 60~100% 쓰고 있었다. 그래서 Host GET 시간만으로도 ±3초가 흔들렸다.

| 구분 | master | 이 변경 | 차이 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 마지막 교대 묶음 중 Host GET < 3초인 3회 (초) | 18.7 / 19.1 / 19.4 | 14.9 / 15.3 / 16.7 | 중앙값 19.1 → 15.3 (−20%) |
| 전체 교대 실행 중앙값 (master 20회, 변경 17회) | 18.8 | 17.0 | −10% (부하 잡음 포함) |
| 첫 문단 DOM부터 입력 반영까지 중앙값 (같은 실행) | 13.8 | 10.6 | −23% |
| 문단 pointerdown부터 입력 반영까지 중앙값 (같은 실행) | 5.6 | 3.9 | −30% |

Chrome Performance 트레이스(master 3회, 변경 2회)에서 메인 스레드의 스타일 재계산은 2.9~3.4초에서 1.5~1.8초로, 접근성 트리 갱신은 3.0~3.7초에서 2.5~2.9초로 줄었다. 상호작용만 따로 기록한 트레이스에서는 3,000개가 넘는 스타일 재계산이 클릭·입력 구간에서 사라졌다. 남은 큰 재계산은 문서를 처음 그릴 때의 약 89,000개와 블록 조작부를 처음 붙일 때의 약 33,500개다.

## PR #2004와의 관계

#2004의 코드는 옮기지 않았다. master와 #2004를 3회씩 번갈아 실행하면 중앙값이 17.3초와 17.8초로 잡음 범위 안이다. #2004에서 늘어난 것처럼 보인 시간은 순차 실행 때 생긴 부하 차이로 판단한다. 근거는 #1997 댓글에 적는다.

## 검증

- 배포 빌드 교대 측정과 Chrome 트레이스 (위 표)
- `pnpm browser:test folder-navigation command-center layout-rules quiet-document block-move footnotes` 6건 통과. 폴더 선택 창 마지막 머리글과 크기 열의 오른쪽 끝 정렬은 folder-navigation이 검사한다. 이후 주석 위치와 규칙 합치기만 바꾼 최종 형태에서는 PC 부하로 Vite 서버가 60초 안에 뜨지 않거나 fixture 준비가 15초를 넘었다. 같은 조건의 master에서도 Vite 서버가 뜨지 않았으며 회귀 검사는 CI 결과로 확인한다.
- 새 테스트는 추가하지 않았다. 선택자 문자열이나 브라우저 내부 무효화 방식을 고정하는 테스트는 공개 동작을 검증하지 않는다.

author: wehos
body:
## 改动概述 / Summary

喵能力里有使魔在办事、在等用户回话、或者刚办完时，她（主对话的角色）派发过来的一句话，要先判断它对这些事做了什么：是在回答挂着的问话（权限问话还要读出选了什么），是叫停哪件，是对哪件补充，还是新事。以前全靠词表和比词（同意 / 拒绝词表、叫停词表、补充词表、「和问话重合几个词」「还说了几个别的实词」），#4082、#4107、#4114 三轮一直在打补丁。2026-11-26 实测仍错得多：挂一条普通的跑命令权限问话时，「帮我运行一下测试」被读成同意、直接批准了命令，「别忘了更新 README」被读成拒绝，「응」「お願いします」不算回答；在办「整理照片」时说「别忘了把照片按月份分」，被叫停词表的「别…了」认成叫停，把在办的事停掉了。

owner 2026-11-26 定：词表整个不要了，改由小模型读（以后换决策模型）；叫停、补充一起改（「叫停主要是对不上号」，要考虑背景里有一堆使魔和猫老大）；超时要有提示；免费档位那两处提示词在这里修。

这个 PR：

- **一次小模型请求，读这句话对在办的事做了什么**（`LexicalDecisionModel.read_under_way`，识别档）。给它看一张编号清单：她在办的委托、委托里在等用户回话的问话、最近一天办完的。每件写明状态、项目、哪只使魔在做（用户叫它的名字，「侦察猫」「猫小弟 "链接"」）、是不是老大转交的、组队成员各在做什么、在问什么。它答 `answer`（第几条）/ `stop`（哪几件）/ `add`（哪件）/ `unsure` / `new`，以及这句话有没有点明是哪件。
- **宿主守几条规矩，不全信模型**：没点明的叫停、几件在办，一件都不停，先问是哪件；几条问话挂着时光说「好」，一条都不答，先问是哪件；**同时挂着几条权限问话时一律先问是哪条**（认哪条要看使魔写的命令），并告诉她请用户点对应问话上的按钮（打字说不清是哪条：候选全是权限问话时，或几条问话给的答法一样、说话分不清时）；同一件委托在清单里出现两行（判读时刚办完）算一件；在等的问话、权限问话都按完整列表数，清单截掉的也算；选项和另一条在等的问话重叠的（两条都给 Cats / Dogs；使魔一起问的几个问题的选项也算），除非说了只有目标才有的选项，都按没点明处理；回答或补充点了几件的先问；在办的多过清单列得下时，停几件的、或停的那件的项目 / 使魔还有没列出来的，先问是哪些（免得漏停）。
- **权限问话选了什么另问一次**（`_read_choice`，同一个模型）。合在一次里读时，小模型常把「好的」读成「始终允许」。这次请求**只给它看宿主自己写的问话类别措辞**（`reports.permission_kind`，去掉命令、路径）、可选的答法、她转交的那句和用户这一轮的原话，**不给它看使魔写的任何字**：使魔读到网页里埋的话、写进命令，原来能借这次请求把「不行」读成「始终允许」（Codex 安全评审）。
- **打字或说出来的回答最多放行这一次**：读成「始终允许」「仅本会话允许」时宿主降成「本次允许」，回执里请她告诉用户点问话上的按钮（owner 的自动评审定为必改：「始终允许」会把整个类别写进设置文件）。按钮作答不变。权限仍由宿主放行，和界面按钮同一条路；话照原样交给那件委托。
- **读不出来、超时、出错**：当新事办，问话还挂着，**回执末尾告诉她这句没判出来**（8 种语言）；超时多半超过第一轮 1 秒，这句随迟到的回执送到时一律主动叫醒她。读完回答（两次请求）以后、交给委托之前，再看一次是不是关了喵能力或点了「全部停止」。
- 一次可以叫停几件（「商城网站的活都停了」）；逐件停，一件失败不耽误别的；回执只列这次停下的（按钮先停了的、判读时已办完的不算），没能停下的写「没能停下：…，可以在界面上再停一次」（会叫醒她），停了但正在跑的部分没能确认都停了的也单独说（包括插件服务器没接受取消、只返回失败不抛错的那种）；一步清理失败不耽误后面的（插件取消失败也照样关掉使魔）；宿主开始关闭后不再接着停。读成补充要转告时，判读等模型的这段时间里点了「全部停止」或关了喵能力的，不再转告（卡住的委托不会被迟到的补充重新开工）。
- 「没听懂你的回答」回执、她转告用户的权限问话、用户问「有什么在等」时她念的那一行，都只列打字能给的「本次允许 / 拒绝」，「始终 / 本会话」请点按钮（和上一条一致；给模型看的清单照旧四个，实测输入不变；权限那一行的上限 140 → 150 token）。
- 砍掉回答、叫停、补充三套词表读法（清单见回归报告）。编排器还在用的补充词、泛用词表留着；按相似度认重复的留在本地。
- 免费档位：旁问、另开一只两段提示词开头改成带逗号的固定写法（原来每次 400）。
- 句子集：原来的三份合成一份回答评测集（873 句，加了跑命令权限、开放问题、三条同时挂着三组）；新建一份叫停 / 补充评测集（8 个背景、213 句，含有猫老大、成员、侦察猫、插件、在等批准、刚办完 / 没办成的繁忙背景）。两份都有一半是不知道读法的模型写的。单元测试用假模型钉流程，评测集在单元测试里只做自检。
- 设计稿 17.17（17.13–17.15 加了指向；main 上 #4116 先占了 17.16，这里排 17.17）；三语 `agent-system.md` 第一轮那段和讲旧读法的两处。

Refs #3683

body:
Fixes #287. Follow-up 3 of 4 from pull request #280 (issue #276).

## The problem

In the native iOS word editor, each saved example sentence's actions menu (the ellipsis icon) was held at a fixed width of 44 points, with a comment saying a menu's label fills its width. That was a workaround for the SwiftUI bridge; since bridge 0.1.0-preview.68 a menu can keep its label's own width, so the reason for the fixed width was gone and the comment was out of date.

## The cause

Checked against the code as it is now; the issue's reading holds. `VocabularyWordEditView.Examples.cs` still had `Views.Menu(Views.Image("ellipsis.circle"), ...).WithFixedWidth(44)`, and both project files pin `Microsoft.SwiftUI` 0.1.0-preview.68, whose `MenuLabel` draws a label without the filling frame when the menu asks (`WithMenuLabelFittingContent`). One correction to the issue: `PaceMenu` is in `Features/Activities/ConversationScreen.cs`.

## The fix

- `src/SentenceStudio.Native.iOS/Features/Vocabulary/VocabularyWordEditView.Examples.cs`: the menu calls `.WithMenuLabelFittingContent()` in place of `.WithFixedWidth(44)`, and its label is the symbol with 12 points of padding at each side (`.WithPadding(0, 12, 0, 12)`). The comment says what is true now.
- The menu is about 44 points wide at the default text size (12 + the symbol + 12) and now grows with the symbol at larger text sizes, where the fixed 44 points did not. The label is exactly as high as before (no padding above or below), so no row changes height.
- Learning Value Gate: does not apply (a menu's width; no activity prompt, response, mode, toggle or default changes).
- No bridge change, no version change: the modifier is in the pinned 0.1.0-preview.68.

## How it was checked

- `dotnet test tests/SentenceStudio.Native.iOS.Tests/SentenceStudio.Native.iOS.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~NativeExampleActionsMenuContractTests" -p:IncludeMobileTargets=false -p:ValidateXcodeVersion=false`: passes with the fix; with the view file put back to `main`'s it fails ("Not found: .WithMenuLabelFittingContent()"). This is the proof named for the runner.
- The view test program (`tests/SentenceStudio.Native.SwiftUIViews.Tests`, built with `-p:ValidateXcodeVersion=false`, 0 errors): 35 passed, 4 failed. The new case, "Word editor: a sentence's actions menu keeps its label's own width, not a fixed one", passes: it builds the page through the real bridge and reads the menu (fits its label, no fixed width, the symbol, the four actions). The four failures are the four that open issue #295 lists as failing on `main`; "Word editor: Reference Sentences have Generate, the add row, suggestions and sentences core first" is one of them, so the issue's "the view tests that draw the examples still pass" could not hold for that case before this change. I did not rebuild on `main` to watch it fail there again; #295 records it.
- With the same filter widened to `NativeConversationVoicePanelContractTests`: `NoViewInTheHeadIsFixedSize` fails, "Features/Import/YouTubeImportView.cs uses WithFixedSize". It fails on `main` (nothing here touches those files); see Next.
- Not checked: the width in points on iOS. The symbol's width (about 20 points at the default text size) is from memory of SF Symbols, not measured, and the macOS test host cannot show an iOS menu's width (it draws a menu as a pull-down button sized to its label). The iOS head itself was not built; the view tests compile the changed file against the pinned bridge.
- App run: no, the session stack's user has no words or sentences, the row's height cannot change by construction, and the look on the simulator is the second task under Next.
- GitHub checks: left to the runner.

## Choices made for you

Merging accepts these. To change one, comment with the `/revise` line beside it.

What a learner will now see: the same row. The example sentence's text runs up to the ellipsis icon, which sits in a target about 44 points wide; at larger text sizes the target is wider, with the icon. No wording changes.

- **Padding at the sides only, not all round.** The issue recommended padding as `PaceMenu` has (13, 12, 13, 12), a 44-point target both ways. I padded only the sides: a sentence of unknown origin with no translation is a one-line row, and a label 44 points high could make that Form row taller, which the issue says must not happen and I could not see on iOS in this pass. The target is as high as the symbol, as it was before. To switch: `/revise pad the examples menu's icon on all four sides for a 44-point-high target`
- **Padding, not a fixed 44-point frame on the label.** A fixed width on the label would be exactly 44 points at every text size; padding follows the symbol. To switch: `/revise give the examples menu's label a fixed width of 44 points in place of padding`

## Next

1. The contract test NoViewInTheHeadIsFixedSize passes on main: it names the YouTube rows' four uses or they are gone. It is red on `main` today, so every run of that project shows a failure that is not the change's.
2. Example sentences' actions menu, seen on the simulator: about 44 points wide, and a 44-point-high target if the row keeps its height. The width here was reasoned, not seen, and the target is still only as high as the icon.

Already open, so not listed again: #286 (the same menu shape in Sam's conversation list) and #295 (the four view tests that fail on `main`).

## Left undone

- A look on your phone: open a word with example sentences and check that a long sentence runs up to the ellipsis icon and the menu opens. (The second task under Next does this on the simulator.)

## Activity log
**The problem, restated.** The word editor's example sentences (native iOS) give each sentence's actions menu a fixed width of 44 points, with a comment saying a menu's label fills its width. That was a workaround for the bridge; since bridge 0.1.0-preview.68 a menu can keep its label's own width, so the fixed width's reason is gone and the comment is out of date.

## First pass

- 18:47 (CST, 00:47 UTC) Read AGENTS.md, /Users/Shared/sstudio-feedback/docs/admin-feedback-fix.md and the issue (a follow-up, 3 of 4 from pull request #280, issue #276).
- 18:48 Checked the issue's reading against the code now. It holds: `VocabularyWordEditView.Examples.cs` line 172-177 still has `Views.Menu(Views.Image("ellipsis.circle"), ...).WithFixedWidth(44)` with the old comment; both project files pin `Microsoft.SwiftUI` 0.1.0-preview.68; `WithMenuLabelFittingContent` has one caller, `PaceMenu` in `Features/Activities/ConversationScreen.cs` (the issue says `ConversationScreen.cs`; it is under Activities, not Conversation). No other `.WithFixedWidth(44)` on a menu in the head.
- 18:49 Read the bridge at the commit that made preview.68 (`1991ead` in ~/sstudio/bridge; `session-bridge.sh where` says "no tag v0.1.0-preview.68", so read by commit). `MenuLabel` in `SwiftUINode.swift`: by default the label sits in `frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`; with `menuLabelFitsContent` no frame is added and the menu is as wide as its label. `WithPadding(top, right, bottom, left)`. The bridge's own test notes that macOS draws a Menu as a pull-down button that sizes to its label either way, so the macOS view tests cannot show the iOS width of a menu.

author: ldelvoye
body:
Sixth step of the core rip out. Each terminal now has a headless screen in the runtime, fed by its shell from the moment it opens. A window's view is loaded from a snapshot of that screen and then follows it, so a view can be thrown away and rebuilt without losing what the terminal shows. A reloaded window comes back with its terminals' contents.

The window's connection to the runtime becomes the terminal channel: `attach`, `detach`, `write`, `resize` and `clear` one way, and `attached` (with the snapshot), `output`, `resized`, `cleared` and `end` the other. A resize and a clear take effect at one point in the output on both sides. While a view attaches, what would be sent to it is kept and follows the snapshot.

What the runtime takes over with the screen: a terminal's size (the window asks, the runtime decides), Clear, titles (the window no longer reports them), the scrollback setting, and a program's questions to the terminal (device attributes, status, cursor position, mode reports). It also pauses a shell whose output it has not parsed yet.

The engine is behind two interfaces, `Screen` in the runtime and `TerminalView` in the window, each filled from one folder that is the only place allowed the xterm packages. `src/conformance/` feeds output to a screen, loads its snapshot into a view stand-in and compares with a terminal fed the same output directly. The five things a serialize round trip is known to lose are expected failures there.

Known limits, for the next step:
- The window still keeps a view for every terminal, so every scrollback is in memory twice.
- Only a view can answer a color query, so one asked before a view attaches gets no answer.
- Loading a full 100,000-line scrollback takes about half a second, during which the runtime sends nothing else.

`scripts/measure/README.md` has one run at this commit. Typing while four terminals print takes 11 ms at the median, where it took about 100.

author: conradkurth
body:
## What

A guest's Verify age start now sends the billing email, so AgeCheck's page can offer a returning guest a one-time emailed code that passes them as a reused check (AgeCheck decision #23, TAX-1839).

- The email is sent only for a guest, and only while GetIntegrationInfo's new `guestReuseCode` is true for the start key. AgeCheck decides when that is; the plugin does not restate its rule.
- Signed-in customers keep `customer_ref` and never send the email.
- The start's idempotency key gains `:e` plus 16 hex of an HMAC of the lower-cased email (a guard-secret key), so a corrected email never replays the earlier create.
- If AgeCheck refuses the email (`invalid_argument`, not the US-only refusal), the start runs once more without it. Only the code is logged.
- The classic checkout copies the typed billing email into the session, as the block checkout's Store API already does.
- Settings shows a "Returning customers" line: on for N days, guests need a store name, or off. In test mode AgeCheck emails codes only to confirmed notification recipients, and the line says so.
- Privacy text, readme (Unreleased changelog), README, CLAUDE.md and the .pot are updated.

## Why

Owner decision #23: repeat buyers who check out as guests should not have to verify again within the store's reuse window.

## How verified

- `phpunit` on PHP 8.3 and 7.4: 637 tests pass. `phpcs` and `phpstan` clean.
- Mock engine tests (`node --test tests/mock-agecheck/server.test.mjs`): 42 pass, including a new guest-reuse test.
- wp-env (WooCommerce 11.3.0) with the mock: `w3b.mjs` passes, with three new groups. The block checkout's Store API `update-customer` does persist the billing email (the start carries it). The classic checkout's typed email reaches the start. A returning guest passes REUSED by the code, and the order is bound, held and released. `prepayment.mjs` still passes.

## Limits

- No version bump or tag: entries are under "Unreleased".
- In production both new GetIntegrationInfo fields read 0/false until `AGECHECK_REUSE` is on, so no email is sent before then.
- Cross-store reuse (E13) is out of scope. If it is turned on later, the privacy text needs a sentence about it.

## Paired PR and merge order

Pairs with ConradKurth/tax#677 (branch `tax-1839-agecheck-guest-reuse`), which adds `reuse_window_days` (8) and `guest_reuse_code` (9) to GetIntegrationInfo and the 90-day default window. Merge and release tax first. This PR is safe before then too: an older engine omits both fields, which read as off. TAX-1838's plugin PR #13 also edits `IntegrationInfo.php`, the mock and readme.txt, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

author: nielsfranke
body:
G18 follow-up from XTSH2 (#1166): offline Develop now knows a photo's sensor kind once it has been verified from the file.

## What
- **Catalog schema 38** (`crates/catalog/migrations/0038.sql`, `sensor_kind.rs`): table `sensor_kinds(asset_id, kind ∈ {bayer, xTrans}, fingerprint of the file read)`: the latest verified read of the photo's file. A new verified read replaces it (also when the file was changed in place and the library has not registered that yet); an Unknown read of another file than the recorded one forgets it (`forget_sensor_kind`), an Unknown read of the same file keeps it; a trigger drops the row when the registered size, time or fingerprint changes (folder sync, relink, save in place) — same pattern as `image_hashes` (schema 20). Unknown is not representable in the stored type. Sessions (`session.sqlite`) and catalogs share the schema, so both get it. Down-compat as for every schema bump: older Rawtonic refuses schema 38 (`migrations::upgrade`), noted in CHANGELOG.
- **`raw_sensor_kind`** (`src-tauri/src/ai_denoise.rs`): readable file → probe as before; for a photo a session/catalog manages, the answer read from an unchanged file (fingerprint before = after) is remembered in a detached blocking task (no write lock when nothing changes); a loose RAW is probed exactly as before (no extra fingerprint reads). Offline file (`preview_proxy::source_available` false, so cloud placeholders are never read) → the remembered kind, Unknown without one.
- **`useRawSensorKind`**: asks the backend also for offline photos; keeps a kind read while the same photo was online. StudioDevelop: while the offline answer is pending, AI Denoise waits (disabled) instead of counting as deferred; stored X-Trans → X-Trans note, stored Bayer → Quality select, exactly as online; nothing stored → the neutral deferred note as before.

## Not changed
Render and export: `ai_denoise::option_for` / `sensor_kind` still read the readable file; the stored kind is UI-only, so no rendered pixel can change. No rendering, decode or export code is touched (existing export identity tests run in the full check).

## Decision (pro photographer, least surprise)
A kind read while the photo was online is kept when it goes offline even if it is not in a library (as before #1166's follow-up); a failed online read is not stored and does not erase a stored kind for the same file.

## Review: coordinator override after round 3
Codex blocked rounds 1–3 (findings R1–R3 below). All are fixed and tested; **the R3 fixes are tested but not re-reviewed**. Shipped with `--no-review "coordinator override after round 3: …"` by the coordinator's decision: the stored kind is UI-only (render/export unchanged) and any missed case falls back to main's deferred note. Guard for catalog data: the migration tests — `migration_fixtures` (every historical schema v01–v38 upgrades to its recorded result; upgraded schema = new library's schema; a failing migration changes nothing) and `sensor_kind::an_older_library_takes_the_table_and_upgrading_again_changes_nothing` (old DB → new via `undo_0038.sql`, reopening is idempotent).

## Review round 1 (Codex) fixes
- blocking (file changed in place → stale or missing kind offline): rows now hold the latest read of the file, not only reads matching the registered fingerprint; an unreadable replacement forgets the old kind.
- should_fix (pending treated as deferred): pending disables AI Denoise; delayed-response test added.
- should_fix (extra fingerprint I/O for loose RAWs): skipped when no library manages the photo.

## Review round 2 (Codex) fixes
- blocking (relink to the original keeps a row read from the replacement): Locate Photo / relink folder / Synchronize Folder moves (files found by the registered fingerprint) drop a row whose fingerprint is not the registered one (`sensor_kind::forget_reads_of_other_files`); test through `Library::relink`.
- should_fix (loose RAW still fingerprinted while a catalog is active): membership (`asset_at`) is checked before any fingerprint read.
- should_fix (out-of-order background writes): each read takes a ticket; the write runs under the library write lock only for the newest read of that file; test writes the later read first, then the earlier one.
- should_fix (ARCHITECTURE wording): updated.

## Review round 3 (Codex) fixes
- blocking (a rename dropped a valid row read from a file changed in place): the round-2 path trigger is gone; only the fingerprint-matched relinks above drop such a row, `relocate` (rename/move in Rawtonic) and `follow_volumes` keep it; test `a_rename_keeps_the_kind_of_the_file_it_carries`.
- should_fix (unlocked no-op check could let an older write pass a newer read): the whole check-and-write runs under the library write lock (in the background; Develop's answer never waits).

## Tests (failing first)
- `crates/catalog/tests/sensor_kind.rs`: stored after a verified read and kept across reopen; a read of the file changed in place replaces it, forget removes it; `file_saved` (new fingerprint) clears it, the row is deleted; old DB (undo_0038) upgrades, reopen idempotent; wire never "unknown".
- `migration_fixtures`: new v38 fixture with rows; all `.expected` re-blessed (only new table/trigger/index lines and `user_version 38`; older `.sql` fixtures unchanged).
- `ai_denoise::tests::a_verified_read_is_remembered_for_the_photo_offline_and_a_failed_one_is_not`: Bayer/X-Trans stored, Unknown not; Unknown of the same file keeps, of a replaced file forgets; a file edited in place re-recorded; a read during which the file changed not remembered; offline answers from the library, serialized in the frontend contract's shape (`src/contracts/rawSensorKind.json`).
- Vitest: hook asks for offline photos (failed on the old hook); StudioDevelop offline with stored xTrans → X-Trans note, no Quality select, slider v3 → v6; stored bayer → Quality select, v3 kept (both failed on the old hook).

`scripts/check.sh --brief --changed` green.

author: gafferongames
body:
Per the owner's ruling (2026-11-25): per pull request, schema runs ONLY compile + one simple happy path per language, one job of 2 minutes or less. Everything else is nightly.

## What changed

- **`ci-fast.yml` (new)**: one job, `happy-path`, on the fleet schema runners, `timeout-minutes: 2`, plus the existing `fork-pull-request` guard. It builds `bin/schema` once, then for each of the 18 legs runs `make happy-<lang>`: generate `test/happy/Happy.schema`, compile one small unit, and run one round trip (write a `ShipCreate`, read it back, compare every field). Each leg is timed and written to the step summary; every leg runs even after a failure.
- **`ci-fast-nightly.yml`**: the old `ci-fast.yml`, moved with `git mv`. It runs on `schedule` (`53 1 * * *`) and `workflow_dispatch` only, with no timeouts (the nightly rule). A scheduled run picks every tracked file, and the verdict refuses any skip on a schedule. No job was deleted.
- **`make/happy-path.mk`, `test/happy/`**: the 18 happy-path targets and programs. Each program was planted red with a wrong field value.
- **The tests**:
  - `TestPerPRIsTheHappyPathOnly` checks that ci-fast.yml holds exactly happy-path and the fork guard, with only the allowed actions, make targets and shell. It also checks that HAPPY_LEGS equals the registry's languages, and that every `happy-<lang>` rule needs only `bin/schema`/`toolchain-<lang>` and runs no other make or test runner. 17 plants, each red.
  - `TestTheScheduleRunsEveryNightlyJob` checks that every nightly job runs on the schedule. Its plant takes leg-gate off the schedule.
  - The existing internal/ci tests and `docs/CI-TIERS.md` were updated for the new shape. They were not weakened.

## Per-language seconds (hetzner1, warm, make startup included)

| leg | s | leg | s | leg | s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c | 2.286 | goose | 1.128 | luau | 1.090 |
| cpp | 1.172 | java | 1.786 | moo | 0.980 |
| cs | 1.864 | js | 1.054 | python | 1.087 |
| dart | 1.285 | lobster | 1.116 | ruby | 1.071 |
| elixir | 1.409 | lua | 1.090 | rust | 1.267 |
| go | 1.222 | | | squirrel | 1.029 |
| | | | | unity | 2.140 |

Total for the legs: **24.1 s**. The other steps:
- cloning the siblings in parallel: about 1.8 s;
- building `bin/schema`: 1 to 2 s warm, about 27 s cold;
- the moo driver's Go build: about 14.6 s on a cold Go build cache.

The worst case is still well under 2 minutes.

author: theatrus
body:
A spike for PSF-Studio, a native companion editor that starts from PSF Guard's channel stacks and does the color processing as a document of layers. It is a draft: the editor, `psf-studio`, lives in its own workspace at `studio/` and is still a prototype, and the design record says what is built and what is not.

## What you can do with it

- Open a target from PSF Guard: a project's color stacks show **Open *target* in PSF Studio**, a `psf-studio://` link the application answers.
- Open stack files from inside Studio with **Open**, or run `psf-guard studio` from a terminal. All three run the same command.
- Prepare a Studio store from a PSF Guard server (`psf-guard studio-sources`) or from stack files on this computer, FITS or XISF, with no server (`psf-guard studio-files --channel ha=Ha.xisf …`). Both run the same preparation.
- Start from a recipe (Narrowband, Narrowband with RGB stars, RGB, LRGB, RGB with emission lines) and then change anything: add any input to any part, such as Ha into the color of an LRGB picture, without redoing the rest.
- Calibrate R, G and B against Gaia, stretch the RGB stars with Seiza's star stretch, and use the layered stretch, which is Studio's default for new documents.
- Run BlurXTerminator, NoiseXTerminator, StarXTerminator or Seiza's noise model on an input from the app.

![Narrowband with RGB stars, layered stretch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theatrus/psf-guard/6fa1390cf0fc8e9b207c12786c4f2cb85612ecc8/psf-studio-spike/narrowband-rgb-stars-layered.jpg)
![An input's controls: where it goes, and its tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theatrus/psf-guard/6fa1390cf0fc8e9b207c12786c4f2cb85612ecc8/psf-studio-spike/input-goes-to-and-tools.jpg)
![Open in PSF Studio on a project's color stacks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theatrus/psf-guard/cd730754331320fed8bf399dd8cb28e2eb1074a5/psf-studio-spike/open-in-psf-studio.jpg)
![R, G and B calibrated against Gaia](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theatrus/psf-guard/6fa1390cf0fc8e9b207c12786c4f2cb85612ecc8/psf-studio-spike/rgb-gaia-calibrated.jpg)

## What changes in PSF Guard itself

- `src/color_steps.rs` holds the color steps both PSF Guard's color previews and Studio call: registration, one channel's tools, the background step, and now the measuring of calibration gains, the star stretch and a whole-image stretch. `compose_color` calls the first three; its behaviour is unchanged.
- `src/studio/` is the toolkit-free document model: stages, layers, groups, palettes per part, shared masks, recipes, places and splits.
- New CLI commands: `studio`, `studio-sources`, `studio-files`, `studio-prepare`, `studio-tools`. No server route or database schema changes.
- Frontend: one row of links over the color stacks (`StackColorPreviewPanel`), a helper `utils/studioLink.ts`, and a release note. Nothing runs on the server for the button; the page only makes the link.
- Some items in `server::stack_preview` became `pub(crate)` so the shared steps can call them.

## Checks run locally

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --lib`: 2966 passed, 20 ignored
- In `static`: `npm run lint`, `npx vitest run` (326 files, 2258 tests), `npm run build`
- In `studio`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --release`, `cargo test --release -p psf-studio` (105 passed)
- By hand, in the spike app on real Sh2-157 stacks (Ha, OIII, SII, R, G, B): the recipe "Narrowband with RGB stars", adding Ha to a part, Gaia calibration (523 stars; red x1.027, blue x1.303), the star stretch, the layered stretch, and `studio-files` on the R, G and B stack files (local solve of 273 stars; red x1.028, blue x1.304).

- By hand: the link on the stacks page of a scratch server has the expected address; that same address, delivered to the bundled application, made Studio fetch and prepare the target. `psf-guard studio --channel …` opened RGB stack files in the application.

Not run: Playwright, in either engine; `cargo test --workspace` beyond the library. Not seen: the Studio window after the link opened the target (the picture's files were written; I could not capture the window), the **Open** file picker, and the link in the Tauri app. macOS registers the `psf-studio` scheme only for an application outside temporary folders, so the test delivered the link with `open -a`.

## Review

A separate review of the `src` diff found these, all fixed in the last commit, with tests for the palette cases:

- The star stretch took its image with stars from before the tools and its starless image from after all of them, so sharpening and noise reduction leaked into the stars. It now uses the starless image plus the removed stars.
- The sky was levelled per state before the star stretch, which left a pedestal in the star residual. The stars are now stretched first.
- A palette paired the layers it keeps by position; reordering two layers swapped their colors on the next slot change. It now pairs by slot.
- A layer moved to another part kept its slot and could be deleted by that part's palette. Moving or ungrouping now clears the slot.
- The stretch range of an RGB image could be resolved from one channel.
- A Color calibration step with `enabled: false` in its settings was still run.

Still open from the review: calibration gains are taken from a ratio of sums, not from Seiza's report; a mosaic would be calibrated against its reference frame's solve where the server uses the canvas solve; `input_deconvolutions` are not run in the preparation; stars that were not star-stretched follow their input's table stretches only.

## Not built

Choosing a server target from a list inside Studio, sign-in for servers with user accounts (the link carries no token), continuum subtraction, tools on the combined color image, groups in groups, saving the star stretch into PSF Guard's `narrowband` settings. body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"paulbland"} -->
_Requested by **Paul** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01G1o6jCez7eNRKgSS37WCw8?thread=cmsg_01G1o6jCez7eNRKgSS37WCw8NDzzV4LwuJfmXrbd7V8VD2)_

## Why

11 of the 14 facepalms before Nov 13 were election admin errors. Once the score and cap rules started blocking those, every scan from Nov 17 to Nov 25 ended with "no pair". In the logs, the funny leads died because they were too old (the inmate-costume speeder, the Bean push), because the verifier rejected anything with an arrest, because UPI pages wouldn't open, or because the run hit its search limit.

## What changes

- **Freshness window:** facepalm gets 14 days and genius stays at 7 (`FRESH_DAYS` in `src/lib/score.ts`). The scan now enforces this in code, for candidates and for bench use and pruning. Before, only the prompt stated it.
- **Score floor:** the scan never publishes a facepalm scored below 5 (`FACEPALM_MIN_SCORE`). Routine admin errors can no longer run. The weekly routine cap stays in place but can't trigger now.
- **Victimless crimes allowed:** a crime whose only victim is the perpetrator qualifies, and an arrest alone is not a reason to reject. Drunk or drugged driving and drug cases stay out, and `DUI`, `drunk`, `meth` and similar words are added to the facepalm block-word lint.
- **Search budget:** facepalm discovery goes from 60 to 90 searches, about $0.30 more per run. The prompt also tells discovery to look for the local outlet or AP version when a UPI page won't open.
- **Headlines:** facepalm headlines lead with the act, with the place and attribution after it.
- The methodology page and CLAUDE.md are updated to match.

## Checks

`npm run validate`, `check`, `test` (71 pass) and `build` all pass, and Prettier is clean. No scan has been run on this branch yet. `gh workflow run scan.yml --ref claude/project-thread-ikaseh -f date=2026-11-26 -f dry_run=true` would try one without publishing.

author: troglodyne-robot
body:
The bot stopped updating itself after #110. This change makes the update install what `dist.ini` needs to build before it asks `dzil listdeps`.

`self_update` pulled the new commit, and then installed what `dzil listdeps` named. But `dzil listdeps` loads every plugin of `dist.ini`. If the new commit names a plugin that the local lib lacks, `dzil listdeps` dies before it lists anything. The update then fails without a restart. The failed job said:

```
dzil listdeps: Required plugin Dist::Zilla::Plugin::Git::ChangelogFromTrailers isn't installed.
```

The code that fails is the code that runs, so no later update fixes it. On the host, I installed the missing modules into the local lib once, by hand. After that, `dzil listdeps` ran in the checkout of the bot.

## The change

- `authordeps` returns what `dzil authordeps --versions` names, each with its version in the syntax of cpm, such as `Foo~0.004`. `dzil authordeps` reads `dist.ini` and loads no plugin. So it works with the plugins missing.
- `install_deps` installs those first, and then what `listdeps` names.
- `self_update` and `clod deps install` use `install_deps`.

`install_needed`, which installs the prerequisites of a spoke into `harness_lib`, has the same gap. It runs in an eval and only notes the failure. Its `dzil` also does not run with `harness_lib` on its path. So it is left for a change of its own.

## Evidence

Without the change to `lib/`, the new subtests of `t/App-Clod-Deps.t` failed:

```
# Failed test 'authordeps'
# Failed test 'install_deps'
```

With it, `t/App-Clod-Deps.t`, `t/App-Clod-Command-deps.t` and `t/App-Clod-Tasks.t` pass. The pre-commit hook ran 10 files, with 137 tests, and passed.

body:
Follow-up to #1. Merging this into `main` also updates ewanc26/shut#19, whose head is this fork's `main`.

## What

New `TEMPLATE` rules in `labeller/src/detect/lexicon.ts` count only towards `incel-language-strict`, never towards the standard label:

- `anypill`: any word of two or more letters followed by `pilled`/`pilling`, joined or hyphenated ("atprotopilled", "bskypilled", "Atproto-Pilled"). It skips "spilled", "unspilled", "dogpilling" and fabric "anti-pilling".
- `anymaxx`: any word of two or more letters followed by `maxx`, `maxxed`, `maxxer` or `maxxing` ("protocolmaxxing", "protocol-maxxing"). It needs the double x, so "climaxing" and "maxing out" are left alone.

Everyday slang such as "sleepmaxxing" now gets the strict label. The README says so.

author: rigerc
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #9. The phase-four skill-library and link-install slice had never been built or tested, and the workspace quality gates were failing. This PR fixes that slice, clears the lint/dependency debt, replaces the unmaintained YAML parser, and adds the missing link maintenance operations. `./scripts/quality-gates.sh` now passes end to end.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Dependency update

## Changes Made

- **Phase-four test fixes:** library tests now create 0700 roots (`tempfile` applies the process umask, so `Library::open` correctly refused them). Staged library objects are now published owner-only.
- **Template profiles:** `rust-crate-discovery` is core (AGENTS.md requires it); `beads` is optional and pruned by `minimal`/`library`.
- **Formatting and lint:** rustfmt across the workspace; all `clippy -D warnings`, rustdoc, markdownlint and yamllint findings fixed without behavior changes. Path and git dependencies get explicit versions for `cargo deny`; the `nosey-registry` bin sets `doc = false` to avoid a doc name collision.
- **YAML parser:** `serde_yaml` (unmaintained `unsafe-libyaml`, RUSTSEC-2024-0449) is replaced by `serde-saphyr` 2.2.0. Duplicate keys are rejected and anchor/alias budgets are zero. The review is in `docs/dependency-review-phase4.md`.
- **Skill frontmatter:** the blanket `& * ! %` ban is gone, so descriptions like "Build & test" import. Tags and directives are rejected at the token level, and anchors/aliases by the parser budget.
- **Link maintenance:** new preview/fingerprint-approved `recover`, `unlink` and fixture `update` operations (library API plus `preview-*` / `apply-* --approve` CLI commands):
  - recover changes only the journal record;
  - unlink removes a symlink only if it is still the exact recorded managed link;
  - update swaps the object directory atomically (`RENAME_EXCHANGE`), so existing links keep working.
- `library.rs` was split (`library/manifest.rs`) to stay under the 500-line limit.

## Testing

- [x] `cargo test --all-features` passes (213 nextest tests plus doctests)
- [x] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` passes
- [x] New tests added for new functionality
- [x] Manual testing performed: the agent that built recover/unlink/update ran an end-to-end CLI smoke test of the new commands

```bash
./scripts/quality-gates.sh   # Overall Status: SUCCESS
cargo nextest run --workspace
```

## Performance Impact

- [x] No performance impact

## Breaking Changes

N/A. Link journal records gain an optional `tree_sha256` field; older records still load.

## Known limitations (tracked in Beads)

- Scanner and registry YAML readers still reject any file containing `& * ! %`, so a Compose file with `command: a && b` is skipped.
- Legacy pending journals without a digest can be dropped but not confirmed.
- Unlink is blocked when the library copy is missing or corrupted.
- Update needs `RENAME_EXCHANGE`.
- The final `unlinkat` can't be conditional on inode, so a same-user external writer can still race it.
