author: caiolombello
body:
## What changed

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `build` job, the revision step: after the APT index, it also reads the bucket's dnf index. It downloads `rpm/repodata/repomd.xml`, then the primary file that `repomd.xml` names, and decompresses it with `zstd` (installed through `scripts/ci/apt_install.sh` if the runner lacks it). The step then passes that version to `next-release` with a second `--also`. The next revision is one above the highest that either index serves, or that is tagged or recorded. Each step writes to a file in `$RUNNER_TEMP`, not to a pipe, so a failed download or decompression stops the job (no `pipefail` in this shell). The dnf value gets the same `<version>-<release>` form check as the APT one.
- `scripts/release/release_manifest.py`, two new subcommands:
  - `dnf-primary <repomd.xml>` prints the primary file's location. It accepts only `repodata/<sha256>-primary.xml.zst`, because that value goes into a URL.
  - `dnf-served <repomd.xml> <primary.xml>` first checks that the primary file's SHA-256 is the `open-checksum` that `repomd.xml` gives. It then prints the highest `<version>-<release>` of `nulavio`, without the distribution (`0.3.fc44` gives `0.3`, the same rule as in `check_published.sh`).
  - Both fail closed: on XML they cannot read, a DTD or entity (createrepo_c writes none), a count of primary files other than one, no `nulavio` package, or a release in another form.
- `docs/architecture/build.md`, "After a failed publish": state 2 (dnf serves the revision, APT does not) now works like state 1. A new run builds the next revision by itself; rename the whats-new record; the failed run's RPM stays in the bucket, unlisted. The `build` row of the table and the paragraph above the states now name the dnf read.
- Also updated: the `release.yml` header, the `release_manifest.py` docstring, CONTRIBUTING (revisions), and the security changelog (Unreleased, the #656 line).
- After review (5111ef96, e665e9f7):
  - Signatures: each index is read only once the release key's signature of its root file verifies. `release_manifest.py verify-signed` checks `repomd.xml` with `repomd.xml.asc`. For APT, since 7bc749ad, `verify-clearsigned` checks `InRelease` instead of `Release` with `Release.gpg` (see below). It uses a throwaway GNUPGHOME holding only `site/keys/nulavio-packages.asc`, which must be 298A9093BAABB26F79BB29F4BF47E5FA9EDB8DB1 alone, and gpg's `--status-fd` must show one good VALIDSIG by that key or a subkey.
  - APT version: it now comes from `apt-served`, which reads `Packages` only when its SHA-256 and size are the ones the signed `Release` text names. The pipe into awk is gone.
  - XML: the dnf metadata must be strict UTF-8, and an expat pass refuses a DTD or an entity in any encoding. The earlier byte search let a UTF-16 entity through.
  - Size limits: every download is bounded with `curl --max-filesize`: 1M for `Release`, `Release.gpg`, `repomd.xml` and `.asc`, 8M for `Packages` and the compressed primary file. The decompression runs under `ulimit -f 32768` (32 MiB). The real files are 0.8 to 6.3 kB.
  - Errors: a missing input file is a clean error.
- After the OpenCodeReview review of e665e9f7 (7bc749ad, 833947ee):
  - APT read from one object: the build verifies `InRelease`, as apt does. `verify-clearsigned` takes exactly one cleartext-signed message, with nothing before or after it. gpg writes the text before it judges the signature, so the text stays in the throwaway home and goes to `$RUNNER_TEMP/Release` only once the checks pass. `Packages` is fetched by the hash that text gives (`by-hash/SHA256/<sha256>`, `apt-packages`, form-checked before it goes into the URL). The upload replaces the plain `Packages` object, then `Release` and `Release.gpg`, and `InRelease` last. With the old read, a publish stopped at any of those points blocked the build, while apt clients still had a good snapshot.
  - dnf: `dnf-compressed` checks the downloaded primary file against `repomd.xml`'s `<checksum>` before zstd reads it. The `open-checksum` check after zstd stays.
  - XML: a NUL byte refuses the dnf metadata. expat reads a BOM-less UTF-16 document as UTF-16 even when told UTF-8, and such a document is valid UTF-8 bytes. A declaration of another encoding is refused too.
  - Time limits: every download stops after 60 s (`--max-time`), with its retries after 180 s (`--retry-max-time`). Before, a stalled server could hold the job until its 300-minute timeout.
  - Tests: the signature tests register their key homes as a class cleanup, so a failed `setUpClass` removes them too.
  - Runbook, state 4: the dnf upload stopped between `repomd.xml.asc` and `repomd.xml`. This was a regression of this PR. On `main`, state 3's route (delete the unlisted packages, re-run `publish`) uploads a new matching pair. Here, the new run stops at the signature first. Fixed in 47e43d0b, below.
  - Security changelog: one #656 line. An earlier merge had kept `main`'s superseded line next to this PR's.
- #740, the maintainer's option 1 (decided 2026-11-26), in 47e43d0b, 696296ae and 4adea39a:
  - `scripts/release/upload_repo.sh` (dnf only): after the packages and the hash-named metadata, it uploads the signed pair under keys named after the revision, `rpm/repodata/<firefox>-<release>/repomd.xml.asc`, then `rpm/repodata/<firefox>-<release>/repomd.xml`. Only then does it upload the served `repomd.xml.asc` and `repomd.xml`, in their old order. A matching signed pair now always stays in the bucket. The APT side is unchanged.
  - The key is the full revision, the tag without its `v` (for example `rpm/repodata/160.0.1-0.4/`), not the bare release number of the issue's example. The release number starts again with each Firefox version (the tags `v160.0-0.3` and `v160.0.1-0.3` both exist), so a later revision would otherwise overwrite an earlier one's pair.
  - The revision comes from the staged RPM names, `nulavio-<firefox>-<release>.<dist>.x86_64.rpm`, the form `release_manifest.py`'s `tag` reads. Every package must give the same one, in the `<version>-<release>` form. Otherwise it exits 2 before the bucket listing and before any write, because the value goes into a key.
  - Runbook, state 4 (`docs/architecture/build.md`, "After a failed publish"): first the 7-day re-run, as before. Otherwise, a copy of the failed run's pair onto the served keys: `aws s3 cp` server-side with the R2 upload token, in the upload's order and with the same environment as `upload_repo.sh`'s `r2()` (696296ae: also without `AWS_DEFAULT_PROFILE` and the pager). Before the copy, the pair must verify with the committed key (`release_manifest.py verify-signed`, as the build job runs it), and the served signature must be byte for byte the pair's (`cmp`). After the copy, the served pair must verify over HTTPS. Then state 2 applies, because dnf serves the revision and APT does not. A run made before this change left no pair; it has only its re-run.
  - After the OpenCodeReview review of 696296ae (4adea39a):
    - The block runs in a `( set -euo pipefail … )` subshell with an `EXIT` trap. A failed download, `verify-signed` or `cmp` stops it before either copy, and a failed check after the copy fails it.
    - The R2 token is asked with `read -rsp` after the checks and exported in the subshell, so it never appears on a command line or in the history (I3). Source: the maintainer's copy of `nulavio-packages-upload`, the pair the `release-upload` environment holds.
    - The upload tests' stand-in `aws` logs JSON argument lists, and their stage path has a space in it.
  - **The build job does not fall back to the revision pair** when the served pair fails to verify. It stays fail-closed: a served pair that does not verify is also what every dnf client refuses (`repo_gpgcheck=1`), so the fix belongs in the bucket, not in a build that reads around it. A fallback would also need the build to pick which revision's pair to trust. The runbook restores the pair; the build then runs as in state 2.

author: phughesmcr
body:
Step 5 of `docs/browser-hosted-rooms.md` ("PRs, in order"), the last piece of v1: a player can host a room in their own tab and others can join it over WebRTC from the menus.

These commits were written in an earlier session on `agent/rtc-client` and never pushed; this branch carries them, merges current `dev` in, and fixes what review found.

## What it adds
- `src/net_rtclobby.js`: the WebRTC driver's lobby signaller. A joiner's lobby socket lasts only until the host accepts it. A host registers once its map is up, heartbeats when its player count changes and every 30 s, and its room ends with `Host_ShutdownServer`.
- `src/menu.js`: Start Game's *Host on* (Lobby server / This browser) and *Listed* (Public / Private (code)) rows, `M_HostInBrowser`, and Join Game's *Room code* field. Web additions, not in the C.
- Exit rules (`noexit`/`samelevel`) are set only for a hosted room and reset when it ends or never registers.
- Tests in `tests/net_rtclobby_test.js`.

## Review findings
- **Fixed:** a host still waiting for its map registered whatever game started next, and kept its exit rules, if the player ended the game first. It now gives up when a second map spawns or another map runs, and resets the rules. Test added.
- **Fixed:** a host cancelled by a newer Start Game printed "Hosting failed: Hosting was cancelled". It now prints nothing.
- **Fixed:** test for a registration the lobby never answers: the next `Host_ShutdownServer` resets the rules.
- **Fixed:** stale notes in `docs/browser-hosted-rooms.md` (the `-listen` handling is restored; no page reload for more slots) and `README.md` (`?listen=N` turns deathmatch on only above 1).
- **Not fixed:** the menu logic itself (code typing, 6/8-length check, the new rows' hit-testing) has no unit tests; the browser check covers it.
- **Not fixed:** the *Room code* field accepts letters that browser-room codes never use (`I`, `O`, `0`, `1`); such a code fails with a lobby error rather than hanging. Lobby-room codes use a different alphabet, so filtering while typing needs care.
- **Still open (in the doc):** `_NET_MultiplayerAvailable` doesn't count WebRTC.

## Verified
- `deno task ci` after merging #200 in: 882 tests pass; lint and check pass.
- Browser, Chromium (the Claude desktop app's browser), tabs on one machine, Deno lobby on `ws://127.0.0.1`, STUN only:
  - hosted a private room; it wasn't listed, and a second tab joined it by code;
  - a third tab joined from the shared `?room=` link;
  - a public room was listed and joined from the list;
  - when the host disconnected, its joiners were dropped and the lobby listed no rooms;
  - after the fix: hosted again and joined by code.
- A joiner without the map downloads it and reconnects (the existing lazy load in `CL_ParseServerInfo`), so the host sees one short-lived connection first. Lobby rooms do the same.

## Not verified
- TURN, the Cloudflare lobby, two machines, Safari, Firefox, mobile.
- The Turnstile widget before `LOBBY_HOST`: unit-tested with a fake token source only.
- Background tabs in that browser stop the game loop, so a host or joiner stalls until it's in front; real browsers' hidden-tab behaviour is still the doc's open question.

## Turnstile (#200)
#200 is merged and `dev` is merged in (conflicts only in an import line in `src/menu.js` and one `server/README.md` bullet). With Turnstile on, the lobby answers a token-less `LOBBY_HOST` with `LOBBY_VERIFY`, which the host ignored, so hosting timed out with "The lobby did not answer". Fixed: the host shows the widget, as `NET_CreateRoom` does, and registers again with the token on a new socket. A server stop or newer Start Game while the widget is up, or while the lobby answers, cancels quietly. Six tests added.

author: yagihash
body:
## Summary

- seccomp のフィルタに「番号 > 上限 → ENOSYS」の規則を足した(x32 の検査の直後)。上限は、`golang.org/x/sys/unix` の `SYS_*` の最大(x86-64、arm64 とも 471)を、定数 `seccompMaxNrAmd64` / `seccompMaxNrArm64` で持つ。
- テスト(`seccomp_ceiling_linux_test.go`、Linux 専用):
  - `TestSeccompCallsAboveTheCeilingAreNotThere`: フィルタの BPF を、テスト内の小さな解釈器で、上限+1 などの番号について走らせ、ENOSYS を確かめる(上限の規則がなければ、リストにない番号は末尾の ALLOW に着くので、この試験は失敗する)。
  - `TestSeccompCeilingCoversXSys`: `x/sys/unix` の `zsysnum_linux_{amd64,arm64}.go` を `go/parser` で読み、最大の番号が上限を超えたら失敗する(x/sys の更新で、新しい call を読む必要がある、と知らせる)。
  - `TestSandboxCallAboveTheCeilingIsNotThere`: サンドボックス内で、プローブ(`probelinux` の `-ceiling`)が上限+1 の call を呼び、ENOSYS を確かめる。
- x32 ABI: 既存の規則(x86-64 で、番号が 0x40000000 以上なら KILL)がある。上限の規則はその後に置くので、x32 の番号は、上限に着く前に殺される(変更なし)。

## Background / Motivation

外部の設計者のレビューの指摘: 拒否リストは、レビューした時点までの番号しか知らず、それより新しい call が既定で通る。上限を超える番号を ENOSYS にして、新しい call は、レビューするまで使えないようにする(clone3 と同じ扱い)。

body:
A source or code change can leave the schematic and wire quantities using an unbound legacy verdict. This adds one persisted, input/code-bound structural evaluation over the existing harness owners and runs it through the existing model-fold worker. It creates no second source model, stock ledger, queue or cron.

- Store immutable private input/code receipts, typed electrical nodes and physical segment-end edges, versioned subject checks and gross per-piece wire plans. Existing source IDs and physical history remain authoritative.
- Invalidate on source changes, detect code/helper changes, recompute atomically, reuse unchanged receipts and retain a bounded failure/backoff cursor. Publish only for the captured epoch/code.
- Serve the current model through invoker RLS only when fingerprints, epoch and visible output counts agree. Exclude superseded/out-of-plan retained revisions, anonymous-owner private reads and unallowlisted raw metadata. Unknown electrical continuity stays isolated.
- Preserve explicit structural-only qualification: engineering coverage holds; progressed pieces hold new-wire eligibility; gross footage is not supplier packs, net stock demand or order release. The existing frontend is not switched in this PR; the coordinated workspace lane consumes this owner next.

Validation: full focused PG17.5 PGlite contract passed, including source -> invalidation -> existing worker -> new receipt, code-only changes, atomic error/backoff/recovery, immutable outputs, cross-vehicle/physical-side guards, public/private withdrawal, incomplete cache denial, reader-extension selection and timezone identity. A pinned combined assay with the parallel material-revision/expanded-reader drafts passed. The enforced repository gate passed. Pure SQL computation on the retained 482-piece public Blazer snapshot produced 6,974 checks and 482 wire plans in 94ms locally; this is a cost assay with catalog identity presence only, not production or engineering acceptance. Native PostgreSQL17 CI and all other applicable checks passed at e24b110e9fea587c8eba82e4acfcade42977fc30. Exact-head code and security reviews completed. Deployment and runtime acceptance remain required. The named rule meanings, next actions and ordered attention IDs are bound into the same input/code receipt. The public all-collections JSON read has an acknowledged medium resource-use advisory (about3.20MB and600ms in the local482-piece assay); bounded collection/sheet reads remain a release requirement for the new builder consumer, not a resolved finding in this foundation PR.

Scope: the owner explicitly authorized the DB-required recursive harness loop, including needed tables, folds, keys, edges and schema. See `docs/wiring/receipts/2026-11-26_database-evaluation-loop.md` for grains, dependency closure, coordinated ownership and remaining acceptance.

Pick of #71043 (commit 5c5d807d234) to branch-4.1.

BUILD INDEX and DROP INDEX on partitions, and the whole-table light DROP INDEX pre-check, look for an unfinished index change job of the same index by the partition name stored in the job, which is the name at job creation. `RENAME PARTITION` is allowed while such jobs run, so after a rename a statement on the new name finds no conflict: a DROP can run while a BUILD of the same index is pending, and the BUILD restores the index afterwards. author: pixelfederico
body:
c44 sweep, panel side (ADR-0043 / ADR-0049, "What cluster eu showed", 25-26 Nov). Agent side: DeploCloud/deplo-agent#138.

## What changes

1. **A removed server leaves every peer's network without waiting for the sweep** (decision 3). `removeServer` pushed only the relay rosters. The cluster network was fixed only by the 2-minute network pass, which runs inside the watch tick, after each cluster's awaited leader, roster and backup work. In c44 the removed member stayed a peer for 8 min 17 s. Now the removal calls `syncClusterNetworkSoon` for each of the server's clusters (`lib/data/servers/removal.ts`).
2. **One Activity line per copy held back for room, with the right size** (decision 4). The line was said again whenever a pass in between read another error for that copy (the server did not answer, or the copy ran for a moment), because its free space is part of the text. Now an in-memory set remembers what was said until the copy runs with no error. The size shown was the App's data plus its biggest file (the rebuild margin): 520 MiB + 165 MB = 685.8 MB. Now it is the App's data, or the copy's own size when that is bigger. The margin still counts in the fit check.
3. **No "Cluster ...'s leader stepped down" after a move Deplo made** (decision 5). The old leader hears the new epoch from a member before `leadFrom` stores it (up to `LEAD_WAIT_MS`, 5 s). A `superseded` event whose epoch Deplo stores within 6 s is now Deplo's own move and says nothing. An epoch Deplo never stores is said as before, and so is an event without an epoch (older leader). The wait runs inline on the watch, so it delays the events after a real step-down by at most 6 s.
4. **A deterministic oldest team** (decision 6): `recordActivity` orders by `created_at, id` (see #406, point 4). `lib/notify/server-teams.ts` `firstTeamId` has the same tie but no test file, so it is left as it was.

Each test fails on main: `a server removed from Deplo leaves every peer's network without waiting for the sweep`, `a copy held back for room is said once with its size, whatever the passes in between read`, `a leader that steps down for an epoch Deplo handed says nothing; one Deplo never stores is said`, `a line no team owns goes to the oldest team, the lower id on a tie`.

## For the test session

Release with DeploCloud/deplo-agent#138. Order: agent, then panel.

- **Remove a member** (a clone joined as eu-4, then `removeServer`): within 30 s no remaining member has eu-4 as a network peer, and the Servers page shows no path to it.
- **A copy that does not fit** (a member near its floor, an App of about 520 MiB): exactly one Activity line `... too little for a copy of <app> (about <its data size>) ...`, even across passes where that member does not answer. The size matches the App's data, not data plus its biggest file. A copy that later runs whole and is then refused again gets a new line.
- **Move the leader A to B and back, and the agent update's hand-off**: no `stepped down` line in Activity. A real step-down (a member holding a newer epoch that Deplo never handed) still writes one, at most about 6 s after the event.
- **Activity of a cluster shared by every team, with no team using it**: it always lands in the same team (the oldest, the lower id on a tie).

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
## Problem

On a **fresh install** of main, every request logs:

```
[Observability] request metrics flush failed, kept for the next flush: … SQLSTATE[42S22]: Column not found: 1054 Unknown column 'sample_count' in 'SET'
```

(163 times in one opencatalogi e2e run.) The cause is the migration order. Nextcloud's `MigrationService::sortMigrations()` compares the number before `Date` first (`(int) 1` < `(int) 002005000`). So all 308 `Version1Date…` steps run **before** `Version002005000Date20251013000000`, which creates `openregister_metrics`. `Version1Date20261116230000` then finds no table, does nothing and is recorded as done. The table is created afterwards without `sample_count` / `sample_sum_ms`. Upgraded instances are fine, because the table was already there when the step ran.

## Fix

`Version002006000Date20261126010000` reruns the same idempotent change (it subclasses `Version1Date20261116230000`). Its number, 002006000, makes it sort after the step that creates the table. On an upgraded instance it does nothing. The app version moves to 2.2.0-dev.52 so an upgrade picks it up.

## Proof (sandbox: Nextcloud 34, MariaDB)
- Fresh install with main 01e805cd: `SHOW COLUMNS … LIKE 'sample%'` returns nothing, and the log fills with the flush error.
- Fresh install with this branch: both columns present (bigint, nullable), and both versions are recorded in `oc_migrations`.
- `Version002006000Date20261126010000Test` (3: Nextcloud's order puts it after the table, a fresh table gets both columns, an upgraded one is left alone) passes. `Version1Date20261116230000Test` (3) is unchanged and green.

## Same ordering, other tables (not changed here)
- `openregister_file_texts` (created by `Version002006000Date20251013000000`): `Version1Date20251118000000` drops it as deprecated. On a fresh install the table is created after that step and stays, without `uuid` / `chunks_json`. It is harmless clutter, and the install logs "openregister_file_texts table does not exist".
- `openregister_vectors`: `Version1Date20251111000000` logs "vectors table not found - skipping model tracking migration". The create step already carries `embedding_model` and its index, so nothing is lost.
- Any future `Version1Date…` step that alters one of these four tables will be a no-op on a fresh install in the same way.

Found by live-opencatalogi-1 (file-management 6.5, a log tail during the opencatalogi e2e run). Left for the OR integrator; not merged by this lane.

author: jasonagentic
body:
## What changes
`check --shard-capacity C1,...,CN` gives each of the N shards a relative capacity, such as its runner's vCPU. Each id, heaviest first, goes to the shard where its load plus the id, divided by capacity, is lowest. The comparison is cross-multiplied, so equal capacities give exactly the partition without the flag; `TestShardCapacityEqualIsTheUnweightedPartition` pins that for N 2–8, with and without a hint and pins.

The flag is refused (exit 2) without `--shard`, without `--durations` (every load is zero then), with a list whose length is not N, when given twice, and when a capacity is not a canonical positive integer up to 1024.

## Why
TakeoffQS runs its formwork matrix with shards 1–3 on 8 vCPU and 4–6 on 4 vCPU, and the even split gives each the same measured load. On develop run 45729207541 the 8-vCPU shards 2–3 finished their gate step in 138s and 110s while the 4-vCPU shards 4–6 took 207s, 192s and 188s. Shard CPU over gate wall was 5.1–5.9 cores busy on 8 vCPU and 2.8–3.2 on 4 vCPU. Replaying that run's per-rule CPU through this placement with capacities 8,8,8,4,4,4 predicts 193/175/168/184/183/171s, 1.15× slowest over fastest, against 1.96× for the even split.

## Tests
- Internal: equal capacities match the nil partition; capacities 2,1 put twenty of thirty equal ids on the wider shard; mixed capacities still place every id exactly once; spec parsing.
- CLI: three capacity-weighted shard reports cover the corpus exactly once; every refusal names its cause.
- `docs/reference.md` documents the flag; `internal/meta` passes.

author: tleeadams
body:
Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent`) sessions get cards marked **Cursor**.

**Where it reads from**
- `~/.cursor/chats/<hash>/<id>/meta.json`: each chat's folder, title, and when it began and changed.
- `~/.cursor/projects/<folder>/agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl`: prompts, replies and tool calls, written as the turn goes, with a `turn_ended` line where each turn ended. It's read a few new bytes at a time, like Claude's and Copilot's.
- `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` and `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` move them, as they do for Cursor.

**Matching windows to chats**
- Cursor records no process for a chat. Each `cursor-agent` window (the Node process running `.../cursor-agent/versions/<v>/index.js`) is matched to its chat:
  1. by `--resume <id>`;
  2. else by its tab's title, which Cursor sets to the chat's title;
  3. else, while a new chat has no title, by the chat begun in it since it started.
- When two chats share a title, neither is guessed.

**Status**
- With Cursor's status indicators on (`/status-indicators`), the tab's title ends with the state, e.g. "- ⏳ Working", "- 🔐 Waiting for confirmation", "- ✅ Ready". *Waiting for confirmation* shows as *Needs you: Approval: run <command>*, taking the command from the transcript.
- Without them, a turn with no `turn_ended` line yet is *Working*. That means an approval wait also shows as *Working*; the README says to turn the indicators on.
- A turn that ended in an error needs you.

**Actions**
- Go to window, Catch up (typed into the window) and Stop work as they do for Claude.
- Complete and Save and close take Cursor chats.
- History lists closed chats. Resume runs `cursor-agent --resume <id>` in the chat's folder, where Cursor keeps it. *Skip permission prompts* adds `--force`.

**Not yet:** starting Cursor from to-dos or the repo menu, and subagents.

**Tested**
- `test/cursor.test.js`, 7 tests:
  - command lines, including the `worker-server` helper, `-p` runs and paths with spaces;
  - the title's states;
  - matching windows by resume, by title, and two new windows by start time;
  - the transcript;
  - status;
  - a card and History's list, from stand-in chat folders.
- Full suite: 129 pass.
- Live on Windows (Cursor CLI 2026.11.22): a real session's card matched its window and showed its title, Idle, 3 prompts, and the last prompt and reply. The title showed "⏳ Working" and "✅ Ready" as the turn ran. The macOS and Linux process paths follow Cursor's install layout, but are untested here.

**Same-name subcategories**
- Category names now only need to be unique within the same parent, or among top-level categories. So 「基础 › 其他」 and 「车 › 其他」 can both exist.
- `sql/schema.sql` drops the old `unique (user_id, name, type)` constraint (`categories_user_id_name_type_key`) and adds a unique index on `(user_id, type, coalesce(parent_id, nil-uuid), name)`. **Existing databases need to run this SQL.**

body:
Closes #264

## やったこと

画面に出る「宿題」を「やること」、「リスク」を「遅れの度合い」「遅れそうな案件」「遅れそうな順」に言い換えた（見出し・タブ・ボタン・表の列名・エラーメッセージ・AIが使えないときの代替文）。変数名・API・DBの列名、リスク判定のルールと点数の計算は変えていない。`docs/用語集.md` に、設計書の呼び方と画面の表示の対応表を足した。

主な言い換え:

| 前 | 後 |
| --- | --- |
| 宿題・提出物 / 宿題テンプレート | やること・提出物 / やることテンプレート |
| 宿題名 / 宿題進捗 | やることの名前 / やることの進捗 |
| リスク（案件詳細の見出し・タブ、案件一覧の列） | 遅れの度合い |
| リスクが高い案件 / リスクが高い順 | 遅れそうな案件 / 遅れそうな順 |

初期データ由来の文言は、新しいマイグレーション `cloudflare/migrations/0027_display_wording.sql` で直した（既存の migration は編集も番号付け替えもしていない）:

- 遅れの理由（`risk_rules` の名前と説明、システム共通の3件）: 「挙式30日以内で重要宿題が未提出」→「挙式30日以内で重要なやることが未提出」、「期限超過の未提出宿題がある」→「期限を過ぎた未提出のやることがある」、「不備ありの宿題がある」→「不備ありのやることがある」と、それぞれの説明文（「提出期限を過ぎたやることがあります」など）。
- 算出済みの理由（`risk_score_snapshots.reasons` の JSON に残る写し）: 上と同じ置き換え。再計算を待たずに新しい言い方で出る。
- AI への指示文（`ai_prompt_templates` の共通行の名前と本文）: 「宿題名」→「やることの名前」、「宿題」→「やること」。引継ぎサマリーなど、AI が書いて画面に出る文がこの言葉に引っ張られるため。
- `id`・`condition_key`・`job_type`・`version` は変えていない。どの UPDATE も固定値か REPLACE なので、手元DBに何度流しても結果は同じ（`tests/d1/display-wording.test.mjs` で確認）。

この PR に入れていないもの:

- 静的デモ `demo/` と `scripts/demo-presenter.html` にも「宿題」「リスク」が残っている。
- 基本設計書と結びついた機能名（`docs/詳細設計/機能画面対応.md` の「3-2 coupleの宿題一覧」など）は変えていない。
- Supabase に依存する12ファイルは #252 で移行中のため、手を入れたのはダッシュボードの表示文言2か所だけ。

## 確かめたこと

- [x] `npm test`（36ファイル・524件成功）/ `npm run typecheck`（エラー0）/ `npm run test:d1`（98件成功。0027 の置き換えと再適用を確かめる3件を追加）/ 変更したファイルの `prettier --check`（成功）/ `eslint src tests`（エラー0・警告53件。警告はこの変更より前からのもの）
- [ ] 画面で動きを確かめ、画像を下に貼った（画面を変えたとき）

未実施の確認と理由: 画面での目視確認とスクリーンショットはまだ。文言の置き換えだけなので、レビューのときにローカルのデモで確かめてほしい。`npm run format:check` はリポジトリ全体ではなく、変更したファイルに絞って実行した。

## AIを使わずに確かめる手順

1. 操作前の状態: ローカルのデモを起動し、新郎新婦とプランナーでそれぞれログインできる状態にする。
2. 操作: 新郎新婦でマイページ下のナビ・「やること・提出物」・やることの詳細を開く。プランナーでダッシュボード・案件一覧・案件詳細（タブ）・準備シートを開く。管理者で「やることテンプレート」を開く。
3. 期待する結果: 画面に「宿題」「リスク」が出ず、「やること」「遅れの度合い」「遅れそうな案件」「遅れそうな順」と表示される。遅れの度合いの根拠文も「提出期限を過ぎたやることがあります」のように出る（手元DBには `0027` を適用してから確かめる）。

author: rohan-bes
body:
### Changes

The MediciReport `locations` and `departments` arrays were ordered by `change_type` before `date`. `change_type` is a `text[]`, so Postgres compared the arrays element by element: a move that changed the location and department together (`{location,department}`) sorted after a later move that changed only the location (`{location}`), whatever their dates. The first or last entry could then be wrong, which is what reporting reads as the admission or discharge location.

Both arrays now list the initial snapshot first, then entries by `date`, with `created_at` as a tiebreaker. Ordering the initial snapshot explicitly (rather than by `assignedTime`) keeps it first even when the encounter start date is later edited to after a move, since a start-date edit writes no history row.

Also parenthesises the `change_type` filter in both CTEs. Without the parentheses, `isnull OR (... AND e.id = $encounter_id ...)` aggregated every encounter's initial snapshot on each materialisation. The extra rows were discarded by the final join, so output was unaffected, but the work scaled with the whole `encounter_history` table.

Tests cover a combined location and department move followed by a single-field move (for both arrays), and a start-date edit past a move. I couldn't run them locally, so CI is their first run. Existing reports keep their old order until those encounters rematerialise.

body:
### Description

Web now reads `enable_meeting` from `/api/server-info` so a self-hosted installation can keep general AI enabled while turning off meeting transcription. The flag is available in [AppFlowy-Cloud-Premium #1664](https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy-Cloud-Premium/pull/1664).

When the flag is false or missing, Document keeps **AI transcript** visible in the slash menu. The transcript command and audio imports show “Meeting transcription is unavailable. Contact your workspace administrator to enable AssemblyAI.” Meeting summary actions show “AI meeting notes are unavailable. Contact your workspace administrator to enable AssemblyAI.” Clicking the item or pressing Enter preserves the typed slash query. Meeting imports, recordings, summary generation and calendar prompts also respect the flag. Saved notes and transcripts stay readable.

### Feature preview

The browser demo types `/transcript`, checks the disabled tooltip and keyboard behavior, then tests inserting a meeting on an enabled server. It also reopens a saved block after the flag is turned off. Run it locally with Chromium.

pnpm exec playwright test --config=playwright.integrations.config.ts --project=chromium --headed meeting-availability.spec.ts
```

Respect the server’s meeting-transcription availability throughout the Web editor while preserving access to existing meeting content.

author: pisit-lerd
body:
## Bugs

1. **Time's up fired for an old deadline.** After the admin set a new closing time (or cancelled it, or closed the topic early by hand), "หมดเวลา!" and its sounds still fired at the old time.
2. **Warning sounds silent or incomplete on phones.** The buzzer and clips unlocked on `pointerdown`/`touchstart`, which phones don't count as a tap that allows sound. The background music (started on `click`) still played.

## Fixes

- **Deadlines follow each topic's current closing time** from the latest snapshot (new `noteTopics`, called by the landing page, `/vote`, `/screen` and admin). A new time replaces the old one; a cancelled, deleted or hand-closed deadline is dropped.
- **Sound unlock also listens to `touchend` and `click`,** and retries on every tap until the audio context is running (with a silent buffer for iPhone).
- **Clips play through Web Audio:** they're decoded once and played through the same context as the buzzer, so they mix over the music.
- **iPhone music dip:** where a page can't lower the music's volume (iPhone), the music pauses for the warning and resumes afterwards.
- **One set of sounds when topics end together:** one stamp and one vibration, not a pile-up.

## Checked

Headless Chrome with phone-like autoplay rules (`--autoplay-policy=user-gesture-required`) and one real tap, on `/screen` and `/vote`:
- The minute clip plays at 60 s left, the buzzer at zero, and the time's-up clip right after.
- Deadlines that were re-set, cancelled or closed early fire once, at the real deadline.

`node scripts/smoke-test.js` and `node scripts/mail-test.js` → ALL PASSED.

author: ffengill
body:
## Summary
Quota History was hard to read: 7D/30D connected each day's low and high into a misleading zigzag, every value looked the same regardless of urgency, and there was no at-a-glance overview. This reworks the page around a compact watchboard and severity-coloured, correctly-shaped charts, using the app theme's own status colours.

## Key Changes

- **Daily bands**: 7D/30D render each day's low–high as a floating band with a thin "latest" line instead of a polyline; missing days are marked.
- **Severity from the theme**: marks use the theme's own `success/warning/error.main`; chips, daily bands and the 0–20% danger zone are translucent `alpha()` tints of the same hues (no off-palette alert colours), and caption text uses the darker/lighter palette variant for ≥4.5:1.
- **Quota watch**: a top table lists every provider×window (chip, current value, range delta, sparkline), most urgent first.
- **Sparse data**: the x-axis follows the data's own span, lines break at coverage gaps, balances are zero-based, per-sample dots and duplicate counts are gone, and a reset countdown is shown.
- **Data shaping**: new pure helpers (day bands, gap detection, delta) in `quotaHistorySeries.ts` with unit tests.
- **Mock**: the history endpoint now returns deterministic multi-day samples with a deliberate gap so the page is useful in mock mode.

## Notes
Window order inside a provider stays semantic (`compareQuotaWindows`) so rows don't jump as values change; only the watchboard and provider ordering are urgency-sorted. Chart marks clear the 3:1 graphics target in both modes (light 3.19–4.83:1, dark 4.89–5.78:1) and chip labels sit ~12–15:1.

author: shepherdjerred
body:
## Why
Flags could show only one deployment at a time, so comparing `scout/beta` with `scout/prod` meant clicking through two lists by eye. The live-vs-inventory drift report existed only as `toolkit flags diff`. The UI also looked older than Hub: a compact header, glyph-and-word states, no icons, no ⌘K.

## What
Built on `main`'s console-ui page kit (and the shared severity badge and ⌘K palette from #5160), so Flags uses the same components as Hub and Go link. The Monaco editor (#5161) and the value registry (#5158) are already merged:
- **Page layout:** every page is `PageBody` + `PageHeading` (`actions` prop). A deployment page has the catalog as eyebrow and the stage as title, with a revision tag, a drift badge linking to `/drift#<id>`, and "Compare with Beta/Prod". Summaries are `SummaryGrid` and `Card`; search is `SearchField`; the compare Differences/All switch is `Segmented`.
- **State column:** `SeverityBadge` pills (On is ok, Off is neutral with a minus glyph, Targeted is info with a crosshair).
- **Sidebar:** lucide icons, a Views group (Overview, Compare, Drift with a total count), and the shared ⌘K button. Below 900px the shared `TopBar` and drawer replace the native deployment select.
- **⌘K palette** (shared console-ui palette): views, deployments, and flags across every deployment, sharing `useDocument`'s cache.
- **Overview (`/`):** one card per catalog with each stage's flag count, revision and sync state.
- **Compare** (`/compare?left=scout/beta&right=scout/prod`): every key is classed as differs, only-left, only-right or identical. `?q=`, `?same=1` and `?key=` live in the URL. A selected row shows a side-by-side JSON line diff with links to both editors. With only `left` given, the catalog's other stage is the partner.
- **Drift** (`/drift`): `GET /v1/diff` as totals, then one section per drifted deployment, worst first: invalid values with schema issues, declared-vs-live diffs, missing and extra keys, each with its documented `toolkit flags` remediation command.
- **Live refresh:** the deployment list and drift report refresh when a document arrives at a newer revision, e.g. after a save.
- **Wire schema:** the diff response schemas move to the browser-safe `feature-flags/src/flags-wire.ts` (`flags-drift.ts` imports Node and the inventory, so the browser can't load it). `invalid` keeps its `.default([])`.
- **`/v1/diff` stays strict:** a seeded deployment missing from the store still fails loudly, because startup seeds every inventory deployment. The drift page shows the error state.
- **Line diff, not Monaco:** compare and drift use a small line diff, because the drift page renders many diffs at once. The single-flag save review keeps the Monaco diff (#5161).

| ![drift-top-dark-1440.png](https://public.sjer.red/pr/assets/5163/drift-top-dark-1440.png) | ![palette-dark-1440.png](https://public.sjer.red/pr/assets/5163/palette-dark-1440.png) |

## Verification
- `bunx turbo run build typecheck test lint --filter=@shepherdjerred/flags --filter=@shepherdjerred/feature-flags --filter=@shepherdjerred/console-ui`: 16/16 pass (flags 79 tests, feature-flags 223, console-ui 259). New tests cover the compare model, line diff, drift model, compare page (rows, identical toggle, URL state, selected diff and links), deployment heading links, the drift page from a mocked `/v1/diff` including the failure state, palette navigation, the sidebar Views group, and the top-bar drawer.
- `bunx turbo run typecheck --filter=@shepherdjerred/temporal --filter=@shepherdjerred/toolkit`: 34/34 pass.
- **Rendered locally**, dark and light at 1440px and 600px, console and uncaught errors empty. Seeded data: beta/prod differences, drift on 3 flags, one invalid variant value, one undeclared and one missing key (written straight into SQLite, since the apply API refuses undeclared keys). ## What

In `client/assets/Grid.js`:
- Target the closest boundary tile within a multi-tile object\x27s footprint relative to the player\x27s current position (or click/hover reference), matching authentic OSRS perimeter pathing.
- Preserve exact origin coordinates (`[localX, localY]`) for 1x1 objects (`sizeX <= 1 && sizeY <= 1`), ensuring zero deviation for standard 1x1 interactive objects across the game.

Clamping `[clamp(playerX, minX, maxX), clamp(playerY, minY, maxY)]` ensures that approaching a multi-tile object (e.g. Duke Sucellus stairs, Leviathan rowboat, Nightmare energy barrier, or Bandos altar) paths straight to the facing edge rather than unnaturally pulling diagonally toward the south-west origin corner.

author: actly
body:
## Summary

This is P4.2 of the South and kernel adoption plan. It moves every South pin from 0.85.1 to 0.88.0. South 0.88.0 (token-station-south #362) puts into the Messages codec what `agent-anthropic` carried as shims since #64 and #65. This PR removes those shims:

- **One wire block per source thinking block.** `AnthropicSseState` now keys thinking blocks by `block_index`. The adapter's thinking-block table and its `thinking_index` writes are gone.
- **A stop for every thinking block at `Done`.** The codec closes them all, so the loop #65 added is gone.
- **K1, the Claude replay markers.** The adapter now decodes with `chat_request_from_anthropic_messages_with(AnthropicRequestOptions { claude_replay_markers: true })`. Its own `replay_markers` and the K1 pass in `restore_adapter_state` are gone.

Client-visible behavior and the upstream wire are unchanged.

## Changes

- **Pins.** Every South crate moves from `174158d` to `bc07c516` (v0.88.0), in the root, desktop and the ten plugin manifests and lockfiles:
  - `south-provider-api` 0.66.0;
  - `south-component-conformance` 0.82.0;
  - `south-contracts` stays 0.57.0;
  - the rest 0.88.0.

  South 0.88.0 still resolves kernel `ce6894d`, so the root `[patch]` and its tree-hash guard do not change. `tests/south-dependency-policy.mjs` follows the new pins.
- **Host.** `SOUTH_RUNTIME` is 0.88.0. `SOUTH_RUNTIME_MIN` stays 0.77.0. The component manifests keep their declared `south_runtime`: 0.86 to 0.88 tightened no component-side gate. Those releases added family-catalog data, served-model `exclude_suffixes` and speech references.
- **Vendored South packages.**
  - South gave its packages a patch round: `provider-openai-compatible` 2.14.2 → 2.14.3 and `provider-anthropic` 1.4.11 → 1.4.12.
  - Our shells compile South's reference code, which now reports the new versions. The old manifests therefore failed the identity check ("the package is not what it claims to be").
  - Both manifests and `Cargo.toml` take the new version. Nothing else in South's manifests changed between the two releases.
  - `fixture-provenance.json` is recorded at `bc07c516`. Both vendored packs match South byte for byte. The four repository packs are unchanged.
- **Admission tests.** They named 0.85.2 and 0.86.0 as runtimes newer than the host, and both are now inside the range.
  - The unit test derives the next patch from `SOUTH_RUNTIME`, so it keeps testing the exact upper bound at every pin.
  - The integration test uses `0.999.0`.

## Design judgment

- **One commit.** 0.88.0 removes `AnthropicSseState::thinking_index`, so the re-pin alone does not compile `agent-anthropic`. The pin and the shim removal therefore go together.
- **The replay rule is the same rule.** I compared the codec's `mark_claude_replay` with the removed `replay_markers`. Both mark a turn only when all of these hold:
  - it carries reasoning;
  - every thinking block has a non-empty signature;
  - every block is text, thinking, redacted thinking or tool use;
  - its tool ids are present and distinct;
  - it has at most 128 blocks.

  Both build the layout from the wire blocks with the same ordinals. The host still removes the markers for a target that cannot replay.
- **Kept shims.** 0.88.0 does not cover these: K2 `anthropic_thinking`, K3 `anthropic_tool_result_is_error`, K4 the request checks, K5 no content on a tool-only turn, D12 the effort clamp, images in tool results, reserved IR keys, the typeless-block refusal, and the stream limits.
- **History comments stay.** Comments that name the release a rule came from ("South 0.85.1's rule") still describe that rule correctly. Comments that name the current pin now say 0.88.0.

## Review focus

- `plugins/official/agent-anthropic/src/lib.rs`: `normalize_inbound` (the codec call with the option), `restore_adapter_state` (K1 pass removed), and `render_frames` (now the codec call and the block limit only).
- `apps/cli/src/south_component.rs`: `SOUTH_RUNTIME` and the derived upper-bound case.
- The two vendored manifests and `fixture-provenance.json`.

## Tests

- The `agent-anthropic` unit tests are unchanged, and they pass against the codec:
  - the replay-marker tests: a signed turn carries its layout, and a turn that cannot be described carries none;
  - `reasoning_source_blocks_remain_separate_within_one_choice`, with the one-stop-per-block assertions from #65.
- The `agent-anthropic` unit tests: 18 passed. The plugin runtime's official-plugin tests pass as WASM: 33.
- Local gates: 13 of 13 passed, 3260 tests passed and 0 failed.

`scripts/install-local-desktop.sh` from this branch passed: the desktop artifact audit passed, the signature verified, and the App launched.

Design record: `token-station-doc` `docs/design/2026-11-24-south-and-kernel-adoption-plan.md` (P4.2 record).

## Related issue ## Problem / pressure Desktop and CLI can follow Loro Streams over the `loro-ds-v1` WebSocket (nightly), but the native iOS and Android runtimes pinned Streams Client 0.13.1, which has no WebSocket code, and always long-poll over HTTP. Both runtimes are built from `apps/mobile/backend-config.mjs`, so the switch must live in that shared resolver. ## Summary - `resolveBackendConfig` adds `LORO_STREAMS_WS_ENABLED: '1' | '0'` from `LODY_LORO_STREAMS_WS_ENABLED` (env over `.env.local`; only exact `1`/`true`, matching `isLoroStreamsWebSocketEnabled`). A string, because iOS reads `LodyBackends` as `[String: String]` and a boolean would make that cast fail, silently falling back to production. Computed after `STORAGE_SUFFIX`, so toggling it never moves credentials or caches. Off by default. - `.env.example` and `apps/mobile/README.md#backend-configuration` document it and its scope. - Consumers (stacked draft PRs, not yet merged; submodule pointers will be bumped here once they land): - LodyAI/lody-ios#191 → #192: SDK 0.16.0/0.24.0, then one pooled socket per workspace for caught-up catalog/session reads, Machine RPC replies, read-only presence and appends (once the socket is ready), with HTTP fallback and no replay of unacknowledged socket writes. - LodyAI/lody-android#65 → #66: same snapshot, plus a gated `WebSocket` that admits each frame exactly as its HTTP request (JOIN = GET, APPEND = POST, create = PUT) plus read-only workspace presence. ## Visual explanation ```mermaid flowchart LR cfg["apps/mobile/backend-config.mjs
LORO_STREAMS_WS_ENABLED '1'|'0'"] cfg --> ios["iOS build-decoder → esbuild define
LODY_MOBILE_STREAMS_WS"] cfg --> and["Android build.mjs define + BuildConfig.STREAMS_WEBSOCKET"] ios --> rt["shared cloud-runtime
reads, RPC replies, presence, appends over one socket"] and --> rt rt -->|"socket drop / error"| http["HTTP long-poll from last confirmed offset"] and --> gate["read-access.mjs gated WebSocket
each frame = its HTTP permission"] ``` ## Before / after | Before | After | | ------ | ----- | | Mobile resolver returns three origins + `STORAGE_SUFFIX` | Also returns `LORO_STREAMS_WS_ENABLED` (`'0'` unless explicitly enabled); suffix unchanged | ## Test plan - `node --test apps/mobile/backend-config.test.mjs`: 5/5 pass (new test: accepted/rejected values, env over file, suffix unchanged with the switch on). - `oxfmt --check` (0.65) on the changed files: clean. `pnpm run docs check`: exit 0, only existing warnings. - iOS `apps/ios/tests/backend-build_test.py`: 3/3 pass with the new key. - Not run: root `pnpm check` (no root `pnpm install` on this host; the change is limited to `apps/mobile`, outside the root workspace). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Problem (POLISH C21, lane C multi-device run 2026-11-26)
A client uploaded a file through the web portal. The partner's open 尽职调查资料清单 tab kept showing 「待提交 1 · 待律师确认 0 · 客户尚未提交材料」 for about 1.5 minutes, until the partner pressed 刷新. Evidence: `readiness/collab/RUN-20261126.md`, POLISH.md C21.

author: tobymac208
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 from the roadmap: everyone viewing a board sees each other's changes live, plus who else is on the board right now.

### Broadcasting
- `open_board` subscribes the socket to the board. Every change is sent to the board's other viewers as the same state events the requester gets, minus the `requestId`. The requester's other tabs get it too.
- Board-list changes go to every member:
  - renames, with each member seeing their own role;
  - being added to a board, which shows up in the new member's list right away;
  - deletes, which also tell everyone viewing the board.
- A socket unsubscribes on `close_board`, on opening a different board, or on disconnecting.
- `Hub` (`apps/server/src/ws/hub.ts`) is an in-memory registry of sockets per user and per board. Phase 6 can put Redis pub/sub behind the same methods.

### Ordering with revisions
- Every board write goes through `writeBoard`. It locks the board row, applies the change, and increments `boards.revision` in the same transaction (migration `0002`).
- That lock queues writes to the same board one at a time. Revisions have no gaps, follow commit order, and a failed write doesn't use one up. It replaces the old per-column locks.
- Each board event carries its revision. The browser's `syncReducer` applies changes in revision order:
  - it holds back early events, including ones that arrive before the snapshot;
  - it drops events the snapshot already includes;
  - it reloads the board if a gap hasn't filled after 1.5 seconds.
- `open_board` checks access, then subscribes, then reads the snapshot, so no change can slip in between.

### Presence
- The board header shows "N here now". People with the board open get a green dot and everyone else is dimmed.
- Each person counts once however many tabs they have, and they drop out when they leave the board or disconnect.

### Other
- If someone deletes the card you're editing, the editor closes and tells you why.
- The protocol version is now 3: revisions on board changes, `close_board`, and `presence`.

## Testing

- `pnpm test`: 16 shared, 15 web and 48 server tests.
- 15 new server tests with several clients cover broadcasts, board-list updates, presence (multiple tabs, disconnects, switching boards), `close_board`, non-members, and revisions under concurrent writes.
- To check that a client got nothing it shouldn't, the tests ping it and collect everything that arrives before the pong, so there are no sleeps.
- Reducer tests cover the ordering cases: shuffled events, events that arrive before the snapshot, duplicates, and recovering from a gap.
- Checked live against Docker Postgres: 100 changes from 5 connections at once, and the watching user received all of them with no gaps.

## Not in this PR (phase 3)

- If two people edit the same card at the same time, the last save wins.
- While you drag, other people's changes are hidden until you drop. If someone moved cards in the meantime, your card can land a slot off from where you dropped it.
- Edits still wait for the server before they show; there are no optimistic updates yet.

author: oaklight
body:
## What and why

Refs #1719. The Chat Completions stream writer defaulted a missing `tool_call_index` to 0 in both the start and the delta handler, so two calls whose IR events carry no index merged into `tool_calls[0]`. Chat counts tool calls per choice from 0 without gaps, so the writer now gives each call the next free slot of its choice when it opens (`StreamContext.claim_tool_call_slot`, additive) and its deltas follow that slot. The slot does not depend on the index the source dialect gave the call (Open Responses gives the first call output position 1 after a text item), and a dropped intrinsic call takes no slot. Without a context the index is 0.

Reproduction on master (writer fed two starts and two unindexed deltas): every `tool_calls[].index` is 0. With n=2 choices, an intermediate head of this PR gave choice 1's first call index 1; master gave 0 and the final head gives 0.

## Risk tier (tick one)

- [ ] Pure move: code moves, no logic edit (a mechanical check proves it)
- [ ] Boundary or contract change: imports, public API, config schema, wire format
- [x] Runtime-behaviour change: logic that runs differently after this PR
- [ ] Security-relevant: auth, keys, credentials, sanitizing, network exposure

## Verification

- [x] `make lint` and `make test` pass. Result: ruff clean; `pytest tests --ignore=tests/integration` 12669 passed, 85 skipped, 10 xfailed (worktree on PYTHONPATH)
- [x] `ty` clean (`python scripts/dev/run_ty.py`; new diagnostics: 0): the pre-commit ty hook passed
- [ ] Pure move only: not applicable
- [x] Overlap check done: `pr_overlap.py` shows no open PR on the same files
- [ ] CI is fully green before review is requested

New tests in `tests/converters/chat_completions/test_stream_tool_call_index.py`: unindexed starts and deltas, a source index not leaking into the slot, a dropped intrinsic call, per-choice counting, no context, and Messages / Open Responses streams read to IR (text before the calls) and written as Chat. With the source files reverted to master, five of them fail.

## Property test (rebased on 538eb048d4)

This PR removes the constraint in `tests/converters/test_leg_agreement_property.py` that put `tool_call_index` on every delta (`_indexed_events` and the module-local `_stream_leg`); the property now uses the table's own `_stream_leg`. With the fix, `pytest tests/converters/test_leg_agreement_property.py` passes. With the source file(s) reverted to origin/master (restored with `cp`), the same file fails on `test_the_legs_agree_and_keep_the_turn[chat_completions]`.


## Review round 1 (head after this push)

- The slot is keyed by `(choice_index, call_id)`: the same id in two choices gets a slot in each (choice 1 had index 1, now 0).
- A call that opens always takes the next free slot, so a source that reuses one id for two calls gets two slots, and later fragments follow the latest. A fragment of a call that never opened claims a slot lazily instead of joining call 0 (probe `ORPHAN` landed on call a's slot).
- `OpenResponsesStreamContext.from_base` now copies `_next_tool_slot` and `_tool_slot_of`.
- New tests: the three cases above, Google generate with n=2 (its calls 2, 3 in the second candidate now write 0, 1), Google Interactions and Open Responses with text before two calls. Against the previous head the first three fail; against master the new foreign-stream and Google cases fail.

## Review round 2

The docstring now says the two-slot rule holds for an IR stream with two starts sharing an id. A Chat source that reuses an id yields one start (the reader logs "Conflicting Chat Completions tool IDs"), so it stays one call; `test_pin_a_chat_source_that_reuses_an_id_stays_one_call` pins that. Changing the Chat reader is a separate behaviour, not done here. Converters and public-API tests: 4261 passed (the full suite ran on the previous head; this delta is a docstring and one test).

## AI disclosure

- [x] AI tools were used for: investigation, the fix and the test. No `Co-authored-by` AI tags are in the commits.

## Skipped hooks

author: wstein-agents
body:
## Container launches (RunPod), part 4: heartbeats

One commit on main. An enrolled container can now send heartbeats, and one whose heartbeats stop is ended, the same way as a VM. Until now, the heartbeat handler recognised an enroll only by a VM's gate report, and the heartbeat watchdog and its due index named `mode = 'vm'`. So an enrolled container's heartbeats were refused, and a dead pod would have billed until its lifetime ran out or the reconcile sweep found it.

Container enroll stays off in production (`container: null` in the Worker). With this, its last blocker on the control side is gone.

### What changes
- **The handler** (`src/heartbeat.ts`):
  - A container's enroll is its boot token's use, on a launch that has its hard lifetime: `max_end_ms` is set only by enroll.
  - That use time bounds the report's times from below, as the gate report's time does for a VM.
  - VM machines are looked up exactly as before.
- **The watchdog:**
  - The due search no longer names a mode.
  - A silent container is marked to terminate (`heartbeat-lost`) in the same guarded batch that rechecks what it read. A heartbeat landing first leaves it alone, and a machine that isn't running is deferred 120 s.
  - The container watchdog then ends the pod: the boot token revoked first, the pod confirmed gone, the accrual closed.
- **`migrations/0018_heartbeat_all_modes.sql`:**
  - The due index is rebuilt without the mode, still holding enrolled launches only, so the search stays a range scan of its bound.
  - The VM test's assertion on the index text follows.
  - The number 0018 is used because 0016 is taken by an open branch.

### Tests (`src/container-heartbeat.test.ts`, 7)
- An enrolled container's heartbeat is kept, and its due time moves on.
- A container that never enrolled (window open, or token revoked by a termination) is refused with 401, with nothing written.
- The enroll time (the token's use) bounds a report's times from below: a millisecond earlier is 400, the enroll time itself is accepted.
- Silent past its due time (not at exactly 120 s): marked `heartbeat-lost`. Then the container watchdog revokes first, ends the pod, terminates the launch and closes the accrual at that time.
- A heartbeat landing first keeps the container; a machine not running is deferred, not marked.
- The search takes container launches.

author: wustep
body:
Stephen picked all four looks. This makes them four themes of one app, with a theme button, and changes the bar of the two reading pages.

> **Do not merge until Stephen says so.** Not a draft: it is ready to review. (#103, #104 and #105 are the drafts these themes came from; this does not close them.)

**Preview:** https://instruments-git-feat-themes-wustep.vercel.app (Vercel: deployed, commit status success; it is behind Vercel sign-in)

## The four themes

| Theme | From | In a line |
|---|---|---|
| **Night Bench** | `main` (the default, a first visit's) | warm near-black, ivory linework, vermilion where something vibrates; Newsreader and IBM Plex; a product studio in 3D |
| **Evening Hall** | `ui-alt-a`, #103 | a concert hall at night: a velvet bar, gold for what is chosen or sounds, ivory paper for what opens; Libre Caslon and Cabin; a stage's boards, one spot and a curtain in 3D |
| **Day Studio** | `ui-alt-b`, #105 | a north-lit white room: plaster and soft shadows, ink for what is chosen, one blue for what sounds; its 2D instruments re-drawn for daylight; a daylight studio in 3D |
| **Night Gallery** | `ui-alt-c`, #104 | a museum room after closing: cool charcoal, light as the only signal; Libre Franklin; a silver light from behind in 3D |

Each carries its layout chrome, type and colour, its 2D drawing and vector lines, and its own 3D room and lights. The three alternates are ported from their branches, not redrawn: each was compared against its own branch's dev server (below).

## The theming framework

Everything a theme is lives in `apps/web/src/themes/`:

```
themes/
  index.ts      the registry and the runtime: THEMES, theme(), setTheme(), onTheme(), themeEpoch()
  types.ts      what a theme is (Theme, Ink, VectorLook, Glyphs, DrawLook, Chrome, Words)
  sheets.ts     the page's one stylesheet: base.css and every theme's three sheets
  base.css      what is every theme's (the theme's sign, data-themes)
  <id>/theme.ts                        tokens, as data: 2D inks by role, the vector palette, the chrome's signs, what else a look sets
  <id>/styles.css, panel.css, vector.css   its chrome and type, written as if it were the only look
  <id>/world.ts                        its 3D room: the scene photographed for the image-based light, key / fill / rim, the floor, what stands behind, exposure, bloom
  <id>/words.ts                        what the Notes page says of the look
  day-studio/draw/                     Day Studio's own 2D drawers
```

* **Registry and tokens.** `theme()` is the one in use; nothing else in the app names a theme. The 2D inks were hues on main (`INK.vermilion`, `V.blue`) and are roles now (`INK.line / sound / warm / cool`, `V.line / sound / slot1…4`): live objects the registry refreshes, so the three night themes are one set of drawings in their own inks. Whatever a branch changed beyond a palette value became typed theme data, never an `if (theme === …)`.
* **Sheets.** Each alternate rewrote the whole chrome in its own vocabulary, so a theme keeps its three sheets whole. The build scopes every rule of a file under `themes/<id>/` to `<html data-theme="<id>">` (`apps/web/theme-plugins.ts`, a PostCSS plugin). The scope is a `:where(…)`, which weighs nothing, so a sheet behaves as it did alone. All four are in the page's one stylesheet: switching asks for nothing and waits for nothing.
* **Switching** (`setTheme`) changes the chrome, the 2D stage, the vector lines and the 3D world together, with no reload. Cached pictures are keyed on `themeEpoch()`. In 3D the world is swapped in place: `three3d.ts` no longer has a look of its own, it asks a `World`; no instrument's shader is compiled again, and four worlds twice round leave the same count of programs, textures and geometries.
* **Persistence and no flash.** The choice is the device's (`localStorage['piano-model.theme']`). The build writes a boot script from the registry into the head of both pages (the app and the 404), ahead of the stylesheet: it puts the stored theme on `<html data-theme>` before anything is painted. A first visit is Night Bench. The e2e test records every value the attribute ever has across a reload: only the stored theme, and before `first-paint`.
* **Day Studio's 2D instruments** were re-drawn for daylight on that branch, not recoloured, so they are drawers of its own (`themes/day-studio/draw/`, a 136 kB chunk fetched only with that theme). The drawers in `ui/` stay the one entry and hand over at their top.
* `lite`, the phone's AO and shadow switches, shader warming and the held first frame work in every world.

## The theme button

Four dots (the four looks' colours, no word) at the end of the top bar, with a tooltip and an accessible name. It opens a small pick of the four; the pick reuses the sheet-music parts menu's markup, so each theme draws it in its own style.

It sits in the bar's right margin rather than in the row. Both the 1366 px laptop bar (an upright in 3D) and the phone bar are full to the pixel, and existing tests pin that: an in-row button pushed the lamp's "tap a key" out at 412 px and made the page 9 px too wide at 1366. In the margin it costs the row nothing, and every pinned fit is as it was. On a phone its touch target is the bar's corner at the bar's full height.

## Measurements and Notes

* The lamp, its "tap a key" / sound status and the MIDI indicator are hidden on those two pages. Audio and MIDI input themselves are untouched; on the stage the lamp is as before.
* **player** is added as the first of the page links there. It returns to the stage as it was (the current instrument or orchestra address) and is styled as its neighbours are in every theme; its touch target is 48 px tall. It is not shown on the stage.
* It replaces the bare ← that stood at the bar's left on those pages, rather than sitting beside it.

## Screenshots

Before is production (one look). After is this branch's build; each theme was asked for as a visitor's device would, by its stored choice.

body:
Lands the stranded local branch `pt/teak-ci-gates` for #141: the idle, input-latency, idle-memory and binary-size gates. Rebased onto current master and reshaped to fit ENGINEERING.md.

## What it does

- `zig build gates` runs, per example, a ReleaseSmall `shot -- --gates-json` (idle per state, one click latency, memory), then `ui-install` and `web` for native exe size and wasm brotli size. It writes `zig-out/gates/ci-gates.json` and compares against `tools/ci_gates_budgets.json` (fail above +10%).
- `teak.headless` gains `latencyCheck` / `latencyAfterClick`, `IdleReport.blinks` / `fullyQuiet()`, RSS and committed bytes on `IdleReport`, `requestsGate`, and the `--gates-json` shot flag.

## Policy fit

- **Not a blocking check.** `zig build test` and the `blocking` CI job are untouched, so the blocking count does not change. The gates are the last stage of `tools/test-e2e.sh heavy` (`zig build test-heavy`), and the scheduled `heavy` job uploads the JSON as an artifact.
- The gates stage runs even when an earlier heavy stage fails. The nightly `heavy` job on master currently fails in `a11yprobe` (focus mirroring timeout, run 45603118981); with plain `set -e` the gates would never have run in CI.
- **No unit tests.** The source branch added 5 `test` blocks in `src/headless_run.zig`, 2 in `tools/ci_gates.zig` and test scaffolding in `src/run_test.zig` (a file master already removed). None are ported.
- **Comments** trimmed to one-line invariants; the policy text moved to `SRC.md`.

## Budgets

- Native exe size and idle memory are budgeted per host triple. The branch seeded only `aarch64-linux`; CI is `x86_64-linux`. A host triple with no entry now reports `SKIPPED (no budget)` per example plus a summary line, instead of the old `recorded`, and never fails. I did not seed `x86_64-linux` from my machine: RSS under lavapipe depends on core count and Mesa version, so the numbers should come from the runner (`zig build gates -- --update-budgets` there, or copy them from the uploaded artifact).
- Wasm brotli is the portable budget. It is reseeded from Zig 0.17.1 on current master (the old seeds were 0.9% to 2.0% above) and is always measured with Node's brotli, so it no longer depends on whether the host has the `brotli` CLI.
- On x86_64 CI this PR therefore gates idle, latency and wasm size, and reports native size and memory.

## Other changes relative to the source branch

- `/proc/self/status` never carries `Committed_AS`, so that branch was dead: committed bytes are always `RssAnon + VmSwap`. The `source` field, the `--mem-check` alias and the public `parseProcStatus` / `readProcessMemory` / `parsePair` are gone.
- The separate `ci-gates` GitHub job from the branch is dropped in favour of the existing `heavy` job. The ported commit "ci: gates job, and document the four gates" still carries its original message; its workflow change is not in this PR.
- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` module trees are regenerated with `tools/gen_tree.py`. They were already stale on master, so that diff includes a few unrelated lines.

## Verification (x86_64 Linux, Zig 0.17.1, lavapipe, 20 cores)

- `zig fmt --check src build.zig`: pass
- `zig build test -j4`: pass
- `zig build audit`: pass
- `zig build gates`: pass, 14 examples, 526 s
- Doctored budgets (`--budgets` copy with a low wasm budget, a low RSS budget and `scene3d` not exempt): `memory FAIL`, `wasm size FAIL`, `idle FAIL`, exit 1
- `zig build test-heavy -j4`: exit 1. The 11 example canaries, `drive-e2e.sh`, the todo web build and the gates stage pass; `a11yprobe` fails locally with `Cannot find package 'puppeteer-core'`. I did not run `npm ci --prefix tools` because `tools/node_modules` is tracked on master as a symlink into another repository's directory.

## Summary

Links #287. Revalidate a tenant administrator's current active grant inside the same transaction as organization-admin group membership mutations. The transaction uses the existing tenant-admin advisory lock, so a mutation is ordered against operator/SCIM/lifecycle grant revocation. Existing tenant/group/user SQL predicates remain unchanged.

Adds an integration regression test for a stale authorization snapshot after grant revocation and for cross-tenant member rejection. It verifies rejected requests leave memberships and successful mutation audit rows unchanged.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — passed.
- `SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo test -p rustshare-server --test share_acl_propagation organization_group_membership_rechecks_revoked_admin_and_tenant_scope -- --exact --nocapture` — Rust compilation passed; runtime test was blocked because the disposable `rustshare_test` database is unavailable locally (`PoolTimedOut`). The suite guard refused the configured `rustshare` application database; it was not used.

## Risk / Safety Notes

This changes a tenant authorization boundary. The only authority remains the existing `organization_administrators` grant; it is rechecked under the same advisory lock used by grant revocation. The test covers revoked authority and cross-tenant group membership. No migration, new role, or database RLS claim is introduced. Human security review remains required.

author: anthonyeleven
body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68946

The RBD Mirroring page says little about `rbd-mirror` daemons in containers,
and the Add Cluster Peer Manually section has misled operators into thinking
that the remote cluster must have a vanity name. This PR changes two parts of
`doc/rbd/rbd-mirroring.rst`.

**Peer cluster names.** The section says that `rbd-mirror` needs
`/etc/ceph/{cluster-name}.conf` and a keyring for the peer, and writes peers as
`client.rbd-mirror-peer@site-b`. A new paragraph says that `{cluster-name}` is
the peer's site name, which `rbd-mirror` also uses to find the peer's files on
the local host, and that it is not the remote cluster's internal name. It also
says that vanity names are deprecated, that neither cluster should be given
one, and that existing clusters with vanity names should be retrofitted to the
default name `ceph`. It points to the existing note about cluster names, which
now has a label, and to the `$cluster` metavariable.

**Containerized and cephadm deployments.** A new subsection of the rbd-mirror
Daemon section:

- Leads with the config-key method. `mirror pool peer bootstrap import`, and
  `mirror pool peer add` with `--remote-mon-host` and `--remote-key-file`,
  store the peer's `mon_host` and `key` in the local cluster's config-key store
  (`librbd::api::Mirror::peer_site_set_attributes()`). `ClusterWatcher` reads
  them and `PoolReplayer::init_rados()` sets them on the remote connection, so
  the daemon needs no files for the peer.
- Shows `ceph orch apply rbd-mirror` with a placement, and notes that cephadm
  creates each daemon's CephX user.
- For anyone who prefers files, gives an `rbd-mirror` spec with
  `custom_configs` that mounts `/etc/ceph/site-b.conf` and
  `/etc/ceph/site-b.client.rbd-mirror-peer.keyring`, then
  `ceph orch redeploy rbd-mirror`. `init_rados()` sets `$cluster` to the peer's
  site name, so the default conf and keyring search paths find these files.
  cephadm bind-mounts `ceph.conf` and the daemon's keyring as single files, not
  `/etc/ceph` (`src/cephadm/cephadmlib/daemons/ceph.py`), so the files are not
  hidden.
- Notes that `custom_configs` puts the peer's key in the service spec, where
  `ceph orch ls --export` shows it.

A label is added to the Custom Config Files section of
`doc/cephadm/services/index.rst` for the cross-reference. The hunks do not
overlap https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/74332 or
https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/74228, which change other parts of the same
page.

The page's example CephX key, which appears three times, is changed in the
middle so that it reads as a placeholder. It still decodes as a well-formed
key.

## Contribution Guidelines
- To sign and title your commits, please refer to [Submitting Patches to Ceph](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/main/SubmittingPatches.rst).

- If you are submitting a fix for a stable branch (e.g. "quincy"), please refer to [Submitting Patches to Ceph - Backports](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/master/SubmittingPatches-backports.rst) for the proper workflow.

- When filling out the below checklist, you may click boxes directly in the GitHub web UI.  When entering or editing the entire PR message in the GitHub web UI editor, you may also select a checklist item by adding an `x` between the brackets: `[x]`.  Spaces and capitalization matter when checking off items this way.

author: santiago-musso
body:
UX plan PR 6 ([plan](https://github.com/FirefightersOrg/firefighters/blob/main/docs/ux/plan.md#pr-6-error-pages-home-redirect-back-link)). Audit items: **A13** (error pages are bare and in English), **A11** (after signing in there is a dead end before the work), **A2** (navigation inside a campaign: the breadcrumb trail), **A10** (words from how the system was built: «Firefighters»). Decision P1 (institution name) from #50.

## What changes

**1. Error pages.** A 403, a 404 or a 500 used to be the words «403 Forbidden» on an empty page. Now it renders inside the navigation the person was using (the campaign shell, the staff bar or the portal) and says what happened and where to go.

- 403: «Sin acceso a esta sección», and whose section it is, from the missing permission («Esta sección es de tesorería / operación / administración»).
- 404: «No se encontró», with what was not found when the server says it.
- 500: «No se pudo cargar», with «Volver a intentar».
- Under a campaign the actions are «Volver a {sección}» and «Ir al inicio de la campaña». No page contains «Forbidden» or «Not Found».
- New: `src/lib/error-copy.ts`, `components/layout/ErrorMessage.svelte`, and `+error.svelte` at the root, `/campaigns`, `/campaigns/[id]` and `/portal`.

**2. Landing.** `/` sends staff who can open campaigns to the only active campaign, or to the campaign list when there are none or several. Collectors still land on the portal. Whoever can open neither keeps the session card on `/`.

**3. Back link.** `PageHeader` shows one link, «Volver a {parent}», instead of the breadcrumb trail. The `breadcrumbs` prop is unchanged, so no page had to change. The link is hidden when the parent is already in the shell (the campaign home, the campaign list, the portal home).

**4. The institution's name.** Page titles, the login page and the ledger labels say «Bomberos Voluntarios» / «Bomberos» instead of «Firefighters» (`institutionName()`, from `PUBLIC_INSTITUTION_NAME`). Moved here from PR 5. `static/offline.html` and the web manifest are static files and keep their text: they change in the wrap-up PR if you want them to.

## What does not change

No SQL, migrations, permissions or service contracts. The only behaviour change is the redirect on `/`, which reads the active campaigns with the session's own client (`listActiveCampaignIds`, limit 2) and is covered by route tests. The ledger's stored values are the same; only their labels changed.

## Acceptance (from the plan)

- [x] A 403 and a 404 under a campaign render the shell, a message in Spanish and a link that works; none contains «Forbidden» or «Not Found» (`tests/e2e/errors-and-landing.spec.ts`).

body:
## What

An account that already has workspaces now picks one, instead of todz silently opening the first. Owner request: PROMPT.md "Tonight's last three", item 2. The decisions are in ADR 0076.

- **Sign-in picker:** shown when signing in with two or more workspaces and no choice remembered on this Mac. It lists each workspace's name and named project count (the Inbox is not counted), and "New Workspace…" stays. One workspace still opens directly, and a new account still gets "Name your first workspace".
- **Remembered choice:** kept per Mac and per owner, in the existing cache field. Another owner's cache is erased before anything is read from it (ADR 0027).
- **Switching:** Settings lists every workspace and switches between them, beside the Workspace menu (⌘1–9) and the existing switcher. The widgets and the menu bar count follow the active workspace.
- **While the picker shows:**
  - ⌘1–9 does nothing;
  - Siri and Shortcuts answer "Choose a workspace in todz first.";
  - a workspace that leaves the listing stops its watches.
- **Not in this PR:** "Last activity" in the picker. It would need a migration and a write on the hot path, so it is the loop's call for v1.1 (ADR 0076).

No server change and no deploy.

## Tests

- **Red-first:**
  - 679f1901: 9 failures on the phase and choice tests.
  - 6e404990: the named project count.
  - a3b507e7: switching by number while choosing, the watches stopping, and Shortcuts readiness.
- **Tenant guard test:** another owner's remembered workspace never opens. It was green when it landed, so it is a guard, not a red-first test.
- **Test harness:** the shared setup no longer picks a workspace silently. Every test with several workspaces states the one it expects (5561e13f).
- **`swift test`:** 1353 tests in 107 suites pass.
- **Tester walk** on the Debug app against a local Worker, at a3473990 and again at c6162bb5:
  - the picker with names and counts;
  - choosing opens the workspace, and the choice is remembered after a relaunch;
  - the Workspace menu and Settings switch;
  - the count and the widget data follow a switch;
  - one workspace opens directly;
  - a new account gets the naming screen;
  - a second owner on the same Mac gets the picker, not the first owner's choice;
  - at c6162bb5 the picker and Settings read 1 project, and the popover's ⌘2 does nothing while the picker shows; the settled picker carries no sign-in text (an earlier shot was mid-crossfade).

## Visual explainer

| Change | Screenshot |
|---|---|
| The picker after sign-in | ![picker-dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/724fdef0-d8d4-487c-bd13-728c61fc3905) |
| Settings lists every workspace and switches | ![settings-workspaces-dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/399c1d8e-7410-4055-b3d8-949b0d55e9d3) |
| The Workspace menu | ![workspace-menu-dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec88160e-b1c8-45b0-a23b-60515dea8b0b) |

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> signedIn
  signedIn --> naming: no workspace
  signedIn --> ready: one workspace, or a remembered choice
  signedIn --> choosing: two or more, nothing remembered
  choosing --> ready: chooseWorkspace (remembered per Mac and owner)
  ready --> choosing: the active workspace left the listing
```

## Review

- **Combined reviewer at 7ff8319d:** NO, with 4 IMPORTANT findings:
  - the popover's ⌘1–9 escaped the picker;
  - "1 projects";
  - the test harness hid the choice;
  - no tenant test.

  All are fixed in a3b507e7..c6162bb5, along with the MINORs: the watches, Shortcuts readiness, the empty Settings section, the spec wording and the plan ticks.

**Blast radius:** the Mac client only. It touches the startup state machine, the per-owner cache, the widget snapshot and Shortcuts readiness. Owners with two or more workspaces signing in on a fresh Mac notice it first. Rollback is a revert, and it loses no data, because the remembered id lives in the existing cache field.

**Merge sensitivity:** MEDIUM. It changes the app's startup flow.

## Security

Security verdict: CLEAR. A choice is accepted only from the list the server returned for this session, and another owner's cache is erased before it is read.

## Learnings and docs

The ADR 0076 and README cells are updated. Learning: a test harness that picks a default for its tests hides the behaviour change it was written for; state the choice in each test instead.
