author: alexisromtz-lab
body: `block_advantage` is affine in the fee with slope `n - 1`, so inverting it is one integer division. This change gives the numerator a reading and a name. Write `delta` for the **defect** of a block, `sum - lcm`, and `k` for the number of its odd parts: - **lcm even:** `floor(lcm / 2) = lcm / 2` and each odd part contributes `(p - 1) / 2`, so twice the advantage at a zero fee is `k - delta`. - **lcm odd:** every part is odd, so it is `n - 1 - delta`. Hence `fee = 2 * B // (2 * (n - 1)) + 1` when `2 * B >= 0`, else `0`. The fee of a block is its defect, halved and divided by one less part. The naive version of this — fee off the defect alone — is wrong, and `(6, 10, 15)` is the witness: defect `1`, naive quotient negative, block looks free, while the least fee that breaks the formula with it is `1`. The correction is `k`: an even grid prices at exactly half, an odd one loses half a unit to the floor. **What ships** | | | |---|---| | `block_defect(parts)` | `sum - lcm`, with `k` and `2 * B` derivable | | `block_fee_closed(parts)` | one division, `0` when the block is free | | `block_fee(parts)` | unchanged — the slow route stays as the independent instrument | | `block-fee ` | prints both rows side by side; `RC 3` for a block of one grid | **The fee-of-one window stops being a coincidence.** For a triple with an even lcm the fee is one exactly when the defect sits within three of the odd-part count — two blocks wide in the whole horizon, `(6, 10, 15)` (defect `1`) and `(6, 14, 21)` (defect `-1`), which is what the census kept finding without explaining. **Exhaustive, not illustrative:** every block of 2 and 3 parts in both universes up to `T = 400` — **42 287 blocks, 0 mismatches** between the two routes, plus a sign test that the free blocks are exactly the ones `block_advantage` says save at a zero fee. **Verification:** `405 tests`, `104` self-test checks `RC 0`, CI on 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13. Version `0.19.0`. ---

author: apex-mochen
body:
`TarFileSystem` finds members in its index, then passes the original name to `tarfile.extractfile()`. The standard library resolves that name by scanning the member list backwards. On a scan of many small shards, this repeats work for every file and can make the name lookup quadratic.

Keep the already parsed `TarInfo` in the index in place of the unused data offset. Pass it to `extractfile()` when its name matches the previous lookup key. This still uses `tarfile` for extraction and link resolution. For unusual regular members with a trailing slash, preserve the previous string lookup, which strips that slash before resolving the name. Exact and normalized duplicate names retain last-entry behavior.

### End-to-end measurement

Each timed run opens a local archive, discovers JSONL shards with `fs.glob()`, reads every matched shard through `fs.cat_file()`, and closes the archive. The fixtures store one synthetic record of roughly 450 bytes per member. Archive creation and output hashing are outside the timer. Windows, i9-14900HX, Python 3.12.14, base `baeaac93e2688cd7bb67b35b75df6d335a42a62b`, warmed OS cache, median of five measured runs after warm-up, alternating order.

| Format | Archive members | Files read | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| tar | 1,024 | 128 | 17.64 ms | 15.88 ms |
| tar | 1,024 | 1,024 | 33.56 ms | 20.87 ms |
| tar | 8,192 | 128 | 145.81 ms | 124.27 ms |
| tar | 8,192 | 8,192 | 1089.30 ms | 203.77 ms |
| tar.gz | 8,192 | 8,192 | 1157.41 ms | 214.63 ms |

The 8,192-member full scans improved by about 81% in both formats. Paths, order and payload bytes matched across all runs. The single-partition case includes reading the entire catalog on each open. These are ordered local reads of small members. Large payloads and random seeks in compressed archives can spend a larger share of time in I/O and decompression.

### Validation

TAR and shared archive suites reported 215 passed and 28 skipped. Coverage includes direct and cached reads, compression, links, path normalization, duplicate members, missing members, and negative offsets. Added cases for repeated raw names and the trailing-slash fallback. Ruff check, Ruff formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the end-to-end measurements</summary>

Run from the candidate checkout with fsspec importable.

```python
import ast
from contextlib import closing
import hashlib
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import statistics
import subprocess
import tarfile
import tempfile
import time

from fsspec.implementations import tar as mod

BASE = 'baeaac93e2688cd7bb67b35b75df6d335a42a62b'
code = subprocess.check_output(['git','show',BASE+':fsspec/implementations/tar.py'],encoding='utf-8')
cls = next(n for n in ast.parse(code).body if isinstance(n,ast.ClassDef) and n.name=='TarFileSystem')
names = ('_index','_open')
ns = vars(mod).copy()
methods = [n for n in cls.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in names]
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=methods,type_ignores=[]),'<base>','exec'),ns)
fs_type=mod.TarFileSystem
variants=[{name:ns[name] for name in names},{name:getattr(fs_type,name) for name in names}]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    rows=[]
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        for fmt, partitions in [('tar',8),('tar',64),('tar.gz',64)]:
            per_part=128
            archive=Path(directory)/f'data.{fmt}'
            payload_size=0
            with tarfile.open(archive,'w:gz' if fmt.endswith('gz') else 'w') as tar:
                for p in range(partitions):
                    for q in range(per_part):
                        name=f'corpus/p{p:03d}/shard-{q:03d}.jsonl'
                        payload=(json.dumps({'partition':p,'shard':q,'text':'data '*80})+'\n').encode()
                        info=tarfile.TarInfo(name)
                        info.size=len(payload)
                        tar.addfile(info,io.BytesIO(payload))
                        payload_size+=len(payload)
            selections=['single','full'] if fmt=='tar' else ['full']
            for selection in selections:
                samples=[[],[]]
                counts=set()
                digests=set()
                for i in range(6):
                    for j in (range(2) if i%2==0 else reversed(range(2))):
                        for name in names:
                            setattr(fs_type,name,variants[j][name])
                        start=time.perf_counter()
                        with closing(fs_type(str(archive))) as fs:
                            paths=fs.glob('corpus/p000/*.jsonl' if selection=='single' else 'corpus/*/*.jsonl')
                            payloads=[fs.cat_file(path) for path in paths]
                        elapsed=time.perf_counter()-start
                        hasher=hashlib.sha256()
                        for path,payload in zip(paths,payloads):
                            hasher.update(path.encode()+b'\0'+payload)
                        digests.add(hasher.hexdigest())
                        counts.add(len(payloads))
                        if i:
                            samples[j].append(elapsed)
                assert len(digests)==1
                expected=per_part if selection=='single' else per_part*partitions
                assert counts=={expected}
                row=dict(format=fmt,archive_members=per_part*partitions,selection=selection,files_read=expected,total=[statistics.median(x) for x in samples],samples=samples,sha256=digests.pop())
                rows.append(row)
                print(row,flush=True)
```
</details>

body:
# Pull Request Description

Stacked on #2436. The Explorer HUD kit drew its context menus with files of its own. They are now shared components exported from `@dcl/one-ui`, with the look they had: no visible change in the HUD.

## What does this PR change?

- New `ContextMenu`, `Submenu`, `KebabMenu` and `AnchoredMenu` (`library/ui/components/ContextMenu`), with tests, a gallery page and a row in `docs/ui-components.md`. The rules are the kit's, with foundation tokens where one has the same value and a comment naming the HUD token where none does. They stay outside the cascade layer: the rows are native buttons, which a host's reset would restyle.
- The shared components know nothing about the engine. A host passes `whileOpen` (`whileSubmenuOpen` on the menu) to register an open list with whatever closes its layers, and `scale` to `AnchoredMenu`. `AnchoredMenu` also takes `open`, so a caller can keep it mounted.
- The kit's four files become adapters with no styles: they pass the engine's cancel layers and the HUD scale. Their callers do not change.
- Three HUD tokens have no reader left and are removed (`--menu-sheet`, `--switch-off-menu`, `--font-body`).
- Figma has `menu-item` and `menu-header` (Menus). These components keep the HUD's look and are not compared with them yet; the stylesheet and the tracker row say so.

## Test Instructions

### Test Steps

1. In `library/ui`, run `pnpm exec vitest run components/ContextMenu gallery/test`. Expect 17 files and 579 tests to pass.
2. In `library/ui`, run `pnpm exec vite --config gallery/vite.config.ts` and open `http://127.0.0.1:6020/?component=ContextMenu`. Expect a dark menu with a header, rows, a switch, two options (one with a ruby check) and a red `Block` row.
3. On the same page, click the first kebab button (three dots). Expect a menu with `View Community` below it. Click outside. Expect it to close.
4. Click `Photo options`. Expect a menu with `Share`, `Download` and `Delete` beside the pointer.
5. In `rendering/bevy-explorer/source/react-web`, run `pnpm exec vitest run ../../../../library/ui/apps/hud`. Expect 164 files and 1766 tests to pass.
6. Needs manual verification: in the HUD, a chat conversation's menu (the flat sheet, with its switch), a profile card's menu with its `Invite to Community` list, and a photo's options in the gallery. Press Escape with a list open: expect only the list to close.

### Additional Testing Notes

Checks run: steps 1 and 5; steps 2 to 4 are covered by the gallery's build check, which mounts the page, and by the unit tests (the menu was not opened by hand on the new page). Measured in Brave against the same pages built with the kit's own files (the kit's Showcase, which draws through the adapters): the menu with its open list, options, check mark and danger row (33 elements), and both kebab menus open (22 elements, with their positions) have the same computed styles. Also `library/ui` and `react-web` typecheck, lint and format on the changed files, `check:shared-inputs` after regenerating the manifest, `figma/lock-digests.mjs`, `gallery/scripts/check-build.mjs` on the build CI checks (`figma/review/review-dist`, prefix `/`), and the `tooling/ui_standards.py` checks. Not measured: the sheet form, a switch row, the header and `AnchoredMenu`. Not run: step 6, the end-to-end suite, the native bundle.

## Review ledger

- P2 (four, none blocking, raised with the approval of 66bfdb7e9: the anchored menu's z-index is a literal and no longer follows the HUD's `--z-popup`; `AnchoredMenu` takes `scale` as a prop while its transform reads `--ui-scale`; its `left` and `top` are inline styles; the latest-callback refs are synced in a passive effect): follow-up in #2263.

## Quality Checklist

- [x] Relevant checks were run; results and any checks not run are listed above.
- [x] Documentation has been updated, if required.
- [x] Performance impact has been considered.
- [ ] For changes covered by `docs/design-feasibility.md`, the design verdict, platform coverage and unresolved blockers are stated.
- [ ] For SDK features: a test scene is included or linked (or not applicable).

## Summary

task 225 mechanism (uvarc wcr 0.09): the ask is top-10 scorers by **points per game** with a 58-game floor. Kimi went straight to `get_leaders(stat_category="PTS")` — the season-TOTALS board (ranked by totals, playoff games mixed in: SGA shows GP 99 / 3172 PTS vs the correct regular-season 76 / 2484) — and answered with a wrong leaderboard (KAT/Siakam/J-Will are top-10 by totals, not PPG; values wrong: 32.0 vs 32.7). The correct tool path already existed: `get_leaders(stat_category="PPG")` returns gold-exact values (32.68, 30.39 verified against silver_leaders_pts arithmetic) — but nothing anywhere names the rate categories, so the model can't know they exist.

Fix is steering-only: the canonical-map bullet now routes per-game leaderboard asks to the rate categories PPG/RPG/APG/SPG/BPG/TS_PCT and warns the plain categories are totals boards, and the `get_leaders` description enumerates them too.

Flagged but out of scope: `_completed_season_totals` mixes playoff games into regular-season totals boards (no season-type filter on silver_boxscores) — a real correctness bug on the totals path, worth its own fix.

## Tests

- `test_leaders_rate_categories.py`: description carries the rate categories.
- `prompt-map.test.mjs`: canonical map carries the PPG/RPG steering (3/3 pass).

PostHog's URL / Screen column reads `$current_url`, which Furball did not send. body:
## 根因

image / video 页特有的 `ParamFilterGroup`（分辨率 / 音频 / 时长筛选）在桌面端左侧栏**没有外层 padding 容器**，内容直接贴左右边框，是「筛选项与边框重叠」的主因。

## 修复

- 桌面端左侧栏给 `ParamFilterGroup` 补上 `px-4` 容器与分隔线（与移动端调用处同构）
- 左侧栏各分组内边距统一从 `px-3.5` 提到 `px-4`
- 各处 chip 加 `max-w-full break-words`，长文本（厂商名 / 协议 / 价格口径）加 `min-w-0 break-words`，超长时在窄栏内换行而非溢出贴边

## 测试计划

- [ ] `?cat=image` / `?cat=video` 左侧「分辨率 / 音频 / 时长」筛选不再贴边框
- [ ] `?cat=text` 页左侧栏布局不受影响（无 ParamFilterGroup）
- [ ] 各分组 chip、厂商名、协议 label 均在栏宽内正常换行
- [ ] 移动端顶部筛选不受影响

## 目的

`taskfile.yaml` の文字列の書き方を、YAML 記述規約に合わせる。関連 Issue はなし。

## 判断

- プレーンスカラーで書けないシェルコマンド（`{{` で始まる 4 つ）は、クォートスカラーではなく、リテラルスタイルのブロックスカラー（`|-`）で書いた。シェルコマンドの中の `'` と `"` を、YAML のためにエスケープせずに書けるようにするためである。
- プレーンスカラーで書ける文字列（`preconditions` の 2 つ目の `sh` と `msg`）は、クォートを外して、プレーンスカラーで書いた。
- `vars` の `HUGO` と、`preconditions` の 1 つ目の `msg` は、シェルコマンドではなく、プレーンスカラーでも書けない文字列なので、シングルクォートスカラーのままにした。
- `.prettierrc.yaml` の `embeddedLanguageFormatting: off` は、変更していない。`off` は YAML 1.1 に従うツールが真偽値として読む文字列だが、Prettier は文字列として読むためである。
- 他の YAML ファイル（`hugo.yaml`、`pnpm-workspace.yaml`、`.taskrc.yaml`）は、規約に反する箇所がなかったので、変更していない。`pnpm-lock.yaml` は、ツールが生成するファイルなので、対象外とした。

author: zacaronii
body:
## What changed

Follow-up to #125: a Wii game plays with the controller its Yomikata catalog entry names (`wii_controller`, Yomikata #146). For that, Genkan now identifies Wii discs.

- **Wii identify:**
  - A Wii game's release id is the first 6 bytes of MEM1 (`RXXJ01`), the disc header Dolphin copies there. It's accepted when the Wii's magic word 0x5D1C9EA3 is at 0x18 (the GameCube's is at 0x1C).
  - Its build for scripts is `id-version`, as for the GameCube.
  - `RamSnapshots` reads MEM1 for `wii`, and a snapshot is checked against the disc's header as on the GameCube. Yomikata's identity table now has the Wii row (Yomikata #151).
- **`CatalogEntry.wiiController`:** `nunchuk`, `classic` or `sideways`; any other value counts as not said.
- **`WiiController`, `GameWiiController` (new):** the entry's choice, else the Nunchuk. Only what's on the device is read: the release id learned when the game last ran, and the cached entry.
- **When it applies:**
  - **At launch,** when the release is already known (`CoreActivity.EXTRA_WII_CONTROLLER`, set as Dolphin's `dolphin_wiimote_default_device`).
  - **On a first play,** once the id is read from the running game, through the new `ICoreSession.setWiiController`. Dolphin plugs the new controller into its ports as the game runs: a change of that option makes it reset the controllers (`Main.cpp` → `ResetControllers`). The controller already plugged in isn't plugged in again.
- **Yomikata** moves to d6b815b (main, with #146 and #151).

## Tests

- `CatalogEntryTest`: the three values, an unknown one, and none.
- `RamSnapshotsTest`:
  - a made-up Wii header gives its id and its `id-version` build (also through `ScriptEvents.buildId`);
  - a GameCube header isn't taken as a Wii's, nor the other way round;
  - the Wii's MEM1 is the GameCube's range.
- `GameFileTest` (the regression check from #126's review): a zipped GBA game isn't identified from the zip itself, and is identified from the file it's unpacked to, which is the file the player reads.

## Run on the device and not

Not run on the device: the library has no Wii game yet. The Wii round (when the owner's disc is in) will check:
- the logged id and build;
- the launch extra on a second start;
- the live switch on a first play, with a test entry set to `classic`.

## Local check with head

`./gradlew clean`, then `./gradlew assembleDebug lintDebug :app:verifyRoborazziDebug testDebugUnitTest`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL at f5050fb, with "pointer: passed", "memory map: passed", "frame fill: passed" and "script host: passed".

body:
> **Depends on** https://github.com/ballerina-platform/module-ballerinax-activemq.classic/pull/12. Please merge it first.

## Purpose

`send()` takes the payload first, so a simple send doesn't need a record. This follows the walkthrough feedback that the payload should be a positional argument.

**What changed**

| Area | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Signature | `send(Message message, Destination? destination = ())` | `send(anydata payload, Destination? destination = (), *SendOptions options)` |
| Simple send | `send({payload: "hello"})` | `send("hello")` |
| Message settings | Fields of the `Message` record | Named arguments, such as `priority = 7` |
| `messageId` on send | Accepted, but ignored | Not available. The broker assigns it |
| `SendOptions` | – | New record with the settings a sender can set |
| `Message` | Declared every field | Includes `SendOptions`, plus the fields the broker sets |

**Behaviour to know**

- The payload's type picks the JMS message: `string` and `xml` give a `TextMessage`, `byte[]` a `BytesMessage`, a map or record a `MapMessage`, and anything else JSON bytes.
- A record or map is always the payload. `send({payload: "hello"})` sends a map with a `payload` key; it doesn't pull out `"hello"`.
- To forward a received message, pass its payload and the settings to keep: `send(message.payload, dest, priority = 7)`. Other settings aren't copied.
- Options can also be passed as a record: `send(payload, (), options)`.
- Transactions work as in #12: a transacted producer sends inside a `transaction` block.

**Docs**

- README, examples and API docs use the new form.
- `backOffMultiplier` is documented to have no effect at 1.0 or below.
- `scheduledCron` is documented correctly: the other schedule settings apply each time it fires.

Fixes:

## Examples

    check producer->send("order placed");
    check producer->send("order placed", {topicName: "order.events"});
    check producer->send(order, {queueName: "orders"}, priority = 7, correlationId = "req-42");

    transaction {
        check producer->send("order placed");
        check commit;
    }

- [ ] Linked to an issue
- [x] Updated the changelog
- [x] Added tests
- [ ] Updated the spec
- [ ] Checked native-image compatibility

author: netzenbot
body:
User impact: the info panel shows which sandbox mode is in force and links to a list of the modes, and a bare `/sandbox` opens that list instead of printing a sentence. `/status` names the flag, file or command that chose the mode.

## Decisions to confirm
1. A mode the managed file refuses is drawn in the list like the others and refused when chosen, with the same sentence `/sandbox <word>` gives. Instead: mark the row as refused when the list opens. Why: choosing goes through the one path that checks the floor, so the list cannot disagree with it. To reverse: read the managed file when the list opens and add a catalog message for the mark.
2. A bare `/sandbox` no longer prints the mode and what chose it. `/status` has a Sandbox mode row that says it, in the words `doctor` uses. Instead: keep the report and add the list under another word. Why: the request is for a bare `/sandbox` to open the list. To reverse: print the report from `decide("")` again in the bare case.
3. The Sandbox section is placed after Model in the panel. Instead: at the end. Why: it is a setting of the session like the model. To reverse: move the variant in `Section` and `Section::ALL`.

## The problem
A person cannot see the sandbox mode without typing `/sandbox`, and the command only prints a sentence, so changing the mode means typing the word of the mode.

## Reproduce
1. Start the terminal client in a wide terminal and look at the info panel. It has no sandbox line.
2. Type `/sandbox` and press Enter. It prints one sentence naming the mode.

It should show the mode in the panel and open a list of the modes, with the mode in force marked.

## The fix
The panel has a Sandbox section after Model with the mode in force, and pressing it opens the same list as a bare `/sandbox`. The list has strict, read-only, workspace-write and off. Enter on a row does what `/sandbox <word>` does, so the managed floor, the reply and the note to a running turn are the same. Escape leaves the mode alone. `/sidebar` lists the section under the id `sandbox`, so it can be hidden and shown again, and a sidebar file written before the section existed still shows it. `/status` has a Sandbox mode row with the mode and the flag, file or `/sandbox` that chose it, so that information is still reachable in a session now that a bare `/sandbox` opens the list. Only catalog messages and the held mode are drawn.

## Test plan
- [x] `BRAVEBOT_ALLOW_UNCONFIGURED_BUILD=1 cargo test -p bravebot-tui --lib --locked -- status sandbox`: 169 passed
- [x] `BRAVEBOT_ALLOW_UNCONFIGURED_BUILD=1 make check-lint-increase`: passed on the head
- [x] `python3 agents/skills/security-audit/security-audit.py --before-pr upstream/main`: exit 0, 0 findings
- [x] a managed-file pin refuses `off` when a row is taken: rejects a pick that skips the floor; demonstrated by passing `Managed::default()` in the pick, which fails it
- [x] a bare `/sandbox` opens the list at rest and while a turn runs: rejects a bare word that still prints the report; demonstrated by a fault that opens nothing, which fails the tests that open the list
- [x] `/status` names what chose the sandbox mode (`the_status_names_what_chose_the_sandbox_mode`): rejects a row that shows only the mode held; demonstrated by showing `sandbox_mode.name()` in the row, which fails it with `left: "workspace-write"`, `right: "strict from /sandbox"`
- [x] the panel row is a click target that opens the list: rejects a row that draws and does nothing; reasoned only for the fault that draws the section before Model
- [x] the section hidden through `/sidebar` is kept by the id `sandbox`, and an older file leaves it on: reasoned only
- [ ] `make check-affected` on the rebased head: `cargo test` fails 19 tests in `bravebot-agent` (`plugin_git::*` and `plugins::tests::*`), which this branch does not touch. 18 reported `git must be on PATH for this test` under the gate; run alone, 66 of those 67 pass and `variables_that_select_code_set_in_the_persons_environment_do_not_reach_the_clone` fails on `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, with no change to `crates/agent` in this diff. `check-lint-increase`, `check-locales`, `check-versions`, `check-spec` and `check-reviewdog` passed in that run.
- [ ] No screen was captured for the panel or the list. The unit tests draw both.
- Docker gates skipped: host-only
- [ ] CI passes cleanly: the macOS job failed on `servers::tests::a_handshake_that_outlasts_its_time_though_each_request_answers_is_left_out_as_too_slow` (`crates/agent/src/servers.rs`), a timing test in a file this branch does not touch, on the head before this push

author: vainnor
body:
## What changes Two settings forms stay editable while Save runs: course settings (`/c/:course/settings`) and branding (`/admin/branding`). When the save succeeded, each form replaced its whole draft with what the server stored. A field you changed while the request was running went back to the old value, and nothing said so. Now, when a save succeeds, each field that still holds the value that was sent takes the server's stored value. A field you edited during the save keeps your edit. The form then still differs from what was saved, so the next Save sends that edit. The per-field merge is `keepEdits` in `web/src/keep-edits.ts`. I kept the forms editable instead of blocking edits during a save, because #506 already makes sure the edit cannot send the save twice, and keeping the edit costs no extra UI. The course settings form has one more step. Its draft already follows the course when the course changes on the server and the draft holds no edits. Doing the merge in `onSuccess` broke one case: you put a field back to its old value during the save, the next render still saw the old course, decided the draft had no edits, and replaced it with the stored value. So the form now remembers its own save (`settle`), recognizes the stored course by its `updated_at` when the course query delivers it, and merges at that point (`useCourseDraft` in `web/src/course/settings-form.tsx`). On the account page's passkey list, Delete shows a pending spinner while the request runs. The list kept one pending id, the latest delete's, so starting a second delete took the first one's spinner away. It now keeps a set of ids, added in `onMutate` and removed in `onSettled`. The list also passes that set to React Aria's GridList as `dependencies`. Without it, GridList reused each item's earlier render, and in the test no delete showed its pending state at all, not even a single one. The sweep for other forms that replace their draft on success found none. `page-edit.tsx` and `email-template-edit.tsx` record the sent body as their saved state and leave the draft alone. The item editor, New course, Copy, Move, Enroll, New page and Rename passkey all close or navigate on success. Notification preferences (`web/src/account/notification-preferences.tsx:55`) has the passkey list's one-pending pattern: toggling a second switch while the first is saving shows the first switch at its old value until its answer lands. This PR does not change it. ## Before and after ``` Before: a save, with an edit typed while it runs draft {code: "GND-101X"} --Save--> PATCH runs user types title " north" draft {code: "GND-101X", title: "Ground school north"} 200 {code: "GND-101X", title: "Ground school"} --> draft := stored title back to "Ground school"; the edit is lost After 200 {code: "GND-101X", title: "Ground school"} --> code: same as sent takes the stored "GND-101X" title: changed since keeps "Ground school north" --> the form differs from the course; Save sends {title: "Ground school north"} ``` ``` Passkey list, two deletes in flight Before: pending = latest delete only laptop: (none) phone: pending After: pending = {laptop, phone} laptop: pending phone: pending laptop answers phone: pending ``` ## Spec `docs/specs/m1/16-learning-ui-components.md` B14 (branding) and B17 (course settings), and `docs/specs/m0/04-local-accounts.md` B13 (passkey list). The specs do not say what a form does with an edit made during a save. This follows the decision in #505. ## Review - [ ] Touches authentication, sessions, permissions, grading, feedback visibility, billing or data deletion (maintainer line-by-line review). Not ticked: the passkey change affects only how a delete's pending state is drawn. The delete request and the server are unchanged. - [x] Every new route has `Require

`, its four-case test and its cross-organization test (not applicable: no route) - [x] `.sqlx/`, `openapi/stepclimb.json` and the API client regenerated where needed (not applicable: web only, no query or endpoint) ## Certification - [x] I certify this contribution under the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/) (`CONTRIBUTING.md`) - [ ] I signed the [Individual CLA](https://github.com/Vainnor/stepclimb/blob/next/docs/cla/individual.md) through CLA Assistant, or my employer signed the [Entity CLA](https://github.com/Vainnor/stepclimb/blob/next/docs/cla/entity.md) (`CONTRIBUTING.md`) - [x] This is the maintainer's own pull request, which needs no CLA (ADR 0033) ## Gates `just ci` green on x86_64 Linux at a6285553 (on 0b95c690): nextest `Summary 3354 tests run: 3354 passed`, Vitest tokens `189 passed`, ui `1107 passed`, ui-docs `8 passed`, web `882 passed`, story screenshots `3717 passed`, e2e `414 passed`, "just ci: all gates passed". New tests: `web/src/keep-edits.test.ts` (3 cases). In `course-settings.test.tsx`: a field edited during the save is kept and sent by the next Save, and a field put back during the save is kept. In `branding.test.tsx`: the same edit-during-save case. In `account.test.tsx`: two deletes in flight both show pending. Each was mutation-checked: reverting a guard turned its test red. Closes #505

author: shoberman2
body:
## Why

Auto-picked clips were boring. The AI picker asked for "self-contained ideas", always returned N clips even when a video had nothing good, and treated most-replayed peaks as strong hints, so it kept choosing explainers.

## What changed

- **Entertainment-first picking** (`src/pick.ts`): the prompt looks for humor, conflict, surprise, a story with stakes and a payoff, emotion, a quotable line, or an **insight** (something new to learn that a viewer would repeat to a friend; dry how-it-works explanations don't count). Claude lists 2-3x more candidates than needed with a harsh 1-10 score, and only 7+ is clipped.
- **Tighter cuts**: payoff-first editing, cold opens at the sentence that hooks, edges snapped to the quoted first/last words using caption word timings, no leaking neighbouring words, clamped to the video length.
- **Hook headers** follow [marketing-rules](https://github.com/Shoberman2/marketing-rules) (MIT): readable with sound off (aim for 6 words, max 10), name the subject and stakes, hold back the twist, specific and true, no AI tells. `cleanHook` strips em dashes, hashtags, emoji and wrapping quotes.
- **Post descriptions**: AI picks include a `description`. `ClipJob.description` (also on the MCP `create_clips` tool) is saved next to the clip as `<name>.txt`, followed by a source credit line built from the video's metadata (title, channel, timestamped link), never written by the model.
- **Long videos** are read in overlapping parts (overlap longer than the longest allowed clip) instead of dropping every other transcript line.
- **Strict validation** (`finishPicks`): malformed, unscored or unusable replies count as a picker failure and fall back to the other pickers as before.
- **Offline heuristic** rewards laughter/applause markers, emotional, story and learning phrases and banter, and marks down lecture phrasing.
- `clipper` agent, MCP tool descriptions, README and ARCHITECTURE updated to the same bar.

## Removed / behavior changes

- **Removed:** when the AI validly judges a whole video boring, watches no longer fall back to the most-replayed or transcript-heuristic pickers. The inbox item is marked `dismissed` with the best candidate's score in its note. The old "AI picker returned no usable moments" warning is gone; real failures still fall back.
- **Changed:** hook headers aim for 6 words (was 10), and em dashes, hashtags and emoji are removed from them (previously only wrapping quotes).
- **Added:** clips with a description write a `.txt` sidecar; `ClipResult` gains `videoId`, `videoChannel` and `descriptionPath`.

## Evidence

- Blind A/B on three videos (an interview, a finance lecture, a comedy show), judged by a model from another provider: the new picks won all three, averaging 6.4/10 per clip vs 4.1/10 for the old picker. Average clip length dropped from 52s to 37s.
- Code review by a second model found 7 bugs in the first draft (malformed-reply dismissal, a prompt-guard hang on one oversized caption line, overlap ordering, score coercion, chunk-seam coverage, snap leaks, wrong phrase occurrence); all fixed with regression tests.
- Replaying real model replies through the strict validator picked the same clips.
- End to end: cut a real clip with a description; the `.txt` had the right channel and timestamped link.

## Tests

- `npm test`: 47/47 pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build`: clean

## Not in this PR

- Burned-in captions can show auto-caption sound tags such as `[snorts]` (caption renderer, untouched).
- Pre-existing: a watch run longer than 5 minutes can overlap the next scheduler tick, since `lastRunAt` is written when a run finishes.
- No npm publish or version bump.

author: ctoth
body:
Adds `objects/chparents_phase_order.yaml`, which pins the order in which `chparents()` checks its arguments. The checks run over the whole list in phases:

1. the target and every parent must be valid (`E_INVARG`)
2. permission (`E_PERM`)
3. recursion: a self-parent or a descendant anywhere in the list (`E_RECMOVE`)
4. duplicate parents (`E_INVARG`)

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| `chparents(o, {p, p, o, o})` | `E_RECMOVE`: the later self-parent beats the earlier duplicate |
| `chparents(o, {c, c})` where `c` is a child of `o` | `E_RECMOVE`: the descendant beats the duplicate |
| `chparents(o, {o, recycled})` | `E_INVARG`: the later invalid parent beats the earlier self-parent |
| `chparents(recycled, {$object})` | `E_INVARG`, not `E_INVIND` |
| as programmer, `chparents(#0, {#0})` | `E_PERM`: permission is checked before recursion |

The failed-call cases also check that the parents are left unchanged.

This comes from MongooseMoo/barn#1188, which fixes MongooseMoo/barn#1186, a nightly ToastDifferential fuzz divergence: on `chparents(o, {#2, #2, o, o})` Toast raised `E_RECMOVE` and Barn raised `E_INVARG`.

## Results

Toast (WSL oracle `/root/src/toaststunt/build-release/moo`), run from the barn checkout with this suite at `./moo-conformance-tests`. Result: **6 passed** (capability_admission plus the 5 new cases).

```
S=$PWD/moo-conformance-tests; uv run --project "$S" --frozen moo-conformance \
  -m "admission or conformance" \
  --server-command='"/root/src/toaststunt/build-release/moo" {db} {db}.new -p {port}' \
  --target-profile-manifest="$PWD/profiles/toast/stock-wsl-testdb.json" \
  --server-db="$S/src/moo_conformance/_db/Test.db" \
  --server-db-dir="$S/src/moo_conformance/_db/startup" \
  --moo-host=127.0.0.1 \
  --oracle-profile-manifest="$PWD/profiles/toast/stock-wsl-testdb.json" \
  --fail-on-unexpected-skip --strict-markers \
  -k "capability_admission or chparents_phase_order" -v
```

Barn at the PR head (64281005, `go build -o bin/ ./cmd/barn`). Result: **6 passed**.

```
S=$PWD/moo-conformance-tests; uv run --project "$S" --frozen moo-conformance \
  -m "admission or conformance" \
  --server-command "$PWD/bin/barn serve --db {db} --listen tcp://127.0.0.1:{port} --config=$PWD/profiles/barn/outbound-on.conf --profile-id=barn-linux-testdb-outbound-on --profile-manifest={manifest}" \
  --server-db="$S/src/moo_conformance/_db/Test.db" \
  --server-db-dir="$S/src/moo_conformance/_db/startup" \
  --moo-host=127.0.0.1 \
  --oracle-profile-manifest="$PWD/profiles/toast/stock-wsl-testdb.json" \
  --fail-on-unexpected-skip --strict-markers \
  -k "capability_admission or chparents_phase_order" -v
```

Pre-fix Barn (the PR's parent commit, run through `cmd/moo`) returns `{E_INVARG, E_RECMOVE, E_RECMOVE, E_INVIND}` for the self-after-duplicate, descendant-duplicate, invalid-after-self and invalid-target cases. Fixed Barn returns `{E_RECMOVE, E_RECMOVE, E_INVARG, E_INVARG}`. Three of the new cases therefore fail without the fix.

## What

Adds a rendering seam for encounters whose map area resides on an upper plane (such as God Wars Dungeon / Bandos Stronghold on plane 2) by allowing encounter descriptors and render configs to specify `floorLevel`:
1. Shifts the elevated floor plane down to level 0 so the room renders at ground level.

4. Keys the floor level shift to the active encounter descriptor being loaded rather than searching all registered descriptors.
5. Filters and adjusts map locations whose level matches or exceeds `floorLevel`.

author: inkless
body:
## What

The Rust daemon now records a starting Codex agent up from its terminal's title, and pushes the agent's queued mail once it is up. A Codex TUI's one sign that it is up is the terminal title it sets to its thread. Until now nothing read it, so a Codex agent stayed `starting` until its start deadline, and its queued mail never left.

- **Where a harness shows it is up** (`bazhen-harness`): `Capabilities.ready` is a `ReadySource`. It is `Title` for Codex, and `Hooks` for Claude Code and the stubs.
- **Titles with their generation** (`bazhen-runtime-holder`, `holder.rs`, `terminals.rs`):
  - The runtime tells each title change (`Event::Title`), and tells `Event::TitlesMissed` once after a lagged reread.
  - `Terminals::title` reads a title with the generation of the process that set it.
- **The title reader** (`titles.rs`, `readiness.rs`, `serve.rs`):
  - While a start of a title-reading harness waits on its harness, the readiness follower watches its terminal.
  - A watch marks its terminal due at once, so a title the TUI set before the start was timed is read. A told title marks a terminal due only if it is watched. A lag marks every watched terminal due. A start that settles is no longer watched.
  - Each read runs on the agents' tracker, off the follower's loop. A sign of life records the agent up only in the same write that finds the terminal and the generation the title was read at still the agent's. So a title set by another process in the terminal records nothing. Nothing of a title is kept.
  - A title that can't be read while its terminal still runs (any error but gone or stale) is read again: three more times at most, after 250 ms, then 500 ms, then 1 s, while its terminal is still watched. Without this, a title the TUI had already set would never be read again, and the agent would stay `starting` until its deadline.
- **Push on ready** (`mail.rs`, `hooks.rs`, `attention.rs`):
  - Recording an agent up pushes its queued mail. That covers a title, a hook, and a sign kept for a start not yet recorded.
  - After a push, #522's re-read in the transaction that records it stays, and now also tells a restarted (`starting`) agent apart, which ends the pass rather than recording the push.
  - Only one pusher at a time pushes an agent's queued mail, oldest first, so no message is pushed twice and none jumps ahead of older mail. A wake while it runs marks it to read the queue again, under the same lock its end takes.
  - A harness that can't take mail now ends the pass until the next wake. A drop guard clears the agent's mark however the pass ends.
  - `deliver` takes only a `Queued` now. A send, an attention answer and a verb's hand-over (#518) push through the agent's pusher alike, rather than each pushing its one message.

### Deliberate differences from the TS daemon

- A title change comes from the holder's events, not from tmux's pane-title hook. Those events can lag, so after a lag every watched title is read again. tmux's hook ran once for each change, so the TS daemon had no lag to make up.

## Known gaps

- **Spoofed titles:** any process of the same user can write an OSC title to the agent's pts, from inside its terminal or not. What bounds it is the record's checks: the title must be read at the generation the agent still starts at, while the agent is still `starting`. A process that sets the thread's title then can record the agent up early. This is no worse than the TS daemon's pane title.
- **A wake lost with a failed pass:** a wake marked while a pusher runs is dropped with the pusher's entry if that pass then fails (a store read errs). Its mail stays queued until the agent's next wake. The boot re-push (BZ-569) covers it.
- **Ordering latency:** a message whose push keeps failing holds later mail back for its retries, about 3 s (waits of 1 s and 2 s), before it is given up as undeliverable.
- **Accepted survivors:**
  - The push after a hook records an agent up (`hooks.rs` `ready`). No hook-ready harness takes mail by push today, so the call is inert. Proving it would take a stub harness that turns hooks into signs of life.
  - `Titles::told`'s early return for a terminal not watched. `next()` drops any due terminal not watched, so deleting the return changes nothing seen.
  - The pusher's drop guard. It clears the agent's mark when a pass ends without finishing: a failed store read, a panic, or its task dropped at shutdown. No test fakes any of those.
- **Doctor's Codex block and the reload clock** come in the next PR.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` and check-standards (exit 0) are clean. So is `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for bazhen-harness, bazhen-runtime-holder and bazhen-daemon.
- `cargo nextest run -p bazhen-harness -p bazhen-runtime-holder -p bazhen-daemon -p bazhen-store`: 1285 passed, on main with #526.
- New tests:
  - the holder tells a title change, and a lag once behind;
  - the runtime reads a title with its generation;
  - a starting Codex agent is recorded up once its terminal is titled with its thread, including a title set before its start was timed and one read again after a lag;
  - a title set by another process in the terminal records nothing;
  - a title its holder refused to read once is read again, and records the agent up;
  - an exited agent's terminal is no longer watched;
  - queued mail is pushed once the title says the agent is up;
  - queued mail is pushed oldest first;
  - mail sent while a push runs is pushed once each, in order;
  - nothing later is pushed once the harness can't take mail now.
- Each new test has a `Control:` trailer, and each Control failed on the test's own assertion 20 of 20 times, never on a timeout. The three mail Controls were proved again after the rebases onto #518, #522 and #526, and the other-process Control was proved again against the record's own generation check once the read's early check went.
- No test here signals a process, so nothing needs `moon run :test-real`.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"every-place"} -->
_Requested by **Aaron** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AEoV7qfAJWncyQcEpGWqQr?thread=cmsg_01AEoV7qfAJWncyQcEpGWqQr2ukXUJSfZ5TMMcSQzRx4md)_

## What this does

Moves recipe photos out of the database into a private Cloudflare R2 bucket, so the database stays small as families add photos.

- `recipekeeper/storage.py`: R2 client via the S3-compatible API (boto3). Turned on when `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `R2_BUCKET` are set; without them photos stay in the database as before (local use, tests).
- Uploads go to `households/<id>/photos/<random>.jpg`; the `photos` row keeps size, owner and the R2 key. Photos are still served through `/api/photos/<id>`, so they're only visible to their own household and the bucket stays private.
- `photos.storage_key` column, added automatically to existing databases at start-up.
- `scripts/move_photos_to_r2.py` moves photos already in the database into R2. The container runs it on every start (no-op once done, and never blocks start-up).
- R2 outages return a friendly 503 instead of a crash.
- `render.yaml` asks for the R2 values (bucket name defaults to `recipe-keeper-photos`); README has the Cloudflare setup steps and the free-tier terms.

## R2 cost

Free each month: 10 GB stored (Standard class), 1M writes, 10M reads, no egress fees ([pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/)). Photos are ~200–400 KB, so tens of thousands of photos fit. Cloudflare requires a payment method to turn R2 on.

## Testing

- `pytest`: 87 passed, including new `tests/test_storage.py` (R2 path with a fake store, household isolation, outage handling, old photos still readable, move script, column upgrade on an old database).
- The real boto3 client was exercised against moto's S3 mock (put/get/content type/delete). Not yet tested against a live R2 bucket.
- Start command run locally: move step prints a note without R2, server starts and `/api/health` answers.

The PostgreSQL restore integration failed because the seeded advertiser wallet had a $10,000 balance but no corresponding ledger entries. Restore verification correctly detected the resulting drift.

- **Migration:** Add ledger entries for nonzero advertiser balances that have no existing transaction history. Split large balances into supported transaction-sized entries.
- **Restore integration:** Update the expected Alembic head to the new migration revision.

```sql
-- Journal an opening balance only when no advertiser ledger history exists.
WHERE a.balance <> 0
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM transactions t WHERE t.advertiser_id = a.id
  )
```

body:
## Overview

The hub kept its own copy of which cards wait on the user, so a question
answered in the card note could still show as waiting, and only one
question per card could wait at a time. Questions now live only in a
card's Open Questions as numbered items such as
`Q4 asked 2026-11-25: text`, and the hub reads, lists and answers them
through the card command.

## Changes

- `card add` numbers each new Open Questions item, and `card show` and
  `card list --json` give every item with its Q number and date.
- A number is never reused on a card: answered questions keep their
  number in Decisions, and hand-typed items number past it, so a late
  reply cannot answer a newer question.
- `card edit KEY "Open Questions" Q3` picks an item by its Q number; a
  bare `3` still means the third item.
- `hub ask` adds a numbered item and refuses a question the card already
  asks; `hub answer KEY 3` or `Q3` moves that item and its answer to
  Decisions, and leaves the question open when that write fails.
- `hub waiting`, status, the brief and the stall alert list every open
  question with its reply key, such as `KEY Q3A`, and a session whose
  card has one shows as `flagged`.
- The hub's own question store and the needs-you mark are gone.
- The herdr-hub, auto-run, status-updates and herdr-handoff skills
  describe Q numbers and point to herdr-hub for card question rules. The
  skill check reports auto-run, herdr-handoff and status-updates as
  grown, each by the lines that replace the old one-question rule.

## Testing

On the branch tip, the hub suite and the kanban suite both pass (Rust:
344 passed; kanban: `150 passed`), with clippy and ruff clean. Putting
back each bug a review found made a test fail, except two the reviews
judged not worth a test.

author: marcodotio
body:
## Describe your changes

Faster streaming for 4.1, plus end-to-end and live API tests that exercise OpenAIKit the way apps use it. Still a draft while more 4.1 work lands.

**Streaming fixes**, found with Instruments' Time Profiler:
- **Each event was parsed twice.** A `JSONValue` pre-pass checked for an `error` key, then the event was decoded again. A byte-prefix check now replaces the pre-pass, and wrapped Assistants events are spliced as bytes.
- **Apple platforms read stream bodies one byte at a time** through `URLSession.AsyncBytes`. A shared delegate-based `URLSession` per transport now delivers chunks as they arrive, on Apple platforms and Linux.
- **The SSE parser built `String`s per line.** It now scans bytes, and `ServerSentEvent.dataBytes` carries event data without a `String` round trip.

Effect on a recorded ~700-word stream replayed locally:

| | 4.0.0 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat stream, delivered | 45.2 ms | **19.9 ms** |
| Chat stream, CPU | 103 ms | **59 ms** |
| Responses stream, delivered | 32.6 ms | **21.1 ms** |
| Responses stream, per-token latency at realistic pacing (p50) | 452 µs | **230 µs** |

**End-to-end tests (`Tests/OpenAIKitTests/EndToEnd/`).** Responses recorded from the live API are replayed by a local Network.framework server, so requests go through a real `URLSession` and real sockets.
- **Covered:** models, Chat Completions, Responses, float and base64 embeddings, chat and Responses streams (every chunk, in order, and the deltas match the final output), pacing (events arrive as they're sent, not buffered), early exit, `Task` cancellation, keep-alive connection reuse, 16 concurrent requests, and HTTP errors.
- **Fixtures:** in `Fixtures/Recorded/`, with account IDs and personal model names scrubbed and the embeddings trimmed to four vectors.
- **Linux:** the suite is compiled out, since the server needs Network.framework.

**Live API tests (`LiveAPITests.swift`).** These run only when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set, so CI stays offline: `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... swift test --filter LiveAPITests`. They cover Responses, both stream types, a tool-calling round trip, base64 embeddings and a Realtime session, and fail if the API sends event types the generated code doesn't know yet. All seven pass against the live API.

**Verified:** 70 tests pass on macOS, with the live tests skipped without a key, and 58 pass on Linux with Swift 6.2. All 7 live tests pass with a key. The generated sources are unchanged.

## Issue ticket number and link

None.

## Checklist before requesting a review
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] If it is a core feature, I have added thorough tests.
- [ ] Do we need to implement analytics? Not applicable.
- [x] Will this be part of a product update? If yes, please write one phrase about this update. Streaming in OpenAIKit 4.1 is 2.3× faster and uses about 40% less CPU.

author: tico-team-cloud[bot]
body:
## What changed and why

A board owner can now change their board without an Admin doing it for them, and everyone can see what changed. This is the server side of the spec plus the Edit pipeline page. The board's own pieces (owner in the board head, Rename in a column head, the Log on the web page) follow in a second task so each pull request reads in one sitting.

- **Who owns a board is the company owner's and Admins' choice.** `pipeline_settings.save` refuses an owner change from anyone else with "Only the company's owner and Admins choose who owns a board." (criterion 4). The pipeline record now has `may_choose_owner` so the page knows.
- **A board owner or manager who is a person and not an Admin cannot loosen a person's OK** on a stage unless the OK names them (criterion 5). It uses the same `_loosens_people_only` check bots already had, with an exception for the person the OK names. The whole save is refused, so nothing in it is kept.
- **The Log says what changed.** New `backend/pipeline_changes.py` turns the `changes` each `pipeline.save` already stored into words: "Cara renamed the stage Intake to Triage", "Ben made Cara the owner", "Cara changed the goal from A to B and 2 more changes". Each save line in `GET /pipelines/{id}/log` now has `version` and `changes` (the full list) (criteria 1 and 7, API part).
- **The owner and manager are told** with one notice each when someone else saves a change, with a link to the board. Whoever saved is not told, and neither is anyone for Tico's own saves. A bot's notice is quiet, so it starts no run (criterion 8).
- **Privacy is the company owner's and Admins'.** Making a board private or company-wide is refused for anyone else, its owner and manager included, even while it is empty: "Only the company's owner and Admins make a board private or company-wide."
- **Who a person's OK names stays put.** For a board owner or manager who is a person and not an Admin, changing who an OK names (one person, or a document approval's list) counts as loosening it, unless the OK names them.
- **Rule changes are in the Log too.** A person's change to a rule in force on a board, such as a stage's Late time, is recorded as a `pipeline.rule` event and shown in the board's Log ("Cara changed the Late time on Sign off from 24 h to 4 h"), and its owner and manager are told as for a save. A bot's rule change is only a suggestion, so it logs nothing until a person accepts it. Rule lines have no `version`: a rule does not change the pipeline's settings version.
- **Every Log line has its from and to.** A reorder says where each stage moved ("Sign off from 2 to 1, Intake from 1 to 2") and an approval change names each field ("who OKs from people only to people, with exceptions").
- **Edit pipeline page:** a new Owner field, read-only unless `may_choose_owner`. Someone who may not change the board reads "Only <owner> (owner), <manager> (manager) and Admins can change this board." (criterion 6, page part). When Owner is read-only, a save sends the stored owner (so Save mine after an Admin changed the owner still saves), and a refused save shows the server's reason first.
- A board with no owner works as before (criterion 9).

## Spec

Board owners rename stages and change board settings, v2 (Tico task "Board owners can rename stages and change board settings"). Follow-up task: "Board shows its owner, renames stages and shows its Log" (criteria 1 header, 2, 6 menu, 7 web).

## Demo steps

1. As the Acme owner, open Tasks, choose a pipeline, then ⋯, Edit pipeline. Set Owner to a member and save.
2. Sign in as that member and open Edit pipeline. Owner is read-only. Rename a stage and change a limit, then save: it holds after a reload.
3. Still as the member, remove a person's OK on a stage that names someone else: the save is refused and names the stage.
4. `tico pipeline log <pipeline>` shows "… renamed the stage X to Y" with version and the full list. The manager has a notice about the change.
5. As a member who is neither owner nor manager, open Edit pipeline: the page names who can change it.

## Risk

Medium. A board owner or manager who is a person and not an Admin is now refused a save that loosens a person's OK they are not named on, so their saves can be refused where before they passed. The refusal names the stage. Only the company owner and Admins now change a board's privacy, and a non-Admin owner or manager can no longer change who a person's OK names. A notice goes to the owner and manager on each save or rule change by someone else, so a busy board means more notices. Bots' notices are quiet.

## Review 1

Four findings, all taken (two of them about permissions; details are on the task). Three automated review comments, all taken.

## How you checked it

- `backend/tests/test_board_owner.py` (new): Admin-only owner choice, an owner's rename, limit and goal changes, the OK-loosening refusal with nothing kept and the named-person exception, no-owner behaviour as before, Log wording with version and full list, and the notices. On main these fail: main has no owner refusal, no `version` or `changes`, and no notice.
- Review fixes (`test_board_owner.py`): who an OK names (one person, and a document approval's list), Admin-only privacy both ways, a Late time change in the Log with notices, and reorder and approval lines with from and to. Each fails on the previous head.
- `web/src/features/tasks/PipelinePage.test.tsx`: 14 passed, including five new ones (two from review: the stored owner on Save mine, the server's reason on a refusal; both fail on the previous head) (an Admin sets Owner, read-only Owner for a non-Admin, the no-access line names owner and manager).
- Pre-push `scripts/check.sh` passed: lint, types (basedpyright), test imports, OpenAPI spec, wire contract.
- Hit every surface: API v2 and its spec (log line fields, `may_choose_owner`), the web app (Edit pipeline), and the CLI (`tico pipeline log` reads the new text). Who acts: a person and a bot (bot rules unchanged; bot notices quiet). Not changed: Slack, Tauri, runners, harnesses. Docs: no page names who may change a pipeline's owner. Demo mode: no new page.

- [x] Tests pass locally; new tests only guard a security or privacy boundary, data safety or a core contract
- [x] No credentials, real company names, people or domains (examples use Acme, `acme.example`)

_Requested by **Zack** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01S1FmouFqAR7siozpQNuuzA?thread=cmsg_01S1FmouFqAR7siozpQNuuzAHYLwXVDGXm5eiTLKBWN9nD)_

## What this fixes

`bwf deploy --preview` failed for the first pull request that adds a Durable Object class (DED-554). A real run showed two faults, so this PR has two changes:

1. **bwf's own check.** The preview build ran the live Worker's class-migration check with `atomic: false`, so it stopped with "needs an atomic deployment". A preview has its own Durable Objects and doesn't change the live migration tags, so the preview build now skips that check. Normal and `--atomic` deploys are unchanged.
2. **Cloudflare's refusal.** After change 1, Cloudflare rejected the preview upload: `[10061] Cannot create binding for class 'SecondDurableObject' that is not exported by script`. The build output has an `env` binding to each of the Worker's own classes. Cloudflare resolves it against the live script, which has no class the PR just added. (It also points at production's namespace, which is why a preview shared its owners' data through that binding.) The preview now leaves those bindings out. The classes stay in `exports`, so the preview reaches its own owners through `ctx.exports`, the pattern Cloudflare's Previews docs recommend. A binding to another Worker's class is kept.

One thing to know: in a preview, code that reads a Durable Object through `env.NAME` directly no longer finds it. bwf's `defineDurableObject` and `defineDurableState` use `ctx.exports` first, so they're not affected.

I also bumped the packages to 1.12.2, as the earlier preview PRs did.

## What was run and seen

A scratch bwf app (`bwf-scratch-preview-554`) with one Durable Object, on the real Cloudflare account:

- First deploy with bwf 1.12.1: deployed.
- Added a second Durable Object class, then `bwf deploy --platform cloudflare --preview pr-554` with bwf 1.12.1 (before the fix): failed, `needs an atomic Cloudflare deployment. Pending migration tags: platform-durable-first-v1, platform-durable-second-v1.`
- Same preview with the CLI built from the first commit of this branch: passed bwf's check, then failed with Cloudflare error 10061 (above).
- Same preview with the CLI built from this branch: deployed. `GET /api/hello` on the preview address returned `{"ok":true}`.
- `bwf deploy --platform cloudflare --remove-preview pr-554`: "Removed preview pr-554."
- Deleted the scratch Worker with `cf workers delete`. The address now returns 404 and it's not in the Worker list. No database or other resource was made.

Tests:

- `cloudflare-deploy.test.ts`: a build with `preview: true` skips the live check, and a normal build still stops with the atomic error. It fails without the fix.
- `cloudflare-preview.test.ts`: the staged preview drops a binding to the Worker's own class, keeps a binding to another Worker's class, and keeps `exports`.
- GitHub CI was green on the first commit. The 22 tests that failed in my cloud session pass when `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is unset (DED-562).

## Not run

- A preview that calls the new owner class through `ctx.exports` and checks it has its own data. The earlier scratch run (counter table in the infra notes) covered `ctx.exports` isolation, but not after this change. DED-561 covers it.
- Rollback past the preview's class (Cloudflare error 100402). It's a note for the docs, not changed here.

body:
## Summary
Wave 7C polish, stacked on Wave 7A (#407). Independent Neon review round 2 result: **CERTIFIED (BLOCKERS: 0)**. Rebased cleanly onto `master` @ `619b1202bd`; `git range-diff` shows both commits unchanged from the certified head `5e293de657`.

### 1. Clean Home close after a permanently refused recurring fire
- **Problem:** a recurring fire refused permanently (for example `UniqueValueTaken` on a duplicate id) left a wake that blocked `close_clean()` / `try_retire()` with `Unsupported(ConditionalRuntime)`.
- **Fix:** `conditional_operation/lifecycle/home_handoff.rs` now allows a wake that ended in `OperationTerminalFailure` or `OperationNoEffect` to close. Such a fire committed nothing and owes no cleanup.
  - Close still refuses while a durable continuation row governs the wake's key. This is checked through the new `QueryObligationHistory::retains_conditional_decision`.
  - The handoff's `.expect()` is also removed.
- **Court:** `on_fire::targeted` now retires the Home after the refused fire. On reopen, nothing partial landed and `fired_count` is unchanged.

### 2. Same-session `catch_up_temporal`
- **Problem:** a rule scheduled in the current session fired 0 times until the Home was closed and reopened.
- **Root cause:**
  - Authoritative deliveries bump the conditional node's output aspect by one per delivered change.
  - Query's fallback output version for a due wake was its Signal wake ordinal, which could equal that baseline.
  - Signal then classified the new occurrence as `ComputedRevertedClean` and suppressed it.
- **Fix, at the owner boundary:**
  - **Signal:** an eligible conditional's computation now receives the node's `output_version_before` through `SignalConditionalCompute`. A blanket impl keeps existing `|| ..` closures working. `SignalConditionalBaselineCompute` is the variant for callers that need the baseline.
  - **Bridge:** new `BridgeConditionalComputeProvider::compute_from_baseline`, which defaults to `compute`.
  - **Query:** new `QueryConditionalComputeContext::{exact, fresh}`. Due wakes and their reconsiderations are `fresh`: without a host output-version provider, their output is `before.checked_add(1)`, and the call refuses on exhaustion. Host providers always receive the true attempt. Producer readiness stays `exact`.
- **Courts:** `on_fire::same_session` and `on_fire::targeted` cover:
  - same-session firing;
  - firing across intervening commits;
  - two rules due together;
  - idempotency on repeat calls and after reopen.
- **Unit tests** cover the fresh, exact and host output versions.

### 3. `WorthQueryUserFacingRefusal` for `WorthQueryOperationCloseDenial`
- Exhaustive categories, `retryable()` and fixed end-user messages for close refusals, such as discarding a held command through `close_unexecuted`.
- Assertions are in `refusal_setup_court`.

### 4. Managed-index Source may be `live = whole_result`
- The declaration (`UnsupportedSourceShape`) and installation (`ManagedIndexSourceUnsupported`) gates now accept a whole-result live Source.
- Still refused, as before: keyed live causes, continuations, parameters, orbit and component selection, nested index selection, non-Public disclosure, and the parent-side laws.
- **Court:** in `sparse_index_dx::live_source`, one `#[derive(WorthQuery)]` backs both managed indexes and `session.subscribe_owned`. It stays accurate across edits and reopen.

`docs/capability-index.md` is updated for all four.

## Verification (local, on the rebased head)
- `git diff --check`, rustfmt `--check`, `check_workspace_rust_line_caps.sh workspace`, `agent-context check`, `boundary-check`, `check_relational_dag.py`: all clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: green for worth-query, plus `worth-signal`, `worth-runtime-bridge` and `worth-court-signal-owner-services`. Before the rebase it was also green for worth-query-bank-world and `worth-signal-wasm`.
- Courts:
  - `worth-query-court-execution-primary-graph-application-contribution -- conditional_operation`: 14/14.
  - `worth-query-host` doctests: 62 + 166.
  - `worth-query-court-decl-host-macros`: 77/82. All W7C courts pass.
- Before the rebase:
  - macros 82/82, single-source 26/26;
  - Signal conditional unit tests 115/115, Bridge conditional unit tests 79/79;
  - integration `temporal` and `application_home`: all green; one load-induced child-writer timeout passed when rerun serially.

### Known master regression (not from this PR)
5 Wave 7A courts fail identically on bare `master` @ `619b1202bd`, without this PR:
- `unified_hard_dx::durable_history_court`, 3 tests;
- `unified_hard_dx::option_preimage_court`, 2 tests.

They fail at `correction_history(..).unwrap()` with `History(ExactHistory(Denied(History(RetiredHistoryGap))))`. They passed on the Wave 7A branch before it was squashed onto the newer master, so the cause appears to be an interaction between #407 and changes that landed on master before it.

author: jeremeybingham
body:
Closes #89.

## What changes

- **Separate worker pool.** `sync --media` / `serve --media` no longer download inside the page loop. Each page's new and changed files are queued, and `[server.media] workers` (default 4) fetch them under the `[server.media]` rate limits while the record sync keeps pulling pages. The run ends once the queue is empty. A key seen on several pages before its download starts is queued once.
- **Streaming, no local copy.** `reso-client` gains `Downloader::download_into` and a `DownloadTarget` trait (`start`/`write`/`finish`/`abort`). `download_to` is now a file target on top of it. Media streams into a new `MediaStore` (`LocalMediaStore`, or `S3MediaStore` with feature `s3`).
- **Skip unchanged, store once.** Files are named `<sha256>.<ext>`, and the index maps `MediaKey` to that file. The timestamp rule and the 304 validators work as before. Beyond that, a changed record whose bytes are the same counts as `unchanged`, and the same photo under another key counts as `shared` and is not stored again. A file no key points at any more is deleted.
- **Buckets.** With `--s3-bucket`/`--gcs-bucket`, files go to `<prefix>/media/<server>/`, and `purge` lists and deletes them there.
- **Metrics.**
  - The metrics file gets `reso_ingest_last_run_media_files{server,outcome}` (downloaded, unchanged, shared, not_modified, failed, expired, deleted), plus `_media_bytes`, `reso_ingest_media_pending` and `reso_ingest_media_index_ok`.
  - `serve /metrics` shows running totals per feed: `reso_ingest_media_files_total` and `reso_ingest_media_bytes_total`.
  - The summary line also shows unchanged, shared and expired counts.

## Done-when test

`reso-ingest/tests/media_scale_tests.rs`:
- 400 media records, a quarter of them repeating a photo: 400 fetches, 300 files stored.
- The same records again: nothing queued or fetched.
- 40 changed records: 40 fetches, 20 counted unchanged by hash, 20 new. Only the files a record points at are kept.
- A slow file host (400 ms per file, 2 workers, 200 files): ten pages are taken in in under 400 ms, and what wasn't fetched stays pending in the index.
- 403 URLs count as expired and stay pending.

`s3_tests.rs` adds a `sync --media` into the fake bucket (dedupe, nothing on local disk) followed by `purge` of the bucket media.

## Decisions I made (please overrule if wrong)

1. **Content-addressed names** (`<sha256>.<ext>`) instead of `<MediaKey>.<ext>`. Files from earlier versions are not renamed; they are fetched again under their hash when their record next changes.
2. **Dedupe is per server**, not across servers (each server has its own `media/<server>/` folder, which keeps `purge` simple).
3. **Default 4 workers per server.** The queue is unbounded (it holds keys only), and the run waits for it to drain before it ends.
4. **Bucket uploads**: up to 8 MiB is buffered in memory and created with one conditional `PUT`. Larger files go up as multipart to a `.part-*` staging name, are copied to the final name, and the staging object is deleted. Locally, the final name is created with a hard link, which fails if the name already exists, so two workers storing the same content cannot both store it.
5. **401, 403 and 410 from the file host count as `expired`.** They are also counted in `failed`.
6. **With a bucket, `--media-dir` is ignored.** The `media` command still refuses a bucket (unchanged).
7. **`serve` reports media as counters since start**, per feed. The `sync` metrics file reports the last run's gauges, per server.

## Breaking (reso-ingest, unpublished)

- `MediaReport` gains `queued`, `unchanged`, `shared` and `expired`. `MediaEntry` gains `sha256`.
- `PageMedia` has no lifetime and no `new`/`finish`; use `page_pipeline`.
- `sync_media` takes the worker count, and `MediaConfig` gains `workers`.
- `ServeOptions.media_dir` became `media: Option<MediaRoot>`.
- `plan_purge` and `execute_purge` take `&dyn MediaStore`, and `PurgePlan.media_dir` became `media`.
- `write_metrics_file` takes the media reports.

`reso-client` only adds API (`DownloadTarget`, `download_into`).

## Not done / follow-ups

- The media index is still one JSON object rewritten after every page (and every 50 files). That is fine for thousands of files and too slow for tens of millions. It is worth its own issue.
- The `media` command does not use leases or stop cleanly on a signal (unchanged).

## Unconfirmed against a real server (#32)

Everything here was tested offline only (wiremock, the in-process S3 fake, `object_store`'s in-memory store). Not yet checked:
- a vendor's file host: signed URLs expiring mid-queue, media rate limits, real volumes;
- multipart upload plus copy against real S3/GCS.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, with and without `--features reso-ingest/s3,reso-ingest/parquet`.
- `cargo test --workspace`: all pass, with and without those features.
- `cargo doc --no-deps -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the MSRV (1.87) check. The lockfile already pulls in dependencies that need 1.88 or newer (`icu_*`, `arrow-*`, `crc-fast`), so `cargo +1.87.0 check` fails in dependencies before it reaches this code. That was already the case before this PR.

body:
## Summary

This is the first Stage S3 batch: every propositional row of `nat.pdf` (自然変換・関手圏) and `comma.pdf` (コンマ圏) is now verified in Lean, in the source's own formulation.

| Ledger | Verified | Non-propositional | Module |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1-NAT | 22 / 23 rows | 例 1 (type-checked by an `example`) | `ProjectEpisteme/Category/AlgD/C1/Nat.lean` |
| C1-COMMA | 9 / 10 rows | 例 4 (Graph, informal) | `ProjectEpisteme/Category/AlgD/C1/Comma.lean` |

Verified items in Chapters 0–2 go from 12 to **43**: 29 numbered items and 14 definitions or prose claims.

### Isomorphisms of categories

The source writes `≅` for an isomorphism of categories, which is stricter than an equivalence (it writes `≃` for that). Those rows are stated with mathlib's `IsoCat` / `Functor.IsIso`: the comparison functor is full, faithful, and bijective on objects. They are not stated as equivalences. The rows are:

- NAT 例 5: `C^0 ≅ 1` and `C^1 ≅ C`
- NAT 例 6: `Set^M ≅ M-sets`
- NAT 例 7: `C^{a,b} ≅ C × C`
- NAT 例 12: `C^2` is the arrow category
- NAT 例 13: `P(X) ≅ 2^X`, compatible with preimages
- COMMA 例 1–3, 例 5 (category of elements), and 命題 6

The first catalog pass said mathlib had no isomorphism of categories, which was wrong: `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/IsoCat.lean` provides it. The coverage report is corrected.

### Library layer (new, candidates for upstreaming)

- `Category/Basic/FunctorCategory.lean`: `Functor.IsIso` instances for the functor categories above. This adds `Discrete.evalPair`, `ComposableArrows.toArrow`, and `Set.characteristicFunctor`.
- `Category/Basic/Comma.lean`: `Comma.liftFunctor`, the functor in the strict universal property. mathlib has only `MorphismProperty.Comma.lift` and the special cases for (co)structured arrows.
- `Category/Basic/Elements.lean`: `Functor.Elements.toCostructuredArrow` is an isomorphism of categories.

### Points to review

- **COMMA 命題 7** keeps the source's strict equalities `P₀ ∘ H = Q₀` and `P₁ ∘ H = Q₁`. Condition (2), `κH = θ`, is stated through those equalities with `eqToHom`.
- **NAT 例 4**: the source writes the rightmost component as (θ_F ∘ Fσ)_a, which is a typo. The Lean statement uses θ_G ∘ Fσ.
- **Modelling choices:**
  - {a, b} is `Discrete Bool`.
  - 2 = {0 → 1} is `Fin 2`.
  - P(X) is `Set X` ordered by ⊆.
  - COMMA 例 5 reads mathlib's `P.Elements` as the source's 1 ↓ P in its pair presentation.

### Not in this pull request

The other 10 Chapter 0–1 ledgers. LIMIT and ADJOINT come next.

## Test plan

- [x] `lake build --wfail ProjectEpisteme`. This includes the per-item axiom guards: every new declaration depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`, and `comma_category` needs only `propext` and `Quot.sound`.
- [x] `lake exe mk_all --check --lib ProjectEpisteme`
- [x] `checks/run.sh`: AxiomAudit, ForbiddenOptions, and LedgerDeclarations, with 43 declarations.
- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s checks/tests` and `python3 checks/ledger.py`
- [ ] CI on this pull request
- [ ] Mathematical review of the statement choices above

### Multi-project & pricing integrity
- `saveMeasurement()` now resolves `_uiState.value.projectId ?: ensureDefaultProject()`, so AR and manual captures from a second project no longer land in the default project (and in-place replacement in project #2 works).
- `createProject()` keeps its `"<name> created."` confirmation instead of having `bootstrap()` clear it.
- `deleteProject()` switches the workspace observer to the fallback project *before* deleting, so no transient "The project could not be found." flashes.
- `applyOverrides()` / `applyOverridesSafely()` clear `customWasteFactor` whenever a non-`CUSTOM` preset is selected — a catalog material's custom waste factor can no longer silently defeat a surface preset.
- Corrupt `CutoutEntity.kind` rows degrade to a per-surface `loadErrors` entry instead of throwing out of the workspace `Flow`.
- `updateSurfaceSettings()` validates the preset name against `WastePreset`.
- Money formatting uses a per-thread `NumberFormat` cache; `surfaceId` is `Uri.encode`d for navigation; the PDF share intent is guarded against `ActivityNotFoundException`.

### AR permission & session lifecycle
- Runtime `CAMERA` permission via `ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission`, with a distinct *permanently denied → Open Android settings* path.
- `ARScene` only mounts when `hasCameraPermission && readiness == READY && sessionErrorMessage == null`.
- Bounded polling (250 ms x 10) while ARCore reports `UNKNOWN_CHECKING` / `TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `ON_RESUME` re-evaluates permission + readiness, clears a resolved `CAMERA_PERMISSION` / `INSTALL_REQUIRED` block and restarts the session.
- `RetrySession` also recovers from a terminal error, and advancing `sessionGeneration` calls `renderer.clear(nodes)`.

### Tracking & R8
- `ReticleHitTester.validateAgainstLock()` compares the real hit normal, so a plane hit that drifted onto an adjacent surface is genuinely rejected.
- `proguard-rules.pro` keeps every name-persisted enum and serialization DTO. Verified in `mapping.txt`: `CutoutKind.DOOR` and friends stay unrenamed after R8.

author: legato-cpave3[bot]
body:
Ticket: [LEG-592](https://burnlite.dev/LEG-592), Stop watching, Watch again, End, the re-entry budget and the idle end. Part of the spec [LEG-559](https://burnlite.dev/LEG-559).

- **Re-entry budget (AC 33):** a push past `max_reentries` (5 by default) makes the loop stuck at its watch. No pass starts, no new agent is started, and the approval stands. Watch again allows exactly one more re-entry.
- **Stop watching (AC 34):** it holds the steward. Nothing is sent, posted or started, but a closed PR and idleness still end the loop. It is offered only while the steward watches an approved PR.
- **Watch again:** pushes made while the steward was held re-enter once, and items found while held are sent then.
- **End:** on any stewarded loop, it gives the outcome `ended`. The pass, wait and confirm steps waiting on that loop now finish instead of waiting forever.
- **Idle (AC 35):** seven quiet days give `idle`. The deadline moves on when a watch read finds changed layers or comments.
- **The actions:** `stop_watching`, `watch_again` and `end`, through the existing step-action route.

**Not in this PR (recorded on LEG-559):**
- Stop watching and Watch again on the host CLI, `review-pass --loop`. The actions work through the run's step action route. A follow-up is suggested for LEG-593/594.
- The End confirmation's wording for a steward ("End the review loop as stuck?") belongs to LEG-593.
- A merge while held is handled by #413 (LEG-591).

**Tests:** `internal/handofftest/review_steward_held_test.go`.

**Docs:** `docs/ai/integrations.md`, `docs/ai/workflows.md`, the site page `using/review-passes`, and GLOSSARY (Held).
