author: yang-dong-yd
body:
## Summary

Add the activation page: read the device license record (`0x2F`) and run the online activation flow (`0x3F`) for arms that ship unactivated. The client is ported from studio, so the two sides share one contract for the license file, registration validation, service errors, and the internal test channel.

An unactivated arm refuses `enable` with `ERR{0x10,0x08}`; until now the tool had no way to activate it.

## Changes

- Add `litetool/activation.py`: license parsing, registration validation, service request/error mapping, internal channel token. Stdlib only; this is the tool's only outbound network point.
- Add `litetool/license_io.py`: `0x2F` record shape (three-state `supported`) and `0x3F` write with read-back; `ERR{0x3F,0x02}` counts as success only when the read-back shows activated.
- Add the Activation page (Parameters group): record display with copyable UID, registration form, consent text/version, and actionable messages for unactivated / already activated / old firmware / enabled device / network errors.
- Run the flow in two stages: read the UID on the SDK owner thread, POST on a page-owned thread (never blocks the serial owner), then write and read back on the owner thread.
- Add `--activation-url` (also `LITEARM_ACTIVATION_URL`); the tool reads the studio token config as a fallback for internal testers.
- Update README/docs and add tests.

## Review follow-ups

A local review against studio's contract and behavior surfaced these mismatches; they are fixed on this branch:

- `diagnostics` now uses the service's `studio`/`sdk`/`firmware` keys (the value is `litearm-tool <version>`); the previous `tool` key was silently dropped by the service schema.
- The page shows studio's `draft-4` Activation Registration Consent document (four itemized items with purposes, privacy link), not a one-paragraph summary under the same version.
- Success is reported only when the read-back confirms `supported && activated`; an ACK with an unconfirmed or negative read-back is a warning.
- A failed re-read keeps the last record and marks it as the previous reading; disconnect clears it. Async read/network/write results from a previous link are discarded.
- The page reads the record on connect and shows the link state in its header.
- The submit button follows studio's `canSubmitActivation` gate (record present and unactivated, consent checked, arm disarmed, form valid); its tooltip names the missing condition.
- `not_found`, `invalid_request`, `invalid_uid` and `code_required` map to actionable text; pre-1.8.0 firmware is told to upgrade.
- The internal test channel also honors studio's `LITEARM_STUDIO_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL_CONFIG`.
- `--activation-url` with no value no longer swallows the following Qt argument.

## Testing

- `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python -m pytest -q` → **484 passed, 12 skipped**; also run on Python 3.12 (the CI version) with the same result.
- `test_activation.py`: license parsing, registration validation, service-error mapping, channel token resolution (including studio's config override); no network.
- `test_activation_page.py`: record states, stale record across a failed re-read, disconnect clearing, consent document, submit-button gating, enabled-device gate, success path with a fake arm, `0x02` read-back verdict, unconfirmed read-back warning, `not_found` mapping, connect auto-read and the connection epoch guard.
- `test_app_flags.py`: `--activation-url` parsing (`--x value`, `--x=value`, missing value).
- Additional local verification (not in the suite): a real HTTP round-trip against a local stub of `POST /api/v1/license`; the full page flow through `MainWindow` + the real `SdkWorker` thread with a fake arm; and the service's own `licenseRequestSchema` (vitest) accepts the tool's request and preserves `diagnostics.studio`.
- Not yet verified: a real submission against `act.nexform.tech` and a real unactivated arm (needs hardware plus a test credential).

author: rajivmucheli
body:
## Problems

### 1. Shell syntax error with special-character passwords
`pscp -pw` and `plink -pw` received the password as an unquoted shell word. Passwords containing metacharacters (`(`, `)`, `|`, `&`, `\`, etc.) cause bash to abort with a syntax error before the script runs:
```
/scripts/barbican_lunaclient.sh: line 44: syntax error near unexpected token `)'
```

### 2. Init container fails on pod restart
Line 9 runs `mv /usr/safenet /thales` unconditionally. On pod restart the target `/thales/safenet` already exists (from the first run), so `mv` fails with:
```
mv: inter-device move failed: '/usr/safenet' to '/thales/safenet'; unable to remove target: Directory not empty
```

## Fixes

**Password quoting** — wrap all 6 `-pw` arguments in single quotes (HSM1 + HSM2 × pscp/pscp/plink):
```bash
# before
pscp -pw {{ password }} ...
# after
pscp -pw '{{ password }}' ...
```

**mv idempotency** — guard the move so it only runs on first init:
```bash
# before
mv /usr/safenet /thales
# after
[ -d /thales/safenet ] || mv /usr/safenet /thales
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Deploy barbican with a password containing `(`, `)`, `|`, `&` — `lunaclient` init must complete without syntax errors
- [ ] Delete the pod and verify it restarts cleanly (no `mv` failure on second run)
- [ ] HA path (`hsm.ha.enabled=true`) covers HSM2 registration lines

body:
The `TransformEditor` class docstring documents its second parameter as
`frame`; `__init__` takes `base_frame`. One line.

The entry's own description already reads "Name of the base frame", and
`base_frame` appears 14 times in the file, so this is just the name.

### What I checked

An AST pass confirms `TransformEditor.__init__` has `base_frame` in
`posonlyargs + args + kwonlyargs`, does not have `frame`, and takes no `*args`
or `**kwargs`. The entry lives in the class docstring rather than `__init__`'s,
so I bound the edit to that node's own span. After the change the same pass
confirms the class documents `base_frame` and no bare `frame` entry remains.
`ruff check` reports an identical finding set before and after, the line is 27

not run the test suite: this is docstring text with no code path touched.

`assert_exponential_coordinates_equal(Stheta1, Stheta2)` in
`transformations/_screws.py` documents:

```
kwargs : dict
    Positional arguments that will be passed to `assert_array_almost_equal`
```

author: tiosos
body:
## Summary

Implements **Stage S7** from `ui-redesign/DESIGN-SIGNOFF.md` §13: the accessibility and keyboard audit for NFR-03. Stage S6 was checked first and found already complete — all five §9 additional workspaces are present in `main` with engines, UI and tests — so no duplicate S6 PR was opened.

## What changed

- **Dialog keyboard ownership** — global workbench shortcuts (F/C/J/L/M/B/T, H, Delete, Ctrl+Z/S/O/N/D) are now suppressed whenever a native `<dialog>` or `role="dialog"` is open. Escape remains with the dialog's own handler.
- **Nonmodal workspace focus** — the four workspaces (Door & Drawer Motion, Front Grain Matching, Stock Optimisation, Sloped-Top Cabinets) now focus their panel on open and restore the opener on close via `usePanelFocus`. They intentionally remain complementary regions and do **not** trap Tab, so the viewport stays reachable per §9.1.
- **Visible focus** — added a global `:focus-visible` ring plus explicit styles for every custom `.zim-*` control and treeitem; removed the bare `outline-none` on the FileMenu project-name input.
- **Light/dark capability** — added an opt-in `html[data-theme='light']` token set while keeping the dark palette as default, so NFR-03's two-theme requirement is testable without changing existing views.
- **Contrast** — replaced low-opacity 8–11px text (perspective numbers, tool keys, cabinet tab numbers, mode class labels, FileMenu hints) with AA-compliant muted-foreground tokens; light-theme destructive/muted tokens were darkened.
- **Single-tab-stop trees** — the sixteen cabinet tabs and the Project & Room hierarchy now use roving tabindex with Arrow/Home/End navigation; Enter on a project row reaches its inline editor. `navigateTree` and the new behaviour are documented in `docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md`.
- **Automated coverage** — new `e2e/accessibility-audit.spec.ts` verifies dialog focus trap/restore, shortcut suppression, both roving trees, visible focus ring, and AA body contrast in both themes. Unit tests cover `hasOpenDialog` and `usePanelFocus`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run check:file-casing`, `npm run build` — pass
- Unit tests in a clean checkout — **260 files, 4609 passed, 10 skipped** (was 260 / 4607)
- CI-mode e2e — **125 passed, 1 flaky, 0 failed**; the flaky test is the pre-existing `production-packet-comparison` order/content check
- All source and docs changes are English-only.

## Note

An intermediate iteration gave the nonmodal workspaces `role="dialog"`, which broke their complementary semantics and existing e2e selectors. That was caught by the full e2e run and reverted to panel focus/restore only; the final suite is green.

body: ## Summary Oilers Trivia is a new page at `trivia.html`, linked next to AirHockey in the More menu and on the home-page play card. Players sign up the same way they do for AirHockey: a username, a device token kept in this browser, and a one-time recovery code. Trivia accounts are stored separately, so rink ratings are unchanged. - **Practice** is a 10-question run you can start anytime. Quick duel waits 8 seconds for another player, then drops into practice if nobody is there. - **Head-to-head** uses the same quick queue and room code as AirHockey (`trivia.html?room=CODE`). Both players get the same 10 questions on a server clock. The higher score wins. A tie stays a tie. If the other seat never checks in within 40 seconds, it is a forfeit. - **Scoring** is 100 for a correct answer, plus up to 50 for time left on the 15-second clock, plus 15 for each correct answer already on the streak (capped at five). A miss is 0 and the streak resets. The reveal shows that split and a short fact. - **Leaderboard** keeps total points, duel wins/losses/ties, accuracy, best streak, and best solo score. The bank has 87 checked questions across History, Franchise Records, Legends, Modern Era, and By the Numbers. Finished events follow `data/history.json` and NHL records. Three questions are dated to the Nov. 24, 2026 McDavid Chase log in `data/mcdavid.json`, so a later game does not make them false. No Oilers or NHL logos were added. `CNAME`, `/players.html`, and `/game.html?id=` are unchanged. `AIRHOCKEY_REG_SEC` and `AIRHOCKEY_OT_SEC` are untouched. The service worker cache is `cbn-v55`. [Question on a phone](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-36918c15-7b9f-5041-8148-c3038f323a2d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Ftrivia-question-mobile.png) [Score and fact after an answer](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-36918c15-7b9f-5041-8148-c3038f323a2d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Ftrivia-reveal-mobile.png) ## Worker deploy GitHub Pages does not deploy `worker/`. From `worker/`: ```bash npx wrangler deploy ``` Wrangler 4 reconciles new SQLite Durable Object exports without a migration tag. This creates `TriviaLobby` and `TriviaMatch` and leaves `GameAlerts`, `AirHockeyLobby`, and `AirHockeyMatch` alone. No new KV namespace, no new secret, and no paid product. Until that deploy, the page loads and the buttons say trivia is not set up. Local check: `npx wrangler dev --port 8787`, then open `trivia.html?api=http://127.0.0.1:8787` from a static server. `npm test` covers the bank, scoring, a solo run, quick match, a room, and a duel recorded on the leaderboard once. This is by an automated agent, not a human.

## Summary

Adds inferred intake for unaddressed content in GitLab's own-account mode:

- a mention or assignment of the monitored account remains an **explicit** request;
- unmentioned Issues, merge requests and comments are now observed and delivered as human Triggers without addressed metadata;
- the admission table therefore admits a listed sender as an **inferred candidate**, which goes through assessment, rather than ignoring it;
- the admission rows expose the unaddressed cells while **The account belongs to the person using the agent** is on;
- marked agent output and self-authored MRs on open Ticket branches stay out of intake.

An inferred candidate needs an accept mode other than `off`; `observe` assesses and records a would-accept, and `auto` may accept on matched rules. The sender must still be on the Source's allowed list. No new configuration switch is added.

body:
## 🔍 Background

| Reference | Link |
|---|---|
| PRD | `docs/product/PRD - Journal d'activité.md` |
| Legal | `docs/LEGAL.md §11` |
| ADR / DDR | `docs/adr/ADR-013-centralised-journal.md` |

EP-017 S01/S02/S03 ont livré la table `activity_log`, l'émission aux points de mutation et les endpoints `GET …/timeline` (#171). Cette PR livre les trois stories restantes : les deux vues qui consomment la frise (S04, S05) et le filtrage par rôle des actions sensibles (S06) — l'épic est clos.

---

## 📦 Backlog

- **Epic** `EP-017` — Journal d'activité & Suivi de cycle de vie
  - `EP-017-S04` ⏳ → ✅ — Frontend : vue `TaskTimelineView` (timeline événementielle réelle)
  - `EP-017-S05` ⏳ → ✅ — Frontend : vue `ReportDetailView` + lien contextuel vers la tâche
  - `EP-017-S06` ⏳ → ✅ — Visibilité : actions sensibles réservées manager / conseil syndical

## 🛠️ Implementation

- **S06 (backend)** : `domain::activity_visibility::can_view_action` — allow-list fermée (`assignee_changed`, `vendor_link_generated` réservées à `manager`/`board_member`, tout le reste visible, action inconnue visible par défaut). Filtre appliqué **en mémoire** dans les deux handlers timeline (`tasks` + `reports`), après `list_for_chain` et avant la sérialisation/masquage d'anonymat : la règle reste en domaine, testable unitairement, zéro SQL. Les événements filtrés sont omis, pas remplacés — la frise résident reste cohérente (statuts et clôture visibles).
- **S04 (frontend)** : `TaskDetailView.vue` → `TaskTimelineView.vue`. Le computed local qui reconstruisait des étapes (dont des étapes non datées) est supprimé ; la frise vient exclusivement de `tasksApi.timeline` avec états chargement / erreur localisée (la fiche statique reste affichée) / vide (`200 []` pour les tâches antérieures à EP-017). Nouveau composant catalogue `CTimelineList` (`components/molecules/`, documenté dans `docs/DESIGN.md §3.2`) : pastille par action, libellé i18n `timeline.actions.*`, acteur (`actor_name`, « Prestataire externe » quand null sur la soumission vendeur), détail lu dans le `payload` (transition de statut avec libellés existants, nom de fichier, expiration, « issue du signalement »), badge « Signalement » sur les événements `entity_type === 'report'`, lien vers la tâche sur `converted_to_task`, action inconnue → rendu générique sans crash. Tailwind/tokens uniquement, pas de `<style>`.
- **S05 (frontend)** : nouvelle route `reports/:id` (`report-detail`, tous rôles — même règle que la liste) et vue `ReportDetailView` : fiche statique (statut, auteur — masquage anonymat réutilisé, lot, date), encart « Converti en tâche » avec badge de statut si `task_id`, **lien actif uniquement pour les rôles qui peuvent ouvrir `tasks/:id`** (`usePermissions.canManageTask`), timeline partagée `CTimelineList` (chaîne signalement + tâche). 404 → retour à la liste. Les cartes de `ReportsView` mènent au détail ; `authorLabel`/`statusVariant` extraits dans `useReportLabels` (déduplication entre liste et détail).
- **E2E** : routes `reports/:id` et `tasks/:id` ajoutées à `access-matrix` (smoke rôles + captures dérivées) ; spec `tests/actions/reports-actions.spec.ts` — résident : frise + encart conversion sans lien ; manager : lien suivi jusqu'à la timeline de la tâche (chaîne créée via l'API, aucune dépendance aux données seedées).

author: aaroncoville
body:
## Problem

Writes to the task ledger now take a lock, and the app waits at most 250 ms for it, because its writes run on the main thread. So a ledger write can now fail: the ledger is busy, the ledger is corrupt, or the filesystem refuses the write. The task IPC handlers return `{ ok: false, error }`, but no window showed that error.

The worst case is on the Ask Me board. An answer that was never saved looked exactly like one that was. Promoting a Slack message to a card ignored the result entirely, so the card could silently never be created.

Separately, on filesystems without hard links, every ledger write failed: `linkSync` throws on exFAT, FAT and some network shares, and the lock is taken with a hard link.

This PR is stacked on #139.

## Change

1. **Retry a busy ledger off the main thread** (`990be1e3`). The three task IPC handlers are now async. When the ledger is busy (`TaskLedgerLockTimeout` only), they pause 50, 100, 200, 400 and 800 ms between attempts. Each attempt keeps the short synchronous wait, so a busy ledger gets about 3 s in all. Other errors are answered at once.
2. **Show the error and keep the user's input** (`c2b8ee4f`, `ac112629`, `7daa9943`, `2e3262a6`).
   - Ask Me uses its existing notice line.
   - The task board and task detail use one store field, `taskWriteError`, shown in the same coral line style. It clears when a later write succeeds. No new components were added.
3. **Slack promotion reports failure** (`a4018579` refactor only, then `a51061e0`). The promotion is moved into its own module with no behaviour change, then a failed promotion is logged and shown on the task board.
4. **Filesystems without hard links.** No fallback: the lock PR now fails closed, and this PR shows that error in the window (see Round 4).
5. **Stale comments** (`4d1cdd9d`). Four comments described the removed `writeTasks`.

New strings are in `en`, `ar` and `zh-CN`. `en-SH` falls back to English, as it already does elsewhere.

## What the user sees

| Path | Busy ledger, after retries | Other failed write |
|---|---|---|
| Ask Me answer | Retried for about 3 s. Then the notice line reads: *Your answer on "<title>" was not saved, and is still in the box: <reason, naming the lock holder>*. The draft and images are kept, and the agent is not told. | The same line with the reason (for example *tasks.json is not valid JSON…*). Not retried. |
| Ask Me dismiss | Retried. Then the card comes back with *"<title>" was not dismissed: <reason>*. | Same, not retried. |
| Task status move (detail) | Retried. Then the card snaps back, with *"<title>" was not moved: <reason>* under the title. | Same, not retried. |
| Task board dismiss | Retried. Then the card comes back, with *"<title>" was not removed: <reason>* above the columns. | Same, not retried. |
| Slack promote | Retried by the handler. Then a warning is logged, and the task board shows *The Slack message "<title>" was not added to the board, so its thread will not get a reply when the work is done: <reason>*. | Same, not retried. Dispatching the work is unaffected. |
| Webhook (unchanged) | No retry: it runs on the main thread with the 250 ms wait. The error is logged and no card is made. An operator-approved webhook stays pending, so it can be approved again. | Same. |
| Voice (unchanged) | No retry. Spoken: *That action failed: could not lock … held by …*. | Spoken: *That action failed: <reason>*. |

## Limits

- **Not checked in the running app.** The new lines were not checked in the running Electron app. To see them, hold `tasks.json.lock` for more than 3 s and try each action.

## Acceptance checks

Head `7bbcd808`, based on #139's head `a193c9b6`. For each fix, the test failed first, and removing the fix turns it red again:

| Fix | Failing test first | Reverting the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Retry | 5 of 9 failed (the retry did not exist) | Without the retry, 3 of 9 fail |
| Error shown on each window path | Ask Me answer and dismiss, task board, task detail and Slack each failed with no reason on screen | Removing that path's notify call fails its test; hiding the detail `notice` fails too |

- `npm run typecheck`: 0 errors (node and web).
- `npm run test:focused`: **3623 of 3626** pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped. That is #139's 3606 of 3609 plus 17 new tests.
- `npm run build` succeeds, and `slackCardNotSaved` is in the renderer bundle.

Tested on macOS.

## Round 3 (head `556658cc`, restacked on the CLI PR's `5e5803de`)

| Finding | Commit | Test |
|---|---|---|
| A busy-retried edit could land after a later edit to the same card | `192f4c06` | `task-ledger-result`: a busy write cannot land after a later write; a failing or rejecting write does not stop the queue |
| The Ask Me dismiss line was not cleared after a later success | `bb10d163` | `ask-me-write-failure` |
| No test that the detail view clears its line | `135c3cd4` | `task-detail-write-failure` |
| The board's shared error line leaked into the detail view and could stick | `9ef83ef7`, `6eb0dd4e` | `task-detail-write-failure`, `kanban-write-failure`: the detail view keeps its own line, and the board's line gets a close button |
| A failed dismissal was reported as an "answer" | `d6c1c4a8` | `ask-me-write-failure` |
| A card stayed hidden for up to 5 s when the delete call threw | `791df8b8` | `kanban-write-failure` |
| A comment overstated what the no-hard-link fallback guarantees | `556658cc` | comment only |

**What changed in behaviour.**

- **One queue for task edits.** Task edits from the window now go through a single queue. While the ledger is busy, a later edit waits for the earlier one, up to about 1.5 s.
- **New strings.** `kanban.closeNotice` and `askMe.cardChangedBeforeDismissal` are added in en, ar and zh-CN.

**Skipped.** A failed edit can still make up to six 250 ms synchronous waits on the main thread. Fixing that means making the lock wait asynchronous, which is a design change.

Typecheck reports 0 errors. The suite passes **3639 of 3642** (0 fail, 3 skipped), and the build succeeds.

## Round 4 (head `7aea33b3`, restacked on the CLI PR's `c74e9a7f`)

**The no-hard-link fallback is removed** (its commits `4bc1923e` and `556658cc` are dropped).

- **Why:** with the fallback in place, a newer lock that was moved aside by mistake could not be put back, because putting it back also needs a hard link. That could lose cards, and a reviewer reproduced the loss.
- **What happens instead:** the app is Mac-only and runs on a local APFS volume, which supports hard links. On a volume without them, ledger writes now fail closed in the lock PR. This PR shows the reason on the window's error line.

| Finding | Commit | Test |
|---|---|---|
| The no-hard-link error reaches the window | `7aea33b3` | When the link is refused, the result is `ok: false` with the reason. There is no retry, one log line, and `tasks.json` is byte-identical |
| The edit queue was unbounded, and edits behind a failed one each waited about 3 s | `dc8569e9` | Edits queued behind one that gave up fail at once with the same error. At most 50 are held, and extras are answered busy at once. The queue accepts edits again once it drains |
| The detail view's own line was untested | `d03c3aa6` | The board's line and the detail's line never show in, or replace, each other |

**Checks:** typecheck shows 0 errors, the suite passes **3647 of 3650** (0 fail, 3 skipped), and the build succeeds.

author: chhwang
body:
`MyProxyService` appends a null entry for the local rank before it appends any peer semaphores. The handle getters and the proxy both index those vectors by peer rank. With two ranks, rank 1 therefore looks up peer 0 in slot 0, which is null, and crashes in `Host2DeviceSemaphore::deviceHandle()` before its first kernel launch.

Size both semaphore vectors to `world_size` and assign each peer's semaphore to slot `r`, as the test already does for connections. Only the self slot remains null. This changes only the test's semaphore construction; it leaves the data check and benchmark unchanged.

**Validation:** `git diff --check`, formatting, and focused local rank-mapping checks for both vectors. No GPU run was performed on this PR or its base (`215f073`). On the earlier `4dab9f5` baseline, the two-rank test exited 139. A broader local candidate on that earlier base, containing the same indexing fix **and** a separate correctness-verdict change, completed the 65,536-byte test on two GB200 GPUs with no reported mismatches. The verdict change is not in this PR.

author: juanmahidalgo
body:
# Pull Request Description

Part of #1661 (the admin side; studio operator grants follow in a separate PR). Part of #1660.

## Evidence of the original problem (optional)

credits-server manages scene studios: studios give Credits to their players out of a budget an operator assigns. The ops dashboard (`CreditsClient/studios.ts`) creates and pauses studios, chooses the wallets that act for them and tops up or adjusts their budgets, over `/admin/studios...` with wallet-signed requests. The node served none of it.

## What does this PR change?

**Studios, their operators and their budget** (`credits.studios`, `credits.studio_operators`, `credits.studio_budget_entries` in `schemas/60_ops.sql`; `shop/src/credits/studios.rs`). They are ported from credits-server's studios migration and store:
- **Studio:** a name (unique ignoring case, one printable line of at most 80 characters) and a status (`active` or `paused`).
- **Operators:** the wallets that act for it.
- **Budget:** a ledger in USD cents (1 Credit = 10 cents) whose balance is the sum of its entries. A `deposit` adds, an `adjustment` moves either way, and a `grant` (written by the operator grants, not yet) takes and names the one `credits.ledger` row it credited.
- **No migration step:** an existing database gains the tables from the object pass.

**Routes**, at credits-server's `/credits/admin/studios...` and the canonical `/shop-api/admin/studios...` (both in `paths.rs`):

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /admin/studios` | every studio with its figures (balance, deposited, granted, grant and operator counts) |
| `POST /admin/studios` `{ name }` | creates an active studio with an empty budget (201) |
| `GET /admin/studios/{id}?limit&offset` | the studio, its operators and a page of its budget history, newest first (50 by default, at most 200) |
| `PATCH /admin/studios/{id}` `{ name?, status? }` | renames, pauses or resumes it |
| `POST /admin/studios/{id}/operators` `{ address }` | lets a wallet act for it (201; 200 when it already did) |
| `DELETE /admin/studios/{id}/operators/{address}` | stops a wallet acting for it |
| `POST /admin/studios/{id}/budget` `{ kind, credits, note?, idempotencyKey }` | records a deposit or an adjustment (201; 200 with `replayed: true` for a repeat) |

**Who may call them**, as credits-server's read and read-write admins:
- **Reads:** `admin::require_read_admin`, the operator bearer or a signed request from `CREDITS_READ_ADMIN_ADDRESSES`, which now also accepts `CREDITS_WRITE_ADMIN_ADDRESSES`.
- **Changes:** the new `admin::require_write_admin`, the operator bearer or a signed request from `CREDITS_WRITE_ADMIN_ADDRESSES` (credits-server's `READ_WRITE_ADMIN_ADDRESSES`). An entry that is not a wallet fails startup.
  - A contract wallet's change is checked with the uncached EIP-1654 validator, as the market's writes are, so a removed owner stops changing studios at once.
  - The proxy's `x-original-path` counts only when it is the route itself, as #2394's read gate does.
- **Body binding:** a signed request proves the method, the route and the time, not the body.
  - **What is verified:** a wallet write that signs `bodySha256` (the hex SHA-256 of the exact body bytes) in its signed metadata is checked against the body, and a mismatch is a 401 before anything is written.
  - **Any spelling:** a legacy signature covers the metadata folded to lowercase, so the key is matched in any casing, and metadata that spells it twice is refused rather than one spelling picked. A DELETE's hash is checked against the bytes it sends, empty or not.
  - **Unbound writes:** a wallet write that signs no hash is accepted and logged at warn, as credits-server accepted it, while `CREDITS_ADMIN_WRITES_REQUIRE_BOUND_BODY` is off (the default); on, it is refused. The bearer is unaffected.
  - **The open risk:** while the flag is off, a captured wallet write could be replayed with another body within its signature's window.
  - **Follow-up, #2437:** the ops dashboard signs `bodySha256`, then the flag turns on.
- **Audit:** every change writes one `ops.admin_audit` row in its own transaction. A wallet's change names the signer's address as the actor (and as `createdBy` / `addedBy`), so the dashboard shows who made it. The bearer's change keeps its token name.

**Budget rules**, as credits-server enforces them:
- A deposit is positive. An adjustment needs a note and never takes the balance below zero (`STUDIO_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`); this is checked under the studio's row lock.
- **Daily ceiling:** new budget (any positive entry), every studio together, is bounded by `CREDITS_DAILY_STUDIO_DEPOSIT_LIMIT_CENTS` (credits-server's `DAILY_STUDIO_DEPOSIT_LIMIT_CENTS`) per UTC day of the database clock.
  - It is read under one service-wide advisory lock (credits-server's lock id).
  - The transaction pins READ COMMITTED, as credits-server does, whatever the session default. Under an inherited REPEATABLE READ, a waiter's snapshot could predate the deposit it waited for, and two deposits could both pass.
  - The clock is read once, after the locks; that one reading is both the day the ceiling counts and the time the entry records.
  - Unset or negative refuses new budget (`DEPOSITS_NOT_CONFIGURED`, 503): fail-closed.
  - Past the ceiling: `DAILY_DEPOSIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (429).
- **Idempotency:** the key is used once per studio, with a hash of the request. A repeat with the same request answers what it wrote, before any ceiling or balance check. With another request it is `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` (409).

**Refusals** answer `{ error, code }` with credits-server's codes and messages: `INVALID_REQUEST`, `STUDIO_NOT_FOUND`, `STUDIO_NAME_TAKEN`, `OPERATOR_NOT_FOUND`, `STUDIO_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, `DAILY_DEPOSIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `DEPOSITS_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The admin gates keep their own 401.

**Notifications:** credits-server posted each budget change to Slack. Here each change is a structured log event (`studio budget changed`, with the studio, kind, amount, balance, note and actor); the Slack feed comes with #1666's alerts.

**A studio's page** (`GET /admin/studios/{id}`) reads its figures, operators, history page and total from one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY snapshot, so they agree while a change commits.

**Docs:**
- `DATABASE.md` gains the studios workload (writers, readers, locks and invariants).
- `METRICS.md` records the index measurements on 200,000 synthetic entries.
- The `paths.rs` header says the operator routes are not in the client's `endpoints.ts` or the UI's pinned routes: the ops dashboard calls them, never the Shop UI.

**Cutover:** the credits-server migration (`tooling/migration/sources/credits-server`) now carries studios, their operators and their budget entries. Earlier they were listed as "no target", which would have dropped every studio budget. The new steps are `studio`, `studio_operator` and `studio_budget_entry`, run after `ledger`:
- **Balances:** after a load, each studio's balance (the sum of its entries) equals upstream's, and a replay writes nothing.
- **Grants:** a grant links to the ledger row that `ledger` imported for its credit. A grant whose credit is not imported yet is carried as an `adjustment` of the same amount, with a note naming the credit, so no money is dropped. A later run links it.
- **Operators:** an operator that upstream removed is removed from the node too (the import records what it added). One added on the node is left alone, and one the node removed is not added back.
- **Studios:** a studio the node renamed or paused later keeps the node's values. A name clash with a studio created on the node stops the run.
- `MAPPING.md` and `source.toml` describe all of this. The tests are in `tooling/tests/migration_financial_cases.py` (5, against PostgreSQL), each rule mutation-checked.

**#2399 review follow-ups:**
- The gateway coverage test also scans the routers the credits mount merges (the operator routes, the studi

author: thiesi
body:
Closes #277 (phase 1). This PR makes five cuts to S11 tick headroom. Each keeps behaviour identical and has its own equivalence test. The technical lead approved the plan with per-cut conditions; phase 2 isn't started. Runtime PR: the gate of record is S11 at both sizes, two independent runs on the remote runner, plus pytest-full (see **Runner**).

## Why

s283-2 (S47 + #276 + #283) failed S11 at 132x50 canonical with 20.666 ms. Main 7e477561 passes, but at the edge: s11-main7e had 80x24 canonical at 19.507 ms. The Npcs segment moves 2–3 ms between runs of the same code. The technical lead's target for #277 is a canonical gate p99 of about 16 ms or less at both sizes, with probes off.

The attribution comes from s277-diag-2: probes on, used for ranking only, gist 00287111.

**The Sable enforcer's hunt.** The slow `act` calls (2.9 ms each) have no navigation inside them; `route_toward` and `search` were called 0 times in the canonical window. The cost is the shot against a player:
- `exchange` → `hostile_contact` ×2 and `hurt` → `remember` each queue a plain character save (a deep `asdict` of the player);
- `record_use` deep-copies the whole player for its draft;
- the pump then JSON round-trips every save's player record.

Only 19 of 122 canonical ticks carry player saves, but they are the tail: act p99 5.94 ms against p50 1.15, pump p99 2.41 against p50 0.28.

**The early-tick spike.** s283-2 tick 572, s11-main7e tick 618 and diag-2 ticks 571/577 are a Sodium Row refill: 7 spawns in one call, 5 of them from the regulars' 2,208-tile region.

## The cuts

| | Target | Mechanism | Equivalence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** `9ae1faf5` | `IO.pump` | Within one outbox drain, a plain save whose records a later plain save in the same drain marks again is not marked itself. | Same fight with coalescing on and off: identical dirty map, first-mark ticks, in-flight and run commands, world, and rows on disk. Writer death at 4 crash points recovers the same DB. |
| **C2** `d9117bbb` | `Player.record()` | `players.plain()`: asdict's conversion with fast paths for exact dict, list and tuple; nested dataclasses become dicts; deepcopy fallback. | 3,000 fuzzed values compared to `asdict`, types checked recursively; every player's record through the fight. |
| **C3** `67232f05` | `record_use` | `skills.proposal()`: deep copies of only `GAIN_FIELDS` (progress, skills, attributes). | Every action and line × 6 ledger states × same day and across midnight: same amount and fields; live player untouched. A guard names any other field `gain()` writes. |
| **C4** `d39dc9f3` | `Spawners.location` | (a) Ground cache keyed by map identity, 8 states per spawner. (b) One refill call reuses each spawner's filter and clearance. Farthest tiles computed only when needed. | Every zone's refills (cold, warm, after `set_door`) against the original per-spawn code: same actors, tiles and RNG. `spawn.CHECK_REUSE` is on suite-wide. Guard run with door toggles, a geometry layer and refills. |
| **C5** `5436fe3a` | `Npcs.hostile` and helpers | Per-template facts and per-zone spawner lookups, each checked by identity. | Every actor pair and actor against the original code through a provoked city; a replaced zone template and a replaced content template take effect at once. |

`abdf71b5`: `scripts/bench_277.py`, the technical lead's local pricing harness, now reports a fingerprint of the final world.

## Per-cut conditions (technical lead), and how each is met

**C1**
- Coalescing happens only inside one drain: the leading run of plain saves, up to the first non-plain effect, which submits and sets the barrier. Nothing carries across pumps.
- The commit message lists every reader of the dirty map and generations: `_batch`, `_clear`, `_mark_effect(covered)`, `_character`'s covered snapshot, `_refreeze`, `_purge_deleted`/`_drop` and `persistence_lag`. The read cache, stats and the barrier read neither.
- Canon: architecture 3.3/3.4/6.2 and `docs/ops/server-core.md` have no wording that implies one mark per effect.
- The crash points are in the test.

**C2**
- It recurses into nested dataclasses as `asdict` does, and keeps the deepcopy fallback. Both are covered by the property test.

**C3**
- The guard fails loudly, naming the field. I checked this with a temporary mutation of `gain()`.

**C4**
- Bounded at 8 states per spawner, oldest first. The bound is stated in the code, and it also caps how many old geometry dicts stay alive.
- References, never `id()`s.
- The reuse guard re-walks the ground on every cache hit and re-filters on every reuse.
- Tick 571's cause is recorded as inference plus local reproduction (no extra runner run, per the technical lead). It isn't an instance rebuild: zones are built once. The old key carried the monotonic `geometry_revision`, which every door toggle bumps, so no earlier state ever matched.

**C5**
- Checked, not assumed, whether content can change at runtime:
  - there's no runtime reload;
  - the records are frozen;
  - the only runtime content mutation is `content.cores`, which isn't read here;
  - `zone.template` *is* replaced by housing, so lookups are keyed on that object.
- There's nothing with a revision to key on.

## Pricing (local, probes off, deterministic replay)

`scripts/bench_277.py`: the production Core with every hub zone active, writes through S47's IO and a ManualWriter, same seed and scripted inputs.
- **Pursuit:** a provoked Sable enforcer against a healed caller, 600 ticks.
- **Refill:** every Sodium Row slot due at once, 10 times.
- **Hit ticks:** ticks whose character outbox received effects (165 per run).
- **Runs:** five rounds, each tree once per round, interleaved. Each cell is the median across the five runs of that run's median or p99, in ms.

| tree | hit NPC tick (median / p99) | hit writes (median / p99) | hit step+writes (median / p99) | refill NPC tick (median / p99) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `7e477561` | 1.258 / 2.195 | 0.297 / 1.053 | 3.641 / 5.383 | 10.821 / 12.476 |
| + C1 | 1.248 / 2.081 | 0.288 / 0.806 | 3.550 / 5.351 | 10.747 / 13.064 |
| + C2 | 1.214 / 1.962 | 0.290 / 0.850 | 3.481 / 5.037 | 9.983 / 13.289 |
| + C3 | 1.231 / 1.989 | 0.297 / 0.685 | 3.499 / 4.957 | 11.016 / 13.862 |
| + C4 | 1.261 / 1.959 | 0.294 / 0.836 | 3.621 / 4.762 | **4.882 / 5.964** |
| + C5 (head) | **1.189 / 1.927** | **0.293 / 0.853** | **3.578 / 5.125** | **5.086 / 5.538** |

- **Same outcome everywhere:** every run of every tree ends in the same world (one fingerprint across all 30 runs).
- **Honest reading:** on this machine the hit-tick gains are modest. NPC p99 is −12%, writes p99 −19%, step+writes p99 −5%. Adjacent rows are inside run-to-run noise, so per-cut attribution on the hit ticks is approximate.
- **Clear win:** the refill spike drops by more than half, median 10.8 → 5.1 ms and p99 12.5 → 5.5 ms.
- **Microbenchmarks per cut** (best of 5, local):

  | Cut | Measured | Before → after |
  |---|---|---|
  | C2 | `record()` | 0.032 → 0.012 ms |
  | C3 | the draft copy | 0.053 → 0.027 ms |
  | C5 | `hostile()` | 1.9 → 1.2–1.35 µs per call |

- **What counts:** the runner's S11 pair at the head, below.

## Runner

Gate of record at the PR head: S11 at 80x24 and 132x50, two independent runs, probes off, plus pytest-full.

**s285-1 at `abdf71b5`: all pass.**
- pytest-full: 3462 passed, 0 failures.
- S11: runs A and B pass at both sizes, with the gate enforced.
- No reruns and no #284 timeouts.
- Each cell ran on a fresh worktree, venv and install (NetBBS v7.45.0).
- Gist (secret, scrubbed): https://gist.github.com/Thiesi/b2773e67bca5a65419a9d85c90ba52ea

**Gates** (p99 ms, first / canonical)

| size | run A | run B | s11-main7e canonical | s283-2 canonical |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80x24 | 14.659 / **18.426** | 15.359 / **16.934** | 19.507 | 16.566 |
| 132x50 | 14.387 / **14.897** | 15.331 / **14.337** | 16.809 | 20.666 |

**Against the target** (canonical ≤ about 16 ms at both sizes):
- **132x50 meets it in both runs**, down from 16

author: himent12
body:
## What & Why

Follow-ups from #308 and `folo-ui` / Desktop focus-restoration polish in `apps/desktop/`:

1. **Carry `refused::check`'s connected loopback socket into the `GET /api/health` probe (#308 item 1)** (`src/api/http/refused.rs`, `server.rs`, `mod.rs`):
   - Previously on Windows, `refused::check` opened a loopback socket with `SIO_TCP_INITIAL_RTO` (no SYN retries), detected a listener, immediately closed that empty socket, and let `ureq` open a second TCP connection. On a listener with a 1-slot accept queue that delays `accept()` past 500 ms, the closed empty connection occupied the last slot and both probe attempts timed out.
   - `refused::check` now switches the winning connected socket back to blocking mode, wraps it with its Winsock guard (`ConnectedStream`, dropping `TcpStream` before `Wsa`), and returns `Found::Listener(Some(conn))`.
   - `server::probe_through` hands that established socket straight into `ureq::Agent::with_parts` via a lightweight `PreconnectedConnector` + `PreconnectedTransport` (chained before `TcpConnector` and `RustlsConnector`), removing the redundant throwaway connect completely.

2. **Eliminate ~9 Hz no-op UI rebuilds while a run trains in the background (#308 item 7)** (`src/app/data/streams.rs`, `app/mod.rs`, `app/render.rs`):
   - Live step events arrive at ~9–10 Hz. Previously `drain_streams` unconditionally returned `changed = true` on every `RunEvent::Step`, forcing ~9 full UI rebuilds/sec on idle screens (Settings, Datasets, Models, Benchmarks, Playground, Runs) even when the sidebar progress bar moved by a tiny fraction of a device pixel and presented zero changed pixels.
   - `drain_streams` still applies every step event losslessly to `Store`, and always notifies every step on per-step views (`Route::Run(live_id)`, `Route::Overview`), while on other screens it compares a compact visible signature (`epoch`, `epochs`, `steps_per_epoch`, rounded `{:.0}%`, device-pixel progress bar bucket at `window.scale_factor()`, queued-run ahead ETA, and stop-dialog epoch boundary) and notifies only when displayed state actually changes.

3. **Harden `overlay_return` focus restoration & positional focus keys** (`ui/src/window/{mod,draw,ops}.rs`, `src/app/{mod,overlay_state,render,navigation}.rs`, `src/screens/datasets/stats.rs`):
   - Added `Window::is_focus_mounted(&FocusHandle)` in `folo-ui` (checking the prepainted dispatch tree during paint and `rendered_frame` outside paint).
   - Preserved pre-overlay `overlay_return` across overlay-to-overlay hand-offs (e.g. Command Palette → `Ctrl+N` / `Ctrl+O` / `ask_delete`) instead of clobbering it with the dropped palette input handle.
   - Stored route and `play_pred_seq` alongside `overlay_return`, cleared stale return targets on navigation, checked `is_focus_mounted` both on close and post-prepaint (catching controls removed on the same tick that closes a dialog, e.g. Disconnect / Stop / Delete), and scoped dataset class-bar focus keys by dataset ID (`ds-class-bar-{ds.id}-{i}`).

## Testing
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (pass)

body:
## Task

ORB-28391 — Choose a worker's task reads when Stored is built

### Description

## Outcome
`get_task` first asks whether the process is a worker and, if so, reads through the drain owner; it has 202 callers. Because of that, following calls, 1,385 of 2,925 functions in `orbit-core` reach a worker field, and the layers cannot hold: a task read would need what only a worker has (2_design.md §4).

## Scope
A task access in `crates/orbit-runtime/src/stored/task_access.rs`, chosen once from `Role` when `Stored` is built: the local store, or the owner route for a worker. The task read functions (`get_task`, `get_task_history`, `get_task_comments`, `get_task_artifact`, `list_task_metadata`, `resolve_dependency_task` and the others that branch to `read_owner`) call it and stop asking the role.

## Constraints
A worker's read returns exactly what it returns today, including a dangling or foreign id. This is not a pure move: it changes a path every drain worker uses, so name each function converted and its old and new path in the PR. Writes and refusals are a separate task.

## Design
`docs/design/architecture-restructure/` on `agent-main`: `2_design.md` is the target, `4_decisions.md` the decisions Daniel approved on 2026-11-25. This task changes no behaviour, no persisted format and no command, tool or HTTP output. Add no test the criteria do not name.

### Acceptance Criteria

- No task read function in `orbit-core` calls `worker_invocation()` or `read_owner` directly; the choice is made in `stored/task_access.rs`.
- Existing worker-read tests pass unchanged, and the PR lists each converted function.
- Each count this change lowers is lowered in `scripts/architecture-ratchet-baseline.json` in the same change, and no count rises.

## Execution Summary

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

Fresh run (no resumed candidate). A worker's task reads are now chosen once in `crates/orbit-runtime/src/stored/task_access.rs` (`TaskRoute::for_role`, set when `Stored` is built); `Stored::task()` returns the `TaskAccess` every task read calls. Not a breaking change; no behaviour, persisted format or command/tool/HTTP output changes; no test added or edited.

## Criteria
1. Met. `grep 'worker_invocation()\|read_owner'` finds nothing in `application/task/query.rs` or `listing.rs`; `RuntimeKernel::read_owner` and `read_owner_request` are deleted. The role is matched only in `TaskRoute::for_role`.
2. Met. Worker-read tests pass unchanged (commands below); converted functions listed below.
3. Met. `worker_or_owner_reads` 216 → 183 and `orbit_runtime_ref_param_fns` 1369 → 1365 in `scripts/architecture-ratchet-baseline.json`; no count rose.

## Converted functions (for the PR)
Old path, all of them: `if self.worker_invocation().is_some()` in orbit-core → `RuntimeKernel::read_owner` / `read_owner_request` / `read_owner_tool_request` (`orbit-runtime/src/run/worker_coordination.rs`) → `route_worker_host_tool` → owner coordinator held by `Run`.
New path, all of them: `self.stored().task().<method>` → `TaskAccess` (`stored/task_access.rs`), which matches the route chosen at build → `OwnerRoute::read` (`stored/task_access/owner.rs`) for a worker, the local store otherwise. Request JSON, tool name, lock-busy retry and decoding are the same code, moved.

`application/task/query.rs` (OrbitRuntime method → TaskAccess method): `get_task`→`get`; `resolve_dependency_task`→`resolve_dependency`; `registered_task_workspace`→`registered_workspace`; `dependency_history`→`dependency_history`; `get_task_artifacts`→`artifacts`; `get_task_artifact_manifest`→`artifact_manifest`; `get_task_artifact`→`artifact`; `get_task_comments`→`comments`; `get_task_history`→`history`; `get_task_histories`→`histories`; `task_history_stamps`→`history_stamps`; `task_bundle_stamps`→`bundle_stamps`; `list_tasks`→`list`; `list_task_metadata`→`metadata`; `list_task_metadata_with_any_tag`→`metadata_with_any_tag`; `list_task_metadata_for_ids`→`metadata_for_ids`; `browser_kit_backlog_waits`→`metadata_covering`; `task_lifecycle_stamps_matching`→`lifecycle_stamps_matching`; `task_status_index`→`status_index`; `task_completion_by_complexity`→`completion_by_complexity`; `task_complexity_by_id`→`complexity_by_id`; `task_terminal_transitions`→`terminal_transitions`; `task_defect_filings`→`defect_filings`; `list_tasks_by_tags`→`list_by_tags`; `list_tasks_filtered`→`list_filtered`; `list_run_tasks`→`run_task_scope` + `RunTaskScope::narrow`; `search_tasks`→`search`; `search_tasks_filtered`→`search_filtered`; `search_tasks_visit`→`search_visit`; `in_task_read_section`→`in_read_section`.
Other files: `collect_owner_metadata` (was `application/task/metadata.rs`, now `stored/task_access/metadata.rs`); `owner_claim_steering` in `application/task/steering.rs`→`claim_steering`; `show_task_row` + `worker_show_task_row` in `adapter/tool_host/task/operation/show.rs` merged into one role-free `show_task_row`→`row_or` + `listed_row`; `admit_task_for_workflow` in `adapter/engine_host/runtime_host/claims.rs`: `read_owner(id, "task")`→`get_task` (same `task` projection).

## Validation (all through `scripts/build-budget.py`, logs in `.orbit/tmp/logs/`)
- passed: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --lib --bins -- -D warnings -A clippy::disallowed_methods` and `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets …` for orbit-runtime and orbit-core
- passed: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" scripts/with-test-build-lint.sh … cargo doc --no-deps -p orbit-runtime` and `-p orbit-core`
- passed: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `make ci-guards` (after lowering the baseline); `git diff --check`
- passed: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- passed: `cargo test -p orbit-cli -p orbit-runtime --lib` (53 passed, 1 ignored)
- passed: `cargo test -p orbit-cli -p orbit-core --lib` (261 passed, 2 ignored)
- passed: `cargo test -p orbit-cli -p orbit-core --test runtime` (909 passed, 10 ignored; includes `distributed_drain`, 137 passed)
- passed: `cargo test -p orbit-cli --test mcp worker_routing` (3), `--test mcp internal_drain` (2), `--test tool claimed_review_bridge` (7 passed, 2 ignored). Two of those cases print `DEFERRED: bubblewrap unavailable`: this sandbox could not exercise them.
- not run: `make ci`, `ci-fast`, `goldens`, `ci-test-affected` (not blanket gates; no golden surface changed); local CodeQL (not owed); the rest of the workspace's test binaries (PR checks cover them).

## Paths outside the task's selectors, and why
- `crates/orbit-runtime/src/stored/task_access/{owner,metadata}.rs` (new), `stored/mod.rs`, `run/mod.rs`, `run/worker_coordination.rs`, `base/mod.rs`, `base/role.rs`, `lib.rs`: a read that needs only `&Stored` must reach the owner, so the owner coordinator field moved from `Run` into `Stored`'s task route, with the send, lock-busy retry, decoding and the `with_owner_read_retry_wait` test seam. `route_worker_tool` stays in `run/` and delegates. `Base.role` is private and re-set through `Stored::set_role`, so the route cannot drift from the role.
- `crates/orbit-core/src/application/task/metadata.rs` deleted, moved to `stored/task_access/metadata.rs` (plain `mv`; the index is read-only): the paged metadata client is a worker read. Its owner-side server moved with it as `RuntimeKernel::owner_task_metadata_page`; `adapter/tool_host/worker_tools.rs` calls that. `listing.rs` re-exports the three metadata helpers; `application/task/mod.rs` drops the module.
- `steering.rs`, `show.rs`: they called `read_owner` directly, which the change deletes.
- `scripts/check-dependency-direction.sh`: `with_owner_read_retry_wait` moved from the run name list to the stored one. `docs/architecture/orbit-runtime.md`: module list, layer table, field inventory.
- Selector `crates/orbit-runtime/src/plugin/broker/socket.rs` was not touched: its `read_owner` is an unrelated socket-owner helper (the file now lives under `host/plugin/`).

## Left for the sibling tasks, and risks
- Replica `coordination_task_reads_visible()` checks stay in the orbit-core callers (ORB-28392).

author: draganoider
body:
## What this changes

Adds everything around `spin()` that milestone 2's simulation needs, so the real spin plugs in: exactly mergeable observed statistics (`src/engine/stats.ts`), a runner over an injected spin function with lane-based splitting (`src/engine/simulate.ts`), the DR-006 tolerance and seed-sweep checks (`src/engine/verify.ts`), a Web Worker and Node worker-thread host behind one protocol (`src/worker/`), and `npm run simulate` for the nightly job.

## Issue

Part of milestone 2 (engine and simulation).

## Checks

- [x] Typecheck and unit tests pass (`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`: 133 tests). No browser tests exist yet.
- [x] No math change, so no simulation run in `docs/findings.md`. The runner only counts; it decides nothing.
- [x] Docs updated: a new section in `src/engine/README.md`, and a new `src/worker/README.md`
- [x] No assets
- [x] No injury content
- [x] No secrets
- [x] No generated files
- [x] `python tools/ci/hygiene.py` passes

## Notes for the reviewer

- **A run can't be split anywhere, because of the Scar Card.** Each spin has its own RNG stream (DR-011), but `spin(config, state, request)` reads the card left by earlier spins. So a chunk starting mid-run doesn't know its starting state. The fix is **lanes**: the card resets to empty at every multiple of `laneLength`, as if a new player sat down, and `splitJob` cuts only there. Merged worker results then equal the single-thread run exactly. The tests check this, and also check that a naive cut that ignores the card is *not* exact. `laneLength: null` means one lane, which is exact stationary play but single-threaded. Starting each lane on an empty card is a small transient bias against the analyser's stationary figures, so the CLI defaults to lanes of 10⁶. The alternative, running every chunk from every card state, is exact but costs `scarCard.size`× the work. **This is probably worth a decision record in `docs/PLAN.md`**; I left PLAN.md alone because it was outside my scope.
- **Typecheck split.** `@types/node` (needed for the CLI and `worker_threads`) gets pulled into any program that imports Vitest. That silently let `src/engine/` use `setTimeout` and `process`; I checked this with a probe file. `npm run typecheck` now runs three programs: `tsconfig.json` (src minus `src/worker/node/`, ES2022 only, as before), `tsconfig.test.json` (tests, Node typings) and `tsconfig.node.json` (`src/worker/node/`). CI's `npm run typecheck` picks all three up unchanged.
- **Workers under Vitest.** I didn't use `@vitest/web-worker`, which runs the worker in the same thread behind a shim. The protocol, progress, cancel and errors are tested through an in-process structured-clone channel running the real `serveSimulations`. Real `worker_threads` (via `tsx`) and the CLI in a child process are tested with a fake spin module. The browser `Worker` entry isn't exercised yet; Playwright will cover it once there's a page.
- **The fake spin** (`tests/support/fake-spin.ts`) is deterministic from the spin's outcome stream and really uses the card: bails add marks and a full card starts a Session. That is what makes the split tests meaningful.
- **Statistics labelling.** Every summary figure is `{ kind: 'observed', value, theoretical: null }`. Only `withTheoretical()` fills the slot, and it accepts only `kind: 'theoretical'` values. `checkTolerance` also refuses unlabelled inputs and uses the analyser's σ, never the sample's.
- New dev dependencies: `@types/node`, `tsx`.

Ticket: [LEG-601](https://burnlite.dev/LEG-601), adopt open handoff loops at upgrade, and delete the Go handoff loop. Part of the spec [LEG-559](https://burnlite.dev/LEG-559).

- **The adoption:** `store.AdoptHandoffReviewLoop` moves an open handoff-owned loop to a run's `open` step, in one compare-and-swap transaction. It keeps the loop ID, marker key, claim, passes (including one in flight), rulings, items and counters.
- **When it happens:** a sweep in the engine holder's tick adopts each such loop into a new `review-loop` run for its handoff (`adoptLoop`, sharing `runStart` with new handoffs, so `ready` comes from the worker's rule). A pass in flight is posted once.
- **The same sweep** also cancels the run of a handoff that closed or is returning. It closes, with `ended`, a loop a closed handoff still owns.
- **Deleted:** the handoff-owned branches of `openLoop`, `movesOn`, `Loop` and `ownsLoop`, and `CloseReviewLoopsOfClosedHandoffs`. No handoff code path drives a loop outside `review-loop` any more.

body:
## What changed

- **One config list.** `lib/config-files.sh` has a `CONFIG_FILES` table (19 rows: `link`, `copy`, `line` or `git-include`, plus which machines want each). `fresh.sh`, `linux.sh` and `refresh.sh` all apply it instead of their own `ln` lines, which removes about 100 lines of duplicated code.
- **`refresh.sh` re-applies the list.** Config added to the repo since a machine was set up now reaches that machine. Before, it needed a `fresh.sh` re-run, which also runs sudo, `.macos` and the Dock reset.
- **`doctor.sh`** checks a machine against the repo without changing anything:
  - config links
  - Claude Code status line, hooks, skills and agents
  - zsh plugins, tools and the Brewfile
  - uncommitted changes, which catch apps that edit a linked file

  It exits 1 on real breakage. `fresh.sh` and `linux.sh` run it at the end.
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has three jobs:
  - **lint:** shellcheck, `zsh -n`, the babysit bun tests and the guard tests.
  - **mac:** scripts parse under `/bin/bash` 3.2, and the guard tests pass with macOS's own grep and sed.
  - **linux-setup:** runs `linux.sh` twice on clean Ubuntu, checks nothing was added twice, runs `doctor.sh`, and checks that `zsh -i` starts with nothing on stderr.
- **fzf fix:** `fzf --zsh` fails on fzf older than 0.48 (Ubuntu 24.04 ships 0.44), so zsh now falls back to the packaged key-binding scripts.

## Behaviour changes to know about

- A real file in the way of a link is moved to `<name>.pre-dotfiles`. It was deleted before (`rm -rf ~/.zshrc`) or silently replaced (`ln -sf`).
- The btop config is copied only when missing. `fresh.sh` used to overwrite it on every run; doctor now warns when it has drifted.
- The config scripts refuse to run from a copy of the repo that isn't `~/dotfiles`. Otherwise, running one from an agent worktree would point the machine's config at that worktree.
- A symlink at `~/.gitconfig` or `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is removed only when it points into this repo (the old-setup migration case), not when it points anywhere else.

## Testing

- **Mac, throwaway HOME** with `~/dotfiles` linked to the checkout:
  - setup ran twice; the second run changed nothing
  - an old `.zshrc` was moved aside, a broken link was replaced, and `CLAUDE.md` kept its machine notes
  - doctor flagged a removed link and a dropped hook, and exited 1
  - the scripts refused to run from outside `~/dotfiles`
- **Ubuntu 24.04 container**, the same steps as the CI linux-setup job: all passed. This run caught doctor missing the Starship that `linux.sh` installs in `~/.local/bin`, which is fixed here.
- shellcheck at warning level is clean, with SC2088 silenced in `.shellcheckrc` because the `~/` paths in messages are display text. The guard and babysit tests pass.

This PR is the first time the workflow runs on GitHub itself.

## Change
- `DEFAULT_C_TEMPERATURE = 0.7` in experiments/g02_generate.py. Used by `iter_generate`, and named in the CLI `--temperature` help. When `n_candidates > 1` and no temperature is given, every arm C candidate call gets `temperature=0.7`, and the arm C record stores `temperature`. An explicit `--temperature 0` is passed through and recorded as given. Arms A/B are unchanged, and so is arm C with `n_candidates == 1` and no temperature (it still calls `model(prompt)`).
- `summarize` now returns `c_deterministic`. It is true when any arm C record counted for the current run has `n_candidates > 1` and a temperature that is 0 or missing. `complete` does not depend on it.

## Tests (written first; the 3 new tests failed with errors before the implementation)
- New: `test_default_arm_c_samples_at_default_temperature` (0.7 passed and recorded; c_deterministic false), `test_explicit_temperature_zero_is_honoured_and_flagged` (0 passed and recorded; c_deterministic true; complete true), `test_c_deterministic_when_temperature_missing_and_ignores_other_runs`.

author: ncecere
body:
Part of #49 (delivery 2 of 3: route health in the API and Admin). #865 (D1) is merged; this PR is based on `main`. No migration.

**Status:** API and dashboard, both done. The API shape was confirmed as briefed, with the 600 s stale window as a fixed constant and no list endpoint.

## API shape (confirmed)

`GET /api/v1/platform/deployments/{deployment}/routing` (Platform Admin and Auditor, as today) adds seven fields to `health`. The existing three are unchanged, so the change is additive.

```json
"health": {
  "consecutive_failures": 3,
  "open_until": "2026-11-26T10:00:30+00:00",
  "last_observed_at": "2026-11-26T10:00:00+00:00",
  "circuit": "half_open",
  "cooling_until": null,
  "probe_in_progress": true,
  "probe_until": "2026-11-26T10:02:33+00:00",
  "reopen_count": 2,
  "observation": "current",
  "as_of": "2026-11-26T10:00:41+00:00"
}
```

Every state is computed in the read's own statement (`as_of` = `statement_timestamp()`).

| Field | Type | States and meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `circuit` | enum | `closed`. `open`: cooling down until `cooling_until`. `half_open`: the cooldown has passed, and one request decides. |
| `cooling_until` | timestamp or null | `open_until` while `circuit = open`; `null` otherwise. |
| `probe_in_progress` | bool | `true` while a request holds the half-open route's **unexpired** probe slot. An expired slot that nobody re-claimed reads as `false`, because any request may now claim it. |
| `probe_until` | timestamp or null | While a probe is in progress: when its slot ends at the latest (request timeout plus 3 s after the claim). `null` otherwise. |
| `reopen_count` | int ≥ 0 | Openings since the route last served a complete success; each doubles the next cooldown, capped. |
| `observation` | enum | `none`: never observed (no health row, or no observation). `stale`: no observation for **600 s** (`routing::HEALTH_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`); a route with no traffic looks like this, and a closed circuit then says nothing current. `current` otherwise. A healthy route's `last_observed_at` lags by up to 30 s, well inside 600 s. |
| `as_of` | timestamp | The time the states were computed. |

**Combinations.**
- `circuit` and `observation` are independent. For example, `closed` + `none` is a route that never failed and was never observed (the dashboard reads this as "unknown").
- `probe_in_progress` is `true` only when `circuit = half_open`.

**Sanitized, as `routing::health` is.** No endpoint, credential reference, payload or raw error text. Not exposed:
- `probe_holder`, which is an execution id;
- `probe_epoch`.

The test asserts that neither the holder's id nor either field name appears in the view.

**One definition.** The view is one SQL expression, `routing::HEALTH_VIEW_SQL`, documented field by field where it is defined; the handler embeds it. `docs/routing.md` "Management health" and `docs/governance-api.md` describe it, and the OpenAPI fragment (`setup-schemas.json`) declares each field with its enum and description. `management.openapi.json` was regenerated (`OMG_REGENERATE_OPENAPI=1`) and the diff reviewed.

## Dashboard

The route page (`/admin/deployments/{id}`: its "Route summary" tile and its "Routing settings" section) and the governance deployment-routing panel read the view through `routeHealth` (`apps/web/src/lib/governance.ts`). It replaces `passiveHealth`. The state is always written out in words; there is no colour.

| View | Shown |
|---|---|
| never observed | "Unknown · no traffic observed yet", Last observed "Never" |
| stale | "Unknown lately · no traffic observed for over 10 minutes", plus "· N consecutive observed failures before that" when there were any |
| closed | "Closed · no recent failures" or "Closed · N consecutive observed failures" |
| open | "Cooling down · left out of routing", "Cooling until" (a time) |
| half-open, no probe | "Half-open · waiting for a request to test it" |
| probe in progress | "Half-open · one request is testing it", "Test ends by" (a time) |
| `reopen_count > 0` | "Backoff: Opened N times since its last complete success; each opening doubles the next cooldown, up to 300 seconds (or the cooldown, if longer)." |

Every view ends with "As of" (an absolute time) and the caveat "Health observations do not establish current upstream readiness." The caveat is now on the route page too, not only the panel.

**Clock.**
- The state comes from the gateway (`circuit`, `observation` at `as_of`); the browser's clock never decides it.
- Each time is shown relative to `as_of` ("in 1 minute", "30 seconds ago"), with no refresh timer, so a skewed browser clock cannot misstate it.
- The view is read again when its cooldown or probe slot ends. The delay is `until - as_of`, from the gateway's own times plus 1 s.

## Tests

- **`management::governance::tests::db::deployment_health_reports_the_circuit_as_it_is_now`**, on the real row through the HTTP handler:
  - never observed; open; half-open;
  - a probe in progress (`probe_until` equals the stored slot end; holder and epoch absent);
  - an expired, unclaimed slot; closed but stale;
  - the same view for an Auditor.
- **The setup OpenAPI fixture** also observes a half-open route with a probe in progress, so the contract's coverage gate sees every branch.
- **Vitest:**
  - `routeHealth` for each state (including stale with failures);
  - `healthRefreshDelay` (none due, cooldown, probe, already due);
  - the circuit taken from the gateway, not the browser;
  - the panel rendered with the browser's clock a day ahead: the cooldown reads "in 1 minute", the observation "30 seconds ago";
  - the updated fixtures of the route and model pages.
- **Browser** (`tests/browser/route-health.spec.ts`, its own project): the real stack with signed OIDC, gateway, disposable database and built SPA. For one seeded route it takes the gateway's real view, checks that it is a never-failed route with no holder field, and replaces only `health` for each of six states. Each state's words, the "As of" row and the caveat are checked in the routing section and the summary tile. A browser test cannot wait out cooldowns or upstream failures, so the states are written into the response.

## Review

One independent code review (not adversarial, since D2 changes no authorization).

| # | Finding | Done |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Medium: the times next to the gateway's state came from the browser's clock and kept counting while the state stayed as read | **Fixed.** Times relative to `as_of` with no timer, `as_of` absolute, and a reread when the cooldown or probe ends (`useHealthRefresh`). Vitest test with the clock skewed by a day. |
| 2 | Low: a stale closed route hid its failure count | **Fixed:** "· N consecutive observed failures before that". |
| 3 | Low: the browser test's "Never" check could match other text; the Rust test did not compare `probe_until` with the stored slot end | **Fixed:** exact match on "Never"; `probe_until` compared with `to_jsonb(probe_until)` from the row. |

The reviewer checked the SQL boundaries (no row; `open_until` and `probe_until` exactly at the statement time; an expired slot; a slot left over on a closed circuit), that every state maps to a sentence, holder and epoch redaction, grants (none needed), authorization (unchanged), same-origin requests, timing, and the docs.

## Gates (local)

Head `ebd2719b`, current `origin/main` (`2b0b6186`, with #865) merged; each exit status was checked on its own.

- **Exit 0:**
  - `cargo fmt --check`;
  - the three Clippy invocations of CI's gateway job;
  - `typecheck:web`, `test:web` (1,943), `build:web`, `test:rules` and `test:structure`.
- **Rust:**
  - `management::governance::tests::db::`, `management_openapi_artifact` and the setup OpenAPI fixtures: 63 of 63;
  - the full fast tier ran on the API commit (`2f421b8e`): all 3,341 lib tests selected, the contract fixtures included; 3,328 passed, 13 ignored, 0 failed. The Rust changed since then only in one test assertion.

author: feong
body: ## Summary `serve` now fetches once the first time a data directory has no recorded serve cycle, then waits for `ASC_SCHEDULE`. Later process starts wait for the next scheduled time and do not fetch just because the process started. A successful or failed startup cycle does not exit the process. SIGTERM and SIGINT still let an in-progress cycle finish, then exit, without starting another cycle. ## What counts as already served The durable record is `$ASC_DATA_DIR/serve.json`. It is separate from `state.json`. - No `serve.json`, or `"runs": 0`, means serve has never started a cycle in this directory. This start runs once immediately (`first_trigger` is `startup`), writes the record before the fetch returns, then waits for the next scheduled time. - `"runs" > 0` means a serve cycle has already started here. This start only waits. The startup log says it will not fetch immediately. - A one-shot `run` updates `state.json` only. It does **not** count as a serve cycle, so the first `serve` still runs once even when an operator has already executed `run`. `init` and `test-notification` do not write `serve.json` either. `state.json` cannot tell an older scheduled `serve` from a one-shot `run`, so this record is serve-specific instead of treating any existing state file as “already served.” - The record is written when the cycle starts, before the fetch returns. A failed cycle, a non-zero result, or a stop that lets the in-progress cycle finish all leave the record in place. The next start waits. - An unreadable or unrecognized `serve.json` is not treated as “never served” and is not overwritten. That start waits. A later scheduled cycle still runs, and it also leaves the file untouched. - Deleting `serve.json` makes the next `serve` start immediate again. Deleting `state.json` only makes the next cycle eligible to push the current summary again. It does not reset the serve record. Directories that already exist have no `serve.json`. The first start of this version performs one immediate cycle, then later restarts wait. If the record cannot be written, the cycle still runs and the log says the record was not saved. A later start will try the immediate cycle again, because nothing was recorded. ## Unchanged Schedule parsing, timezone handling, image publishing, and the one-shot commands are unchanged. `serve` help text now describes the startup cycle. ## Tests `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` (45 tests). They cover an immediate first cycle followed by a wait, a later start that does not run, a failed startup cycle that stays up, and a restart after that failure that waits.

author: yi-luo-hua
body:
## Problem

Clicking the center of a PDF++ crop and then clicking outside the layout can coincide with a stalled caret move. In the Windows reproduction, the layout and its DOM stayed mounted. Profiling attributed the long tasks to PDF++ rasterizing and encoding crops concurrently, including crops CodeMirror mounted beyond the viewport.

## Change

Live Preview reserves crop dimensions up front, starts PDF++ work when the crop enters the viewport, and renders one crop at a time per window. Pending work is discarded when its component is unloaded. Reading View and print still render through the existing path.

## Verification

- Windows, Obsidian 1.15.1, PDF++ 0.40.31. In a note with 12 four-crop layouts, clicking the crop center kept the layout in place, and the next click in the paragraph set the caret. The fixed run avoided the multi-hundred-millisecond frame gaps seen during the baseline load and deferred eight of the 20 crops mounted at the test position.
- Unit coverage for visibility, serial rendering, off-screen queue entries and disposal.
- `npm run check` (630 tests) and `npm run build` passed.

An installed extension could fail to load when its manifest entry lacked an install spec. The loader built the recovery message before importing the package, so a healthy package could trigger a TypeError and block commands such as `cotal spawn --dry-run`.

Build reinstall advice only on failure. When an operator-installed extension has no usable install spec, keep the original failure and name the package in the existing removal advice. Leave the manifest reader and its accepted inputs unchanged.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec tsx implementations/cli/smoke/operation-space.smoke.ts`: 180/200 on unchanged main with the reported TypeError, 200/200 with the fix.
- `pnpm exec tsx packages/workspace/smoke/import-remedy.smoke.ts`: 72/72, including an installed extension that loads without a spec and a broken one that reports both the cause and the removal command.
- `pnpm exec tsx packages/workspace/smoke/materialize-concurrency.smoke.ts`: 21/21.
- `pnpm exec tsx bin/smoke/ext-live.smoke.ts`: 96 checks passed.
- `pnpm exec tsx implementations/cli/smoke/ext-install-copies.smoke.ts`: 39/39.
- `pnpm exec tsx bin/smoke/status-default-agent.smoke.ts`: 20/20.
- `pnpm exec tsx implementations/cli/smoke/foreground-up-signals-live.smoke.ts`: the `delivery-repair` cell fails at the same assertion on both unchanged `bdb5aca769` and the fix. Its manifest already records a spec and supplies only `status-fixture`. The default application is Claude, so status names its missing connector instead of suggesting `cotal spawn`.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm changeset status`, `pnpm check:file-size`, `pnpm smoke:sandbox-guard`, `pnpm check:comment-history`, and `pnpm check:function-length`: passed.
- `pnpm check:docs-voice`, `pnpm check:docs-literals`, `pnpm check:doc-comments`, and `pnpm check:docs-site`: passed.

### Not run here

`smoke:usage-format`, `smoke:cli-entry`, `command-kernel.smoke.ts`, `smoke:stack-settle-live`, and the tree-wide censuses are reserved for merged-tree verification.

Cap Zygote at 0.7.16 to preserve the Core7 StaticArrays constructor gradient checks. Zygote 0.7.17 began deferring array broadcast cotangents, and the resulting thunk can reach its tuple pullback, which expects a tuple. The compatibility bound keeps the existing lower bound and leaves the test code intact.

Part of #1684

## Verification

Julia 1.13.4, two Julia threads, four precompile tasks. The two saved Core7 test manifests differ only in their Zygote entry (0.7.21 before, 0.7.16 after).

The full Core7 group ran locally against the fresh resolution and against the capped resolution. This used the same source and test files for both runs. The after command disabled automatic precompilation for the test sandbox and preserved all dependencies when asking the resolver to update Zygote under the new cap.

```bash
export GROUP=Core7 JULIA_NUM_THREADS=2 JULIA_NUM_PRECOMPILE_TASKS=4
# Before, on master
julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'
# After, with the cap applied to the previously resolved project
JULIA_PKG_PRECOMPILE_AUTO=0 julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.update("Zygote"; preserve=Pkg.PRESERVE_ALL); Pkg.test()'
```

Before, exit 1. The sole error was the `gradtuple1` thunk error above at `test/Core7/adjoint_oop.jl:25`. Output from the test summary:

```text
Test Summary:                               | Pass  Error  Total     Time
Core 7                                      |  127      1    128  8m15.8s
  Physical ODE Adjoint Regression Test      |   12            12    57.1s
  Continuous adjoint params                 |    5             5  1m53.3s
  Continuous and discrete costs             |  106           106  4m59.4s
  Fully Out of Place adjoint sensitivity    |           1      1     1.8s
  Differentiate LazyBuffer with ReverseDiff |    4             4    24.3s
```

After, exit 0. Output tail:

```text
Test Summary: | Pass  Total      Time
Core 7        |  178    178  15m00.3s
     Testing SciMLSensitivity tests passed
```

I extracted the original SVector and SMatrix gradient checks from `test/Core7/adjoint_oop.jl` and ran them in the respective resolved test environments. Here `TEST_ENV` selects the environment and `CONSTRUCTOR_CHECKS` is the extracted script.

```bash
julia --compiled-modules=existing --project="$TEST_ENV" "$CONSTRUCTOR_CHECKS"
```

Before, exit 1. The error line from the SVector check:

```text
ERROR: LoadError: Gradient Thunk(ProjectTo{ChainRulesCore.Tangent{Tuple{Float64, Float64}}}(elements = (ProjectTo{Float64}(), ProjectTo{Float64}()),) ∘ Zygote.Deferred{SVector{2, Float64}}(Zygote.var"#...) should be a tuple
```

After, exit 0. Output tail:

```text
Zygote 0.7.16
```

The standalone constructor reproducer passed on Zygote 0.7.15 and 0.7.16 and failed on each version from 0.7.17 through 0.7.21. Downgrading ChainRules to 1.74.8 or StaticArrays to 1.9.24 individually with Zygote 0.7.21 still failed. [Green master job](https://github.com/SciML/SciMLSensitivity.jl/actions/runs/41620707966/job/125867841508), [upstream change](https://github.com/FluxML/Zygote.jl/pull/1743).

## Verification limits

Julia 1.10.14 also reproduced the constructor error with 0.7.21 and passed the constructor checks with 0.7.16. Full-group verification was on Julia 1.13.4. Other Core groups and downstream package resolution were outside the local verification.

## Reviewer attention

Please push back if the package-wide compatibility cap would block a downstream project that needs Zygote 0.7.17 or newer. The cap should be revisited when a Zygote release passes the constructor reproducer.
