author: ajaykr089
body:
An audit of the editing plugins every editor uses (link, list, history, table and the source view in `code`) found 15 bugs, all fixed here. Three of them were in `@editora/core` and one in `@editora/react`. Each fix is its own commit with a test that fails without it, and each was checked with real key presses in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. ## Source view (`code`) - **Saving without an edit changed the document.** The formatter put every tag on its own line and trimmed the text between tags, so `foobarbaz` came back as "foo bar baz" and a `
` lost its leading spaces. Line breaks now go only between blocks, and Save leaves the document alone when nothing was edited.
- **Undo could not take back a source edit.** A save is now one undo step.
- **Edits were thrown away without asking.** Escape, the close button and the backdrop closed the dialog at once; only Cancel asked. They now all ask first. Escape in the find box closes only the find box.
- **Keyboard users could not save.** In the code editor, Tab indents and Escape then Tab is the way out, but Escape closed the whole dialog. Escape in the code is now left to the code editor.

## Table

- **Merged cells broke the row and column commands.** A new row came out a cell short, a new column went in at different places in different rows, and Delete Column deleted a merged cell along with its text. The commands now work on a grid of which cell covers each row and column (`table/src/tableGrid.ts`).
- **New cells next to header cells were data cells.** For example, adding a column put a `` into ``.
- **The shortcuts were the browsers' own keys.** Mod+Shift+R is hard reload in Chrome and Firefox (Reader in Safari), and Mod+Shift+C opens the DevTools inspector. They are now **Mod+Shift+Enter** (add row below) and **Mod+Alt+Enter** (add column right). They also used to work only after the table toolbar had been shown once. The tooltips name the new keys, and the "Add row above" tooltip no longer claims the row-below shortcut. The docs page is updated.

## Lists

- **Switching a list off joined the items into one paragraph** (`
a
b
`) in every browser. Each item now becomes a paragraph again.
- **Switching between bullets and numbers** converted item by item, and Chromium wrapped each item in a `font-family` span. The whole list is now switched.
- **Lists get word-processor keys:**
  - Tab nests an item under the one before it; Shift+Tab moves a nested item out. Shift+Tab on a top-level item still moves focus out of the editor.
  - Enter in an empty item, and Backspace at the start of an item, move a nested item out one level or turn a top-level one into a paragraph. This also fixes Firefox making a `
` when you leave a list.
- **The list shortcuts never ran.** With Shift held, `event.key` is `*` or `&`, so Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+8 and +7 never matched. `KeyboardShortcutManager` now falls back to the physical key (`event.code`) when a modifier is held.

## Undo and selection

- **The core lost the selection when it sanitized.** `` replaced the content and then put back a range that pointed into the removed nodes, so the selection fell to the start of the document. Chromium fires `input` halfway through its list command, so after turning paragraphs into a list, the next list command changed only the first item. The selection is now restored on the same characters.
- **In Safari, each list command took two undo steps.** WebKit's own report of the change and the plugin's clean-up were recorded separately. A second report of the same change that comes straight after the first now replaces it.
- **A paste was not an undo step of its own** in `` or React. Undo took it back together with the words typed before it. With `paste.keepFormatting`, pasted HTML was not recorded at all, and no `input` event or `onChange` fired.

## Link

- **Every link got `target="_self"`.** It's no longer written for links that open in the same tab.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Behaviour changes:**
  - The table shortcuts moved to new keys.
  - Tab, Enter and Backspace inside list items now act as described above.
  - Switching list type now changes the whole list.
- **Not changed:** the core ignores plugins' `keymap` fields. Only its own shortcut list and listeners that plugins add themselves run. So the indent plugin's Tab binding has never done anything. The list plugin installs its own listener.
- **Changesets:** 11 files, all patch, for `@editora/plugins`, the five plugin packages, `@editora/core` and `@editora/react`.

## Checks

- **CI replayed locally:** lint, typecheck, build, `check:ui-size`, `build:types`, `verify:packages`, `npm test` (713 plugin DOM tests), `test:core:unit`, `test:server-import` and `test:packages` all pass. The UI, libs and React 19 jobs were not replayed (those packages are untouched).
- **`check:plugins-size`:** two plugins grew, so their budgets are raised to the measured size plus 10%, as the script's `--update` writes it. `ListPlugin` went from about 3.3 to 4.3 KB gzipped (the list keys). `CodePlugin` went from 57.3 to 57.7 KB (the source-view formatter and the discard prompt).
- **Browsers:** every fix was driven in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit on the web component. The paste fix, the list keys and the list shortcut were also checked in the React editor.

author: jannef
body:
Three uniques of the class and race list, each in the drop pool (`pool = true`) and placed nowhere but the test world's quarry (south wall of the arrival room), with three new powers read in one place, `world/combat/struck.rs` (asked by `World::resolve` for an attack rolled against Defence that hit, after Negate, before the damage):

- **Hǣrsceorp** (`haersceorp`, padded coat, item level 24): Featherweight 50, Nimble 4 (+4 Dodge), Reinforced −1 (the coat's Armour 1 written to 0), of the Ox 4, of Vitality 12, of Stillness 4; `counts_as_unarmoured = true` (`Actor::wears_body_armour` says no: Mage armour, Step of the wind/Fleet). **Pain** power: a hit that does damage gives 1 ki, a critical 2, up to the pool's maximum; nothing without a ki pool.
- **The Kettle Hat** (`kettle_hat`, iron helm, item level 12): Featherweight −67 (2,505 g, the design's 2.5 kg; said "67% heavier"), Hardened 3, of the Ox 4; no ward. **Ring** power: any hit, soaked to nothing too, makes a clang (new `SoundKind::Clang`, `noise::Act::Clang`, `n` in the dump's sound layer) 20 cells × `STEP_LOSS` loud (a critical twice, capped at `MAX_LOUDNESS`), says so, and every actor beside the wearer, friend or foe, that fails a Toughness check (difficulty 15, `World::resists`) is Staggered; never the wearer.
- **Scarhide** (`scarhide`, item level 30): Reinforced 2, Hale 20, of the Ox 4, of Health 3. **Scars** power: every critical suffered draws (`unique/scar/<wearer>`) +1 Armour, +1 max hp, or +1 Toughness, kept on the stack (`Stack::scars`, saved, left out while none, valid only on a unique), read by `Mods::add_magic` like those affixes; no cap. The player is told; the identified description counts them ("It bears 5 scars.").

Finnish for every new line (`uniques.*`, `noise.heard_clang`, `describe.does_armour_less`, the three uniques' phrase and lore). Wiki: `wiki/src/magic-items.md` (the three powers, the unarmoured note) and the generated uniques table (`xtask/src/wiki/uniques.rs`: the powers' exact words, `counts_as_unarmoured`). Docs: `docs/dev/magic-items.md`, `docs/dev/enchanting.md`, `docs/dev/cli.md` (sound layer), `spec/11-magic.md`.

## Decisions the issues left open

- **Scarhide's base is a leather jerkin, not a hide tunic.** The hide tunic is clothing with no `kind` (#1173), and magic cannot sit on a kindless base (`Magic::check`, `Mods::add_magic`, the description all need it). The leather jerkin is the lightest hide body armour with a kind (Armour 1, Protection 1, 3.5 kg); with Reinforced 2 its Armour is 3.
- **A unique is never trimmed to its capacity** (`content/level.rs::hand_made`). Hǣrsceorp's six affixes cannot fit a padded coat by any make (a cloth body has no ornament and no binding material but silk's +1; Masterwork would add +3 Armour the design forbids), and a make on the Kettle Hat or Scarhide would add Protection or Armour past the owner's numbers. So a unique holds every affix its table sets; `capacity_tests.rs::hand_made_items_are_never_trimmed` holds that for uniques, and Appraise says "It bears all it can." of a unique past its capacity. No shipped unique changes (all fitted already).
- **`of_the_tortoise=4 (Toughness)`** is Natural armour in the data; the issue's label and "a hair shirt turns nothing" say Toughness, so Hǣrsceorp has `of_the_ox=4`.
- **Armour "written to 0"** is `reinforced=-1`, a unique's penalty (new line `describe.does_armour_less`, "−1 to Armour"), as the Grandmother's Dodge −2.
- **Weight 2,500 g** is `featherweight=-67`, a penalty said "67% heavier" (the curse's existing words): 1,500 × 1.67 = 2,505 g.
- **The Kettle Hat's critical "Staggers for two turns"**: the power gives twice the degrees, but Staggered is `max = 1` (one slowed action, refresh), so in play a critical's din staggers as long as any; its clang still carries twice as far (capped at 30 cells). The Toughness check's difficulty (15) is mine; the issue named none.
- **Ring's loudness** is `cells × STEP_LOSS` (200 for 20 cells): heard 20 cells off by the keenest ear, a little less by a duller one.
- All three join the drop pool (the consolidated list marks the race uniques "(pool)"; the class ones have item levels and no placement), placed in the quarry as the pool's others are.
- Pain, Scars, and Ring answer attacks rolled against Defence (a blow, a shot, a throw), not traps, spells, breath, or blasts, as Negate does.

## Verified

- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask docs-check`, `cargo xtask lang --check --strict fi`, `cargo xtask wiki` and `--check-links` (read the generated uniques rows and the edited page).
- New tests `world/combat/struck_tests.rs`: Hǣrsceorp counts as no body armour, Armour 0, Protection 0, Dodge +4; Pain pays 1 or 2 ki over 200 seeds, stops at the maximum, gives no pool to one without; the Kettle Hat's clang heard 17 cells down a hall and by those beside, Staggered on most of those beside (Toughness 10 against 15) and never its wearer or the far one, nothing without it; Scarhide takes a scar only on a critical, each of the three kinds moving exactly its number, valid and kept across a save; scars without end and their description line (only once identified); loot never makes these powers or scars. `unique_values_tests`, the pool lists, and the unique roster updated.
- Replay: `--scenario showcase --actions "travel:quarry move:S*4 pickup move:E move:E pickup move:E move:E pickup identify equip:body:b equip:head:c resource:ki wait*3"` (written out step by step), `replay --create` then `replay --verify`: ok, 19 steps. `dump --layers inventory,equipment,messages` shows the three (`Hǣrsceorp, a padded coat (Dv +4, Pv 0) (2 kg) (holds 6/2)`, `Kettle Hat, an iron helm (Dv +0, Pv 4) (2.5 kg)`, `Scarhide, a leather jerkin (Dv +3, Pv 1) (3.5 kg)`), worn: hp 38, ki 9 at most.
- Nothing visible changed but text (messages, descriptions): no capture.

Golden entries: none. No manifest entry shows the quarry (`tests/golden/manifest/*.toml`), and the new powers draw only on their own keyed stream (`unique/scar/<wearer>`) or `drain/resist/<key>` when a ring goes off, so no other fight's draws move.

Closes #2115
Closes #2127
Closes #2137

body:
## Summary

- Integrates Hospiq (open-source hotel PMS) into the existing Damview Resort Next.js webapp, customized for a Zimbabwe lodge
- Adds full admin system: dashboard, rooms, guests, check-in/checkout, billing (nightly + hourly), reservations, food menu, orders (KOT kanban), restaurant tables, staff management, analytics, reports, cash reconciliation
- Public QR-based food ordering for rooms and tables (`/order/[roomNumber]`, `/order/table/[tableNumber]`)
- Role-based access: superadmin, admin, manager, cashier, kitchen
- Supabase migrations for both website and PMS schemas with RLS policies
- Offline support with IndexedDB cache and service worker
- TypeScript types generated from live Supabase project

## Key decisions

- PMS activities table named `pms_activities` to avoid conflict with website's `website_activities`
- Old admin pages moved to `admin-damview-backup/` — the new `(admin)` route group replaces them
- Zimbabwe localization: USD currency, EcoCash/Bank Transfer payment modes, 15% VAT
- `requireAuth()` server action guard with role-based access control
- Redis-backed versioned caching via `getOrSetVersionedCache()`

## Setup required

1. Add `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` to `.env.local`
2. Optionally set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` for QR code generation
3. Create first superadmin user via `/admin/setup`

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes (0 errors outside backup files)
- [ ] Admin login flow → staff profile setup → dashboard loads
- [ ] Room check-in → guest billing → checkout flow
- [ ] QR order page renders for occupied room
- [ ] Order appears on KOT kanban board
- [ ] Role-based nav: superadmin sees all pages, cashier sees subset

author: tekulvw
body:
On mag-test, now on the PostgreSQL character store, Medius, MAPS and every `mag-admin character-store` call print:

```
Cannot load library libgssapi_krb5.so.2
Error: libgssapi_krb5.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The cause is Npgsql's default `GssEncryptionMode=Prefer`. It tries GSSAPI encryption before TLS, and the image has no GSSAPI library. Connections built from the CNPG secret directory now set `GssEncryptionMode = Disable`; TLS (`Require`, or `VerifyFull` with the CA) still protects them.

**Test (synthetic):** `postgres character store connections from a secret directory use TLS without GSSAPI` builds the connection string from invented secret files and checks host, port, database, `SslMode.Require` and `GssEncryptionMode.Disable`.

author: sjawhar-agent[bot]
body:
A pull request's filter generation is now measured against the first parent of the merge commit its run checked out: main as GitHub merged the branch into it. Before, it was measured against the pull_request event's own `base.sha`, the commit the branch is based on. That is older than the first parent whenever main has moved since, and it then counted main's own merged commits as part of the pull request's change.

## What it cost

The generation compares the base tree's filters with this tree's when the change touches a file the filters are computed with, and makes each filter that differs `'**'`. Against the event's `base.sha`, the diff to the merge commit also holds every commit main merged since the branch's base. Over the 149 successful pull-request `changes` jobs of ci.yaml runs created 2026-11-26 03:31-05:30 UTC:

- 98 had a `base.sha` older than the merge commit's first parent.
- 35 counted at least one of main's own files as a file the change touches.
- In 21 of those, every file counted was main's, none the pull request's own. Each ran the base tree's generation (17.8-19.6 s) for main's files alone: 444 s of step time.
- In those 21 runs, the filters main's commits had moved were `'**'` and started jobs no file of the pull request reaches: **474 job-minutes (530 billed)**. They include the browser suite's pull-request lane (7-9 jobs a run), dispatch-ui, envoy-infra-build, docs, plugin-pack, and on one pull request with the `lane:dispatch_browser` label the full browser lane twice (110 and 115 min). To count, each forced filter was matched against the pull request's own files (paths-filter's list from the API) with the engine's own `PathsFilter` over that run's computed filters: a filter that matches none of them selected its job only because it was forced.
- This branch's parent shows it too: #5649's second run (job 139795756572) was measured against f69d69d2 after main had moved on, counted 24 files as touched and forced 24 of 105 filters.

## What changes

- The changes job's base step, now "Find the commit this run's change is measured against", runs on `pull_request` as well as on a dispatch of a branch. It runs `.github/scripts/edited-migrations-base.sh`, which already gives envoy-go-build's migration check the first parent of the commit a pull request's run checked out, for the same reason.
- `CI_FILTERS_BASE`, and the key of the base's cached filters (#5649), read `github.event.merge_group.base_sha || steps.base.outputs.sha`.
- Places of the router that read `pull_request.base.sha`: the generation's `CI_FILTERS_BASE` and the cache key, both changed. The paths-filter step takes no base on a pull request (it reads GitHub's list of the pull request's files), so it is unchanged. Outside the changes job, `ci-job-tool-fallback.yaml` checks out the base tree for the tool proof and `check-pr-text.sh` reads the commits from the base for the pr-title check; neither selects jobs, and both are left as they are.
- `ci_router_outputs.py` takes `--pull-base`, the event's own base, apart from `--base`, the commit the base step finds. ci-router-outputs.test.sh holds a pull request to the first parent. Two new broken copies of ci.yaml fail it: a generation step that reads the event's `base.sha` first, and a base step that runs on no pull request. The existing copy whose generation step reads no base now fails the pull-request case as well.
- `ci-caches-changes.yaml` (#5649) looks the `ci-filters` entry up under the same key text as ci.yaml's restore, so rule 11 keeps holding the two to one key.
- envoy-go-build's migration check is left as it is. It runs `edited-migrations-base.sh` itself and on a merge group compares with the entry's first parent, which is not the group's `base_sha`. No output of the changes job hands the base on; the first job that needs one adds it with its reader.
- Notes: `ci.md#the-commit-a-change-is-measured-against`.

## Proof

On 11 open pull requests' merge commits (build-cluster Jobs, 4 CPUs), each head's own `ci-filters-generate.sh` was run against the event's `base.sha` (before) and against the merge commit's first parent (after). The filters the paths-filter step reads, the computed filters, their inputs list and the step's GITHUB_OUTPUT were compared by sha256. For a stale head, the two base trees' own filters were generated as well, to see which filters main's commits between the two bases moved.

| head | base.sha vs first parent | files counted as touched (before / after) | filters `'**'` (before / after) | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #5567, #5598, #5616 | same | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | identical |
| #5608 | same | 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 | identical |
| #5576 (touches computation inputs itself) | same | 8 / 8 | 3 / 3 | identical: ci_ok_test, envoy_go and envoy_go_race stay `'**'` |
| #5564, #5651 | older | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | identical: main's commits since touched no input |
| #5609 | older | 1 / 0 | 6 / 0 | 6 filters fewer, all moved by main (#4369, ci_job_reads.py) |
| #5636 | older | 1 / 0 | 2 / 0 | 2 filters fewer, both moved by main (#4369) |
| #5585 | older | 23 / 0 | 25 / 0 | 25 filters fewer, all moved by main (#5173, #5221, #5493, #5505, #5514, #5577, #5602, #5605) |
| #5631 (touches computation inputs itself) | older | 20 / 1 | 22 / 4 | 18 filters fewer, all moved by main (#5493, #5505, #5605); its own daemon_go_tests, docs, plugin_pack and private_names_port stay `'**'` |

Every filter that is `'**'` only against the event's `base.sha` is one whose patterns differ between the two base trees, so main's own commits moved it. On every head, none was left outside that set. Where the base is the first parent already, nothing changes. A pull request that touches a computation input itself still has each filter it moves forced: #5576 and #5631 are the gate-input controls.

This pull request's own run shows the step working: changes job 139807499079 found e7a7d580, the first parent of its merge commit 2ddfe795, in 0.4 s and handed it to the generation. The generation counted 2 files of its own as touched and found 0 of 104 filters different.

CI run 45859842972 at c2e20a78ded (rebased onto main 9abe4e53 after #5649 merged; range-diff marks both commits '=', and the PR's diff is unchanged but for hunk offsets) is green (47 jobs success, 25 skipped, ci-ok success): ci-router-outputs.test.sh 161/0, check-ci-filters.test.sh 1000/0, edited-migrations-base 56/0.

The changes job took 165 s (job 140047687026), against 46 s for the merge group at this PR's merge base 9abe4e53 (job 140032978613). The difference is Setup Bun: 136 s, its download of `bun-linux-aarch64.zip` from GitHub's release host running from 16:33:34 to 16:35:49 UTC. This PR does not change that step, and it took 2 s p50 and at most 3 s in the other 236 changes jobs read today. The job's other steps took 29 s. The checkout took 2 s after a `changes-git` hit. The generation took 15 s: it read 9abe4e53's cached filters in place of generating the base tree, because this PR is now measured against the first parent and the push of that commit filled its entry.

### Harness cases renamed

These 8 (case, check) pairs of ci-router-outputs.test.sh pass at the merge base and are absent at the head because they were renamed; each passes at the head under its new name.
- Case "the filter generation measures a dispatched branch against its merge base with main, as a merge group against its base" is now "the filter generation measures a change against the commit it lands onto". It covers pull requests too, and its 6 checks keep their names but one.
- In that case, "a pull request: its base" is now "a pull request: the first parent the base step finds, not the event's own base". The expectation changed: a pull request is measured against the first parent.
- Case "a generation step handed no merge base fails the branch case" is now "... fails the branch and pull-request cases". Its 2 checks keep their names, and a third, "nor does a pull request", is new.

## Verification records

author: alih-b
body:
Fixes #129

Adds an opt-in that lets page fetch reach `198.18.0.0/15`, the fake-IP range that Clash, sing-box, Surge and similar clients answer DNS with. It is off by default.

- `Josty(allow_fake_ip=True)`, `JOSTY_ALLOW_FAKE_IP=1` (an explicit argument wins over the variable) and `--allow-fake-ip` on both `josty` and `josty fetch`.
- `validate_public_url` skips the `is_global` test for an IPv4 address inside that one network when allowed. Loopback, RFC 1918, link-local and metadata addresses, `100.64.0.0/10`, multicast, IPv6 (including `::ffff:198.18.0.1`) and non-HTTP schemes are checked exactly as before. Redirect hops use the same setting.
- When the blocked address is in the range, the error now says so and names the setting, e.g. `... blocked (198.18.0.1 is in 198.18.0.0/15, the fake-IP range of proxy and VPN clients; set JOSTY_ALLOW_FAKE_IP=1 or pass --allow-fake-ip to allow it)`. Other blocks read as before.
- Documented in the README limits section, the SKILL flag table and the AGENTS.md SSRF invariant, which now names this single opt-in.

Checked live on a machine whose resolver returns `198.18.0.1`: `josty fetch https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html` fails with the new message, and with `--allow-fake-ip` returns 3,779 characters.

Tests (`tests/test_fake_ip.py`, DNS stubbed): blocked by default with the new message; both ends of the range pass when allowed; 11 other addresses stay blocked with the setting on; the edges of the range are exact; schemes stay blocked; redirect hops; env variable values; argument beats env; the flags parse. 24 of the 27 fail without the change.

`pytest -q`: 619 passed. `ruff check .`: clean. Live `josty "python packaging"` emits valid JSON.

body:
## Summary
Fixes the macOS spinning beach ball / Aqua Tk deadlock in Ultra7's Preferences panel (`dev_tools/ultra7/`).

### Changes
- Make `PreferencesDialog` a non-modal single-instance window instead of using `grab_set()` + `wait_window()`, which deadlocks Cocoa/Aqua Tk when opened from native menus.
- Replace native `ttk.OptionMenu` popups with themed readonly `ttk.Combobox` controls.
- Guard `ttk.Style.theme_use("clam")` so switching themes or clicking **Apply** doesn't tear down ttk layouts while dialogs are open.
- Put the Live Preview `tk.Text` inside a fixed-pixel container (`pack_propagate(False)`) so font-size changes don't trigger resize loops on a non-resizable window.
- Cache installed `tkfont.families()` once.

## Verification
- `cd dev_tools/ultra7 && bash check.sh`: `ruff`, `bandit`, `mypy` (37 source files), and **159 unit tests** pass.
- Verified live open, theme switching, font-size changes, Apply, Reset, and Cancel on macOS.

## Summary
Packed line diffs now handle exact hash collisions with less time and allocator traffic. Exact equality, shortest scripts, and both owned buffers remain unchanged.

The fallback stores four octets per list cell instead of one. Byte lengths and partial words preserve trailing NULs and all octet values. No cost moves into the scan or verification stages.

| Collision fallback | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median time | 237.535708 ms | 55.285292 ms |
| Allocator requests | 8,671,220 | 1,659,172 |
| Requested bytes | 93,503,680 | 20,627,920 |

- `python3 text/bench/collision.py`: small inputs first, five paired samples, collision detection, 200 shortest-script changes, arbitrary-octet round trips, and owned-buffer checks.

### What changed
- Added a manual-only workflow bound to the protected GitHub `staging` environment.

`SUPABASE_STAGING_URL`, `SUPABASE_STAGING_SECRET_KEY`, and `STORAGE_TEST_OWNER_ID`. Missing values are reported by name only and block acceptance. No credential values are logged.

author: aiedwardyi
body:
## What the user saw
Settings > Usage and Settings > Connections: after **Sign Out** on Codex, the row stayed, showing "Not signed in" / "Signed out." with Sign In.

## Why
Sign Out on an **added** account already logs out and retires it, so its row goes away. The row that stayed is the engine's **own login** (the base, e.g. `~/.codex`). `AccountService.list()` always lists the base, so a signed-out base kept a Sign In row next to the other accounts.

## Fix (shared store + board, no per-screen filter)
- `server/accounts.ts`: `accounts.json` gets an optional `signedOut` list of base ids the user signed out. `list()` marks such a base row `userSignedOut`.
- `server/account-lifecycle.ts`: a successful user Sign Out of a base saves the mark: the plain sign-out here, and the Main hand-over drain through `finishDrain`. A base sign-in that completes clears the mark.
- `server/usage-board.ts`: a marked base that is not signed in folds into the board's existing `duplicates` list (#2139) while another account of its engine is listed. Usage, the quick usage card and Connections already hide by that list, and the board is pushed to every device and the relay link.
- A login that expired or a missing folder (#2100) sets no mark, so its row keeps Sign In. A lone base keeps today's signed-out engine state.
- Main hand-over goes to the first signed-in account (`/destination`); see Gate fixes for its order. Running workers are untouched: the existing turn, pane and bot guards still refuse the sign-out.

## Proof
- Red on 4c9d99684: 4 new tests fail for Codex and Claude, non-Main and Main (`a user Sign Out removes the account from Usage and Connections`). Green after: 10/10.
- Targeted suites (account-*, usage-board, AccountConnections*, EnginesSettings, UsageRedo, store.signed-out*, engine-sign-in-path, instance-sign-out-route): 30 files, 962 tests pass. `tsc -b` and `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` are clean.
- Phone (390 px) with stub CLIs and scratch data: before, Codex 1 stays "Signed out." with Sign In. After, only Codex 2 is listed in Connections and Usage, and it is Main.
- Merges cleanly with #2218 (`git merge-tree`).

## Notes
- An existing signed-out base from before this fix has no mark, so it still shows until it is signed in and out once. The signed-out row's ... menu has no Remove.
- An older Wink reading an `accounts.json` that has `signedOut` fails its strict parse, the same as `defaults` and `drains` did when they were added. The key is dropped once it is empty.

## Remove on a leftover signed-out row (be7e43585)
- A row that reads "Signed out." with Sign In now has a ... menu on desktop too (phone already had one), with **Remove** at the bottom in the same button style. Signed-in rows keep Sign Out and get no Remove. There is no confirm step, matching Sign Out.
- Remove sends the same `POST /api/accounts/:id/sign-out` request: a base is marked and leaves Usage and Connections through the board, an added account is retired, and a Main hands over through `/destination`. The existing guards still refuse it while a turn, pane or bot uses the account.
- Strings: `accounts.remove` is "Remove" in English and "제거" in Korean.
- Red on d80499133: on desktop the signed-out row has no menu, and on phone its menu has no Remove. Green after.
- Usage rows have no ... menu, so Remove is in Connections. Removing there clears the row from Usage on every device.

## Signed-out row layout (a9b33d770)
- A signed-out row now uses the same head as a signed-in row: name, then "Signed out." where the address goes, with the controls in the head's one slot.
- **Desktop:** Remove and Sign In sit side by side where Sign Out sits on a signed-in row. There is no ... button, as on signed-in desktop rows. The two rows are the same height, 54.8 px against 55.8 px, and the 1 px is the divider.
- **Phone:** Sign In sits beside the ... button, and the menu (Name, Remove) opens with the same spacing as a signed-in row's menu (Name, Sign Out).
- Only the layout changed. A row with no name from the usage board keeps the old Signed out / Sign In line.

## Gate fixes (0ac3a8b59, on review-base e0d4abc18 with #2218)
- **A later login keeps its Sign In row.** Any confirmed login on a base now retires the user Sign Out mark, including one made outside Wink (`registry.onProbed` in `AccountLifecycle`). Before, only a sign-in started from Wink cleared it, so a replacement login that later expired vanished from both screens.
- **A busy worker refuses Sign Out with no added accounts too.** Base Sign Out always runs the same block + turn/helper/pane check. Before, it ran only when some account was saved anywhere in the profile. A lone base still ends unblocked after sign-out, as before.
- **Remove only where it clears the row.** A lone signed-out base (no other account of its engine listed) offers no Remove in Connections, and on phone the ... button shows only when its menu has something in it. The server refuses (409, "This engine's only account is already signed out") a sign-out of a lone base that is not signed in, instead of answering 200 and leaving the row.
- **Main follows the saved Usage order.** `/destination` picks the first ready account in the saved order (`config.json` `usageOrder`, #2218), the order Usage and Connections show. Accounts not in the saved order come after, in store order.
- Tests (added first): red on a9b33d770's code for all four, and the busy-worker case also red on review-base (200, not 409). Green after: account-lifecycle + Connections 157/157, 43 related files 1580/1580. `tsc -b` and `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` clean.
- `account-routes.test.ts` lone-base sign-in: a sign-out of the blocked (signed-out) lone base now answers 409 instead of 404.

## Gate fixes 2 (ced4b8fc0, 0c431890e)
- **An empty shell no longer blocks lone-account Sign Out.** The terminal host counts a pane of unknown ownership only when Wink sent it a command, a worker CLI started in it, its shell is running a command, or its shell has no prompt marks to show it idle. A Windows bot shell marks every prompt, so an idle empty one is no worker on any login. A Linux or macOS bot shell has no marks and stays unknown (Sign Out refuses, as before). Sign Out uses the same single guard as before.
- **The browser-only launch (`pnpm dev`) can sign out its lone account.** With no terminal bridge no bot pane can exist, so the guard finds none (the same reading as `liveWorkerRuns` "no-host"). An unreachable host still refuses with 409 `host-unknown` and keeps the login. A busy worker still refuses with 409.
- **A replacement login shows while Wink stays open.** After a user Sign Out or a Main hand-over, the base stays blocked, and a blocked base answered every refresh and rescan from its old signed-out check. A refresh or rescan now reads a base the user signed out again. A confirmed login there lifts the block and the Sign Out mark, so the row lists and keeps Sign In when it later expires. A drain, a pending sign-in or a running sign-out skips this, and a base blocked by a turn's sign-out error keeps today's behavior.
- Tests (added first, red on c91392dbd): the host's empty-shell count, lone Sign Out with no host, and the replacement login after Sign Out (refresh, rescan) and after hand-over. Green after. Live with the production terminal host and bridge (fixture PTY) and a real server: empty shell 200, unknown-owner worker pane 409 `host-unknown`, busy managed worker 409, no host 200.
- Two assertions that pinned "no bridge = unknown" now pin "unreachable host = unknown" instead (`account-lifecycle.test.ts`, `worker-launch.test.ts`).

body:
Serves **M64** (bug rounds), row **B27**, from Niclas: under lava or slime there should be no see-through window up out of the surface. Only water should have one.

## Two causes
1. **Water's window was drawn in lava and slime.** `eye_water_body` (`plugins/brush/app/bsp_liquids.cpp`) took any liquid leaf (water, slime or lava) as being in water. It then picked the nearest water body whose level stood over the eye. So a player in lava or slime, with a pool's level higher anywhere on the map, was drawn as being under that pool, with water's view from below and Snell's window onto the world over it. The eye is now in a water body only in a water leaf, as its comment already said.
2. **Slime's own view from below had a window.** `liquid_under.wgsl` showed the world over the surface through Snell's window. The surface from below is now the slime itself, with its scum's dark patches on it. Lava already had none.

## Evidence
- `tests/brush_bsp_liquids_test.cpp`: the fog fixture's pit leaf is set to water, slime, lava or empty, with a water pool's level over it. Water finds the pool; lava, slime and air find none. Without the fix, `an_eye_in_lava_or_slime_is_under_no_water` fails on both checks.
- `gpu-slime` from-below, before and after (`--tag=before`, `--compare=before`): "up at the surface" no longer shows the sky's window, for both the toxic slime and the gel. The pictures are in the project's files (bug-rounds/b27); the lab's caption is updated.

body:
**Harness tracking (for SEQ harness's tooling — teammates can skip this block)**

Opened by the harness after TUI-097's Builder settled `done` (HARN-197) — no GitHub credential ever entered the dispatched run.

- Mission: `projects/seq-tui/missions/TUI-097-castable-chief-cast-cue-in-the-terminal-client-presentation-a3.md`
- Report: `projects/seq-tui/reports/TUI-097-report.md`
- Builder run: `TUI-097-builder-1795683802`

---

### What changed
The terminal client's Target panel now shows what a monster (or another player) is casting: the move's display name, who it is aimed at (`you` or a name) and a countdown. For Brow Breaker it also states the 2.5 m reach and where the target stands (in reach / OUT of reach, as a prediction). When the cast ends the panel says how: landed (or missed), interrupted, stunned, or out of reach. The combat log lines for a monster's broken cast say why from the event's reason.

### Why
The castable Chief experiment (Brow Breaker, a 2 s wind-up) needs players to see what is cast, on whom, how long is left, whether they are in reach and how it ended. This is presentation only: no gameplay, server or content change; nothing is enabled.

### How it was tested
Unit tests in `model` and `screen` driven by a copy of seq's four-case wire records (`testdata/castable/castable-chief.txt`): delayed start, stale start, resync of a drifted local clock, interruption mid-cast, each ending, and the prediction keeping the cue. Six golden screens at 80x24 and 140x45 from a new recorded log. `TestClientReachMatchesTheWorldPack` (scenario) validates the client-side 2.5 m against the pinned seq-world pack's `range_mm` for `chief-brow-breaker`; that pack still has `cast_ms: 0` for the move, so only the range is checked. The repo's `make verify` ran at the finish. No terminal UI was launched; the visual result is what the goldens show.

### Risk and rollout
Client-only and additive: the cue appears only on a `cast_started` from someone other than the character, which no live server sends for the Chief while the variant is off. The Target panel can grow by up to three rows when there is room (Nearby keeps 5); on a short panel the cue replaces the fight line. The reach is a client-side constant, labelled so in the UI; if content changes the range, the reach test fails and says so.

## Summary

This is owner feedback E1: tickets get the same type, priority and labels as a Missions issue, with the same shape ([ADR 0058](docs/decisions/0058-ticket-type-priority-labels.md)).

- **Fields:**
  - `type` is `task`, `bug`, `feature` or `epic`.
  - `priority` runs from 0 (critical) to 4 (backlog), and the CLI also accepts `P0`–`P4`.
  - `labels` holds up to 16 unique lowercase labels. The `luuna-ticket-` prefix is reserved for Luuna's delivery marker.
  - All three are left out of the record when they hold their defaults (task, 2, none), so existing tickets keep their exact bytes and hashes.
- **Everywhere a ticket goes:**
  - the domain type, `schemas/ticket.schema.json` and `@luuna/api-client`
  - `POST …/tickets` and `PUT /tickets/{id}`
  - `lu create-ticket` and `lu edit-ticket`, with `--type`, `--priority`, `--label` (repeatable or comma-separated) and `--clear-labels`
  - the desktop ticket form, editor and list
  - the terminal ticket view (Type, Priority, Labels) and the board cards (a "Triage" line when a field isn't at its default)
- **Missions-backed projects:** these are the issue's own Missions fields, not part of Luuna's description envelope.
  - Delivery passes `--type`, `--priority` and `--labels`, with the marker first.
  - Edits use `--set-labels` and keep the marker.
  - Reconcile reads the fields back and drops the marker.
  - The ledger request names a field only when it isn't at its default, so an uncertain edit recorded before this change still matches its retry.
- An edit to these fields advances the ticket revision like any other edit. That matches Missions, where any change already changes the source fingerprint that plans bind to.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passes.

  - New tests: domain bounds and defaults, a runtime API test (create, refusals, an edit that only changes triage fields), a Missions test (delivery, `--set-labels` edit, clearing to defaults, an edit that changes nothing) and CLI flag parsing.
  - The real export and import test now carries all three fields through Missions on both sides.
  - The Missions tests marked `--ignored` also pass with `--include-ignored`.
- `node scripts/check-contracts.mjs`: passes (29 schema checks, catalog and traces).
- `node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs`: passes.

author: heyaibi
body:
Fixes #752

This change updates the config write tests in `crates/clio/src/setup_config_tests.rs`. It renames the test that used to be called `write_reports_flush_failure_without_replacing` to `write_reports_backup_failure_when_a_file_blocks_the_parent`, and it now asserts the backup error that really occurs. A file occupied the parent directory slot, so opening the config path for backup failed with "not a directory" before any flush could run.

The old test never reached a flush failure. This change adds a new `write_reports_flush_failure_without_replacing` test that seeds a readable config, creates a writable backups directory, and makes the parent directory read-only. Backup succeeds, the atomic write fails, and the test checks that the write reports "failed to write" and that the old config survives. No production code changed.

Verification actually run: the two target tests passed under nextest with temporary, uncommitted workarounds for two pre-existing macOS compile defects, #778 and #779. `make lint` and `make quick BASE=origin/master` failed on those same defects. The local release rebuild needed a temporary, reverted workaround for the pre-existing macOS compile defect #778. After that rebuild, `make precommit` passed locally with all eight hooks green. CI owns the Linux verdict.

Not run: the full suite on Linux, and any check that needs the macOS compile defects #778 and #779 fixed. Those defects predate this change and are not fixed here.

Risks: the new flush-failure test uses Unix permissions and is marked `#[cfg(unix)]`, so it does not run on Windows. The test restores the directory mode before it checks the config, which keeps the temporary directory removable.

Remaining step: CI must run the full suite on Linux and report the verdict.

Public-content confirmation: this change and this description contain only public repository material. No private paths, session records, credentials, or internal notes are included.

- taskpane.html carries no token. `OFFICE_TOKEN` is gone.
- New `ui/office_pair.py`. The panel calls `POST /office/pair` and shows a six-digit code. The app shows the same code in a prompt, and only the app's own window can answer it (launch-key token, `POST /api/office/pairs`). Once the user allows the code, the panel reads its session token once through its secret pairing id (`POST /office/pair/check`). The id travels in the body, never in the URL.
- When several requests are waiting, the app lists every code and tells the user to allow only the one their panel shows. At most 4 requests can wait at once, and each one expires after 2 minutes.
- The pairing routes take no token. A web page cannot use them because they require `application/json` and the panel's own Origin.
- Sessions live in memory and end when the app quits. The panel keeps its token in sessionStorage, never on disk. Credential storage is unchanged.
- A missing or bad panel token now gets a 401, and only a 401 makes the panel pair again. A chat the panel does not own still gets a 403.
- Settings > Office apps shows how many panels are connected and has a "Disconnect Office panels" button. Removing the add-in also disconnects them.
- The name-constrained local CA and the consent-gated trust step are unchanged.

**Tests**
- New `app/tests/test_sv_office_pair.py` (7 tests). It sends real HTTPS requests to the Office listener and HTTP requests to the app. With the old server.py and taskpane.html, a token scraped from the page answers 200 and the first test fails. With this change, every candidate string from the page and script gets a 401.
- `test_office.py` and `test_pr20_review.py` now get a panel token by pairing.
- `testkit/office_panel.js` takes the app link as a second argument and allows the code in the app's real prompt. A live run passes for Excel, Word, PowerPoint, outside Office, and too-old Office. The "office question demo" step fails the same way on the branch without this change, because the mock reports no `ask_user` tool. I ran the rest with that step left out.

**Known limits**
- A panel has to pair each time it is opened and each time the app restarts.
- A process that reads the Office webview's memory, or one whose code the user allows by mistake, can still use the panel routes.

author: sorte1
body:
Follow-up to #521.

- `remove-js-confuser-integrity`: `lock.integrity` wraps a function in a check that hashes another function's source text (cyrb53 over `toString()` with spaces and punctuation removed) and hangs on a mismatch, so any reformatted output used to hang. The pass hashes the checked function's source itself; when it gives the expected value it folds the check to `true` and drops the hash cache and the hash functions. README states the premise about the cache key.
- The string and global passes now accept `astScrambler`'s self-redefining helper (`function h(){h=function(){}}`) and the minified global mapper (`return g.console`).

js-confuser matrix (safe/unsafe perfect, before -> after): lock-integrity 0/0 -> 7/9, pair-strings+scrambler 0/0 -> 7/9, pair-minify+globals 0/0 -> 7/9, pair-scrambler+globals 0/0 -> 7/9. Krunker byte-identical in both lanes; obfuscator-io and obfuscator-versions BASELINEs unchanged; obfuscator.io sweep default 0 fail, single layer 655/655, unsafe 9 fail as on main.

The Render service was crash-looping (502): a startup database failure killed the process before it listened. Now the server listens first, retries the database with backoff, and `/api/health` reports `database: ready|connecting|error` with a sanitised error. Also handles Neon idle-connection errors (which would crash an unhandled pool) and loads PGlite only when `DATABASE_URL` is unset.

관련 사건: matchharper/harper_incidents#139

## 문제
후보자가 "모든 연락을 멈춰 달라", "수신 거부"라고 해도 Harper 메일이 다 꺼지지 않았습니다. 채팅의 '모두 멈춤'(update_setting stop_all)은 프로필 공유만 끄고 외부 공고 추천은 켜 둔 채였습니다. "메일 그만"처럼 범위를 말하지 않은 요청은 범위를 먼저 묻고 설정을 바꾸지 않는 규칙 때문에, 답하지 않은 사람은 아무것도 꺼지지 않았습니다.

| 요청/상황 | Harper가 한 일 | 실제 결과 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 후보자 A, 11/25 "Please unsubscribe me" | stop_all 호출, 프로필 공유만 끔 (`src/lib/talentOnboarding/tools.ts:3945`, 고치기 전) | 외부 공고 추천이 켜진 채라 3일 주기 정기 점검이 11/28 07:03 KST에 그대로 예약됨 |
| 후보자 B, 11/14 "No more emails." → 범위를 묻자 "Just want to not receive another email from u again" | update_setting을 부르지 않고 "정기 검색이 메일을 안 보내게 했다"고만 답함 (규칙 `src/lib/llm/toolDescriptions.ts:259`, 고치기 전) | 설정이 그대로라 정기 점검이 3번 더 실행됨 |
| 후보자 C, 6/30 "더이상 이메일 보내지 마세요." | 외부 공고 추천만 꺼짐 (옛 메일 답장 처리) | 프로필 공유가 켜진 채라 회사 소개 메일 4통 (8/19~9/24) |

11/26 prod 기준: 중단을 요청했는데 덜 꺼진 사람 73명(stop_all을 했는데 외부 추천이 켜진 61명 + 수신 거부 요청이 반영 안 된 12명). 중단 요청 뒤 실제로 나간 메일은 6명에게 12통. 데이터는 이 PR과 별도로 11/26 18:10 KST에 SQL로 정리했습니다(61명 + 12명 설정을 '모두 멈춤' 상태로 바꿈. 확인 쿼리로 덜 꺼진 사람 0명).

출처: `talent_activity_events`(summary, changed_domains), `talent_setting`, `talent_agent_schedules`, `career_email_messages`

## As-is / To-be (expected)
| 상황 | As-is | To-be (expected) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stop_all | 프로필 공유만 끔(dont_share) | 설정 화면 '모두 멈춤'과 같은 함수(`resolveAccountSubscriptionUpdate`)로 외부 공고 추천과 프로필 공유를 같이 끔 (테스트로 확인) |
| 이미 dont_share인데 외부 추천이 켜진 사람이 다시 stop_all | 바뀌는 것 없음 | 외부 추천을 끔 (테스트로 확인) |
| "unsubscribe", "no more emails"처럼 범위 없는 중단 요청 | 범위를 묻고 설정은 그대로 | 바로 stop_all, 그 뒤 회사에서 오는 직접 제안은 계속 받을지 한 번 물음 (모델 판단이라 기대치. 도구 설명 문구는 테스트로 확인) |
| "외부 공고만 그만" | stop_external | 그대로 |
| 지금 이야기 중인 회사·기회·예약·질문에 대한 '그만' | 그 대상의 도구로 처리 | 그대로 (규칙 문구 유지) |
| resume | 둘 다 켬 | 그대로 (테스트로 확인) |

## 변경
- `src/lib/talentOnboarding/tools.ts`: stop_all이 `resolveAccountSubscriptionUpdate({ harperEnabled: false })` 결과를 써서 외부 공고 추천과 프로필 공유를 같이 끔. 바뀐 항목마다 활동 기록을 남김.
- `src/lib/llm/toolDescriptions.ts`, `src/lib/career/prompts/toolPolicyPrompt.ts`, `src/lib/career/prompts/cases/lifecyclePrompts.ts`, `src/lib/talentOnboarding/onboardingCompletionWrapup.ts`: 범위 없는 수신 거부·연락 중단은 되묻지 않고 stop_all. 외부 공고만 끄겠다고 좁힌 경우만 stop_external.
- `src/lib/talentOnboarding/updateSettingStopAll.test.ts`: 테스트 4개 추가.
- `AGENTS.md`의 11/26 지침 기록(범위 없는 중단 요청은 되묻지 않고 모두 멈춤)은 dev의 회사 메일 PR(#462) 기록과 같은 자리라 충돌해서, 이 PR에서는 되돌리고 배포 뒤 dev 대상 PR로 따로 올립니다. 이 PR이 바꾸는 파일은 위 6개뿐입니다.

커밋: stop_all 처리 수정, 되묻기 규칙 변경, 지침 기록과 그 되돌림.

## 확인
- 새 테스트 4개: 고치기 전 코드에서 3개 실패(stop_all 2개, 도구 설명 1개), 지금 4개 통과. resume 테스트는 전후 모두 통과.
- `tsc --noEmit` 통과.
- 관련 프롬프트 테스트(`toolPolicyPrompt.test.ts`, `lifecyclePrompts.test.ts`, `generalProvider.test.ts`, `guidance.test.ts`): `toolPolicyPrompt.test.ts`의 "document tools use paginated metadata…" 1개만 실패. 이 PR 전 코드에서도 같은 이유(`max_chars=4000` 문구)로 실패.
- 실행하지 못한 것: 실제 모델로 수신 거부 사례(범위 없는 "unsubscribe", "외부 공고만 그만", 특정 회사에 대한 "그만")를 돌리는 평가. 클라우드 환경의 LLM 키가 만료돼 돌리지 못했습니다.
- 그대로인 것: 옛 메일 답장 처리(harper_worker `email_reply/tools.py:4804`)도 stop_all이 프로필 공유만 끄지만, 10/26 이후 이 경로로 들어온 설정 변경이 0건이라 이 PR에서 다루지 않습니다.

## 요약

휴대폰·태블릿 등 터치가 기본인 기기(`pointer: coarse`)에서 제어 모드로 연결하면, 원격 화면 왼쪽 아래에 포인터 이동 조이스틱, 오른쪽 아래에 게임 패드 A/B 버튼처럼 둥근 **좌클릭**·**우클릭** 버튼을 표시합니다. 툴바에서 **터치 / 조이스틱** 입력 방식을 고를 수 있습니다. 웹사이트 버전은 1.5.0입니다.

## 변경 사항

- **조이스틱** (`lib/virtual-pointer.ts`, `components/touch-controls.tsx`)
  - 데드존과 기울기 제곱에 비례하는 속도로 가상 포인터를 움직이고, 화면 비율을 반영해 가로·세로 이동 속도를 맞춥니다. 최대 기울기에서 초당 화면 너비의 0.9배를 이동합니다.
  - Mac 화면 영상에는 커서가 포함되지 않아(`mss` 캡처) 포인터 위치를 화면에 따로 표시합니다.
- **좌·우클릭 버튼**: 가상 포인터 위치에서 기존 `pointer` down/up 이벤트를 보냅니다. 좌클릭을 누른 채 조이스틱을 움직이면 드래그, 빠르게 두 번 누르면 더블클릭입니다. **커넥터 변경이 필요 없습니다.**
- **입력 방식 선택** (`lib/touch-input-mode.ts`)
  - 터치: 조이스틱을 숨깁니다. 조이스틱(기본): 조이스틱과 버튼을 표시합니다.
  - 두 방식 모두 화면을 탭하면 그 위치를 클릭하고, 포인터 표시도 그 위치로 옮깁니다.
  - 모바일 툴바에서도 이름과 선택 상태가 보이는 두 칸 선택 버튼이며, 선택은 이 브라우저의 localStorage에 저장합니다.
- 컨트롤은 원격 화면 안에 그려 전체 화면에서도 보이고, 이벤트가 화면 탭이나 입력 해제로 번지지 않도록 막습니다.
- 영문 번역, README(한·영) 사용법, i18n 검사 대상 추가
- 웹사이트 버전 1.4.4 → 1.5.0 (호환되는 새 기능)

## 검증

- `pnpm test` 276개 통과(조이스틱 이동·입력 방식 저장 테스트 10개 추가), `pnpm typecheck` 통과, `pnpm build` 성공
- iPhone 13 에뮬레이션(세로·가로)에서 실제 멀티터치로 확인
  - 조이스틱 오른쪽 기울임 → 포인터가 오른쪽 끝까지 이동, y 고정
  - 좌클릭 버튼 유지 + 조이스틱 아래 → `좌↓ → 이동 → 좌↑` 드래그

author: eaknathsivakumar-glitch
body:
## Summary
Replace the todo API’s database-backed behavior with mock-only responses for demos and API exploration. Keep the same CRUD routes and validation, but make clear that changes are temporary and reset when the process restarts.
**Tasks:** 3 - **Estimated effort:** ~2-9 hours

## Background
The current Express API has persistent SQLite storage. This change makes it a lightweight mock API rather than a durable todo service, suitable for demos and clients that need predictable responses.

## Scope
| In scope | Out of scope |
|---|---|
| Preloaded mock todos, temporary in-process CRUD behavior, current endpoint contracts, validation, and tests | Database persistence, authentication, UI, and production-grade multi-user data |

## Sub-Tasks
| # | Task | Area | Effort | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Replace the data service with sample-backed mock behavior and remove unused SQLite/Drizzle modules and dependencies | API | M | - |
| 2 | Update API tests to cover mock CRUD responses, filtering, validation, and non-persistence after restart | Test | M | 1 |
| 3 | Run tests and available checks; confirm the preview setup still works | Test | S | 2 |

## Proposed Changes
| File / module | Action | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/todos.js` and todo fixtures | Modify | Serve sample todos and emulate create, update, delete, filtering, and bounded pagination using temporary in-process mock state. |
| `src/db/*` and `package.json` / lockfile | Delete / Modify | Remove the database bootstrap, schema, and dependencies no longer needed by the mock API. |
| `test/todos.test.js` | Modify | Verify CRUD responses, validation failures, list filtering/pagination, and that runtime changes do not survive a restart. |

**Design and technical decisions**
- Keep the existing `/api/v1/todos` route contract and use deterministic sample records.
- Mock mutations may affect responses during the current process, but all changes reset on restart; no SQLite file is used.
- Keep Zod request validation and the consistent API error format.

## Risks & Assumptions
- This API is now for demos/testing only; it must not be treated as a durable todo store.
- The API remains unauthenticated and should stay private unless access controls are added.

## Verification Plan
- [ ] All five routes return the planned mock response shapes and validation errors.
- [ ] List filtering and bounded pagination work against sample records.
- [ ] Mock changes reset when the service is recreated; no database dependency or storage remains.
- [ ] Project tests, JavaScript syntax checks, and preview configuration validation pass.

author: alaindargelas
body:
New checks for illegal code that sv-tests (ivtest + chapter-6) expects a tool to reject. They run on the parse tree after compilation, because the compiled model has already lost what they need. A compiled `enum_const` keeps only a folded value: its x/z bits are gone and it is truncated to the base type.

**Enum declarations (LRM 6.19).** Only *literal* values are judged; a value built from parameters is left alone.

| Code | Rule |
|---|---|
| CP0355 | x/z value in a 2-state base (`bit`, `int`, no base) |
| CP0356 | member with no value after an x/z-valued member |
| CP0357 | literal value, or implicit increment, the base cannot hold. A based literal is a bit pattern, so `'hFFFF_FFFF` fits an `int`. |
| CP0358 | an int-atom typedef with a packed dimension (`T [1:0]`, T = int), or an enum that is its own base type |
| CP0359 | non-constant system function (`$time`) as a value |

**Structure and declarations**

| Code | Rule |
|---|---|
| CP0361 | module instantiated in a program (24.3; the parser reads it as a checker instance) |
| CP0362 | zero replication outside any concatenation (11.4.12.1). A concatenation holding only zero replications stays UH0745's to report. |
| CP0363 | default value on an inout ANSI port (23.2.2.4) |
| CP0364 | class method with `static` lifetime (8.6) |
| CP0365 | net (with a net keyword) of string / chandle / event / class / queue / dynamic / associative type (6.7.1). `T x [$];` without a net keyword is a variable the grammar reads as a nettype declaration, so it is skipped. |
| CP0366 | body-local automatic variable driving a procedural continuous assignment, or as a nonblocking target (6.21). A local or formal as the `assign` *target* acts as a blocking write and is synthesized, so it is left alone. |
| CP0367 | attribute value naming a variable or net (5.12) |

CP0360 is unused. A nested-generate check was dropped: yosys accepts and synthesizes a generate region inside a generate block (its own `gen_test9`, this repo's GenerateBlock / GenerateRegion), so rejecting it is not this tool's job.

**UHDM bump:** chipsalliance/UHDM#1202 adds UH0751 (`reg` on an inout terminal), UH0752 (unassignable target), UH0753 (real/string operand type), UH0754 (void function value), UH0755 (event as value), and UH0718 for a select of a wire array.

**Goldens updated.** Each change is a correct new error:
- Google: `6.19--enum_xx_inv` and `enum_xx_inv_order` (CP0355, CP0356).
- Icarus: `port-test3.v` (UH0751) and `repeat2.v`, a standalone `{0{1'b1}}` (CP0362).
- YosysTests: `write_firrtl_error/top2.v`, `inout reg` ports (UH0751).
- ModPortHighConn: `a||b` on an inout port (UH0752).
- DoublePres: `real % real` (UH0753).

Local regression: 878 PASS, plus these 5 updated goldens.

The YosysTests golden keeps master's syntax-error text. A local run renders some `PA0207` messages for `synth_xilinx_srl` differently (`no viable alternative at input 'int['`). That difference is unrelated to this change and was left out.

author: delusional-png
body:
## What and why

**Symptom:** **Stray** (`010075101EF84000`, `1.0.0` / `v0`, build `0DBE0A904FD98595`) crashed ~1–3 s into launch on Peanuts Native `0.1.8` (`6eb10e52955e`) with a `GameThread` `SIGSEGV` (`SEGV_MAPERR`, write to `addr=0`) at `main+0x38042b0` (and `main+0x3abb10c` on other runs). Decoding the UTF-16LE strings in the crash registers showed a UE 4.27 PhysX alignment abort (`PHYSX: (D:/p4/ue4/r-4_27` in `*x1`, `aligned.` in `x12`/`x13`), alongside 8-byte aligned heap pointers (`0x...b8`, `0x...18`).

**Cause:** In `dm/host/hle_uemalloc.c`, `alloc()` skipped `plat_zone_memalign()` (`posix_memalign`) and called `plat_zone_malloc()` (`malloc`) whenever `a == 16`, and `realloc_aligned()` called `plat_zone_realloc()` (`realloc`) directly when `a == 16` without verifying alignment. When the host allocator returned an 8-byte aligned block, UE 4.27's PhysX allocator aborted during initialization.

**Change:** In `dm/host/hle_uemalloc.c` (marked `PEANUTS(upstream-candidate)` since this is a general Banana Native host fix):
- In `alloc()`, round any non-power-of-two alignment up to a power of two and always allocate via `plat_zone_memalign(g_zone, a, n ? n : 1)`.
- In `realloc_aligned()`, remove the `a == 16` `plat_zone_realloc()` shortcut so `realloc` always preserves `a`-byte alignment.

Existing game packs boot immediately without rebuilding.

## Checked

- Unit tests / Python tests: not run locally (edited via GitHub web UI; relying on repo CI checks)
- Phone runs on the test app: Stray (`010075101EF84000`, `1.0.0`) with existing pack imported into a `-PnxAppId=strayfix -PnxPackEngine=fake` test APK; boots and runs past initialization without hitting the `GameThread` `SIGSEGV`
- GPU drivers: Turnip (Balemuni Apex Ultimate, Mesa 26.3.0-devel) on OnePlus OPD2403
- Phone, chip, RAM and Android version:
  - OnePlus OPD2403, Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (SM8650 / Adreno 750), 12 GB RAM, Android 16 (API 36)
  - Motorola Moto G75, Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, 8 GB RAM (verified by a second user who hit the same startup crash)

## Docs

- [ ] The finding is in its game note or its `docs/reference/<subsystem>.md` entry, and `python3 dm/tools/docs_symptoms.py` was run (not added yet)
- [ ] A chain tool changed (not applicable)
- [x] No game files, keys or data extracted from a game in the change or the attachments
- [x] Source only: no binaries, nothing under `dm/third_party/`, no change to `dmsh_chain.lock`

author: toxickevinferm
body:
Three hunter fixes.

## Hawks take the owner's whole crit

The hotfix notes that gave tamed pets' white swings their crit (#1201) also say:

> Fixed an issue where Summoned Hawks had ~5% less critical strike chance than intended.

A hawk's crit is now the tamed pet's: the higher of the owner's melee and ranged crit (`inheritedCrit`), plus Ferocity.
The sim gave it half the owner's crit, from the level 30 logs in EV-0074. The live logs of Nov 12 to 16 already read
about 0.89 of the owner's crit less 2.7 (95%: 0.71 to 1.07), which at a level 60 hunter's crit is close to the 5% the
notes name.

The other hawk lines in the notes change nothing in the sim. Its hawks have no passive state and always attack, and
when their target dies they move to the next one with the rest of the raid. Nothing in the sim dismisses a hawk.

`TestHunterPets` average: 756.8 to 770.7.

## Only a Cat carries Faster or Slower Attack

Owner ruling of 2026-11-22: a Cat is the only family with a Faster Attack passive, and every other family swings every
2 s. The sim takes the pet attack speed option for a Cat alone, the settings show its picker only with a Cat chosen,
and the BM and SV Melee builds, whose pet is a Raptor, drop their Faster Attack II.

The speed is normalized, so damage a second barely moves: the Cat rows of `TestHunterPets` stay put, the other
families move by a few DPS, and the average goes from 770.7 to 768.0.

## Traps arm after 0.8 s and check every 0.4 s

EV-0218 counts 5,757 placements in 531 live reports where the target already stood on the trap. Nothing springs before
0.8 s; three in four spring evenly between 0.8 and 1.22 s and the rest evenly between 1.22 and 1.64 s. The trap arms at
0.8 s and checks every 0.4 s from a point that falls evenly in its first 0.4 s, and about one in four springs a check
later. The sim armed every trap at 0.5 s.

The later arming exposed a range bug. Immolation Trap's effect row has a 10 yd range, which the sim measured from the
hunter. A weaving hunter was still in reach at 0.5 s, but by 1.1 s they had walked back out to 12 yd and the debuff
never landed (37 to 6 DPS on the default weave). The trap casts the debuff where it lies, so the effect has no range of
its own now; the placement already springs only a trap within its trigger radius. With both, the default weave reads
910.5 against 909.8 before, Immolation Trap 37.3 against 37.4 (3,000 iterations).

`TestHunter` rows move by at most 1.25 DPS; `TestHunterPets`, whose rotation places no trap, does not move.

## Gates

On 47e69ef27d, all green: the SIML extension check and tests, `make skills-check`, locales, oxfmt, lint:js, lint:css,
type-check, unit tests, the Storybook build, the dist build, simlnames, the wowsimcli and SIML Go tests, and
`go test --tags=with_db ./sim/...`.

author: pmm-automation
body:
## Failures fixed (investigator)

- source: Percona-Lab/pmm-submodules PR #4753 (FB Tests run https://github.com/Percona-Lab/pmm-submodules/actions/runs/45774464662, attempt 1)
- tests:
  - cli/tests/mongoDb-psmdb.spec.ts / `@pbm-external` (PMM-T2832's `backup failures` `beforeAll`, `fixStorage` → `resync`)

## What failed

Job `CLI / Integration tests / PBM external / Replica set and standalone`, on pmm-qa `9f871c4d` (#1831, merged about an hour earlier). 19 passed, 1 failed:

```
Error: no resync has ended since pbm config --force-resync
  at resyncWith (cli/helpers/pbm.ts:382)
  at Object.fixStorage (cli/helpers/pbm.ts:401)
  at cli/tests/mongoDb-psmdb.spec.ts:551
```

Timing from the job log: PMM-T2831 ended at 07:42:03.7Z and the failure was reported at 07:44:06.4Z. So the `config --set` resync ended within about 2.6 s, and the `--force-resync` that followed showed no outcome for the full 120 s. The `afterAll`'s `fixStorage` (two resyncs) then finished within 8 s. Nothing was still holding PBM's lock.

The job left **no evidence**: `actions/upload-artifact` rejected `artifacts_for_@pbm-external-@standalone-psmdb-PBM-external:-replica-set-and-standalone` because of the colon (`The artifact name is not valid ... Colon :`). The same happens on every failure of the three `PBM external: …` jobs in `integration-cli-tests.yml`. PBM's own log lives in MongoDB and went with the runner.

## Not reproduced

- **CI re-run** of the failed job (attempt 2, job 139774829445, same FB image and pmm-qa SHA): 20 passed, 2 skipped, PMM-T2832 included.
- **CHAOS VM**, set up like the job (`perconalab/pmm-server-fb:PR-4753-421827e`, the FB client tarball, `pmm-framework --parallel --client-debug --database psmdb,SETUP_TYPE=pss,EXTERNAL_PBM=true --database psmdb,SETUP_TYPE=standalone_no_pbm`, the same three specs and `--grep`). On `main`: 20/20 idle, and 20/20 under 12 CPU hogs on 8 vCPU.
- PBM's resync log at Debug severity across both VM runs: 23 resyncs. Every one the helpers started was taken by an agent (`started`) and ended. No near-miss.

## What PBM 2.9.1 can do that the helper can't see

From `cmd/pbm-agent/resync.go` and `pbm/lock/lock.go` at v2.9.1:

- An agent that can't take the lock drops the resync and says so only at **Debug** (`get lock: …`, `lock not acquired`). The helper read the log at the default Info severity, so it couldn't tell a dropped resync from a running one.
- A held lock is **not** the cause here. With a backup holding the lock on the VM, `pbm config --force-resync` exits 1 with `another operation in progress, Snapshot backup/…`, and the helper's command retry absorbs that. A drop would need a lock taken between the CLI's check and the agent's acquire.
- Other terminal outcomes the helper doesn't treat as an end: `get config: …`, `reset epoch: …`, `acquiring lock: …`, `get node info data: …`. None of them appears in any run I can name, so this PR only makes them visible rather than changing what ends the wait.

## Fix

- `resyncWith` reads `pbm logs --event=resync -s D --tail=200`. Debug includes every Info entry, so `succeed` and `resync: …` end the wait as before. When the wait times out, the message lists every entry PBM logged for the new operation:
  ```
  no resync has ended since pbm config --force-resync; PBM logged for it:
  2026-11-26T08:35:43.000Z rs103:27017 D lock not acquired
  2026-11-26T08:35:47.000Z rs101:27017 I started
  ...
  ```
  or `nothing` when no agent handled it. The next recurrence then names its own mechanism.
- `runner-integration-cli-tests.yml` replaces whitespace and every character `upload-artifact` rejects (`" : < > | * ? \ /`) in the test name, not only spaces. `PBM external: replica set and standalone` becomes `PBM-external--replica-set-and-standalone`. Names without those characters don't change.

## Verification (CHAOS VM, same setup as above)

- Branch, CI-equivalent run of the three specs: 20 passed, 2 skipped (PMM-T2846 and PMM-T2833 are skipped on `main` too).
- Message with no agent handling the resync (scratch spec, not committed: all three `pbm-agent@rs10x` stopped, then `resync`): `no resync has ended since pbm config --force-resync; PBM logged for it:\nnothing`. With only rs101's agent running, it took the resync and the helper returned normally.
- The entry formatter run over a real Debug log from the VM gives the lines shown above, including the `E resync: init storage: … NoSuchBucket` entry that `breakStorage` produces.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint helpers/pbm.ts` pass. I checked the new `test_name_processed` expression with node against the three `PBM external:` names and the existing ones. The upload step itself runs only on a failed job, so a real failure has to confirm it.

author: wking66
body:
## Summary

```text
Model execution
  First visible text → commit text and body marker together
  Terminal transition → save the finish reason and up to 16 attempts
  SSE polling → read the existing snapshot fields
```

Alembic `0012` backfills historical executions and validates the new constraints. Attempt records contain allowlisted numeric fields and a truncation flag. A stream that ends before producing any generation chunks can fall back to the next candidate. Phase 2A is available on `dev` through #127.

## Evidence

- **Before** Execution records could not distinguish an empty reply from an upstream timeout or show which candidates were attempted.
- **After** A fresh PostgreSQL 16 database upgraded through `0012`, and all 43 Python tests passed. Tests cover high-ID historical rows, downgrade and re-upgrade, competing terminal writes, and fallback after an empty stream.
- Ruff and Pyright passed. Independent review approved all eight changed files. The rebase onto `dev` preserved the reviewed file contents.

## Merge Danger

**Door** Two-way. Pause AI request intake and drain the old worker before upgrading. To restore the previous writer, drain the new worker and downgrade to `0011`. The downgrade removes the new checks and default while preserving diagnostic data.

**Blast Radius** Python AI execution persistence and model routing.

body:
## Summary
- **Shared wire contract (`shared/progressive-intake.ts`)**: Defines `ProgressiveIntakeMode`, `ProgressiveIntakeState`, `ProgressiveIntakeMeta`, `ConcurrentWorkerMeta`, transition helpers, and augments `WireMessage` with optional `intake` / `concurrentWorker` metadata.
- **Busy intake classification & seamless continuation (`server/progressive-intake.ts`, `server/steer-queue.ts`, `server/index.ts`, `server/routes/bot-messages.ts`)**: Preserves Channel 1 tri-state `steer()` (`steered | refused | indeterminate`, no indeterminate replay), persists immediate user rows with `intake` state linked by `rowId` (zero duplicate rows on drain/steer, `superseded` on cancel), coalesces Channel 2 progressive continuations, and routes explicit mid-turn cancellations/pivots to protocol interrupts (`turn/interrupt` / `session/cancel`, zero `SIGTERM`) carrying prior progress forward.
- **Delegated sub-worker propagation (`server/host/question-routing.ts`)**: Adds `forwardDelegated()` to propagate parent busy follow-ups and redirections to active delegated child workers via safe question/steer paths while preserving `mayReach`, `recipientLevel`, `keptPrivate`, `personOnly`, and `handedInUnproven`.
- **OpenCode & Antigravity native `steer()` verdict**: Both drivers (`opencode-go` and `antigravity` / `antigravity-acp`) expose no `/steer` slash command or tri-state mid-turn steer RPC; kept on Channel 2 (`progressive-continue` + protocol `session/cancel` `soft-redirect`) and tracked separately if upstream ACP `/steer` lands.
- **Verification**: `oxlint --deny-warnings` (0 warnings/errors across 12 touched files); targeted Vitest passed (`file-size-ratchet` + `steer-e2e` 25/25 + `quote-context.e2e` 1/1 = 27/27; `progressive-intake` 5/5 + `question-routing` 36/36 + `steer-queue` 44/44 + `bot-messages` 33/33). `server/index.ts` shrunk to 15,490 lines; CI runs full typecheck & Ubuntu suite.

author: markusweigelt
body:
[MODTEMPENG-136](https://folio-org.atlassian.net/browse/MODTEMPENG-136) - Add Karate tests for the Handlebars template resolver

## Purpose
MODTEMPENG-136 added Handlebars as a second template resolver in mod-template-engine, next to Mustache. It is selected per stored template via `templateResolver` and optionally per preview request. The module's own unit and integration tests cover the resolver, but nothing yet shows that it is registered and reachable in a deployed module behind Kong/Eureka, with real permissions and tenant entitlement. This PR adds that end-to-end coverage.

It also carries the Karate tests for the template preview endpoint ([MODTEMPENG-135](https://folio-org.atlassian.net/browse/MODTEMPENG-135)). The Handlebars preview scenarios build on them, and that endpoint had no tests in this repository yet.

## Approach
- New `handlebars.feature`:
  - preview with `templateResolver: handlebars` renders `{{#if}}…{{else}}…{{/if}}` (both branches)
  - preview without `templateResolver` defaults to Mustache, shown with a template that is valid in both engines but renders differently (`{{#user}}Hi {{name}}{{else}}nobody{{/user}}` → `Hi Alex` vs `Hi Alexnobody`); an explicit `mustache` matches the default
  - unknown resolver → 400 `Template resolver 'foo' is not supported`
  - malformed Handlebars (unclosed block, unknown helper) → 400, not 500
  - one line using the module helpers `equalsAny`, `nl2br` and `numberFormat` (explicit `de-DE` locale, so the result doesn't depend on the tenant's locale)
  - stored Handlebars template rendered via `POST /template-request`, and a stored malformed one → 400 on render; both are deleted afterwards
- New sample `samples/template-handlebars-entity.json`.
- Preview endpoint tests: `templatePreview.feature` + `samples/template-preview-request-entity.json`.

[MODTEMPENG-136]: https://folio-org.atlassian.net/browse/MODTEMPENG-136?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
[MODTEMPENG-135]: https://folio-org.atlassian.net/browse/MODTEMPENG-135?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: lucas-koontz
body:
## User story

A person on the free tier who uses up their free allowance, or reaches the daily pause on free serving, reads a message that fits the model they picked.

## Why this matters

The free-allowance and free-pause messages named MindsHub Air as the free model. When the free allowance covers more than one model, a person stopped on another free model reads about a model they never used.

## What should happen

The free-allowance and free-pause messages, in turn replies and in the coding fallback, name no model. The coding fallback no longer promises a refill, matching the turn message, because an account with no free grant gets the same code and nothing refills for it. The Max Tokens setting's description says tokens count against your credits or your allowance, which is true on every tier, and the comments on the spent-allowance card say the reason fires for any model the Free tier covers.

## Test plan

- The free stop messages name no model: new tests pin each turn message and both coding messages. Passed.
- Channel replies and remote frames carry the new text: the remote-backend and turn-pool tests read the producer's constants instead of copies. Passed.
- Source-walking tests still pass. Passed.
- The settings description names no model: the test checks every model name as a whole word. Passed.

author: jwanjhi
body:
Server-side rules (previously only enforced by the UI):
- Status changes go through dedicated endpoints: mentee submits (/submit), mentor approves or requests changes (/review), mentor reopens approved work (/reopen). PATCH can no longer set status.
- Mentee can only submit once every task is ticked; a note is required and an optional http(s) evidence link can be attached.
- Mentor can only review submitted milestones; requesting changes requires a reason. Removed the mentor's direct sign-off shortcut and the auto-submit when the last task is ticked.
- Milestones are locked while under review and once approved (no ticking, adding, editing, or mentee deletion).
- Transitions are atomic conditional updates inside a transaction.

author: al-kindi-0
body:
A leaf in `Smt` or `LargeSmt` holds at most 1,024 entries. Replacing an entry in a full leaf could fail if the insertion ran before the removal. A failed `Smt` apply could also leave the tree partially updated while retaining its old root.

- `Smt` and `LargeSmt` now process removals first when preparing mutation sets. `LargeSmt` uses the same order when applying them, so leaf capacity is determined by the final contents.
- `Smt::apply_mutations` and `Smt::apply_mutations_with_reversion` roll back earlier leaf writes if a later write fails. They update the inner nodes and root only after all leaf writes succeed.

Regression tests cover full-leaf replacements, reversion, and rollback after a failed apply.

author: arkenoz
body:
### Summary
Fixes truncated `quant_step` escape-code handling in `Decoder::subframe` (`crates/victory-formats/src/xma.rs`):

1. **Silent exit on truncated escape:** the previous `while b.pos + 5 < b.end` loop exited silently without signalling an error when the bitstream ended before a terminal 5-bit value (`!= 31`), allowing truncated subframes (e.g. second subframe with `reuse_sf`) to decode and return `Ok(())`.
2. **Corrupted `quant_step` accumulation:** after a premature loop exit, `quant_step += if negative { -(quant + step) } else { quant + step }` reused the stale `step` value — adding `+32` when `step == -32` with 0 iterations (cancelling the initial `-32`), or double-counting the final `31` after one or more `31` escape codes.
3. **Off-by-one boundary (`<` vs `<=`):** `b.pos + 5 < b.end` prevented reading a valid 5-bit escape when exactly 5 bits remained.

The escape loop now reads 5 bits via `b.read(5)`, returns `Err(Error("quant step"))` on `b.overread()`, and accumulates `quant += esc` directly before breaking on `esc != 31`.

### Testing
- Added three synthetic unit tests in `crates/victory-formats/src/xma.rs` (all verified failing before the fix and passing after):
  - `truncated_negative_quant_step_escape_returns_error`
  - `truncated_positive_quant_step_escape_after_31_returns_error`
  - `quant_step_escape_reads_exact_five_remaining_bits`
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/victory-formats/src/xma.rs` — 0 diffs on modified/added lines
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` — passed

## What and why

Read-only diff, merge, and revision viewer panes showed the default arrow cursor over code text instead of the I-beam (`cursor: text`), even though text can be clicked, selected, and copied (and editable panes in the same diff showed the I-beam).

`body` sets `cursor: default`, while `global.css` only restores `cursor: text` for `[contenteditable="true"]`. Unlike `openideaTheme` (`src/editor/core/cm/theme.ts`), `viewerTheme` (`src/features/vcs/cm.ts`) set `userSelect: "text"` on `.cm-content` without `cursor: "text"`, so non-editable panes (`EditorView.editable.of(false)`) inherited the arrow cursor. Setting `cursor: "text"` on `.cm-content` in `viewerTheme` matches the main editor while keeping the arrow cursor on scrollbars (`.cm-scroller`) and gutters (`.cm-gutters`), and `cursor: pointer` on collapsed-line buttons and hunk controls.

author: austinschuh
body:
Module map paths are relative to each map, and Clang resolves `extern module` paths without normalizing them, so they grow with every hop.  On deep graphs they pass PATH_MAX (1024 bytes on macOS), Clang silently drops headers it can't open, and layering_check fails with "does not depend on a module exporting".  gRPC hits this when a Mac builds it for Linux.

Enable module_map_home_cwd with -fmodule-map-file-home-is-cwd, and write the system module map to match, so paths stay a fixed length.

- Przekierowania slugów nie są kopiowane ani tworzone: powstają tylko w akcjach Update, a kopia z nich nie korzysta.
- Trasy `POST admin/pages/{page}/duplicate` i `POST admin/articles/{article}/duplicate` z `->can('duplicate', …)`. Ability `duplicate` w `PagePolicy` i `ArticlePolicy` = `canEditContent()`.
- UI: akcja wiersza „Duplikuj” i przycisk w edycji. Przy niezapisanych zmianach UI pyta o potwierdzenie. Po kopiowaniu redirect do edycji kopii i toast z informacją, że kopia jest szkicem.
- Audyt: dedykowane `PageDuplicated` / `ArticleDuplicated`, spójne z rodziną `page.*` / `article.*` i z `FaqDuplicated`. Wpis zawiera `duplicated_from` i nowe slugi per locale.
- i18n PL/EN/DE, `docs/panel/README.md`, checkbox kroku 3.

AC:
- [x] Brak kolizji slugów w żadnym locale. Testowane: slug zajęty w koszu, przez przekierowanie i przez rekord w innym locale; powtórna kopia; kopia kopii.
- [x] Kopia niewidoczna publicznie do publikacji (publiczny URL kopii zwraca 404, także `/pl/…` i na liście artykułów).
- [x] Viewer dostaje 403; nie powstaje rekord, tłumaczenia, przekierowania ani audyt.

## Weryfikacja

Wykonane:
- Implementer: nowe testy 14 passed na SQLite, `make test-mysql` i `make test-pgsql`; `make test` 1358 passed; `make check` exit 0 po poprawce formatowania 3 plików TSX (`vp fmt`); ui-contract PASS (7 wyjątków, bez nowych); Pint na zmienionych plikach.
- Orkiestrator niezależnie:
  - `make test` → 1358 passed (21149 assertions);
  - `make test-mysql` (Page/Article/FaqDuplicateTest) → 20 passed (285 assertions);
  - git czysty, HEAD `928afc7`.

Niewykonane:
- Pełna suita na MySQL i PostgreSQL (uruchomiono tylko testy duplikowania; pełną suitę uruchomi CI).
- `make generator-smoke`: generator i stuby bez zmian.
- E2E i przeglądarka (RWD przycisków w nagłówku edycji).

## Ryzyko i review

**HIGH-RISK (policy).** Zgoda właściciela R1: admin i redaktor. Zmiana ogranicza się do dodania `duplicate` w `PagePolicy` i `ArticlePolicy`. Żadna z nich nie ma reguły własności, a `update` też sprawdza `canEditContent()`. Bez migracji i bez innych zmian ról. Cofnięcie: revert.

`foundation-reviewer` (tylko odczyt): **brak uwag blokujących**. Potwierdził:
- poprawność regexu i escape LIKE;
- kopiowanie wyłącznie pól `#[Fillable]` (bez id, timestampów, `published_at`);
- brak hooków przekierowań w modelach;
- autoryzację tras i test odmowy bez skutków.

Nieblokujące:
1. Dwie równoczesne kopie tego samego źródła mogą wybrać ten sam slug. Unikalny indeks i rollback zapobiegają uszkodzeniu danych, ale użytkownik zobaczy 500. Możliwy follow-up: ponowienie po `UniqueConstraintViolationException`.
2. Akcja wiersza (`router.post`) nie ma stanu oczekiwania ani throttle, więc podwójne kliknięcie utworzy dwie kopie. Dotyczy też #142 i #143; propozycja: jedna wspólna poprawka dla wszystkich trzech modułów.
3. Brakujące dowody: test sluga blisko 200 znaków, test duplikowania rekordu z kosza (oczekiwane 404), test tagu w koszu.
4. Tytuł kopii pozostaje taki sam jak oryginału (spójnie z FAQ); kopię odróżniają slug i status szkicu.

Środowisko: `make test-pgsql` odtworzył kontener `starter-local-postgres-1`. Wolumeny Compose są wspólne z innymi worktree.

Delegacja: implementacja przez subagenta-implementera, review przez `foundation-reviewer`, weryfikacja i PR przez orkiestratora.
