author: sovereigntechnology
hybrid2102
body: ## ELI5 On Windows, if you picked a whole drive like `C:\` as the parent folder in Clone from URL, Orca stopped right away with a permission error. Orca was asking Windows to create a folder that already exists, and for drive roots Windows answers "access denied" instead of "already there". Now, if that step fails but the folder already exists, Orca carries on with the clone. ## What Changed - **Before:** Clone from URL with a drive root as the parent folder (`C:\`, `C:/`) failed immediately with `EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir 'C:\'`, before git started. - **After:** the clone goes into `C:\` like it does for any other parent folder. Mechanism: both clone paths (the local `repos:clone` IPC handler in `repo-clone-lifecycle.ts` and `RuntimeRepositoryCloneController`) called `mkdir(destination, { recursive: true })` to make sure the parent folder exists. On Windows, Node's recursive `mkdir` rejects with `EPERM` for an existing volume root, because libuv maps `CreateDirectoryW`'s `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` to `EPERM`. A new `ensureCloneDestination()` in `repo-clone-path.ts` runs the same `mkdir`. Only when that throws does it `stat` the destination: if it is an existing directory, the error is ignored, otherwise the original error is rethrown. Both callers now use it. ## Why The clone only needs the parent folder to exist, so a failed `mkdir` on a folder that is already there should not stop it. Alternatives considered: - Special-casing drive roots (`path.parse(p).root === p`): narrower, and tied to one Node quirk rather than the actual requirement. - Calling `stat` before `mkdir`: adds a syscall to every clone. Here the `stat` runs only on the error path. Real failures still show up unchanged, because the original error is rethrown when the destination is not a directory: a missing drive (`ENOENT`), a file in the way (`EEXIST`), or a path under a file (`ENOTDIR`). ## Linked Issue Fixes #49929 ## Visual Proof Before (screenshot from #49929): After: there is no in-app screenshot. The bug only happens on Windows, so the fix was verified at module level on a real Windows host. The real `repo-clone-path.ts` from `main` and from this branch were each bundled and run through the clone destination steps: ensure the parent, claim `\`, then clean up. ``` node v24.18.0 win32 "C:\\" main: ERR EPERM fix: ok(clonePath=C:\bb49933-…-f claimedDir=true cleanedUp=true) "C:/" main: ERR EPERM fix: ok(clonePath=C:\bb49933-…-f claimedDir=true cleanedUp=true) \… main: ok fix: ok \…\new\nested main: ok fix: ok \…\afile main: ERR EEXIST fix: ERR EEXIST \…\afile\sub main: ERR ENOTDIR fix: ERR ENOTDIR "Q:\\nope\\x" main: ERR ENOENT fix: ERR ENOENT "R:\\" (subst root) main: ok fix: ok ``` ## Testing - Reproduced on a real Windows host (Node v24.18.0, win32) with the probe above. Drive roots fail on `main` and work with the fix. Every other case gives the same result before and after, including the error cases. - New `src/main/git/repositories/cloning/repo-clone-path.test.ts` mocks `node:fs/promises` and covers both branches. When `mkdir` rejects with `EPERM` and the destination is a directory, the helper resolves. When `stat` fails, it rethrows the same `EPERM` error object. The first case fails without the fix. - vitest on `src/main/git/repositories/cloning/`: 16/16 passed. - oxlint, oxfmt, the anti-slop and native-plugin oxlint configs, ast-grep and the changed-code quality gate all pass on the 4 changed files. - macOS: behavior is unchanged, since recursive `mkdir` on an existing directory already succeeds there, so the new branch never runs. - [x] I manually tested these changes locally (Windows, module level) - [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below - [x] Every added test fails without this change and avoids the [test anti-patterns](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/docs/agents-md-refs/test-antipatterns.md) ## Performance None, because this runs once per user-started clone, the success path makes the same `mkdir` call as before, and the extra async `stat` runs only when `mkdir` throws. Measured on Windows: an existing directory took 0.22–0.24 ms/op on main and 0.23–0.24 ms/op with the fix, which is noise. A drive root took 0.17–0.20 ms/op with the fix, and the worst single call was 0.28 ms. There is no sync I/O, subprocess or polling. ## Risk The riskiest part is that, for a destination that already exists as a directory, any `mkdir` error is now ignored, not only `EPERM`. That is intended, because the folder existing is all the clone needs, and the next step (`claimCloneTarget`) plus `git clone` still report real access problems on the target folder. The `\\?\C:\` long-path form still fails, but the folder picker never produces it. Saved data, settings and protocols are unchanged. Back out with a plain revert. **Level:** Low ## Review - **Cross-platform:** the fix targets Windows. On macOS and Linux the new branch cannot run for existing folders. - **SSH/remote:** the runtime clone controller uses the same helper, and its success path is unchanged. WSL hosts still go through `refuseWslHostWindowsDrivePath` first. - **Mixed versions:** no protocol change. - **Follow-up (not in scope):** Create Project (`repo-creation-handlers.ts`) and runtime project creation use the same recursive `mkdir` pattern and may hit the same `EPERM` on a drive root. ## Agent skill upstream boundary - [x] Not applicable, or this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation. ## Notes Ensure no issues in: Security, Cross-platform support (Linux, Windows, Mac), Remote SSH, Mobile, general backwards compatibility, performance ## Checklist - [x] This PR is small and focused - [x] I explained what changed and why (ELI5, the user-facing before/after, the mechanism, and why over the alternatives) - [x] I stated the risk: what could break, for whom, and how to back it out - [x] Before/after screenshots or videos attached for UI changes, or `N/A` with reason - [x] Self-reviewed for correctness, security, and performance - [x] Cross-platform, SSH/remote, and path/shortcut impact considered (or N/A) - [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` pass (or CI will cover; local preferred) Original fix by @hybrid2102 in #49933

## Summary

Adds log out to the account menu, the last part of the MVP of #196. It uses `logout()` from #197.

## Changes

- New `// SESSION` group with **Log out** (This device only). It turns into a confirmation panel (`role="alertdialog"`) with Cancel and Log out.
- After the reload the landing page announces "Logged out on this device" (`role="status"`), which dismisses itself after 5 seconds. A one-shot flag in `sessionStorage` carries it over the reload.
- `PgButton` gets a `danger` variant.

## Testing

- [x] `yarn test` (282 tests, run as `vitest run --coverage`)
- [x] `yarn lint`
- [x] `yarn build` (run as `vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build --mode test`)

Also checked in headless Chromium at 375px against the dev server with the Spotify API mocked: confirm, log out, landing page with the toast, the toast dismissing itself and not coming back on another reload. **A real Spotify re-login (the account dialog) has not been tried.**

## Notes for reviewers

- **The `vrt` check is expected to fail**, on the three existing account menu stories and the two `PgButton` stories at both widths. The confirmation and after-logout stories are new.
- Choices the issue and design don't cover: focus starts on Cancel; Esc in the panel cancels it without closing the menu.
- The log out item darkens on hover instead of lightening like the other items, so the red text keeps 4.5:1.
- The toast is a little wider than in the design, so the text under it doesn't peek out at the cut corner.

## Summary
With the US ROM the Banjo-Tooie picture left a black bar on the right and another at the bottom, in 4:3 and in 16:9. This crops the frame pane's texture rectangle in `FrameLayout.arc`, which closes both bars on every side.

## Type of change
- [ ] feat (new feature)
- [x] fix (bug fix)
- [ ] refactor / perf
- [ ] docs / test / chore / ci
- [ ] Breaking change

## Related issues
None.

## Changes
- `N64FrameLayoutPatcher.Apply` takes an optional `FrameCrop` (share of the right and bottom to drop) and rewrites the frame pane's four texture coordinates. A crop alone does not touch the pane size or the dark filter.
- `N64Profiles.FrameCrop`: Banjo-Tooie US and JP get 33/640 on the right and 24/480 at the bottom. EU gets none and keeps `ClipRight = 33` in the ini.
- `N64Injector` patches the layout when a crop is requested, even without widescreen.
- Why not the ini: the engine honors only the first key of `[Render]`. `ClipRight` first dropped `ClipBottom` and the reverse; the four keys in the community order still dropped `ClipRight`.
- Tests: 139 Core and 110 Mac pass. The test base now has a valid `FrameLayout.arc`, like every real base.

## How to test
1. `dotnet test mac`
2. `vc-layout <US ROM> <F-Zero X US base> "Banjo-Tooie US" out` (with and without `--widescreen`)
3. Run in Cemu, with START pressed through `tools/graphicpack-forceinput`, and look at the file select.

## Screenshots / logs (if applicable)
Measured on the file select captured from the Cemu window (2560 x 1496):

| Title | Left bar | Right bar | Bottom gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4:3 before | 319 | 415 | 71 |
| 4:3 after | 319 | 319 | 0 |
| 16:9 before | 0 | 126 | 71 |
| 16:9 after | 0 | 0 | 0 |

In 4:3 the 319 px on each side are the 16:9 window around the 4:3 pane. ClipBottom 20 left 12 px of the bar and 24 closed it. The bars were also seen in screenshots from the person testing, who then reported the 4:3 stretch and the full 16:9 screen working.

## Risks and rollback
Only Banjo-Tooie US and JP change, and only the layout. The EU title is not touched. Not tested on a real Wii U. Revert the squash commit to roll back.

## Checklist
- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits
- [x] Branch is up to date with the base branch
- [x] Tests added or updated and passing
- [x] Lint and type checks pass
- [x] Docs / changelog updated
- [x] No secrets or debug code committed
- [x] Self-reviewed the diff

## Backgrounds for Physikalisches Glas
The material gets a background choice. Its own script fills every `select[data-pg-bg-choice]` and remembers the choice per browser (`localStorage` `pg.bg`); apps only place the selector.

| Background | Source | Tile pixels changed by refraction (desktop, Chromium) |
|---|---|---|
| Konturen (default) | CSS | 4.8 % |
| Gebürstetes Metall | CSS: fine horizontal grain at four unrelated periods over a steel ramp with a gloss band | **6.6 %** |
| Polarlicht | `wallpapers/aurora.webp` | 1.0 % (0.2 % with the veil, see below) |
| Morgenlicht | `wallpapers/morning.webp` | 0.1 % |
| Rosé | `wallpapers/rose.webp` | 0.6 % |
| Lagune | `wallpapers/lagoon.webp` | 0.5 % |

- The four wallpapers are original images supplied by the project owner, generated with an image model. They imitate no vendor wallpaper. Each is 1672×941 WebP, about 20 KB, and scaled to cover the page. Provenance is in `assets/physical-glass/wallpapers/README.md`.
- On the dark *Polarlicht* picture, a light veil under the glass keeps dark text readable on every tile. Without it, the tiles on the dark right-hand side could not be read.
- The desktop places the selector in its top bar and serves the pictures at `/static/physical-glass/wallpapers/*.webp`. The lookup is an exact match; only `.webp` assets are served.

## Render permits held until the render ends (Codex finding on report-rs#230)
The lab's map and rear routes now move an owned permit (`acquire_owned` on an `Arc<Semaphore>`) into the blocking task. Before, a cancelled request released its permit while its render kept running, so the two-render limit held only while every request stayed connected.

## Checks
- `a2ui-theme`: 24 + 3 tests. The material test now requires a rule and a selector entry for every background, and a valid WebP asset for every wallpaper.
- `a2ui-paint-web`, `pwa` feature: 29 tests. New: wallpapers are served; `README.md`, a path containing `..` and unknown files get 404. Without the feature: 17 tests.
- Clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.
- Ran it in Chromium: all six backgrounds switch, the choice survives a reload, and the page logs no errors.

## Summary

Closes #170

What one buys is an **item** now (GLOSSARY.md), and the backend says so below the API. A meal's rows stay *ingredients*. The API is unchanged: the exported OpenAPI document is byte-identical to `frontend/src/api/generated/openapi.json`, so the frontend doesn't change.

```diff
 database (migration 0019)
-ingredients                         → items (constraints/indexes renamed: pk_items, ix_items_*, …)
 meal_ingredients.ingredient_id      → item_id
 list_meal_ingredients.ingredient_id → item_id
   ingredient_name/brand_snapshot    → item_name/brand_snapshot
 list_extra_items.ingredient_id      → item_id   (ck_…_ingredient_or_text → ck_…_item_or_text)
 list_hidden_due_items.ingredient_id → item_id
 recurring_items.ingredient_id       → item_id   (uq_… indexes follow)
```

```diff
 backend/app/
-├── models/ingredient.py         (Ingredient)
+├── models/item.py               (Item)
-├── repositories/ingredients.py
+├── repositories/items.py
-├── services/ingredients.py
+├── services/items.py
 ├── domain/…                     IngredientAttrs → ItemAttrs, ingredient_key → item_key, …
 ├── api/ingredients.py           unchanged paths, handlers and params (#171 renames them)
 └── schemas/ingredients.py       unchanged schema names and fields (#171)
```

- Kept as they are, because they are API: paths, schema classes and fields, `ErrorCode`/`AdminAction` values, notice kind `recurring_item.ingredient_deleted`, error params, line keys `i:<id>`. CLI output texts are unchanged too.
- Meal rows keep `MealIngredient`, `ListMealIngredient` and their tables.
- In the recurring-item code, the recurring item's variables are now `recurring_item`/`recurring` so that `item` means the item.
- The migration rebuilds each table from its own `CREATE TABLE` with the identifiers replaced, and copies the rows unchanged. SQLite can't rename a constraint. The downgrade does the same in reverse.
- GLOSSARY.md: the design session's patch (Item, Supply, Ingredient, Eaten, Leftover meal added; Pack size removed). docs/plan.md's data model names the new tables and columns.

### Evidence

- New migration tests on the 0013 demo fixture at 0018, with a recurring item and a hidden due item added so every referring table has rows:
  - `test_0019_renames_ingredients_to_items_and_keeps_every_row`: every row and FK reference is intact, including the 15 frozen rows on the list being shopped and the 10 on done lists, the other tables are unchanged, and no schema name says ingredient except the meal-row tables'.
  - `test_0019_names_the_constraints_as_the_models_do`: the constraint and index names match the models, per table.
  - `test_0019_keeps_the_constraints_working`.
  - `test_the_0019_downgrade_restores_the_ingredients`: the schema and rows are the same as at 0018.
- `test_0014_through_the_api` reads the old database through today's app, so 0019's rebuild runs on it temporarily.
- Backend: 1888 passed, coverage 100 %, ruff and mypy clean. Other test changes are internal names and raw SQL table names only.
- OpenAPI: `mealmate export-openapi` gives the same document before and after (`cmp`).

author: luraess
body:
A model cell takes the material at its level, so a Quaternary deposit of a few metres turns a whole top cell (25–50 m) into soft fill as soon as it reaches below the cell's level. In the 1 Hz Valais runs, 13.6 % of the Quaternary top cells hold less than half a cell of deposit (median 4 m in 25 m cells), which over-represents soft material and makes some isolated bright points in the peak-velocity maps.

This PR adds an option for that, off by default:

- `valais_model_maps(...; min_fill = 0.5)` (also `build_valais_model`) drops the deposit (thickness 0, bedrock at the surface) in the columns where it fills less than half of the top solid cell. The cell height is the distance between the midpoints to the neighbouring levels. The rule is applied to the swissBEDROCK thickness before `model_interfaces`, so `bed`, `base_cs` and `quat_thickness` stay consistent.
- New functions `drop_thin_deposits` (exported) and `top_cell_height`, with tests.
- With the default `min_fill = 0` nothing changes.

Whole canton at 50 m with 25 m vertical cells in the fill band: Quaternary top cells 240 949 → 205 245 (−14.8 %); the dropped deposits are 6.2 m thick in the median. We use it in the next ValaisRawilWaves runs (1 Hz and 2 Hz). It merges cleanly with your `gravity-subsoil-density-inversion` branch (checked on its state of 2026-11-26).

author: chitrangpatel
body:
## Why

Sonnet 5.5 is the current Sonnet, at $2 / $10 per MTok against Sonnet 4.6's $3 / $15. Its tokenizer counts about 30% more tokens for the same text, so an equivalent request should come out roughly 10–15% cheaper, before thinking. Ahead of the CMC demo.

## What

`sherlock/agent.py`:

- Default model `claude-sonnet-5-5`; `SHERLOCK_EFFORT` (default `medium`) sets the effort level. Thinking is on by default on 5.5 and billed as output; `medium` keeps it short for a tool-heavy chat agent.
- `max_tokens` 4096 → 16000, since thinking counts toward it.
- Thinking blocks are kept in history exactly as received (`thinking` with its `signature`, `redacted_thinking`). Their signature binds them to the conversation, so they must not be rebuilt.
- `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"` (beta `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01`). The system prompt is rebuilt on each reply (Tier 2 memory, agent docs), which invalidates earlier thinking blocks; this drops them instead of failing the request.
- `fallbacks: "default"` (beta `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01`). Sonnet 5.5's safety classifiers can decline a request; cyber and frontier-LLM declines are re-run server-side on Sonnet 5. After a fallback, only text from before the fallback block is kept, so the declined model's thinking and tool calls are neither echoed back nor run (`_served_content`).
- A decline that survives the fallback ends the turn with an error chunk carrying a written message. The partial output is discarded, and the same text goes to the audit log as the response.
- Prices for `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` added, so the audit log's cost is right. The cache multipliers (1.25× write, 0.1× read) hold for 5.5.

Also: `claude-sonnet-5-5` added to the pre-initialised Prometheus model labels, and `AGENT.md` env table.

## Testing

- `pytest`: 90 passed. The same 2 failures are already on main (`test_memory_post_returns_entry`, `test_load_chime_bundled_config`). New tests cover thinking-block echo, fallback content filtering and 5.5 pricing.
- Live check from the production pod with these exact request settings: a tool call, then a reply carrying the echoed history. Both accepted, `input_transformations` empty (nothing dropped).

## Not covered

- Cost per question still needs measuring on real questions: rehearsals in #sherlock-test, compared against the Sonnet 4.6 rows in the audit log.
- `display` stays at its default (`omitted`), so Sherlock's narration between tool calls (text blocks) may be sparser on 5.5. Only the final answer is posted to Slack anyway.
- The guardrail still uses Haiku 4.5, and its `_PRICING` row ($0.80 / $4) is out of date. Separate change.

Seit 0.141.0 scheitert der M365-Abruf beim Anlegen der UTCM-Aufträge mit 400 (BadRequest) für alle Workloads. Geändert hatte sich nur der `displayName` (von 24 auf 39 Zeichen). Arbeitsthese: UTCM begrenzt die Länge, Microsoft dokumentiert dazu nichts.

author: paolo-de-rosa
body:
## Summary

`scripts/remote-check.sh --tree` deleted on the proving machine what `.gitignore` ignores: the build, the toolchain state and `lean/.lake/`.

**The cause.** The rsync of the working tree passed the rules as a dir-merge filter (`:- .gitignore`). Such a filter keeps the ignored files from being sent, but it does not protect them in the destination from `--delete`. Both openrsync (the macOS `rsync`) and rsync 3.2.7 then delete every ignored directory there, as isolated tests on small trees show. Every tree run therefore built from scratch. Since Lean entered the gate, the step `lean` of a tree run also failed from the second run on: the Lake packages were left as bare `.git/` directories.

**The fix.**
- The rules go in with `--exclude-from=.gitignore`, which the receiving side applies to `--delete` too.
- `--exclude-from` reads one file and gives a negated pattern another meaning. So, before the machine is reserved, a tree run is refused when the tree has any other `.gitignore`, tracked or untracked, or a negated pattern. The other `.gitignore` files are listed under the root rules alone, so one that ignores itself, as a venv's does, is found too.
- The header of `--tree` says that the machine keeps what `.gitignore` ignores between tree runs, as its clone does for the commit mode.

**Checked on the proving machine.** Three tree runs from this branch: `build`, `partitions-check`, `lean`.
- All passed.
- After each one, `obj/`, `alire/`, `config/` and all nine Lake packages under `lean/.lake/packages` were intact.
- The step `lean` of the third run passed on the `.lake/` kept from the earlier runs.

The refusal was checked by hand on a tree with a plain nested `.gitignore` and on one with a self-ignoring nested `.gitignore` (`*`). `scripts/remote-check.sh` has no test harness of its own.

Closes #218

## Proof

No Ada, no contract and no proof setting changes. The SPARK and Lean proof inputs are those of `main`: the gate reuses both proofs.

## Measurements

None.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Every acceptance criterion of the issue is met
- [x] `verify`, `lean` and `prove` are green
- [x] Every check in the touched units is proved; no justification, no `pragma Assume`
- [x] No contract weakened and no assurance level changed, or the maintainer's agreement is recorded

author: obegg
body:
## What does this PR do?

Consolidates the duplicated trip and charging-session JSON field allowlists in `GenAiContext.java` and `GenAiVehicleHistory.java`.

- The original `TRIP_KEYS` and `CHARGING_SESSION_KEYS` arrays in `GenAiContext` remain private and unchanged, including their order: 47 trip keys and 28 charging-session keys.
- Adds package-private `copyTripFields()` and `copyChargingSessionFields()` methods that delegate to the existing `copyAllowed()` implementation. No mutable key array is exposed to callers.
- Routes four existing context projections and two vehicle-history card projections through these methods. Removes the duplicate arrays from `GenAiVehicleHistory`.
- Preserves the existing history card ID validation, `kind` and `id` assignments, event allowlist, and subsequent provider-evidence ID removal. The charging context projection still does not include `id`.
- Adds a regression-test method in `GenAiContextTest` covering representative retained fields, omitted fields, separation of trip and charging fields, and null input. Existing privacy and history-card tests are retained unchanged.

Production: 15 insertions, 37 deletions (22 fewer lines). Test source: 25 insertions. Three files total. No new dependency or public API.

## Why is this change needed?

Both modules previously contained exactly the same two allowlists. Independently maintained copies can drift when a field is added or removed, including fields that should remain outside the AI context. Keeping the shared projection policy in one place reduces duplication while retaining the existing explicit field selection. This is not an expansion of the data supplied to an AI provider and does not change the surrounding privacy policy.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Context projections] --> T[copyTripFields]
    B[Trip history cards] --> T
    C[Charging context] --> S[copyChargingSessionFields]
    D[Charging history cards] --> S
    T --> P[Existing private trip allowlist]
    S --> Q[Existing private charging allowlist]
    P --> F[Existing copyAllowed projection]
    Q --> F
```

The history-card-specific metadata handling and provider-evidence transformation remain outside the shared helpers. No changes to provider calls, authentication, consent, event filtering, prompts, or data acquisition are intended.

## How to test

Static verification on `21340d57a86210aa015e57f4ccbdf173bc1c1bdb`:

- Verified the original three files against the uploaded clean archive and Git objects. Compared the duplicate arrays exactly (apart from the charging constant name); both lists matched in contents and order.
- Reviewed all six changed production call sites, unchanged `copyAllowed` behavior, and unchanged history card ID and evidence handling. Reviewed existing GenAI privacy and source-contract test source.
- Generated the patch with `git diff --cached --binary --full-index`. Git whitespace validation and strict index applicability checks passed in a fresh sparse worktree. The staged diff matched the supplied patch byte-for-byte.
- The 21 prepared cleanup patches touch disjoint paths and produce the same combined Git tree in forward and reverse order on the audited revision.

**Compilation, automated tests and device verification have not been performed.** Suggested pre-merge verification:

1. Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew test` as required by the contribution guide.
2. Run `GenAiContextTest`, `GenAiVehicleHistoryTest` and `GenAiAssetContractTest`, including the new projection regression test and the existing history-card privacy assertions.
3. With synthetic input containing both allowed and excluded keys, compare the prior and new trip/charging projections and history evidence. Check that coordinates and tariff identifiers remain excluded wherever previously omitted, and that history-only metadata is still handled separately.
4. Exercise latest-trip, trip comparison, charging context and vehicle-history queries with a disposable test configuration; verify the same field sets and card rendering.

## Risks and limitations

This refactors active data projection code. The arrays and filtering expressions match the originals by static inspection; compilation and runtime equivalence have not been demonstrated. A future change to the shared list affects both consumers, so any policy change should explicitly review both paths. Existing nested values, exception behavior, and the broader context privacy design are intentionally unchanged; this is not a privacy-hardening audit. No performance improvement is claimed. Non-public build consumers cannot be verified here.

## Screenshots (if applicable)

Not applicable; no visual changes are intended.

author: rayditya12
body:
## What

ROADMAP 1.5 — the bundled fonts.

- `backend/fonts/`: the seven SPEC.md section 9 fonts as TTF files, plus
  `backend/fonts/LICENSES/<Font>.OFL.txt` for each, plus
  [backend/fonts/README.md](file:///C:/Users/Rayyhan/Documents/Manim-made-simple/backend/fonts/README.md)
  recording which upstream file each one came from. 2.9 MB total:
  `Inter.ttf` 856 KB, `Montserrat.ttf` 727 KB, `Roboto.ttf` 477 KB,
  `PlayfairDisplay.ttf` 294 KB, `FiraCode.ttf` 254 KB, `Poppins.ttf` 157 KB,
  `BebasNeue.ttf` 60 KB.
- [backend/scenes/text_scene.py](file:///C:/Users/Rayyhan/Documents/Manim-made-simple/backend/scenes/text_scene.py):
  `BUNDLED_FONTS`, `font_file_for()`, and `register_bundled_font()`, called from
  `MmsTextScene.setup()` before any `Text` is built. A whitelist id whose file is
  absent or which the system refuses to load raises `font_file_missing` /
  `font_registration_failed` rather than silently rendering a different face. A name
  outside the whitelist is still passed through to Pango, so hand-written parameter
  files can use a system font.
- [backend/tests/test_fonts.py](file:///C:/Users/Rayyhan/Documents/Manim-made-simple/backend/tests/test_fonts.py):
  34 tests. The bundle is checked four ways (file exists, license exists and is really
  OFL, the family name inside the file equals the id the API advertises, and no file on
  disk is unlicensed), then one frame per font is rendered through the template.
- `backend/app/models.py`: the docstring no longer says the fonts are coming later.
- `backend/fonts/LICENSES/.gitkeep` removed, `ROADMAP.md` ticked.

257 changed lines excluding the seven license texts (which are verbatim upstream and
make the diff stat read 908).

## Why

SPEC.md section 9 allows only OFL fonts, requires each license text to ship with the
font, and says registration "differs by OS" so it must be verified rather than assumed:
a font that exists only as a file in the app bundle is invisible to Pango until it is
registered.

## How I tested it

```
$ .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff check .
All checks passed!
$ .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff format --check .
17 files already formatted
$ .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q
249 passed, 1 warning in 67.35s
```

The distinctness test compares each frame's text outline resampled onto a 32x32 grid;
seven fonts must give seven different shapes. Raw ink pixels per rendered frame, from
the same probe the test automates:

```
Inter              ink= 32797      Poppins            ink= 34509
Montserrat         ink= 26875      Roboto             ink= 31264
Playfair Display   ink= 25206      Bebas Neue         ink= 39502   (condensed caps)
Fira Code          ink= 30439
```

Also end-to-end through `render_video`, so the video path uses a bundled face too
(Indonesian text, outline on, preview quality, decoded back through PyAV):

```
Playfair Display   -> playfair-display.mp4 854x480 frames=22 wall=4.0s
Bebas Neue         -> bebas-neue.mp4       854x480 frames=22 wall=3.9s
```

## OS-specific registration findings (the acceptance criteria asked for these)

1. **Windows, registration required.** `manimpango.register_font(path)` returns `True`,
   the family appears in `manimpango.list_fonts()`, and `unregister_font(path)` removes
   it again. Without it the render falls back to a system face silently — the old
   behavior the tests now rule out.
2. **Windows, variable fonts pick the right instance.** Four of the seven upstream files
   are variable, and their *default* named instances are not Regular: reading the files
   directly with PIL gives `Montserrat -> ('Montserrat', 'Thin')` and
   `FiraCode -> ('Fira Code', 'Light')`, and rendering the same string from that default
   instance yields 1,737 / 5,326 ink pixels against Inter Regular's 7,019. Through the
   template, Montserrat lands at 26,875 and Fira Code at 30,439 against Inter's 32,797 —
   so Pango/DirectWrite selects the Regular named instance, not the file default.
   `test_regular_weight_is_selected_for_the_variable_fonts` asserts ink > 0.6x Inter so
   a system that did render the default instance fails loudly.
3. **Linux, verified afterwards in a container.** `manimcommunity/manim:latest`
   (Debian 13 trixie, fontconfig 2.15, ManimPango 0.7.0, Python 3.14) passes all 34
   font tests and the full 249-test suite, including the POSIX `killpg` timeout path.
   `FcFileManage` registration needed no `fc-cache` run, none of the seven fonts are
   preinstalled there either, and the rendered shapes match Windows to within 0.5%
   (Montserrat 26,842 ink px on Linux against 26,875 on Windows). Numbers in the
   comment below.

## Screenshots

No UI change. Frame evidence is the ink table above.

## License notes

- Every font is under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; the exact `OFL.txt` published
  beside each file in google/fonts is included unmodified. Only the file names were
  shortened (square brackets and commas), the fonts and their internal family names are
  untouched, so the reserved font names still describe these files. Playfair Display is
  the one family whose OFL text declares a Reserved Font Name.
- Sources checked: each license's first line names the project authors, and all seven
  contain "SIL Open Font License" and "PERMISSION & CONDITIONS" (asserted in tests).
- No new dependency. `manimpango` 0.7.1 (MIT) is already Manim CE's own Pango binding;
  `PIL`/`numpy` were already used by the existing tests.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally (249 passed)
- [x] SPEC.md still matches the behavior (section 9 whitelist implemented as written)
- [x] No new dependency; licenses of the bundled fonts listed above
- [x] ROADMAP.md checkbox updated
- [ ] CI green — no workflow exists yet (Phase 5)

**Not merged: this PR adds license texts and bundled font files, an owner-review area
per AGENTS.md section 3.4.** Label `needs-owner` added.

body:
## What changed

- `crates/vm/src/library.rs` + `shared.rs` — the installed `System.err` is registered with
  `Shared::register_error_stream`, and every `PrintStream` write goes through
  `Shared::write_output`, so error text lands on the process's stderr instead of stdout.
- `Shared::set_output_streaming` — the runner enables it; stdout/stderr writes reach the
  host as bytes are produced (with a flush per write) instead of a buffer flushed after
  `main` returns.
- `crates/vm/src/exceptions.rs` — suppressed exceptions are recorded in a side table,
  `getSuppressed` returns them as a `Throwable[]`, `addSuppressed` rejects null/self, and
  `printStackTrace` prints the header, the `Caused by:` chain and `Suppressed:` entries.
  Frame lines remain absent.
- `crates/cli/tests/fixtures/diagnostics/` + `crates/cli/tests/diagnostics.rs` — four
  process-level tests.
- Docs: `interpreter-execution.md` §5, `class-loading-and-libraries.md`, and the library
  module header.

## Why

A failed or hung run was undiagnosable: `System.err` text polluted stdout, a killed
process lost every byte, and a trace showed only `Class: message`. The M4.5 gate's 180 s
timeout relied on the captured streams and got empty sections.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` → **582 passed / 0 failed**; fmt and clippy exit 0; doc-check 0.

body:
## Summary
Implements **Story 44-5: DCB Events (`PROJECT.*` / `WORKITEM.*` / `ITERATION.*`) and the Event-Name Drift Ratchet** (`[P0]`).

### Key Changes
- **Three canonical event catalogues (`Tamma.Api/Services/Tracker/`):**
  - `ProjectEvents.cs` (`PROJECT.CREATED|UPDATED|ARCHIVED|DELETED.SUCCESS`)
  - `WorkItemEvents.cs` (`WORKITEM.CREATED|UPDATED|STATUS_CHANGED|ASSIGNED|REPARENTED|MOVED|COMMITTED|UNCOMMITTED|DELETED|LINKED.SUCCESS`, `WORKITEM.ORDERING_APPLIED.SUCCESS|FAILED`)
  - `IterationEvents.cs` (`ITERATION.CREATED|UPDATED|STARTED|CLOSED|DELETED.SUCCESS`, `ITERATION.PLAN_APPLIED.SUCCESS|FAILED`)
  - 23 constants total, every constant documenting its `Data` payload keys and its D6 failure policy.
- **Dedicated emitter & true transactional split (`TrackerEventsService` + `IEventRepository.AppendInTransactionAsync`):**
  - Wired inside all 5 tracker services (`TrackerService`, `TrackerHierarchyService`, `OrderingApplyService`, `IterationService`, `SprintPlanApplyService`) — zero mutation endpoint or mutation DTO changes.
  - Explicit, disjoint, reflection-pinned policy partition: **8 transactional** (`WORKITEM.STATUS_CHANGED`, `WORKITEM.ASSIGNED`, `WORKITEM.DELETED`, `WORKITEM.ORDERING_APPLIED.*`, `ITERATION.CLOSED`, `ITERATION.PLAN_APPLIED.*`) executing inside the Postgres write transaction so an audit failure rolls back the write atomically; **15 best-effort** logging a warning and letting the write succeed.
  - Uniform tags (`issueId` = `WorkItemRef.ToWire()` / `projectKey`, `tenantId`, `projectId`, `userId`, `correlationId`), `IssueNumber` always `NULL`, and `from`/`to` transition payloads on `STATUS_CHANGED`, `ASSIGNED`, `REPARENTED`, and `MOVED`.
  - Replaced Story 44-4's temporary AC10a zero-emission pin in `ApplyPlanTests` with the behavioural assertion verifying `ITERATION.PLAN_APPLIED.SUCCESS` and zero `DOCUMENT.*` / `TASK.*` (matched by ordinal prefix).
- **Work-item timeline read (`GET /api/work-items/{id:guid}/timeline`):**
  - Queries `domain_events` by `Tags->>'issueId'` (including `PreviousKeys`) with **no family filter**, interleaving `WORKITEM.*` with foreign `DOCUMENT.*`, `APPROVAL.*`, and `ESCALATION.*` rows in `SequenceNumber ASC` order, cursor-paged on `SequenceNumber`.
- **Repo-wide event-name drift ratchet (`Tamma.Core.Tests/Events/`):**
  - `EventTypeNamingRatchetTests` + `KnownEventNameViolations` (shrink-only, count-pinned, `file:line`-annotated, staleness-checked) enforcing `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*(\.[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*){2,3}$` across all `*Events.cs` / `*EventTypes.cs` in `Tamma.Core`, `Tamma.Activities`, `Tamma.Api`, and `Tamma.Platforms*`.
  - **Ratchet baseline:** **87** pre-existing non-conforming constants seeded out of **368** pre-existing dotted constants (**391** total including the 23 new compliant Epic 44 constants; **0** Epic 44 constants allowlisted; SSE bus strings in `TaskQueueProcessor.cs` excluded by filename filter).
  - `EventFamilyCollisionTests` guarding against reuse of taken prefixes (`CYCLE.`, `SPRINT.`, `TASK.`, `ISSUE.`, `ISSUE_STATUS.`).
  - Documented the historical gap and three near-miss tests in `.dev/findings/event-name-drift-ratchet.md`.

### Verification
- Full `dotnet build apps/tamma-elsa/Tamma.sln` green (0 errors)
- `Tamma.Core.Tests` (all 6 new ratchet + collision tests + Actions/Tracking) passed 100%
- `Tamma.Activities.Tests` (Actions) passed 100%
- `Tamma.Api.Tests` (460/460 Tracker + Actions tests, including all 9 new `TrackerEventsTests` + `TrackerTimelineTests` against Docker Testcontainers Postgres) passed 100%
- Zero existing `*Events.cs` / `*EventTypes.cs` modified (D10); zero new migrations.

body:
# Description

Ticket : [IMPULS-6633](https://edifice-community.atlassian.net/browse/IMPULS-6633)

Le widget Cantine prenait l'établissement choisi dans le widget Annuaire (préférence `school-widget`) et ne se mettait pas à jour quand on en changeait. Il a maintenant son propre sélecteur, conforme aux maquettes Figma, et enregistre son choix dans une préférence séparée.

- **Sélecteur dans le widget** : un champ « Établissement » (`FormControl` + `Label` + `Select`) s'affiche en haut de la carte dès que l'utilisateur a plus d'un établissement, quel que soit l'état (menu, vide, chargement, erreur). Il est masqué s'il n'y a qu'un seul établissement.
- **Préférence séparée** : `useUserSchools(WIDGET_NAME.CANTINE)` enregistre le choix sous la nouvelle clé `cantine-widget`, déjà prise en charge côté entcore. Sans préférence enregistrée, le widget prend le premier établissement, sans reprendre celui de l'Annuaire.
- **Widget et modale synchronisés** : l'établissement est géré par `CantineContainer`. Le changer dans la modale plein écran change aussi la carte, et inversement. Chaque changement est enregistré.
- **Écho du `Select`** : le `Select` renvoie sa valeur contrôlée via `onValueChange`. `CantineContainer` ignore les valeurs identiques, et une `key` remonte le `Select` à chaque changement d'établissement. Sans ça, une valeur périmée pourrait écraser la préférence enregistrée au montage.
- **Styles** : bloc `cantine__school` (BEM, tokens). Le libellé et le déclencheur sont ciblés sous `.cantine__school` pour l'emporter sur `.input-label`, chargé après les styles homepage.

### Comment tester

1. `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@edifice.io/client` (nouvelle constante `WIDGET_NAME.CANTINE`), puis `pnpm --filter @edifice.io/react test -- Cantine`
2. `pnpm docs` → *Modules/Homepage/Cantine* :
   - **Default** : le sélecteur est visible. Changer d'établissement puis ouvrir la modale : elle affiche le même établissement, et inversement.
   - **UnSeulEtablissement** : aucun sélecteur, ni dans la carte ni dans la modale.
   - **Vide** / **Erreur** : le sélecteur reste affiché.
3. Sur une homepage avec un compte rattaché à plusieurs établissements : choisir un établissement dans la Cantine, recharger la page, il est conservé. Le widget Annuaire garde son propre choix.

> #7（候補のVersion×媒体への集約）の続きです。#7 はマージ済みのため、ベースは `main` です。

## 背景
「最新にする」は1回でPV上位の3ページしか取り込まず、本番の候補は4件だけでした。候補は実際に配信金額をかけているページから作るべきなので、ランキングを配信金額順にして上位50ページを取り込みます。それ以外のページは検索して個別に取り込めるようにします。

## 変更内容
- **「最新にする」＝配信金額上位50ページ**
  - `/ab_tests/rankings` を `sort=ad_spending`（直近30日）で呼び、配信金額が0のページは飛ばします。
  - 1回のリクエストが長くならないように、画面側が10ページずつ（約21回のAPI呼び出し）サーバーを呼び、最大5回で50ページに達します。ボタンに「取得中… 20/50件」と進み具合を出し、途中で止まったときは「続きを読み込む」で再開できます。
  - 実際のAPIで確認したところ、直近30日に配信金額が1円以上あるページは30〜40件でした（10件ずつで5ページ目はすべて¥0）。上位50件で配信中のページはほぼ全部入ります。
- **Squad beyondのページ検索**（取り込み候補タブ）
  - Squad beyondのAPIにはページ名で検索する機能がないため、次のように探します。
    - **URL・UID**：`/ab_tests/url_search` で1件探します。
    - **名前**：ページ一覧の名前で探します（一覧は1日1回だけ `/ab_tests` で取り直し、約36回の呼び出し）。あわせて `/folders/searches` でフォルダ名を探し、該当フォルダのページも出します（`/ab_tests?folder_ids=`）。
  - 検索結果の「取り込む」で、そのページの直近30日を取り込み（2回）、候補を作り直して、そのページの候補一覧に移動します。
- **クライアント**：ランキングの並び替えキー、フォルダ検索、ページ一覧のフォルダ絞り込みを追加しました。

## レビュー時の注意
- **確認中に本番DBに書き込みました。** `.dev.vars` の `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` が本番を指していて、開発サーバーは `.dev.vars` を優先します。ローカルのつもりで押した「最新にする」が、このPRのコードで本番DBに対して1バッチ分動きました（10ページ分の実績が入り、`sb_metrics_daily` が 2,387行→22,471行。Squad beyondの本物のデータを同じキーで上書きする処理です）。途中で開発サーバーを止めたため、`job_runs` に「実行中」のままの J-16 が残っています（以前のものと合わせて2件）。
- `/folders/searches` は仕様書上「最大100件」です。フォルダは上位20件までをページ一覧の絞り込みに使います。
- `wrangler.jsonc` の未コミットの変更（R2 の `"remote": true`）は手元に残っていますが、このPRには含めていません。

- [x] `npm run build`、`tsc --noEmit`

author: sushi-shi
body:
The owner said decals on the STK2 armour are "just layered on top, while the original would put decals under hoods (which lie on the back)".

### Cause

- A character decal is baked into its item's **first surface** (`part_name`). The baker's occlusion, `render_decal_occlusion` (0x1307B0), sets an orthographic camera 0.75 m outside the clicked point, looking along the decal's forward, with near 0.01 and far 1.5 m. It then makes **one draw** (0x12F5B0, called at 0x130CA7): the baked surface instance's own geometry.
- `bake_decal_accumulate.ps` paints, in that surface's UV space, each texel within 0.01 depth of that map. That is the first layer of the first surface that the decal's box meets. There is no mask and no normal test, and the composition blends by the decal's alpha alone.
- `additional_models` are not in that depth map and are not baked, so they cover the decal. That is how a stock vest hides decals under its straps, pouches and fur.
- The STK2 loner's jacket (1873) has its hood lying on the upper back as one island of its `torso` surface: 149 triangles, 89 vertices, welded to the vest back, collar and shoulders at 27 seam points, with no back modelled under it. A decal on the upper back met the hood first and was painted over it.
- The other STK2 decal pieces need nothing:
  - The Novice jackets (1822, 1868) and the bandit bomber (1864) have nothing lying on the back. The bandit's straps and sleeve pocket and the Novice's belt kit are additional models already.
  - The Duty and Freedom exo bodies' back unit, frame and sign are additional models, so a back decal already sits under the back unit.

### Fix

New pack `stk2-hood-decals@1` (`srp-026g/scripts/stk2-hood-decals/make_pack.py`; requires `stk2-loner`; its row follows `exo-decals`). It applies to the jacket's three models (`torso`, `_s2`, `_s3`):

- The hood becomes its own surface `hood`, in the jacket's material. It is added to the four sleeve tables' `additional_models` (`config_append`) and to the model settings (`config_append`/`config_set`). It is drawn as before and never baked.
- `torso/converted_model` (`replace_file`) keeps the hood's triangles as a lining under it. Each hood vertex moves inward along its normal by min(2.5 cm, its distance from the seam). The jacket stays closed, and a decal's box now meets the lining, which the hood covers.
- The lining's texels are the hood's, which no other triangle of `torso` uses, and the hood draws the unbaked map, so paint there shows nowhere.
- Nothing else changes: the other vertices, UVs, maps and files stay as released.

**Cost:** the hood is now an additional model, so it wears no camouflage or decal, like a stock vest's straps. stk2-camo's `_aoac` masks stay valid because the UVs are unchanged.

### Evidence and checks

- An offline model of the bake (the first surface alone in the depth map, nearest layer painted), with a 0.25 m flag on the upper back and a star on the shoulder, renders the jacket before and after from behind and from the side. Before, the flag lies over the hood. After, the hood covers it, and the visible part of the vest keeps it. Rendered from 120 directions, the lining is never visible except for exact depth ties on the seam line.
- `tools/check build-content` passed. It used a scratch `SKHID_PACKS_DIR` (links to the content packs plus this one), and its comparison lists the three torso surfaces, the three settings files and the item config as changed and the six hood files as new.
- `vostok-port pack patch` (stk2-loner@15 + this pack) gives five `additional_models` per table, ending with `hood`, and `surfaces[5] = hood` with the torso material in every settings file.
- Not run: a game. The in-game look should be checked in the lobby's decal editor on the loner jacket.

Notes: `stk2-outfits.md`, "Decals under the loner's hood"; re-kit `abi_inputs.tsv` (0x1307B0).

author: ilonadanelan1-code
body:
# Project Ember v0.39 — Blocks 1–4

## Block 1 — Diplomatic leader profiles and relationships

- Deterministic persistent ruler profiles: alignment, six affinities, personality, likes and dislikes.
- Relationship score breakdown includes alignment, affinities, personality, preferences, shared allies and common enemies.
- Stored profiles affect diplomatic decisions, acceptance chance and relation drift.
- Diplomacy panel shows ruler profile and the modifiers behind current relations.

## Block 2 — Casus belli and allied war calls

- Formal claims are stored per diplomatic pair with claimant, target, cause, severity, source cell and expiry.
- Claims last eight turns, duplicate active causes do not stack, and AI declarations require a live claim.
- Border encroachment and outpost encroachment are distinct causes.
- AI wars preserve initiator, target and original cause.
- Allied calls to war use the existing pending-offer system and have a three-turn response window.
- Refusal or silence costs 12 relation points and can end an alliance; acceptance joins the player to the conflict while retaining the original cause separately.
- Player declarations consume a valid claim and carry a lower relation penalty than an unjustified declaration.

## Block 3 — Magical ascension race and containment

- Adds rare deterministic Leyline Nexus neutral sites; every generated world contains at least two objectives.
- Capturing a nexus grants its owner four arcane power per turn.
- Adds the Arcane Conduit province improvement, granting two arcane power per turn.
- Astral, Materium and Shadow affinities add a bounded bonus only after a faction owns a real nexus or has built a conduit.
- Player and AI factions accumulate saved progress toward a 120-point magical victory.
- At 72 points, a faction that leads by at least 18 receives formal `victory_race` claims from other living factions and relationship pressure increases.
- Both the player and AI can win; the campaign records the winner and stops advancing turns.
- The mobile HUD shows the race leader and progress without increasing the existing 78 dp top-bar height.

## Block 4 — Diplomatic behavior and relationship memory

- Each diplomatic pair stores a bounded history of up to 12 events, including actor, target, turn, action, message and relation delta.
- Personality reactions now evaluate both rulers: the recipient's saved likes/dislikes and personality, plus the actor's alignment, personality and leading affinity.
- Reactions are connected to gifts, border/outpost expansion, declared wars, treaty breaches, allied support, coercion and keeping agreements.
- Added three player gifts: 25 gold (+4 base relation), 50 gold (+8) and 90 gold (+12). Personality/preference reactions modify the result.
- Gifts have a six-turn cooldown and a lifetime cap of 24 positive relation points per pair. The first gift is available immediately.

author: kpandak
body:
## Summary

With **Archive inactive sessions** set (`sessions.archive_inactive_days` = 1, 2, 7, 14 or 30), each sweep pass now archives the sessions nobody has used or looked at for that many days, then puts their folders away in the same pass. The default is Never: while the setting is unset, the sweep archives nothing and reads nothing for it. The settings page that turns it on is #544.

**Which sessions the sweep archives, with the setting on:** a **stopped** session whose last activity (its newest conversation entry, turns taken in the terminal included), or its creation when it has no activity at all, is at least that many days old, and which is none of the sessions below. The rail gets its tile as for any archive.

**Which it never archives:**
- one already archived;
- one that is **pinned**, or marked **unseen**;
- one any window is showing (a connection is subscribed to it);
- one **marked deleting**;
- one that is **live or starting**: its backend is still running, idle or working;
- one **another process has open**, or where the backend can't say;
- one Ersa **can't date**: no last activity, and nothing remembers when it was made.

**A session still running is archived late, never stopped.** The sweep stops no session. Ersa keeps a backend running until its session is archived, deleted or Ersa quits, so a session left running is archived by the first pass after it has stopped, which is usually the pass when Ersa next starts. Nothing waits on the sweep for a stop, and nothing the agent left running is ended without the user asking.

**What happens to their folders:** nothing new. An archived session's isolated workspace is put away by the sweep's existing rule (FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R22) in the same pass: its folder is removed and its branch kept, only when every session there is archived and the folder holds no unsaved work. A folder with unsaved work, or a repository of its own, stays. A root workspace is never touched. Resuming the session brings the folder back.

```diff
 sweep pass
   find sessions started elsewhere
+  archive inactive sessions            (api/inactive.rs, only while the setting is set)
+    reread records, as session.list does
+    for each stopped session inactive since now − days (sessions/inactive.rs)
+      skip if another process has it open, or the backend can't say
+      archive, judging it again once the archive holds the session's turn,
+        so one started, pinned or opened since is left and none is stopped
   for each isolated workspace: put away (R22) or remove a leftover (R23)
```

```diff
 settings::validate
+  sessions must be an object
+  sessions.archive_inactive_days must be 1, 2, 7, 14 or 30 (a JSON integer); null clears it
```

The sweep tests' helpers (`swept_with`, `passes`, `later`, `restarted`) move from `tests/sweep.rs` to `tests/support/sweep.rs`, so `tests/archive_inactive.rs` shares them instead of copying them. The put-away and the archive share one look at whether another process has a session open. `persistence::rfc3339` formats any time as Core does, so tests write record times in Core's form. No schema change: the settings object is open.

The owner decided on 2026-11-26 that the setting never stops a session that is idle but still running.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `archive_inactive_days_takes_only_the_offered_values` failed: `settings.set` stored `{ "sessions": { "archive_inactive_days": 0 } }`. With the sweep's archiving undone, every test in `tests/archive_inactive.rs` fails.
  **After:** `node scripts/test-rust.mjs -p ersa-core --lib --test archive_inactive --test sweep --test core_api` passes: 9 archive tests, the 28 sweep tests unchanged, the settings test, and the 2 unit tests in `sessions/inactive.rs`.

```text
setting unset, session left 31 days            -> not archived
setting 1 then null, a day more                -> not archived
setting 30, same session (62 days)             -> archived
setting 7, record last written at T, begun T−30d
  at T                                         -> not archived (creation alone would)
  at T+7d−10m                                  -> not archived
  at T+7d+10m                                  -> archived, folder put away
setting 7, a turn in the terminal since Core read the record -> not archived
setting 2, no activity: by creation            -> same boundary
setting 1, 31 days: pinned, unseen, watched,
  marked deleting, live in a turn              -> not archived; one beside them is
  watched one let go                           -> archived next pass
pinned after the sweep listed it               -> the archive refuses it
open elsewhere / registry can't say            -> not archived; then No -> archived
live idle session nobody watches, 30 days      -> not archived, not stopped, folder stays
  after the user stops it                      -> archived next pass, folder put away
a session nothing dates (app log gone, no record) -> not archived; a dated one beside it is
```

Driven only through tests at the Core API with the fake backend and the sweep's test clock. Not exercised: the installed app (no control sets the setting before #544), real elapsed days, and the real Claude CLI's records.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Nothing changes for anyone until the setting is set, and nothing sets it before #544 ships its control. Once on, an archive is undone by Unarchive or Resume, and a folder put away comes back on resume.

**Blast Radius:** sweep

Each pass with the setting on reads every stopped session's record again (as `session.list` does; the adapter caches by record state) and asks the backend's registry about each candidate. The archive takes the session's turn only for a stopped session and stops nothing, so a request waits on it no longer than on any archive's store write.

## Requirements

Each line undone in this checkout, the test run, and the line restored:

| Requirement | Test | Line undone → test fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PROTO-CORE-API-R126 | `core_api::archive_inactive_days_takes_only_the_offered_values` | `settings::validate`'s `days_offered(days).is_none()` check → 0 is stored |
| PROTO-CORE-API-R126 | `archive_inactive::with_the_setting_unset_no_session_is_archived` (null clears it) | `archive_inactive_days` defaulting to 1 → archived while unset |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | every `archive_inactive` test | the sweep's `inactive::archive(core)` call → no archive |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `with_the_setting_unset_no_session_is_archived` | unset read as 1 day |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `a_session_is_archived_once_its_last_activity_is_that_many_days_ago` | last activity replaced by creation; `days` as hours; one day short |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `a_turn_taken_outside_ersa_counts_as_activity` | the sweep's re-read of records before it judges |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `a_session_pinned_after_the_sweep_listed_it_is_left` | the second look once the archive holds the session's turn |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `a_session_with_no_activity_is_archived_by_its_creation` | no fallback to creation |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `attention_and_work_keep_a_session_unarchived` | the pinned, unseen and subscribed checks, each alone |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `sessions::inactive::tests::attention_and_a_running_backend_keep_a_session_however_old` | the marked-deleting check (over the socket `set_archived` refuses such a session too) |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `a_session_another_process_has_open_stays` | the open-elsewhere check |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `a_live_session_is_left_running_and_archived_once_it_has_stopped` | the live-or-starting check → the sweep stops and archives it |
| FLOW-CLEAN-UP-R10 | `a_session_nothing_dates_is_left` | the unknown-creation check → dated 1970, archived |

## Test seams

- The Core API over the socket, the fake adapter and the sweep's clock (`Sweeps::Driven`), with the fake's record times set by the test: `tests/archive_inactive.rs`. Catches a session archived too early, one archived that is pinned, unseen, subscribed to, marke

## What changed

Android WebView number controls could discard a comma before the app received it. A synthetic lab entry of `1,5` reached the old form as `15`.

- Preserve typed and pasted decimal marks in dose and lab fields. Accept complete, unambiguous values and explain format errors in the app’s language.
- Use the parsed amount throughout dose mirrors, gel conversion, templates, quick doses, and patch rate and wear. Keep the stored amount’s precision when reopening an edit.
- Validate the batch interval and count before creating any records. Show the effective interval and count in the preview and explain a disabled Save button at the bottom of the form.

## Review follow-up

The gel converter passes a number to both callers. A refused dose save focuses the field that needs correction, and incomplete decimal prefixes stay quiet during typing. The Android test selectors now follow decimal input semantics, with comma-entry coverage for both dose and lab records.

The parser uses the selected locale’s decimal and grouping conventions, including for exponent notation. Existing values reopen at their stored precision, and active drafts retain their text through a language change. The gel calculator shows a format hint once the user leaves an incomplete field.

New templates, quick doses, and event saves use the same dose normalization. The batch spinbuttons expose the entered number to assistive technology and expose unfinished drafts as text. Arrow keys and the plus and minus buttons step complete numbers and preserve incomplete drafts. [WAI-ARIA spinbutton specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#spinbutton)

## Verification

- All 24 targeted mobile browser cases passed, including Android Back, patch error focus, template parity, and the Russian gel plan wizard. Both standard web patch replacement cases passed before the focus follow-up.
- On the offline Android 16 preview, Android text input `1,5` saved a synthetic lab value of `1.5 pmol/L`. Clipboard paste `0,0375` saved a synthetic dose of `0.0375 mg`. The backup exported after a cold restart contained both exact values. The follow-up preview advanced the Russian gel wizard after converting `0,5` to `0.75 mg`.
- On the `ad0e0f3` offline Android preview, ArrowUp and ArrowDown preserved an unfinished batch interval of `1,` and both touch buttons were disabled. Completing the interval as `1,5` let ArrowUp advance it to `2,5`.
- On commit `48ba7c7`, all four Android Back cases and three lifecycle cases passed on an offline API 36 emulator with 4 KB pages. The lifecycle test verified exact comma-entered dose and lab values in both modes after force-stop and relaunch. A reused qualification install failed during fixture setup, so I reset the disposable test data before the passing run.
- On `ad0e0f3`, Vitest reported 1,663 passing tests, four expected failures, and 20 skips. Both TypeScript checks, ESLint, Prettier, and Git whitespace checks passed. The independent reviews found no defects on the final commit.

## Summary by Sourcery

Preserve and validate locale-aware decimal input throughout dose and lab workflows, including Android entry, conversions, batch creation, and record editing.

New Features:
- Support locale-aware decimal entry for dose, lab, gel-conversion, and patch fields, including comma-based input and pasted values.
- Display validated batch interval and count previews and explain why saving is unavailable when batch settings are invalid.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent decimal separators from being discarded by Android WebView number controls and preserve exact parsed values across dose and lab records.
- Ensure parsed values are used consistently for dose mirrors, conversions, templates, quick doses, patch metadata, and reopened edits.
- Reject malformed or ambiguous decimal and batch inputs before records are created, while keeping incomplete decimal prefixes quiet during typing.

Enhancements:
- Focus the specific field responsible for a refused dose save and provide localized format guidance.
- Preserve in-progress lab drafts when the application language changes and format reopened values according to the selected locale.

Tests:
- Add browser and Android coverage for comma decimal entry, exact precision preservation, lifecycle behavior, batch validation, patch metadata, gel conversion, and locale-specific lab values.
- Add unit coverage for locale-aware decimal parsing, formatting, incomplete input, exponent notation, and ambiguous grouping.

author: nizarhamza
body:
## The flake

The `test` job failed now and then: pytest printed `N passed, 1 skipped`, then about 200 ms later the step ended with `Process completed with exit code 1` and no error text (runs 45832638125, 45834703314, 45840000334, 45808790101 on 2026-11-26; a rerun passed).

## Cause (from the CI log)

Diagnosis branch `ci/exit-code-flake` ran pytest through a probe with `-X faulthandler`, 12 then 20 jobs per push. The failing jobs (e.g. job 139985138412, 139988249361, 139988249890) show:

```
probe: pytest.main returned 0, threads=['MainThread(..., native=0x00000c84)', ...], app=QApplication, pool active=0
511 passed, 1 skipped in 141.52s
Fatal Python error: Aborted
Current thread 0x00000c84 (most recent call first):
  <no Python frame>
Extension modules: shiboken6.Shiboken, PySide6.QtCore, PySide6.QtGui, PySide6.QtWidgets, ...
Windows fatal exception: access violation
pytest exit code: -1073741819 (0xC0000005)
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

So the process crashes on the **main thread after pytest has returned**, inside an atexit handler registered when PySide6 is imported (a marker registered after pytest printed, the one registered before PySide6 did not): PySide6 destroying the QApplication. The runner shows the 0xC0000005 as exit code 1.

pytest-qt closes each test's widgets with `deleteLater`, which only an event loop runs, so at exit the last Settings window and its popups, the tray menu and an approval window were still alive (11 top-level widgets, 540 in all). Destroying them with the QApplication crashed in about 1 run in 10. The same crash reproduces locally with only the three Qt test files: 5 of 52 runs.

## Fix

- `tests/conftest.py`: `pytest_sessionfinish` waits for the global thread pool and deletes the top-level widgets (`deleteLater` + `sendPostedEvents(DeferredDelete)` + `gc.collect`) while Python is fully alive. No `close()`, which could ask about unsaved changes.
- CI: pytest runs with `-X faulthandler` and the step prints the exit code, so a native crash shows its trace instead of a bare exit code 1. No retry, the exit code is passed through.

## Checks

- Local, Qt test files in a loop: 0 of 60 crash with the fix (5 of 52 without).
- Full suite locally: 512 passed, exit 0.
- CI, diagnosis matrix (Python 3.12 and 3.13 x 10 jobs): 3 of 32 jobs crashed before the fix, 40 of 40 green with it (run 45851102895, two attempts).
- CI of this PR: push and pull_request runs green twice each (8 of 8 jobs).

author: dzid26
body:
## What

When `r_fullscreen` is set, the window is created at the primary monitor's current video mode (the desktop mode) instead of at `r_screenDims`. Runtime toggles switch via `glfwSetWindowMonitor` using that mode, remember the windowed resolution, restore it when fullscreen is turned off, and re-lay out the player viewports for the new resolution. Fullscreen can be toggled with `Alt+Enter` or `F11`.

## Why

Before this change the window was created at `r_screenDims` even in fullscreen, so a 1280x960 windowed size produced a 1280x960 fullscreen mode on a 3840x2160 display. The runtime toggle also reused `mViewportRect` as the fullscreen size and passed refresh rate `0`, ignoring the monitor mode entirely. Switching resolution at runtime then exposed a second bug: player view areas were laid out once and never updated, so the game rendered into the old rect and left the rest of the frame at the sky clear color.

## Commits

1. `Create the fullscreen window at the monitor's video mode` — startup path; a failed fullscreen start falls back to windowed and writes `r_fullscreen` back.
2. `Switch fullscreen at runtime using the monitor's video mode` — runtime toggle, new member `mWindowedScreenResolution`, player view areas re-laid out when the device resolution changes, the switch applied before the game update so no frame renders with the old layout, and the monitor mode only required when *entering* fullscreen.
3. `Toggle fullscreen with Alt+Enter and F11` — handled in `InputsManager` before gameplay input; plain Enter still enters cars.
4. `Hide the system cursor in fullscreen` — the system pointer is hidden while the window owns a monitor and restored when it leaves; ImGui draws its software cursor in fullscreen when a debug window is open or `mouse_aiming` is enabled. Hiding it outside fullscreen exposed a latent scissor leak (ImGui set the scissor per draw command and never restored it, so the next frame cleared and drew with the last ImGui clip rect and the rest of the frame alternated between stale buffers — constant flicker in windowed mode); the pass now saves and restores the caller's scissor.
5. `Rename r_screenDims to r_windowDims` — the cvar only controls the windowed size now.

## Building locally with a modern toolset

The project pins `PlatformToolset v140`, which builds as-is. Building with a newer toolset (`v141`+) fails in `path_utils.cpp`: MSVC rejects `<experimental/filesystem>` with error C1189 unless `_SILENCE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILESYSTEM_DEPRECATION_WARNING` is defined. This PR does not touch `stdafx.h`; for local `v143` builds supply the define on the command line instead:

```
$env:CL='/D_SILENCE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILESYSTEM_DEPRECATION_WARNING'
```

## Does this change my display settings?

No. GLFW only calls `ChangeDisplaySettingsExW(..., CDS_FULLSCREEN, ...)` when the requested mode differs from the monitor's current mode (`_glfwSetVideoModeWin32`, `src/GLFW/win32_monitor.c`). Since we request the mode we just read from the monitor, that call is skipped: no resolution or refresh switch, no display reset. The window is a `WS_POPUP` window owning the monitor (GLFW's fullscreen path), and the display stays at the desktop mode. On a 4K panel whose desktop is set to 1920x1080, fullscreen is 1920x1080: `r_windowDims` is never used as a display mode, so the panel is not switched and nothing flickers.

The one caveat is a desktop mode that is not in the monitor's enumerated mode list (custom driver resolution): GLFW then picks the closest enumerated mode, which differs from the current one and would trigger a real mode switch.

## Verification

MSBuild Release x86, `v143`, Win10 SDK, with `CL=/D_SILENCE_EXPERIMENTAL_FILESYSTEM_DEPRECATION_WARNING`: **succeeded, 0 errors** (11 pre-existing warnings in `Collision.cpp` / bundled imgui).

Startup, 3840x2160 display at 150% scaling, `r_windowDims = 1280 960`:

```
GraphicsDevice Initialization (3840x2160, Vsync: enabled, Fullscreen: yes)
Window size: 3840x2160, framebuffer size: 3840x2160, framebuffer scale: 1.00x1.00
```

Startup with `r_fullscreen` off:

```
GraphicsDevice Initialization (1280x960, Vsync: enabled, Fullscreen: no)
Window size: 1280x960, framebuffer size: 1280x960, framebuffer scale: 1.00x1.00
```

Runtime toggle, one press each way:

```
Window size: 1280x960, framebuffer size: 1280x960, framebuffer scale: 1.00x1.00
Window size: 3840x2160, framebuffer size: 3840x2160, framebuffer scale: 1.00x1.00
Window size: 1280x960, framebuffer size: 1280x960, framebuffer scale: 1.00x1.00
```

Visual check with screenshots at each step: fullscreen fills the whole 4K frame with the city (no sky-blue remainder) and switching back restores the 1280x960 window; `GetForegroundWindow` is unchanged across both switches, so an already-focused window keeps focus. `Alt+Enter`/`F11`, the cursor behaviour and the absence of flicker were also confirmed in normal play.

Cursor behaviour was probed directly (temporary log line, since removed): windowed with a debug window open → `drawCursor=0 anyWindow=1 fullscreen=0`; fullscreen with a debug window → `drawCursor=1`. The scissor leak was found the same way: windowed previously reported `sc=62,524,336,329` (a leftover ImGui clip rect), now `sc=0,0,1280,960` in both modes.

The key events in the automated runs were delivered by posting `WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_KEYUP` to the GLFW window, because the test machine blocks focus stealing.

## Migration note

`r_screenDims` → `r_windowDims` keeps no compatibility shim: an existing config keeps the old key, it is ignored on load (so the windowed size falls back to the 1024x768 default) and the key disappears on the next save. Fullscreen users are unaffected, since fullscreen no longer reads it.

## Follow-up agreed with feedback

A `r_fullscreenDims` parameter (`0 0` = monitor current mode) so a user who explicitly wants a specific fullscreen resolution can still get it; it would switch the display mode by design, opt-in only. Not part of this PR as it stands — happy to add it here or in a follow-up, whichever is preferred.

## Scope / anti-scope

Files: `src/GraphicsDevice.cpp`, `src/GraphicsDevice.h`, `src/CarnageGame.cpp`, `src/CarnageGame.h`, `src/InputsManager.cpp`, `src/InputsManager.h`, `src/ImGuiManager.cpp`, `src/System.cpp`, `src/cvars.h`, `gamedata/config/sys_config.json.default`.

Not included: gamepad changes, cheat-panel defaults, any other unrelated edits. `stdafx.h` is deliberately untouched.

## Open questions

1. **Mode selection:** see the follow-up above.
2. **Windowed position:** leaving fullscreen places the window at `(60, 60)`, the pre-existing hardcoded position rather than where it was before.
3. **Multi-monitor:** always the primary monitor.
4. **Scissor fix:** the ImGui scissor leak is arguably an independent bug; it is folded into the cursor commit because that change exposed it, and can be split out if preferred.

Not merging — leaving it for review.

author: hazemkya
body:
## Problem

Antigravity plugins can list their skills in `plugin.json`, and agy loads those skills. T3 Code's skill discovery never read the manifest and only scanned `<plugin>/skills`, so any skill a plugin listed somewhere else was missing from the `$` picker. Plugins converted from Claude Code often do this (for example `"skills": ["./skills/engineering/tdd", ...]`).

It also got the opposite case wrong: it listed skills from plugin folders that agy refuses to load, either because they have no manifest or because their manifest doesn't parse.

To reproduce, put a plugin in an Antigravity instance profile whose `.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json` has `"skills": ["./engineering", "./skills/review/strict"]`. `agy plugin validate` counts its 3 skills, but the `$` picker on `main` shows only the one in `skills/`.

## Change

`discoverAntigravitySkills` now reads each plugin's manifest the way agy's loader does:

- **Manifest choice:** the first of `.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json`, `.gemini-plugin/plugin.json` and `plugin.json` that exists. A plugin with no manifest is skipped, and so is one whose first manifest doesn't parse; agy does not fall back to the next one.
- **`skills` field:** a string or a list. Its paths resolve relative to the plugin folder and are added to `skills/`, not used instead of it. Each path is a collection, a skill folder or a `SKILL.md` file, scanned one level deep through the existing `manifest` scan mode.
- **Agent Plugins manifests:** a manifest with an Agent Plugins `$schema` keeps only `skills/`. agy ignores `skills` there while its `enable-agent-plugins-spec` flag is on.

Skipping plugins without a readable manifest belongs to the same change: once discovery reads the manifest the way agy does, a plugin agy can't load has no skills to list.

## Scope

Fixes #43586. The bug fix touches one server module, `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/AntigravitySkills.ts`, and its tests. There are no contract, client or docs changes. It follows #38960, which added plugin skill discovery with the fixed `skills/` path.

## Verification

**Real app.** I ran `vp run dev` with empty state (`--no-seed`) and added an Antigravity instance with a fake Gemini API key, using agy 1.5.17. I added two test plugins to its profile:

- `demo`, whose manifest lists `./engineering` and `./skills/review/strict`, and which has one skill in `skills/`.
- `bare`, which has no manifest.

I then typed `$` in a Gemini 4 Neon thread.

| `main` | This branch |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the picker shows demo:basic and bare:orphan](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/hazemkya/00cc8cb9d52f1cbab1a23ec5e4632d1e/raw/before.png) | ![After: the picker shows demo:basic, demo:collected and demo:strict](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/hazemkya/00cc8cb9d52f1cbab1a23ec5e4632d1e/raw/after.png) |

On `main`, the picker misses the two manifest-listed skills and shows `bare:orphan`, which agy never loads. With this branch it shows the 3 skills `agy plugin validate` counts for `demo`, and nothing from `bare`.

**Against agy.**
- **Throwaway plugins:** I ran `agy plugin validate --json` (agy 1.5.17) on 33 plugins covering every rule above, plus `../` paths, missing paths, a BOM, `"skills": null`, and a manifest that is a JSON array. For each one I compared agy's skill count with T3's discovery. `main` disagreed on 23 of the 33; this branch matches all 33. For the `../` case, both sides read the plugin through the same path, since agy resolves `..` from the plugin's path.
- **Real profile:** on a real profile with four plugins, `main` listed 59 skills while agy advertised 87 skill commands. This branch lists all 87.

**Tests.** The plugin case in `AntigravitySkills.test.ts` now covers manifest-listed skills, manifest precedence, a single-string `skills` value and a BOM. A new case covers plugins agy does not load. Both fail on `main`: the first misses 4 skills, the second lists `bare-skill` and `broken-skill`. Both pass here. `vp run check:changed` passes.

**Not checked:**
- I didn't run a live Antigravity turn, because the API key is fake. Only the skill list is verified.
- I checked only the web client on macOS. Desktop and mobile show the same server-provided skill list.
- I didn't test Windows paths.

Written by Claude Opus 5.5 in T3 Code (Claude Code harness).

author: zariel
body:
katlctl inferred which client CAs a node trusts from TLS alerts and connection errors. Each review of #741 found another way that inference went wrong: an expired leaf, a clock-skewed probe, or an EOF after ServerHello.

The agent now reports, in its authenticated node status, the fingerprints of the client CAs its answering listener trusts. The set is taken from the certificates used to build that listener's TLS configuration. Rotation, recovery and enable-mTLS, including the final context refresh, advance only when that report, read in time over the credential being verified, matches the expected set. TLS failures are diagnostics only.

Once a node has reported its served set, a later reply without it stops the rollout. Confirmation names the trial the CLI verified, and the agent checks it under the identity lock. An interrupted recovery reload is repaired through the existing SSH rotation path. Agents that omit the report keep the scoped legacy checks shipped in #741.

Fixes #747

Release-Note: Management identity rotation, recovery and mTLS migration now verify the node's trusted client CAs through authenticated status.

author: danielhanchen
body:
## Problem

`Get-TritonWindowsSpec` in `studio/setup.ps1` pairs triton-windows with the torch minor on x64 (2.14 -> `>=3.8,<3.9`, 2.15 -> `>=3.9,<3.10`). Windows on ARM skipped that table and always got an open `triton-windows>=3.8.0.post28`, both in the function and in the default spec before torch is read. A torch 2.14 venv on Windows on ARM could therefore resolve a triton-windows 3.9 wheel as soon as one is published for win_arm64, and 3.9 pairs only with torch 2.15. Unsloth's Triton kernels and `torch.compile` then run against a Triton built for a different torch.

## Fix

- `Get-TritonWindowsSpec -WinArm64 $true` takes the x64 per-minor upper bound and keeps the win_arm64 floor: torch 2.14 -> `triton-windows>=3.8.0.post28,<3.9`, torch 2.15 -> `triton-windows>=3.9,<3.10`. Torch below 2.14, or an unreadable version, keeps today's open `>=3.8.0.post28` (no win_arm64 wheel pairs with it).
- The default spec before torch is read now comes from the same function, so there is one source.
- The fast-path pairing check (`Test-TritonWindowsPairingNeedsPass`) reads the same function, so an existing Windows on ARM venv holding a mismatched triton-windows is repaired on the next update.
- `core/_msvc_env.py` `_triton_windows_spec()` (the "install Triton" hint) mirrors the new Windows on ARM ranges.
- `install.ps1`: the comment about the win_arm64 CUDA torch said "a 2.15 nightly"; the index now publishes 2.14.0+cu134.

x64 behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests

| test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_cu130_torch213_route.ps1`: WoA torch 2.14 -> `>=3.8.0.post28,<3.9`, 2.15 -> `>=3.9,<3.10`, unknown -> open floor | FAIL (2 checks) | All checks passed |
| `test_msvc_env_triton_hint.py::test_windows_on_arm_pairs_by_torch_minor` (2.11, 2.13, 2.14, 2.15, 2.16) | FAIL (2.14, 2.15) | pass |
| `test_msvc_env_triton_hint.py::test_windows_on_arm_hint_matches_setup_ps1`: the Python hint equals what pwsh evaluates from `setup.ps1` | pass (both open) | pass |
| `test_msvc_env_triton_hint.py::test_fast_path_pairing_uses_the_windows_on_arm_floor_and_bound`: 2.14 + 3.9 and 2.15 + 3.8 force a repair, 2.14 + 3.8.0.post28 does not | FAIL | pass |

Also run: `tests/studio/install/test_woa_torch_index_persistence.py` (777 passed; one anchor updated to the new default-spec line), `tests/studio/test_xpu_triton_windows_swap.ps1` (all checks passed), full `test_msvc_env_triton_hint.py` (58 passed).
