body:
## Description

Adds end-to-end provider token usage monitoring and inspectable reporting across all Code60 execution surfaces (Relay, Custom Assistants, project chats, workers, Scheduled Jobs, Workflows, and background helpers):

- **ACP turn telemetry capture (`src/agents/usage-collector.ts`, `src/agents/acp-client.ts`, `src/agents/index.ts`):** Captures quantitative per-turn signals at the ACP boundary while staying on the stable `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` import: optional `PromptResponse.usage` (Tier 1), `usage_update` snapshots and session-cumulative `cost` deltas (Tier 2), `compaction_update` markers, parallel tool-call wave grouping, and observed wire byte/character sizes (Tier 3). Never stores prompts, assistant replies, source code, file paths, or credentials.
- **3-tier token estimator & private SQLite ledger (`src/core/usage-estimator.ts`, `src/core/usage-store.ts`, `src/core/usage-report-format.ts`):** Computes both cumulative burn-rate tokens (new vs. cached/re-read vs. output) and net context growth with explicit method and confidence labels (`exact`, `derived`, `lower_bound`). Persists quantitative turn rows in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/code60/usage/usage.sqlite` (mode `0700`/`0600`, bounded to 90 days or 500,000 turns) using Node 24's built-in `node:sqlite`.
- **In-app Carbon UI (`src/renderer/usage-page.tsx`, `src/renderer/carbon/usage.scss`):** Adds the database-independent **Manage → Usage** (and **Apps → Usage**) page with provider/model burn-rate breakdown, burn timeline, surface breakdown, heavy session/workflow hotspot drill-down, expandable Turn Inspector audit rows, live `usage-changed` SSE refreshes, JSON/CSV/Markdown report export, and confirmed history clearing.
- **Read-only CLI (`src/management/usage.ts`, `src/management/cli.ts`):** Adds `code60 usage [--since ...] [--until ...] [--provider ...] [--surface ...] [--model ...] [--format table|json|markdown|csv] [--turns] [--limit N] [--out file [--force]]`, reading via loopback `POST /management/usage` when Code60 Gateway is running and falling back to offline read-only SQLite reads when stopped.
- **Documentation & self-knowledge:** Updates `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `src/contracts/knowledge.ts`, `docs/capabilities.md`, `FAQ.md`, and `TERMINOLOGY.md`.

## Testing done

- Automated checks and results:
  - `npm run check:precommit` (`check:instructions`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `check:unused`): **passed** (0 errors, Knip clean).
  - `npx vitest run --coverage --maxWorkers=1 && node scripts/check-coverage.mjs`: **379 / 379 test files passed** (3,566 passed, 2 skipped), **all four coverage non-regression gates passed** (Statements 73.32%, Branches 65.67%, Functions 67.08%, Lines 75.95%). Note: ran with `--maxWorkers=1` to avoid shared-host CPU contention where `test/removal-support.test.ts` SIGINT hit its 1s `waitFor` window under parallel load; confirmed passing in isolation and in the full sequential run without relaxing timeouts or gates.
  - `npm run build && npx playwright test usage.e2e.ts`: **passed** (8.2s) — verified live Relay turn capture, live SSE update on **Manage → Usage**, Carbon Dropdown filters, hotspot drill-down into Turn Inspector expansion, Markdown export, live `code60 usage --format json` CLI query, and confirmed Clear usage history.
- Manual verification and environment (OS, architecture, Node.js version):
  - macOS Apple Silicon (`darwin/arm64`), Node.js `v24.22.0`, branch `usage-monitoring` (worktree `/Users/matthew/.gemini/antigravity/worktrees/Code60 Live/usage_monitoring_branch`).
- Checks not run and why:
  - Full `npm run test:browser` across all 19 unrelated E2E specs was not run locally; targeted `test/usage.e2e.ts` verified the built backend + UI end-to-end and CI will run the path-routed browser matrix.

## Relevant context

- Related issues or design: Fresh local usage monitoring ledger (`usage.sqlite`); no legacy `events.jsonl` backfill required.
- Affected interfaces, modules, and platforms: `contracts`, `agents`, `core`, `automation`, `application`, `bridge`, `gateway`, `management`, `renderer` (zero new module boundaries or npm dependencies; `test/boundaries.test.ts` unchanged and passing).
- Compatibility changes, risks, and follow-up work: Additive only. Read-only monitoring without hard token budgets or guessed dollar price tables; `code60 usage --out <file>` refuses to overwrite existing files unless `--force` is passed.

## Review checklist

- [x] `npm run check` passes.
- [x] Tests cover changed behavior, including unit tests (`usage-collector.test.ts`, `usage-estimator.test.ts`, `usage-store.test.ts`, `management/usage.test.ts`, `usage-page.test.tsx`), capability/docs freshness tests, and Playwright E2E (`test/usage.e2e.ts`).
- [x] Behavior changes have been verified with Playwright (`npx playwright test usage.e2e.ts` against the built Node backend).
- [x] CLI help and relevant documentation reflect user-visible changes.
- [x] `FAQ.md` and `TERMINOLOGY.md` reflect user-visible changes (using `refreshingly-simple-english`, alphabetical terminology, and updated metadata).
- [x] Capability-affecting changes update `src/contracts/knowledge.ts` and `docs/capabilities.md` (`npm run generate:capabilities`).
- [x] Changes follow `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions.
- [x] Each commit includes the Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off required by `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

author: adam-ghanem
body:
## Security finding

The enterprise worker persisted free-form exception messages into `enterprise_jobs.last_error` and `enterprise_outbox.last_error`. Exception text can contain bearer/API tokens, webhook URLs, private IPs/hostnames, filesystem paths, or event payload fragments. Truncating the string to 500 characters does not make it safe.

## Changes

- Map common built-in exception types to a small fixed set of diagnostic codes; never call `str(error)`.
- Enforce the same allowlist again at both SQLite persistence functions, so future callers cannot bypass the worker-side mapping by passing arbitrary strings.
- Preserve useful coarse categories such as `timeout`, `connection_error`, `permission_error`, and `runtime_error`; unknown values become `worker_error`.
- Add regressions for job and outbox worker failures containing synthetic tokens, URLs, private addresses, hostnames, and paths, plus a direct persistence-boundary allowlist test.
- Document the privacy boundary and recommend access-controlled external diagnostics for deeper troubleshooting.

## Latest validation — 2026-11-26

Final head: `5bafe798608f4f4748a4d8ea9cd9e7615069ef0b`.

- [Python CI #45883837848](https://github.com/Adam-Ghanem/NetWatch/actions/runs/45883837848): success. Black, isort, Flake8, mypy, compilation and pytest passed (**798 passed, 1 warning**).
- [Security CI #45883837836](https://github.com/Adam-Ghanem/NetWatch/actions/runs/45883837836): success. Dependency audit, secret-boundary checks, Bandit, Python compilation, frontend validation, Docker Compose, production image build, container privilege checks and pytest passed (**798 passed, 1 warning**).
- An initial Python CI run on the preceding head failed only because one test call needed Black formatting. The formatting was corrected, then the job passed.
- The job logs show the worker privacy regression now invokes the registered `approved` handler, ensuring the synthetic exception message is actually raised and checked.
- Codecov upload completed successfully on the final head.

GitHub Actions checked the PR's generated merge ref against current `main`. The PR remains Draft for human review; no merge or deployment is requested.

## Safety

Synthetic in-memory SQLite tests only. No provider calls, real credentials, network scans, production data, active remediation, or deployment.

Closes #7

## Description
Checks the finished page against WCAG 2.2 AA with axe, a keyboard pass and VoiceOver, and fixes what turned up.

- **Range beside the paging buttons:** when nothing is loading and there's no error, the line above Previous and Next shows "Results 26 to 50 of …". Unlike the loading and error text there, it is readable by screen readers, and it isn't a live region, so nothing is announced twice.
- **Spinner in forced colours:** both border colours became the same system colour, hiding the moving segment; the segment now uses the system highlight colour.
- **Accepted:** VoiceOver reads a page 2 result as "26" and "1 of 25"; both are true (overall position and position on the page). The operator select keeps the browser's native styling.
- **Not checked:** a real Windows contrast theme; forced colours were checked with Chromium's emulation.

1. Run `npm run dev`, search and press Next: the line above the buttons reads "Results 26 to 50 of …", and while a page loads it shows "Loading results" with a spinner instead.
2. With VoiceOver on, read through to the paging buttons with Control-Option-Right Arrow: the range is read before Previous and Next, and "Loading results" is announced only once, from the message near the top.
3. Open the VoiceOver rotor: headings are "Search Europe PMC", "Query preview", "Results" and the result titles; landmarks are the search form, main and "Results pages".
4. Turn Wi-Fi off and press Next: the error is announced once and shows in red above the buttons.

author: tomaarsen
body:
Hello!

## Pull Request overview

* Move sparse embeddings to CPU once before decoding.
* Simplify per-row ranking and reuse the tokenizer lookup.

## Details

While reviewing #4443, I found that `decode` repeatedly synchronizes CUDA tensors when converting each row's tokens and scores to Python lists. I've moved the coalesced sparse tensor to CPU before the loop and removed duplicate token indexing. This PR is independent of the intersection changes in #4443.

I benchmarked decoding 256 real document embeddings and their query intersections with `top_k=5`. These are ranges of median times across two fresh processes, comparing `90c815ee` with this PR:

| Input device | Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| CPU | Query intersections | 12.16-12.27 ms | 11.51-11.55 ms |
| CPU | Document embeddings | 17.57-17.91 ms | 16.85-17.16 ms |
| CUDA | Query intersections | 45.21-47.77 ms | 10.55-11.40 ms |
| CUDA | Document embeddings | 43.36-46.45 ms | 11.41-12.10 ms |

The benchmark used `sparse-encoder-testing/splade-bert-tiny-nq`, 256 distinct paragraphs from the repository docs, PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128, an RTX 3090, and an i7-13700K with 2 Torch CPU threads. Each process used 5 warmups and 20 timed calls per implementation, alternating their order and synchronizing CUDA before and after timing. Encoding and intersection computation were excluded.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the decoding benchmark</summary>

Run from the repository root on the base and PR revisions:

```python
import re
import statistics
import time
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from sentence_transformers import SparseEncoder

torch.set_num_threads(2)
torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)
model = SparseEncoder("sparse-encoder-testing/splade-bert-tiny-nq", device="cpu")
texts = list(dict.fromkeys(
    paragraph.strip()
    for path in sorted(Path("docs").rglob("*"))
    if path.suffix in (".md", ".rst")
    for paragraph in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if 80 < len(paragraph.strip()) < 1200
))[:256]
query = model.encode_query("How can I train a sparse encoder for semantic search?")
documents = model.encode_document(texts)

for device in ("cpu", "cuda"):
    docs = documents.to(device)
    intersection = model.intersection(query.to(device), docs)
    for label, embeddings in (("intersections", intersection), ("documents", docs)):
        for _ in range(5):
            model.decode(embeddings, top_k=5)
        times = []
        for _ in range(20):
            if device == "cuda":
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
            start = time.perf_counter()
            model.decode(embeddings, top_k=5)
            if device == "cuda":
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
            times.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
        print(device, label, statistics.median(times), "ms")
```

</details>

Validation: `python -m pytest -q tests/sparse_encoder/test_model.py -k 'decode or intersection' -p no:cacheprovider` passed all 33 selected tests with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. Ruff, formatting, and typos commit hooks passed. Benchmark outputs matched exactly for float32 with `top_k=5` and `top_k=None`. CPU and CUDA can choose different tokens among equal scores at the cutoff.

AI assistance was used for implementation, benchmarking, and drafting this description.

- Tom Aarsen

author: kevimota
body:
### Summary
Closes the sensor-related security and scalability gaps:
- `POST /sensor` is no longer open to unauthenticated callers.
- Sensor payloads are size-limited.
- `GET /sensor/names` no longer runs one query per sensor name.
- `GET /sensor` can no longer pull an unbounded number of rows.

### Changes
- **`backend/app/routes/sensor.py`**
  - `POST /sensor` now requires `X-API-Key: <SENSOR_API_KEY>`.
    - Missing header → `401 Missing API key`
    - Wrong key → `403 Invalid API key`
  - Request body capped at 1 MB via `Content-Length`.
  - `GET /sensor/names` replaced the N+1 loop with a single PostgreSQL `DISTINCT ON` query (SQLModel `select`, so model rows are returned).
  - `GET /sensor` applies a hard 10,000-row cap; default remains 100 when no time range is supplied.
- **`backend/app/models/sensor.py`**
  - Sensor `name` limited to 64 characters.
- **`backend/app/core/config.py`**
  - Added required `SENSOR_API_KEY` setting.
- **`.env_reference` / `README.md`**
  - Documented `SENSOR_API_KEY`.

### Rollout / breaking change
The sensor publisher must send: X-API-Key:

Existing firmware receives `401` until it includes this header. Set the same key in the deployment `.env` and on the ESP32.

### Testing
- Syntax-checked the modified Python files.
- Verified the `DISTINCT ON` query and SQLModel result handling.
- Run as test in the production machine

### Notes
- `GET /sensor` and `GET /sensor/names` remain public, matching current dashboard usage.
- No rate limiting beyond the body-size cap was added.

author: jpsaud501
body:
Closes #335.

## Root cause

`RoomRouting.test.ts > gives a room message of work the operator stopped its round, and wakes nobody for it` means to record a room Stop while Ana's `say` is still on its way. Nothing held the engine's interrupt back, though. `Rooms.stop` records the Stop, and the Stop runner interrupts her turn in the background. When that interrupt lands between the test engine recording the tool call and the server admitting the `say`, the turn has ended. The `say` is then rightly refused, so the room's last message is still the operator's: `expected [ 'Ana, ask Bo for the date.', +0 ] to deeply equal [ 'Bo, the date?', 1 ]`.

This is a race in the test, not in the product. A `say` that arrives after the engine ended its turn should be refused.

It started showing up after #328. The per-bot lock that #328 put in front of every `say` adds an async step before admission, which widened the window. The paced hello itself isn't involved: `createBot` ends a new bot's first turn without a `say`, so these bots never pace a hello, and the lock isn't contended here.

## Fix

The test now delays the Stop's effects (`delayNextStopEffects`) until the `say` is answered, then releases them and waits for the Stop to settle and the turn to end. `RoomIntegrity.test.ts` and `Speech.test.ts` already handle the same moment this way. No timeouts changed and no server code changed. No other test records a Stop and then calls `say` without holding the effects.

## Proofs

- **Reproduced:** forcing the race order (tool call recorded, then the Stop's effects released and settled, then the `say` admitted) gives CI's exact assertion, `expected [ 'Ana, ask Bo for the date.', +0 ] to deeply equal [ 'Bo, the date?', 1 ]`.
- **Stable:** the whole `RoomRouting.test.ts` file ran 20 times in a row under `nice -n 10`, 38/38 each time.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm fmt:check` pass.

## Review

One reviewer, since no first-contact code changed.

| Reviewer | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| Opus 5.5 | MERGE, no blockers |

What the reviewer confirmed:
- `stillAdmitted` is the only gate this `say` can fail on.
- The room-stopped check applies only to `message_bot`.
- The first-contact Stop check applies only to a follow-up message.
- `delayNextStopEffects` keeps the turn admitted and unfinished until release.
- Only Ana's session gets a Stop target, so hers is the stop that's held.
- `stopSettled` and `turnEnded` can't hang.

Refs #198

## Why

The host reaper splits CSV at physical newlines. Incus config values may contain newlines, so a malformed expiry or hold can break the boundary between instance records before the script decides what to delete.

## Change

Parse and validate the full Incus JSON listing with the Python 3 standard library already installed by host setup. Abort on list or parse failure. Skip missing or invalid expiries and use the later of a valid UTC expiry and hold. An invalid hold is ignored. `--dry-run` reads the same listing and reports decisions without deleting anything.

## Screenshots

None. No dashboard or tray UI changes.

## Agent-facing text

No agent-facing text changes. `--dry-run` is a host operator preflight.

## Verified

- Box job `agent-box-9771.20261126-190401-64f2` passed gofmt, shell syntax, mode vet and all 72 mode tests. The fake Incus fixture checks decision order, multiline config, dry run, list failure, truncated JSON and invalid records.

Rodada diária (trava da assinatura, savepoint do gateway, conciliação, idempotência da fatura e do evento), corrida entre webhook e rodada, volta de inadimplente para ativa e os quatro bloqueios.

author: aqm857886159
body:
协作看板 #1586 · Q-ui-atomic 第 2 轮。派工 7202914618 ⑥，审查 7201457485。

## 变更意图

- 意图：纯修复
- 候选档位：短
- 单一意图：是
- 声明：纯修复：不改用户可见元素、布局、文案

## 短版设计卡

- ★1 走查客户端应当第一次看到文件就能读全当前请求、回执或启动状态。量具是两个 Node 进程运行真实 CLI 和驱动，用 features 往返比对首次发布内容。
- ★2 客户端发布 req，驱动发布 state、ready 和 res。双方共享协议版本与写入边界。常驻驱动持有实例锁并负责退出。
- ★3 选用支持写入前指定暂存路径的原子写库。第 1 轮手写改名可替换，删除握手会使全部走查失去驱动入口。
- ★4 当前协议照常收发。旧协议在删除前次回执和发布请求前提示 down、up。停旧驱动按原 quit 请求和实例退出完成。重启时仅回收本协议、当前用户、确认死 PID 的普通暂存文件。
- ★9 三处分别退回直写必须各红一次。缺失版本、版本不匹配时普通命令零交接，保留安全关闭。死 PID 残件消失，活 PID、外来文件、目录、符号链接保留。回滚可撤销本轮实现提交，保留红灯测试。

## 三个写入口及版本握手

| 生产者 | 首次可读的文件 | 消费者 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.mjs` | `req.json` | 驱动取出、解析并执行本条命令 |
| `ui-driver.mjs` | `res.json` | 客户端第一次看到回执即可解析 |
| `ui-driver.mjs` | `state.json` | 启动、关闭及取证脚本读取实例状态 |
| `ui-driver.mjs` | `ready` | 状态发布后公布 `{ipcVersion: 2, driverPid}`；启动方等待自己拉起的 PID |

`send` 在删除旧回执和写入普通请求前验证版本。遇到旧 PID 标记、未知版本或损坏标记时，CLI 提示先 `down` 再 `up`。原有 `down`、`quit` 和本轮补齐的 `stop` 别名都向旧端发布 `quit`，等回执出现，再等持锁进程退出。即使旧驱动刚写了回执的第一个字节，关闭也能继续。

## P0 依赖取证

初始 manifest、lockfile 和 pnpm 虚拟仓均无 `write-file-atomic` 或 `atomically`。实测 npm 维护的 `write-file-atomic` 同步入口，8.0.0 和兼容仓库 Node 下限的 7.0.0 都生成 `req.json.<数字哈希>`。例如 PID 11146 对应 `req.json.3745321328`。API 在打开暂存件之后才回调，无法从遗留文件名确认写入 PID。8.0.0 的 Node 22 下限另为 22.22.2，仓库下限是 22.19.0。[上游源码](https://github.com/npm/write-file-atomic/blob/main/lib/index.js)

采用 `atomically@2.1.1` 并锁定为 devDependency。实测 `tmpCreate` 在创建文件前接收目标路径，可以指定同目录的 `.nomi-ui-ipc-p<PID>-<UUID>.tmp`。库负责从打开暂存件到最终替换以及失败清理，第 1 轮手写改名逻辑已删除。后续 Q-atomic-scripts 可直接引用同一库。[上游接口](https://github.com/fabiospampinato/atomically#options)

## 系统改进

最早漏检发生在握手验收。第 1 轮只让夹具调用共享函数，各真实入口自行退回直写仍会绿。现在用独立进程执行实际 `ui.mjs features` 和实际 `ui-driver.mjs` 命令循环，只替换 Electron 启动。探针在目标文件直写的截断与填入之间读取，在原子替换时保留即将公布的字节，并核对这次请求、回执和状态。原有 2,048 × 256 KiB 压盘改成一次小消息往返。

驱动取得实例锁后回收专属暂存件，复用临时目录分配器的 `ownerIsGone`，仅将 `ESRCH` 视为写入者已退出。按完整文件名、普通文件类型以及平台提供的 UID 核对归属。测试在改名前强杀真实写进程，下次启动能收掉其暂存文件，活 PID 文件、异名前缀、目录和符号链接均保留。第 1 轮暂存名缺少专属前缀，继续保留。PID 被复用时回收会推迟。复查日为 2026-12-11，任一入口首读不完整、误删活文件或旧端收到普通命令即重开。[根因合同](docs/fixes/2026-11-27-ui-driver-ipc-publication.root-cause.json) · [回收约定](docs/engineering/direction-checks/2026-10-28-test-temp-reclaim.md)

## TDD 与逐入口回退证据

本轮仅两笔提交。基线 `dd1bd4649` 已包含 `origin/main` 的 `1fad1ce47`。测试提交 `446d71d11` 在旧实现上得到 8 红、3 绿；三个真实写端当时已使用第 1 轮的原子发布。红项覆盖重启回收、版本公布、三种不兼容标记，以及三个关闭入口。实现提交 `51bf26916` 上 11 项全绿。

下表每行对应一次单独运行的 `pnpm exec vitest run tests/ux/uiIpcPublication.test.mjs`。每次只替换该入口的一行，运行后逐字节还原。

| 临时退回 `fs.writeFileSync` 的入口 | 实际断言输出 | 结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.mjs` 写请求 | `req.json was visible before its content: expected '' not to be ''` | 1 红、10 绿，退出 1 |
| `ui-driver.mjs` 写回执 | `res.json was visible before its content: expected '' not to be ''` | 1 红、10 绿，退出 1 |
| `ui-driver.mjs` 写状态 | `state.json was visible before its content: expected '' not to be ''` | 1 红、10 绿，退出 1 |

## 真实场景复现

原报告是在图层分离走查中点击确认后，中文轨收到 `bad req`。第 1 轮在文件系统复现过半包，并在宿主屏外完成 `ui-fake-vendor.walk.mjs` 和 `remove-node-lock.walk.mjs` 两条走查。第 2 轮使用真实文件系统和 Node 进程验证三处公布、写入者被杀、旧标记拒发和停旧实例，并在宿主屏外（`NOMI_E2E_OFFSCREEN=1`）构建实跑通过 `tests/ux/ui-fake-vendor.walk.mjs` 及 `ui.mjs --instance ... up --offscreen` → `features` → `down` 真 Electron 全链路握手。

## 本机检查

- 定向 Vitest 共 26 项通过，覆盖 `uiIpcPublication`、`uiDriverOptions` 和 `viteOptimizeDeps`。另跑临时目录回收的 9 个 Node 测试。
- `npx tsc --noEmit`、变更脚本定向 ESLint、`check:packaged-deps`、`check:package-budget`、`check:self-written`、`check:supply-chain-pins`、`check:root-cause-contracts` 以及 frozen lockfile 校验均通过。预算门岗校验仓库预算基线，本轮未制作安装包。
- 按派工约束跳过本机全量 gates 和全量 Vitest。第 2 轮独立复审待协调派发。

## 碰到的规则与门岗

沿用 2026-10-28 的暂存归属方向检查。fix-churn 仅命中临时目录归属概念，本轮复用该概念既有的 PID 判据，并删除旧的手写发布。依赖、预算和打包门岗保持原判据。

按 R33.4 在 `docs/engineering/concept-owners/test-harness.ui-driver-ipc.json` 登记走查驱动 IPC 文件的公布，由 `check:concept-owners` 核对合同中的两个写接口：`writeUiIpcFile` 负责完整公布文件，`send` 在发送普通命令前核对驱动协议版本。

author: ifpintac
body:
Community request: "on the render window: add the options to zoom in - zoom out, fit to frame, view 100%, pause and stop rendering. Im open with the position of each tool, whatever make sense with tequila".

## What changed

**A toolbar over the picture** (`app/src/render_view.rs`, new): zoom out, the zoom ("63%"), zoom in, Fit, 1:1 (100%), and while a render runs, Pause/Resume and Stop. Lucide icons (zoom-in, zoom-out and square added to `icons.rs`; Fit reuses the viewport's Frame all icon; 100% is written "1:1"), each with a hover text.

**Viewing**
- The zoom is screen pixels to a pixel of the render, so 100% is one-to-one at any display scaling (a 1920 px render at 100% is 1280 points wide at 150%).
- The wheel and a pinch zoom about the pointer. Dragging with the left or middle button pans a picture that's bigger than the stage. In an A/B compare, the left button still moves the split and the middle button pans. Double-click goes to 100% at the pointer and back to Fit.
- Keys: `+`/`=`, `-`, `0` or `F` for Fit, `1` for 100%.
- Zoom range: from the fit (or 100% for a picture smaller than the stage) up to 3200%. The buttons step through image-viewer stops and land on the fit when they cross it.
- Fit follows the window as it's resized. Any other zoom keeps its scale.
- **Every pixel at 100% and above:**
  - A finished render's developed pixels are kept as it finishes: this session's newest, up to 256 MB. Older renders are read back from their file.
  - A render in progress is sent at the size it's shown: every pixel when zoomed in, up to 4096 px on the longest side.
  - Tequila's renderer remakes its picture straight away if the zoom changes while it's paused.
  - Pictures bigger than one texture can hold are drawn in tiles.

**Pause** holds the render after the pass it's on. Nothing is spent on it, nothing is lost, and Resume carries on from the same samples (`app/src/batch.rs`: `Hold`, `Clock`, `pausable`).
- "Paused" shows clearly in several places:
  - in amber, over the picture and in the stage header;
  - "Pausing after this pass…" until the current pass is done;
  - on the job's card;
  - "1 paused" above the filmstrip;
  - "Paused 45%" on the main Render button;
  - "Export 45% · Paused" in the status bar;
  - `Paused` as the job's message in `query jobs`.
- Time spent paused doesn't count, either in the job's reported time or against its Stop after limit.
- The queue waits behind a paused job. The next job starts unpaused.

**Stop** ends the render and saves the picture so far. It's the old footer "Stop & save" moved onto the toolbar, so there's one button for it.

**Scripts**: `ui` takes `render_view` (`zoom` as `"fit"`, `"100%"` or a number; `at`; `pause`), and `query ui` reports it (`docs/SCRIPTING.md`).

## Decisions, and why

- **The toolbar floats as an island at the foot of the picture**, like the viewport's tools. It takes no room from the picture, and it sits where image viewers put their zoom. Pause and Stop share the island and show whenever a render runs, even while you're looking at an older render.
- **Nearest filtering above 100%, smooth at and below it.** Zooming in is for judging pixels: noise, fireflies, antialiasing. A smooth filter blurs exactly that and makes a noisy render look cleaner than it is.
  - At 100% the picture is snapped to whole screen pixels, so the filter doesn't matter there.
  - Fit keeps the smooth look it always had. A small render enlarged to fit would show unevenly doubled pixels with nearest.
- **What each engine supports for pause:**
  - Tequila's renderer has no pause, but it renders in passes, so the job waits at the top of its loop.
  - Cycles' `Session::set_pause` is ignored in a final-render (background) session; Cycles' `run_wait_for_work` returns at once when `params.background` is set. So Cycles' own thread is held inside the progress callback it makes after each stretch of samples. Its render loop is driven by that thread, so nothing renders on the CPU or the card while it waits.
  - In `tequila-render-cycles`, the stop flag is now checked *after* that callback, so Stop is heard as soon as a pause ends.
  - The floor-reflection thread is held between its passes too.
  - No change to the C shim or the Cycles DLL.
- **A Cycles render with a time limit can't be paused**, and the button is greyed out with the reason. Cycles times Stop after from the start of the render on its own clock (`RenderScheduler::check_time_limit_reached`), which a hold doesn't stop, so it would end the moment it was resumed. A wireframe has nothing to pause either.
- **Stop saves; there's no separate Save.** The filmstrip, compare and history all work on files, so a picture kept only in the window would be lost with it. Every ending (finished, out of time, stopped) writes its file, as before.
- **The zoom belongs to the window, not to each picture**, so flipping between two renders of the same size at 100% keeps your place.
- **Keys:** the Render window is a window of its own, so its keys don't collide with the main window's. In the main window, `F` frames the selection, which is the same idea. Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+Plus were avoided because egui uses them for interface zoom.

## Tests

- New, all passing:
  - `render_view`: fit, 100% at 1x/1.25x/1.5x/2x scaling on whole pixels, zooming about the pointer, panning clamped to the edges, zoom limits, steps landing on the fit, fit following the window, percent labels, tiling.
  - `batch`:
    - `a_hold_waits_until_let_go_and_counts_its_time_once`
    - `a_jobs_clock_leaves_out_the_time_paused`
    - `what_can_be_paused_is_said`
    - `a_paused_render_holds_its_samples_and_carries_on`: Tequila's renderer with a time limit the pause must not use up, and Cycles on the processor; no samples while held, then carries on from them, not from zero.
    - `a_paused_render_stopped_keeps_its_picture`
    - `a_preview_is_the_size_the_window_asks_for`
  - `render_window`: `a_live_render_is_asked_for_at_the_size_shown`, `stop_and_pause_reach_the_renderer`, `a_zoomed_render_shows_every_pixel_it_had`.
  - `channel`: `a_script_zooms_the_render_window_and_pauses_only_a_render`.
  - `protocol`: parsing of `render_view`.
- Full runs on this PC (Windows, RTX 2060):
  - `cargo test -p tequila-scripting`: all pass.
  - `cargo test -p tequila-render-cycles`: all pass.
  - `cargo test -p tequila-app --bin tequila-app`: 713 passed, 5 failed. The 5 are the known failures on this PC: two `library_tab` tests, `the_about_window_lays_out`, the glass-ball and fibres parity tests.
  - `python/test_tequila_mcp.py`: 23 OK.
- Before and after screenshots were taken from the app over the scripting channel, using the Headphones sample (not attached here).

## Not done, or not proven on this machine

- No Mac, no second GPU. Cycles pausing was tested with Cycles on the processor; Cycles on the card uses the same path (the session thread drives the card), but that wasn't tested here.
- A render in progress bigger than 4096 px is enlarged at 100% until it finishes; the finished image is exact.

## Summary

Replaces private, duplicated test fixtures in the Android unit tests with shared helpers. Only test code changes; production code is untouched.

## Problems fixed

- **Copied settings store.** `SettingsViewModelTest` had a private `FakeSettingsStore` identical line for line to the shared `TestSettingsStore`. It now uses the shared one.
- **Own game builder.** `GameIdentityMatcherTest` built `GameInfo` with a private helper instead of the shared `testGame`.
- **Two private dispatcher providers.** `CdnPayloadTest` and `OkHttpDownloadTransferTest` each defined a `DispatcherProvider` object that duplicated `TestDispatcherProvider`. They now use `TestDispatcherProvider(Dispatchers.IO)`. Both subjects only read the `io` dispatcher, the same pattern `PreviewTwitchLiveServiceTest` already uses.

It is now one `DownloadTransfer.succeedsWriting` extension in `service/apk/ApkTestFixtures.kt`. They now use `testTransferOptions` in `service/download/DownloadTestFixtures.kt`, with `maximumAttempts` and `inactivityTimeout` as parameters.

- Small value differences between the old and shared fixtures are irrelevant to the tests that use them: `GameIdentityMatcher` only compares id and name; `DownloadFileStore` only reads the cache directory name and age, so its `inactivityTimeout` going from 1 ms to 1 s has no effect.

author: camielvs
body: # Human Words Organize projects int he tangent sidebar by workspace. When I have a lot of projects it just starts to turn into a messy and confusing soup, so having collapsible workspace sorting makes it easier to navigate # AI Words ## Intent Help people with many projects find a project that lives in a particular workspace from the Tangent page's Projects window. Workspaces carry their own configuration, so which workspace a project belongs to matters when choosing where to work. ## Current behavior The Projects window lists every project in one long list with no indication of its workspace. Someone looking for a project in a given workspace has to recognize it by name alone. ## What changes When projects span more than one workspace, the list below "Pinned" is split into one section per workspace, in alphabetical order. Each section has a heading showing the workspace icon and name, with a chevron that folds its projects out of the way, and the window remembers which sections were closed across reloads. Sections start open. Searching still finds everything. A closed workspace that holds a match opens to show it while the search is active and closes again once the search is cleared, the same rule the project rows already follow during a search. The "Pinned" section is unchanged and stays on top. When every project is in a single workspace, the list looks exactly as it does today, and it also stays flat until the workspace names have loaded. A project from a workspace the viewer cannot see, such as one opened from a shared link, is listed last under "Other workspace". ## How to test Needs an account with projects in at least two workspaces. 1. Open a project in Tangent. In the "Projects" window on the left, the projects below "Pinned" appear under one heading per workspace, sorted by name, each heading with a chevron and the workspace icon. 2. Click a workspace heading. Its projects fold away and the chevron points right. Reload the page: that workspace is still closed and the others are still open. 3. In "Search projects and sessions", type the name of a project in the closed workspace. The workspace opens and shows only the match. Clear the search with the "Clear search" button or Escape: the workspace is closed again. 4. While searching, click an open workspace heading to close it, then clear the search. It is open again, since changes made during a search are forgotten with it. 5. Open a project row's menu in the Projects window and choose "Pin project". The project moves to a "Pinned" section above the workspace sections, as it does today. 6. With an account whose projects are all in one workspace, the window shows the same single list as before, with no workspace heading. Unit tests cover the grouping, folding, remembering, and search behaviour, and the whole Tangent page test folder passes. The change has not been checked in a browser. ## Related Issue and Pull requests None. ## Type of Change - [x] Improvement ## Line Breakdown | Category | Added | Removed | | --------------------- | ----: | ------: | | Production code | 210 | 38 | | Comments | 21 | 2 | | Tests | 275 | 9 | | **Total** | 506 | 49 | ## Checklist - [ ] I have tested this does not break current pipelines / runs functionality - [ ] I have tested the changes on staging 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: kevindoeschemistry-droid
body:
Nobody publishes an itemised graduate chemical engineering content standard. I checked: **ABET**'s programme criteria are undergraduate; the Engineering Council's **AHEP4** master's outcomes (M1–M18) are competency statements with no technical content ("communicate effectively on complex engineering matters"); **AIChE's Body of Knowledge** is staged by career rather than degree and states that students heading to graduate school share Stage 1 skills with new hires. So waiting on a syllabus was the wrong call regardless — and five catalogue lines from one department were never a basis.

Two things are usable, and neither needs one.

**`icheme-level-f`** (read: part) — the only accreditation standard that formally separates master's-level chemical engineering from bachelor's. Its Level F outcomes extend the Level B column rather than naming new topics, so what they anchor is *depth*: the same underlying principles on more complex problems with the limits of the assumptions critically evaluated, and computational techniques selected and adapted while recognising the limits of standard commercial software. That is a published warrant for what a graduate core course actually is.

**`cheme-grad-core`** (read: full) — our crosswalk of fifteen departments' published core-course and preliminary-exam pages, each read in full: CMU, Northwestern, Michigan Tech, NC State, UMass Lowell, NJIT, Colorado State, Wisconsin, URI, Minnesota, Houston, Tufts, UPRM, UIC and Drexel. Labelled a house list, because the pages are published but the synthesis is ours. The convergence is the finding: **mathematical methods recurs 15 of 15**, advanced transport 14, advanced thermodynamics 14, advanced kinetics 11, process systems 1.

`aiche-bok` is registered too and goes on **Process Design**, where career-staged plant practice belongs — never on the graduate framework.

### What this changes

**Unit 7, "Mathematical methods past Kreyszig"** — the course every one of the fifteen requires and draft 1 had no unit for. 12 objectives, 24 items: the Péclet crossover length and why a large group does not license dropping a term outright, boundary-layer and thermal-layer scaling, regular perturbation against the exact root, sizing a singular layer, similarity depth, curvilinear eigenvalues and how many terms a tolerance costs, stiffness and the explicit step limit, condition number against residual, the optimal difference step, observed order of convergence. It carries the assumption checks Level F asks for — *when the semi-infinite solution stops being valid*, what a condition number does to a small residual, why shrinking the step stops helping.

**A real defect the catalogue basis had produced**: unit 5 is process-control content but was titled "(CBE 200)", which is the applied-mathematics course — the one whose PDE midterm is already in Engineering Math. Titles now carry no course numbers, and they live in the spec, because opl_fill regenerates the framework block.

Unit codes 1–6 are unchanged and the math unit is appended as 7, since the Library's RemNote ids are keyed by code. The `gc` domain was a placeholder since draft 1 (its units borrow fm/mass/thermo/cre/design/sep skills); it is now real, with four `gc.*` skills and a source file. All three standards are fully answered: **23/23, 7/7, 8/8**. GC goes 38 → 50 objectives, all drilled, 2.0 types. Source count 55 → 56.

### Two latent bugs found on the way

- **`opl_fill.py` has been crashing for weeks.** `scripts/second_specs/fe3_{mt,re,pd}.py` did `import fe3`, which needs `scripts/second_specs` on `sys.path` — where its own `re.py` shadows the stdlib. opl_fill loads every file in that folder. They now import by path, and opl_fill skips a module with no `ADD`.
- **opl_fill regenerating a block silently drops `std` citations.** The cite scripts are add-only writes into framework YAML, and regeneration reverts them — this is how `acs-accm-analytical`'s citations vanished from `chemistry-olympiad.yaml`. It also restores spec order, undoing the ramp. The run order is now recorded in CLAUDE.md, and citations that must survive belong in the spec (GC's are in gc.py's `_CW` map). After re-running the cite scripts and `ramp --all` I diffed every framework objective by objective against main: **0 objectives, 0 drills and 0 citations lost**; the only shifts are two NGSS auto-picks re-selecting, which is that spec's documented behaviour.

Also recorded: never round-trip `drills/standards.yaml` through `yaml.safe_dump` — it reflows all 95 one-line entries and silently dropped `psi4numpy-tutorials` item `"08"` by unquoting it.

### What is still open

Kevin's syllabi are worth having when he finishes the classes, but to **check** this framework covers what he was examined on, not to define it — which is the right order anyway.

### Checks

`tests/run.ts` (246,510 problems, 0 failures), sympy on all 24 new templates (720/720), all six sims, `tsc`.

body:
## Summary

A box that avoids a break after it (`break-after: avoid`, e.g. a heading) is held with the first row of the table that follows. The nested path (inside wrappers) and the body-level path disagreed on which row is first, and both disagreed with Chromium for tables with generated content.

- **Header group that does not repeat** (taller than a quarter of the page, or `break-inside: auto`): inside wrappers the first row skipped every header group, so the heading was held with the header *and* the first body row and moved to the next page with them. Pagination now records the repeated header/footer groups (`HeaderRepeats::prepare` moved before candidate collection, `LayoutContext::repeated_table_groups`), and `first_table_row` treats only those as non-rows, like `first_row_ends` at the body level.
- **Generated content before the rows** (`table::before`, inline or block, also loose text before the rows): it sits in an anonymous row that comes first. `leading_anonymous_row_end` finds that row (skipping repeated groups, seeing through `display: contents`, taking a `break-inside: avoid` row group whole) and both `held_table_end` and `first_row_ends` hold it. `held_step` no longer holds every table with `::before`/`::after` whole.
- **Generated content after the rows** (`table::after`): the table was dropped from the run at the body level (and held whole when nested); now the first explicit row is held as for a plain table.
- **Forced breaks** (review rounds): what the anonymous row holds ends at the first forced break inside its content, including breaks nested in its ordinary blocks (`anonymous_row_cut`, `first_forced_break_cut`), and a `break-inside: avoid` group holds only up to the first forced break before, after or inside its rows and the blocks between them (`held_anonymous_row_end`), floats breaking it as pagination does.

Not in this PR (filed RAIKIRI-1810): anonymous rows that are not first (`::after`, `::before` after a thead/caption, tables without explicit rows) are not break candidates and do not follow moved rows (same on main).

## Verification

- Chromium probe (Playwright print, Ahem 20px/30px, 100px pages): 944 cases (tables x wrappers x spacer heights). 159 mismatches fixed, 0 new mismatches vs main; the remaining ones are pre-existing (RAIKIRI-1810 and border-spacing at a page break). Forced-break cases from the review rounds probed separately and pinned.
- New `crates/raikiri-html/tests/avoided_run_table_first_row_surface.rs` (15 tests, values from Chromium).
- `scripts/gate.sh --base origin/main` PASS (incl. patch coverage); strict WPT unchanged (PASS 4966 / XFAIL 108 / FAIL 0).

Fixes RAIKIRI-1078.

author: plastic-time
body:
## Summary

Refs #14234. `trace_web_source_location` refused `source_map_limits.*` per-call budgets using prose only, without structured `details.limit` (or `details.refusal` on `AnalysisResourceConstraintError` memory-limit refusals). This PR defines a domain-owned `SOURCE_MAP_BUDGETS` table and `sourceMapBudgetLimit` helper in `src/domain/sourceMapLimits.ts`, attaches `details.limit` (`control_kind: "parameter"`, `parameter: "source_map_limits.<field>"`) across the local source-map read, decoder admission, codec reply, and process memory/output limit paths, and removes `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapCommand.ts` from `scripts/verify/untyped-budget-refusal-baseline.json`.

## Problem and expected behavior

Before this change, `source_map_limits` refusals in `SourceMapCommand`, `SourceMapDecoder`, `SourceMapReply`, and `LocalWebSourceLocationArtifacts` named `source_map_limits.<field>` only in `remediationAction` and `detail` text without setting `limit`. Callers inspecting `details.limit` (and `details.refusal` for `AnalysisResourceConstraintError` memory-limit refusals) saw neither the parameter name, effective value, range, default, nor (for `map_bytes`) the observed byte size required to admit the next call.

Expected behavior:
- All `source_map_limits.*` bounds live in one domain-owned `SOURCE_MAP_BUDGETS` table in `src/domain/sourceMapLimits.ts` shared by `sourceMapLimitsSchema`, `sourceMapLimitRecovery`, and `sourceMapBudgetLimit`.
- `SourceMapCommand.#memoryLimitFailure` attaches `sourceMapBudgetLimit("codec_heap_mib", this.limits.codecHeapMiB)` and omits hand-authored `remediationAction` so `projectAnalysisError` projects both `details.limit` and `details.refusal` (`kind: "adjustable_budget"`, `control: "source_map_limits.codec_heap_mib"`) with generated CLI/MCP recovery guidance.
- `SourceMapCommand.#outputLimitFailure` (`stdout`) attaches `sourceMapBudgetLimit("output_bytes", this.limits.outputBytes)`; `stderr` diagnostic allowance overflow remains fixed without `details.limit`.
- `SourceMapDecoder` pre-spawn admission refusals attach `sourceMapBudgetLimit("map_bytes", limits.mapBytes, inputBytes)` (with `required_value`) and `sourceMapBudgetLimit("output_bytes", limits.outputBytes)` (without `required_value`, since chunked serialization stops on the first excess).
- `SourceMapCodecProtocol` splits codec `"failure"` replies into `reason: "limit"` (with optional `limit: { field, maximum }` constrained to codec-enforced fields in `CODEC_SOURCE_MAP_LIMIT_FIELDS` and each field's `SOURCE_MAP_BUDGETS` min..max bounds) and `reason: "malformed" | "unsupported"` (no `limit`), so `SourceMapReply` binds `sourceMapBudgetLimit` on valid limit replies and rejects malformed `limit` payloads as `AnalysisOutputError` (`unreadable_output`).
- `LocalWebSourceLocationArtifacts` attaches `sourceMapBudgetLimit("map_bytes", mapBytes, observedBytes)` (when `boundary === "file-size"` and `observedBytes` fits in `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) so public CLI `--source-map-bytes` refusals project `details.limit` with `cli_flag: "--source-map-bytes"` and `required_value`.

## Change and scope

- `src/domain/sourceMapLimits.ts`: add `SOURCE_MAP_LIMIT_FIELDS`, `sourceMapLimitFieldSchema`, `SOURCE_MAP_BUDGETS`, and `sourceMapBudgetLimit`; drive `sourceMapLimitsSchema` and `sourceMapLimitRecovery` from `SOURCE_MAP_BUDGETS`.
- `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapCommand.ts`: attach `sourceMapBudgetLimit` to `#memoryLimitFailure` (`codec_heap_mib`, relying on `adjustable_budget` recovery) and `#outputLimitFailure` (`stdout` -> `output_bytes`).
- `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapDecoder.ts`: attach `sourceMapBudgetLimit` to pre-spawn `map_bytes` (with `required_value`) and `output_bytes` refusals.
- `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapCodecProtocol.ts`, `SourceMapCodecProcess.ts`, `SourceMapReply.ts`: restrict optional `limit: { field, maximum }` to `reason: "limit"` codec replies with codec-owned fields and `SOURCE_MAP_BUDGETS` range checks, and bind `sourceMapBudgetLimit` on `ArtifactOperationError`.
- `src/browser/assets/WebArtifactReads.ts`, `WebSourceLocationArtifacts.ts`: add optional `limit` resolver to `WebArtifactReadContext` and bind `sourceMapBudgetLimit("map_bytes", ...)` on source-map `file-size` refusals.
- `scripts/verify/untyped-budget-refusal-baseline.json`: remove `"src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapCommand.ts": 1`.
- `docs/reference/limits-and-recovery.md`: list `trace_web_source_location` (`source_map_limits.*`) alongside operations reporting `details.limit`.
- Tests: update `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapCommand.test.ts`, `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapDecoder.test.ts`, `tests/boundary/javascript/sourceMapDecoder.test.ts`, `tests/boundary/mcp/webSourceLocationMcp.test.ts`, and `tests/acceptance/webSourceLocationCli.test.ts`.

Contribution scope: not applicable (ordinary refusal-contract fix within existing read-only source-map inspection boundaries; no new provider, execution, injection, or mutation).

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: `src/domain/sourceMapLimits.ts` owns `SOURCE_MAP_BUDGETS` and `sourceMapBudgetLimit`; `sourceMapLimitsSchema`, `sourceMapLimitRecovery`, `SourceMapCommand`, `SourceMapDecoder`, `SourceMapReply`, `SourceMapCodecProtocol`, and `LocalWebSourceLocationArtifacts` all consume it.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: not applicable.
- CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract: input/output JSON Schemas and tool names are unchanged. `trace_web_source_location` budget refusals now carry `details.limit` (and `details.refusal` on `AnalysisResourceConstraintError` memory-limit refusals); CLI `--source-map-bytes` refusals include `details.limit.cli_flag: "--source-map-bytes"` and `required_value`, while MCP refusals omit `cli_flag`.
- Provider, bridge, target-format, or platform compatibility: internal `SourceMapCodecProtocol` `reason: "limit"` failure schema adds an optional `limit` field (backward-compatible with replies omitting `limit`, while rejecting non-codec fields, out-of-range maxima, or `limit` on `malformed`/`unsupported` replies).
- Evidence, artifact, provenance, or reconstruction contract: unchanged.
- Target selection, authority, upstream behavior, and cleanup details (if applicable): unchanged.
- Generated metadata (`docs/public/product-catalog.json`), package, or installation impact: none.

## Evidence and regression coverage

- Tests added or updated:
  - `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapCommand.test.ts`: asserts `error.limit`, omitted duplicate `remediationAction`, projected `details.limit`, and `details.refusal` (`adjustable_budget`, `control: "source_map_limits.codec_heap_mib"`) on codec process memory-limit refusals.
  - `src/javascript/sourceMaps/SourceMapDecoder.test.ts`: asserts `details.limit` on pre-spawn `map_bytes` (with `required_value`), pre-spawn `output_bytes` (without `required_value`), codec `stdout` `output_bytes`, `stderr` diagnostic overflow without `details.limit`, `parseSourceMapReply` `decoded_records` limit replies, backward-compatible `reason: "limit"` replies omitting `limit`, and rejection (`AnalysisOutputError` / `unreadable_output`) of malformed `limit` payloads (`fetch_bytes`, `codec_heap_mib`, out-of-range `maximum`, `reason: "malformed"` with `limit`).
  - `tests/boundary/javascript/sourceMapDecoder.test.ts`: asserts `limit` on real codec `output_bytes` refusal (without `required_value`) and `codec_heap_mib` memory-limit refusal.

body:
## Ringkasan

Skor lebih adil (chain tidak bisa di-spam), chain panjang tidak tersendat, piece tegak di atas tidak langsung kalah, dan ada menu ganti nama. Kecepatan maksimal juga dinaikkan menjadi 0,10 detik/baris di level 40.

## Isi

**Chain dihitung per penempatan** (masukan tester: spam piece bisa sampai chain 100)
- Sebelumnya chain hanya reset kalau seluruh pasir diam. Spam piece membuat pasir terus bergerak, sehingga setiap clear baru dihitung sebagai chain +1 dan pengali ×8 terus aktif.
- Sekarang setiap piece yang mendarat mengakhiri chain. Chain = clear beruntun dari satu penempatan. Tilt tetap boleh memperpanjang chain.
- Simulasi bot acak yang menunggu pasir diam: chain ×3 di 28/40 game, ×5 di 5/40 game. Prestasi chain tetap tercapai.

**Piece tegak tidak langsung kalah** (masukan tester)
- Sebelumnya piece yang terkunci sebagian di atas papan langsung *lockout* walau pasirnya belum sempat runtuh.
- Sekarang butir di atas papan antre dan dituang masuk begitu ada ruang. Piece berikutnya menunggu tempat muncul kosong sampai `SPAWN_WAIT` (1,5 detik). Kalah atau tidaknya diputuskan garis bahaya seperti pasir lain, jadi pemain masih bisa menyelamatkan diri dengan tilt. Papan yang benar-benar penuh tetap kalah.

**Chain tidak lagi lambat**
- Kedip clear sebelumnya naik tanpa batas (chain 97 = 4,1 detik per langkah, total sekitar 215 detik). Sekarang maksimal 0,5 detik, dan 0,2 detik mulai chain 15 (total chain 97 sekitar 23 detik).

**Input saat kedip diabaikan**
- Tombol selama kedip tidak lagi ditumpuk lalu dijalankan sekaligus. Geser-otomatis mulai dari jeda awal setelah kedip.

**Ganti nama**
- Pengaturan → `NAMA: <nama>`. Teks `M = SUARA   P = JEDA SAAT MAIN` dihapus.

**Kecepatan maksimal 0,10 detik/baris di level 40**
- Sebelumnya kecepatan berhenti di 0,15 mulai level 27.
- Sekarang level 26–30 turun 0,01 per level (0,16 → 0,12). Kecepatan 0,12 bertahan sampai level 34, menjadi 0,11 di level 35–39, lalu **0,10** mulai level 40.
- Kodenya di `fallFor()` (`js/config.js`). Tabel GDD 4.2 sudah diperbarui.
- Toast mode uji sekarang bertuliskan "SKOR DAN PRESTASI". Font pixel tidak punya karakter `&`, jadi sebelumnya tampil "SKOR ? PRESTASI".

**Reset skor lokal saat aturan skor berubah**
- `SCORE_VERSION = 2` di `js/main.js` (versi aturan skor, bukan versi aplikasi). Browser dengan versi lebih lama mengosongkan skor terbaik, riwayat skor lokal, dan skor tertunda **sekali**. Nama, token, prestasi, tema, suara, dan tutorial tidak disentuh.
- Dites di browser: skor terbaik 1.930.480 tanpa penanda versi → 0. Muat ulang berikutnya tidak me-reset lagi. Data lain tetap utuh.

**Kecepatan level 40** (`93a8cfd`, dari sesi tuning kesulitan)
- Batas kecepatan jatuh dinaikkan ke 0,10 detik/baris di level 40.

**Prestasi disesuaikan dengan aturan chain baru**
- **BADAI PASIR** (chain ×5) jadi hadiah **Tema Kertas** (sebelumnya hadiah NYARIS!). Posisinya dipindah ke bawah, dekat trofi ungu, dengan tier baru `legend`: ikon & suara ungu, toast *TROFI LEGENDA!*, tetap terlihat. `ACH_VERSION = 2` mencabut BADAI PASIR sekali bagi yang mendapatkannya dengan aturan lama.
- **MARATON**: level 10 → **level 15**.
- Baru: **MURID TELADAN** (selesaikan tutorial, perunggu) dan **TAHAN BANTING** (bertahan dari 5 event dalam satu game, emas).

## Setelah merge: reset papan peringkat

Skor lama didapat dengan aturan chain yang lama. Disepakati untuk reset semua skor. Jalankan di Neon SQL Editor **setelah** deploy ini live:

```sql
DELETE FROM sandtilt_scores;
DELETE FROM sandtilt_runs;
```

Tabel pemain tidak dihapus, jadi nama yang sudah diklaim tetap milik pemiliknya.

## Tes

- Headless: piece mendarat di tengah chain → chain 0 dan event `chainEnd` terkirim. Piece tegak di atas tumpukan: versi lama langsung *lockout*; versi baru runtuh lalu bisa diselamatkan dengan tilt. Papan penuh tetap kalah (`spawn`, 1,5 detik).
- Browser: spam jatuh instan 76 piece → chain terbaik 1. Main normal dan tutorial jalan, console bersih.
- Kecepatan: `?level=30` → 0,12 dan `?level=40` → 0,10 di game. Nilai per level sudah dicek: 26 = 0,16, 30 = 0,12, 35 = 0,11, 40 dan 100 = 0,10.

body:
## TLDR

Step 6 of [the agent-login spec](https://github.com/contember/fabrika-platform/blob/main/docs/specs/agent-login-into-applications.md): IAM gets an account page on its own host, `/auth/account`. A signed-in person sees every OAuth grant that acts as them (the command-line client's and each agent's at an application) and revokes any of them. Nothing changes for an existing installation besides the new page.

## What changed

- **`packages/iam/src/auth/account.ts`**, routed by `handleAuth`. GET lists the person's grants in force, newest first, at most 50: not revoked, not expired, the approving login not revoked. A same-origin POST revokes one by id and redirects back with its outcome. A browser with no login is sent to sign-in and back; a POST then revoked nothing.
- **Only the person's own grant.** `OAuthRepository.revokeOwnGrant` names the person in its UPDATE. Another person's id, an unknown id and a spent one all answer "That access had already ended." and change nothing. A revocation writes `iam.oauth.grant.revoke` under the person, `reason: 'owner'`, in its own statement.
- **Words** in en, cs and uk from IAM's catalog; the person's own language wins (`chooseLocale`). An agent's label is marked as its own words.
- **The device page's success screen** links to the account page.
- **Docs.** The IAM invariant in `packages/iam/CLAUDE.md`, "Ending a grant" in `docs/reference/cli-device-grant.md`, and backlog 192 now says the page exists and that item adds its password and sign-in sections.

## Tests

- `packages/iam/src/__tests__/account-page.test.ts`, on SQLite and Postgres (12 pass locally against Postgres 18): the sign-in redirect; only grants in force are listed (revoked, expired, ended-login and another person's are not); an own revocation happens once, is recorded as the person and leaves the page; another person's grant, an empty id, a cross-site POST and a POST without a login revoke nothing.
- Affected IAM suites (`oauth-device`, `agent-grant`, `auth-routes`, `entrypoint-isolation`): 80 pass on both engines.
- `tests/browser/iam-account-revokes-a-device-grant.test.ts` (opice, tier standard): a command-line device grant is approved on IAM, the person revokes it on `/auth/account`, and its next refresh is `invalid_grant`. It uses the command-line client because the browser stack's Notes example declares no `agent` caller. **Not run yet**: the fixed local-stack ports are taken by another checkout's stack; it runs once they are free.

| "agent-write on protected environments: off, plus passkey vs refuse" (decided: `off` plus a passkey at the device approval; fail closed until the step-up works) | the agent-write PR (step 5) | deferred to step 5, a separate PR of the same task; the passkey ceremony is still being decided |
| "one act claim shared with agent task keys" (decided: one claim name, two shapes by token kind) | step 5's docs commit | deferred to step 5 |

1. Generated files: none. 2. Environment variables: none. 3. Provider state: none; no migration. 4. Floating pins: none.

author: cneckar
body:
Natively, an `await` at a module's top level failed when it ran ("await is only valid in async functions here"). This adds asynchronous module evaluation (ECMA-262 16.2.1.5.3). It is the last part of P2's ESM linking. #1491 already lifts a module's top-level await, so this is the lowering's side.

## Changes
- **Which modules are async.** An ECMAScript module is evaluated asynchronously when it has an `await` at its top level, or when it imports (transitively) a module that does. That is a fixpoint over the program record.
- **How an async module runs.** Its body (dependencies, statements, namespace) runs as an async function's coroutine, and that function's promise is the module's evaluation promise. Before its own statements run, the body awaits each async dependency's evaluation promise.
- **`import()`** of an async module resolves once that module has been evaluated. The runtime keeps each evaluating module's promise for this.
- **Namespace marking.** A module's namespace is now marked as soon as its exports object is made, instead of after its statements, so `import()` recognizes it while it is still evaluating.

## Test
`emit-llvm-program` has a new `tla/` fixture with four modules:
- one module awaits at its top level;
- one imports it without awaiting, so it runs after it;
- the entry awaits `import()`s and promises;
- the entry then `import()`s a module that itself awaits.

The order of evaluation and the values seen match Node's exactly.

Tests run: `emit-llvm-program`, `-node`, `-boxed`, `-gc` and `-async-gen`, 118 in all, all passing.

author: marioparaschiv
body:
When the loader reloads Discord's runtime before it draws (a bundle update at launch, or a dev hot reload), the old runtime keeps starting addons after its native modules are gone. UI-runtime plugins then fail with `The UI runtime version is unsupported (JS 4.8.0-main, native undefined)`, and each failure is sent as a crash report for a runtime that is about to be thrown away. #2332, #2333 and #2335 came from exactly this on the vphone. Its `unbound.log` shows every failure about 60 ms after `Tearing down libdiscore`, before the new runtime evaluated Unbound.

Start failures are now reported from `afterFirstFrame`, which a torn-down runtime never reaches. They are still logged, stored in `errors` and shown in the UI right away.

#2364 doesn't cover this: `__UI_WORKLET_RUNTIME_HOLDER` is undefined on Discord 357.0.

Tests: `tests/addons/report-start-failure.test.ts` checks that nothing is reported before the first frame and that it is reported after. `lazy-patch.test.ts` now runs first-frame callbacks right away. `bun run typecheck` passes. I couldn't trigger the reload race on purpose on the vphone, so it hasn't been reproduced on a device.

author: victorlucss
body:
Closes #933. Closes #929.

## Why
- **Claude's Auto stopped on read-only commands.** Milagre's Auto maps to Claude's `acceptEdits`, which approves edits only. Any Bash outside Claude's own read-only list waited on a card, including `gh issue view` in an unattended CLI run (#933). Kiro and Pi already send commands in Auto through `command-risk.cjs`, so Auto meant less for Claude than for them.
- **`milagre command run worktree:create` required `--chat`** even though it creates the Chat (#929). `command list` and `command describe` already showed owner operations without `--chat`; only `run` refused.
- **`worktree create --prompt` looked like it should start the agent.** The prompt only names the branch and folder. The desktop sends the first message itself, so sending it here would double it.

## Change
- `claude-provider.cjs`: in Auto, a Bash request goes through `commandRisk` with the Chat's folders as roots. A command inside the Worktree runs. A risky one (writes to GitHub, reaches outside the Worktree, hard to undo) gets the usual card, with the reason. A request Claude already flagged with `blockedPath` always asks. Ask and Full are unchanged.
- `product-commands.cjs`: `command run NAME` without `--chat` runs the owner operation, the same as `milagre <family> <action>`. Help lists both forms.
- `WorktreeRequest.prompt` (contract) and the `worktree_create` MCP schema say the prompt only names the branch and point to `chat send` / `chat_start`.
- `docs/desktop-guide.md`: Auto now describes Claude, Kiro and Pi together.

## Surfaces
- **Desktop and phone:** no UI change. The shared Auto description ("Allow changes inside this Worktree") still fits. Approval cards already show `reason` on both.
- **Providers:** Claude changes. Kiro and Pi already did this. Codex keeps its sandbox. Antigravity keeps `auto_edit`.
- **Entry points:** CLI `command run`. The MCP `worktree_create` description.
- **Computers:** host-side, so it applies wherever the Chat runs.

## Checks
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`
- `npm test -- --only workspace-roots` (new test: Auto runs `gh issue view` and `npm test && git log` without a card, asks for `gh pr merge` and an outside `rm -rf` with their reasons, and Ask still asks)
- `npm test -- --only command` (new: `command run project:current` and `command run chat:patch` with named flags, no `--chat`)
- `npm test -- --only claude`, `--only permission`, `--only local-mcp`

## Screenshots from
None: no visible change.

author: amstreem
body:
## Root cause addressed
The earlier fix stripped literal U+25CC characters and grouped marks when a preceding segment existed, but it still allowed a leading/orphan combining mark to be rendered without an Arabic base. Some fonts display those orphan marks using a dotted-circle placeholder. The same risk existed in the server parser and in pre-parsed Tajweed segments.

## Changes
- Keep Arabic combining marks attached to a preceding Arabic base; if a mark arrives before any base, buffer it and attach it to the next base instead of rendering it alone.
- Apply the same clustering to server-generated and client-supplied Tajweed segments, covering Verse-by-Verse and Page-by-Page fallback rendering.
- Strip literal dotted-circle characters and common numeric HTML entity forms from all sanitized Qur’an text, including QCF code strings.
- Bump the Mushaf local cache key from v17 to v18 so previously cached affected text cannot keep displaying after deployment.

## Verification
Render production build will run the repository's TypeScript checks and test suite.

body:
## Resumo

- **T2.1** — Recupera a abertura do banco de fichas após uma falha, fechando a conexão com erro e reabrindo o mesmo arquivo ao tocar em **Tentar novamente**.
- **T2.2** — Preserva a causa da falha de gravação quando o SQLite já reverteu a transação. O APK de integração permite pausar uma edição antes do commit para testar a recuperação após o encerramento do processo.

## Evidências

- **RED → GREEN da T2.1** — O teste de componente reproduziu a falha da nova tentativa. Após a correção, confirmou a reabertura do mesmo banco e a exibição da ficha. A integração com SQLite em disco confirmou persistência após fechar e reabrir a conexão.
- **RED → GREEN da T2.2** — O teste com SQLite real reproduziu a perda da causa original da falha. Após a correção, confirmou a preservação da ficha e da biblioteca e o sucesso de uma nova gravação. Os testes também cobrem migrações repetidas e a manutenção do rascunho na interface após falha de escrita.
- **Android físico** — No Galaxy A54, o APK instalado criou, editou e reabriu uma ficha em modo avião e sem Metro. A criação foi feita no tema claro e a edição no escuro. No APK de integração, o processo foi encerrado pelo ADB antes do commit. A ficha original e o vínculo com o exercício permaneceram íntegros ao reabrir.
- **Verificações** — `npm test` (36 testes), `npm run lint` e `npx tsc --noEmit` passaram. Os APKs normal e de integração foram compilados localmente.

[História 2 e roteiro detalhado](../blob/feat/offline-persistence/histories/MVP/2-Persist%C3%AAncia%20Local%20Offline.md)

## Checklist de testes manuais

- [ ] Instalar o APK normal em um dispositivo de teste com banco vazio. Ativar o modo avião, fechar o Metro e abrir o app. Confirmar que a lista de treinos está vazia.
- [ ] Em **Treinos**, criar uma ficha com um exercício usando o teclado. Salvar e confirmar que o cartão aparece na lista.
- [ ] Encerrar o app e reabrir em modo avião. Abrir a ficha e conferir o nome e o exercício salvos.
- [ ] Alternar para o tema escuro. Editar o nome da ficha, salvar e reabrir o app. Confirmar que o novo nome permanece e verificar o retorno de navegação pelo botão Voltar.
- [ ] Gerar e instalar o APK de integração com `EXPO_PUBLIC_RUN_SQLITE_TESTS=1` na etapa de empacotamento do JavaScript. Abrir em modo avião e conferir que os cenários SQLite passam e que o relatório indica **Banco de teste vazio** na primeira execução.
- [ ] Tocar em **Pausar edição antes do commit**. Quando a tela indicar que a transação está pausada, executar `adb shell am force-stop <pacote>` e reabrir sem Metro. Confirmar a mensagem **Ficha original íntegra**.
- [ ] Restaurar a conectividade e reinstalar o APK normal.

author: alisku
body:
Part of pbinitiative/zenbpm#940, the UI's side of the engine change in pbinitiative/zenbpm#947.

> **Not to be merged before** pbinitiative/zenbpm#947 is in and the properties panel of pbinitiative/zenbpm-js-properties-panel#10 is released (as `0.7.0`). `package.json` still pins the panel `0.6.0`, which has no FEEL value for a timer, so the new designer tests fail with it. The bump to `0.7.0` is to be added to this branch once the panel is reviewed and published.

## What the engine does now

A timer's `timeDate`, `timeDuration` or `timeCycle` which starts with `=` is a FEEL expression: the engine evaluates it against the variables of the process instance when the timer is created, and a value it cannot use becomes an incident. A timer start event of an event sub-process is one more place where resolving an incident can be refused, while its expression still does not evaluate.

The designer takes such a value through the panel's new **Timer** group (a Value which is static or FEEL, with the *fx* toggle); the UI itself needs no code change for it. The instance page shows the timers and incidents as before.

## What changes

**API**
- `openapi/api.yaml`: the 409 of `POST /incidents/{incidentKey}/resolve` names the timer start event of an event sub-process whose expression still does not evaluate, as the engine branch does.

**Tests**
- Mocked: `e2e/pages/process-designer/timer-feel-expression.spec.ts` (new, with the fixture `timer-feel-expression.bpmn`): a literal shown in a plain input and an expression in the FEEL editor, the Type options, the FEEL toggle both ways, an unparsable expression flagged, and expressions exported to the XML and read back.
- Live, element suite: a timer value as a FEEL expression is designed, re-imported and deployed on three elements: a date on an intermediate catch event, a duration on an interrupting boundary event and a cycle on a non-interrupting event sub-process start event. New helpers `editTimerExpression` (`helpers/eventProperties.ts`) and `expectTimerValue` (`helpers/bpmnAssertions.ts`). README counts and coverage updated.
- Live, processes: `e2e/live/processes/timerExpression.spec.ts` (new) designs a timer whose date is `=dueAt`, starts an instance with that variable through the definition's page and expects the timer among the instance's timers, due at that moment. For that, `startProcessInstance` and `deployAndStartDesignedProcess` take the variables of the instance.

## Verified

Against an engine built from the head of pbinitiative/zenbpm#947 (`e6ed7045`), with the panel of pbinitiative/zenbpm-js-properties-panel#10 (`b416884`) built locally in place of `0.6.0`:

author: autumnsgrove
body:
Closes #1769.

The first write path, and the thing the platform exists for: a writer puts words in and they come out the other side. 14 tests across `happy`, `bad`, `sad` — create, update, publish, and the read-back that proves it landed, through the real worker with real D1 and the real Threshold Durable Object.

## The suites

**happy** — a draft only its writer can see; a publish-on-create that renders at its slug; an update whose new words replace the old; a draft that becomes reachable when published.

**bad** — unauthenticated create is `401`; publishing with no words is `400`; a taken slug is `409`; publishing into another writer's grove is `404`.

**sad** — writing after the rate-limit DO is evicted; two publishes of the same post at once (both `200`, page agrees with one of them, no half-written row); a suspended grove refusing the write; a just-written post rendering with the content DOs evicted; and a tier's post limit refusing the 26th publish with `403` rather than `500`.

## A bug this found, fixed here

`PUT /api/blooms/:slug` without a `status` field answered **500**. `updatePost` passed `data.status` straight into the update, so an absent status became a JS `undefined` in a D1 binding, which D1 rejects outright (`DatabaseError: Update posts failed`). The editor always sends a status, so nothing caught it. Fixed in `31bdd4e98`: the status falls back to the row's current value, and a regression test pins it.

## Two things the issue assumed, which are not true

1. **Post content never touches `PostContentDO` or `PostMetaDO`.** Both are bound in `wrangler.toml` and referenced nowhere in `apps/aspen` or the engine. The write path is D1 only, so "save when the content DO was evicted" has nothing to evict. The suite asserts the consequence — a just-written post renders with those namespaces evicted — and this PR says so rather than inventing a DO interaction to test.
2. **The only Durable Object on the write path is `ThresholdDO`**, the per-user sliding window for rate limiting. The eviction sad case targets that, and the `wanderer` post limit covers the quota-adjacent case; there is no storage-quota enforcement on create, only post counts.

If wiring content through the DOs is still the plan, that is a product decision worth its own issue — the tests are honest about today's shape.

## Harness

`testTimeout` for the routes project is now 20s: a create-and-read cycle against real workerd/SQLite/DOs occasionally crosses the 5s default, and the test was slow, not stuck.

## Local

`pnpm --filter grove-aspen test:run`: 391 tests, all green (47 route tests, 344 unit). `svelte-check`: 0 errors.

## Summary
`pgf test dem --short` (50 solver steps) now passes 7/7. Under `--short`, `checkInvariants.py` checks a `>=` bound above 0 as `> 0` and a `<=` bound below 0 as `< 0`: the direction of lambda (#194) is still checked, the full-run magnitude is not. Every other invariant is checked as declared, and full runs are unchanged. Each relaxed check is printed with its declared form, e.g. `OK lambdaMinusOneMax max(lambdaMinusOne) < 0 (short run; declared <= -1e-06)`.

## Why
The MicroTGA-DEM invariant bounds are calibrated for the full-length run (e.g. `average(lambdaMinusOne) >= 1e-8`, about 1/10 of the first sample at t=2e-4). A short run ends at t=5e-5, where lambda has moved the right way but less: 3.1e-9 and 6.5e-9 for lambdaDotTemperature. So 5 of 7 cases failed `--short` on every machine, while the full tier passes 7/7. Found while verifying coupling v2 on Open MPI 4.1 (#336).

## Changes
- `tools/checkInvariants.py`: `--short` option and `shorten()`; strict `>` / `<` checks.
- `tools/runDEMCase.sh`: passes `--short` when `--short-steps` is set.
- `tools/tests/test_checkInvariants.py`: unit and CLI tests for the relaxation, including a wrong-sign run that still fails.
- `doc/regression-testing.md`: one sentence on what `--short` checks.

## Verification
- `python3 -m unittest` on `test_checkInvariants.py`: 10/10.

author: christopherstyles
body:
Closes #598

## Summary

The PostgreSQL adapter reads a connection string's `connect_timeout` as libpq reads it. libpq skips only ASCII whitespace around the number (`strtol` and `isspace`), but the pattern used `\s`, which also matches a no-break space, a line separator and the other Unicode spaces.

```diff
 // packages/arbor/src/adapters/postgresql/connect-timeout.ts
-const wholeNumber = /^\s*[-+]?\d+\s*$/;
+const asciiSpace = "[ \\t\\n\\v\\f\\r]";
+const wholeNumber = new RegExp(`^${asciiSpace}*[-+]?[0-9]+${asciiSpace}*$`);
```

```text
connect("postgres://…?connect_timeout=%C2%A05")      before: 5 s limit    after: TypeError
connect("postgres://…?connect_timeout=%20%093%0D%0A") before: 3 s limit    after: 3 s limit
```

Docs: one clause in the contract, one sentence in the 0.14 Upgrading step (and its intro), and a `minor` changeset, since a value that used to be read now throws.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `tests/integration/pg/connect-timeout.test.ts`, "with a no-break space before / after its digits throws" and "with a line separator before its digits throws": 3 failed, since `connect()` returned a Database.
  **After:** 20 of 20 pass. The guard "with connect_timeout=3 between ASCII spaces fails after 3000ms" (`%20%09%0B3%0C%0D%0A`) passes before and after.
- `vp run validate` with `DATABASE_URL` set to a local Postgres: all steps pass (check, test and coverage, build, public types, knip, docs build, package contents, deploy dry runs).
- The pattern is now built with `new RegExp` from a module-local string. A probe file with a super-linear pattern built the same way was flagged by `regexp(no-super-linear-backtracking)`, so the lint still checks it.

## Review

8 findings: 5 fixed, 2 rejected, 1 deferred.

| Finding | Tag | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connect-timeout.ts:17` the six spaces were written out twice, not as the agreed module-local `asciiSpace` | Nit | Fixed in 67816742 |
| `connect-timeout.test.ts:118` expected values held a raw U+00A0 and U+2028 instead of escapes | Nit | Folded into 8c786ce5 |
| A commit message held the same raw characters | Nit | Gone with the fold into 8c786ce5 |
| `upgrading.mdx:10` the 0.14 intro named only the attributes | Nit | Fixed in 09491d52 |
| `upgrading.mdx:16` "just as libpq refuses it" was filler, and libpq was unintroduced | Nit | Fixed in 09491d52 |
| `contract.md:61` the added "with only ASCII spaces around them" goes past the agreed docs outline | Rejected | It is the contract's own sentence for this behavior, and accurate. Kept |
| Guard test waits out 3 seconds | Rejected | It runs on fake timers |
| `connect-timeout.ts:47` `URLSearchParams` reads `+` as a space, where libpq doesn't (`connect_timeout=5+`) | Pre-existing | #603 |

The decisions also deferred a `connect_timeout` past C's `int` range, which libpq refuses and this caps: #602.

**Check candidates:** raw invisible Unicode spaces in files and commit messages. The same thing came up in #601's review, so this time it got an issue: #605.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** narrow

Only a Postgres connection string whose `connect_timeout` has a Unicode space around its number changes. That string now throws `TypeError` when the Database is built, where it used to set the limit. A Hyperdrive binding and a `pg` Pool are untouched.

- There were also two fixed ~120 s 429 lock-outs, which our 30 s cap probed 3 times each.
- The live run due at 15:47 waited 8.7 minutes behind it.
- The 12:50 cycle's change did not help, and its "0 refusals" check had a warm cache (now corrected in the register).

**Backend** (`providers/base.py`, `others.py`, `collect.py`)
- **Outages:** when every attempt fails with a 5xx or network error, the provider is marked down for 5 minutes. While it is down, URLs we already have are served from the old (stale) cache at once, and other URLs fail immediately.
- **Lock-outs:** a 429 sets a cool-down of min(max(Retry-After, back-off), 130 s). If the cache already has that URL and the block is longer than 30 s, the old answer is served at once.
- **Lasting limits:** at most one lock-out wait per provider per process; a second 429 fails fast. This prevents 30 URLs × 3 × 130 s from reaching the 80-minute job timeout.
- **Retries:** no sleep after the final 5xx or network attempt.
- **Circuit breaker:** requests skipped because the provider is down or locked out never count towards the 6 h circuit breaker. The overdue step stops on them.
- **Pacing:** TheSportsDB spacing goes from 5 s to 6.5 s. At 5 s, 429s came after 10–12 requests in the previous minute.
- **Tests:** the shared rate state is reset between tests; new tests cover every case above.

**Frontend**
- The Overview bankroll tile now headlines equity (cash + open stakes), with cash underneath.
- A match that started but has no score stays on the "today" lists for up to 12 h, so it no longer disappears at midnight Rome. Postponed and cancelled matches are excluded.
- The health banner and sidebar now name the cause, e.g. "results (18 overdue), live".
- The bet slip says "Model probability (at placement)".

**Checks:** pytest 202 passed, frontend build OK, node tests 16/16, actionlint clean.
