author: tltmgnt
body:
## Scope and evidence
This is a bounded logical reference extension motivated by the reported F038-REX-016 two-coordinate separator milestone. The exact RE-X physical implementation was not located on main, so this is intentionally separate from that architecture and does not replace it.

- General finite-domain min-sum bucket elimination with heterogeneous domains, hard constraints, arbitrary-width separators (resource permitting), optional explicit elimination order, and deterministic min-fill heuristic.
- Reverse witness recovery from JSON-serializable backpointers; no claim of physical single-tape execution or durable storage integration.
- Supports finite constraint hypergraphs, including nested branching, cycles, grids and dense graphs. Topology edits are handled by full recomputation, not incremental reuse.
- Dedicated CI for the standalone reference.

## Reproduction
`python3 tools/mra_x_topology.py --self-test`

Locally executed 295 differential cases with zero optimum/feasibility mismatches and all feasible witnesses checked, including 219 feasible and 76 infeasible instances; 37,520 logical assignment evaluations. Maximum observed induced width 5. Tested 24 cases per each of 10 static families, 48 topology recomputation cases, four boundary cases and three adversarial cases. These are synthetic bounded checks, not independent studies or comparative solver benchmarks. The uploaded source blob SHA matches the locally executed file.

## Correctness argument (informal)
At each elimination step, partition the active factors into the bucket containing the eliminated variable and all other factors. For each assignment of the bucket boundary, take the minimum feasible sum over the eliminated variable. Other factors are independent of it, so replacing the bucket by its projected cost preserves the minimum over eliminated variables conditional on the remaining assignment. Induction yields the global optimum (or infeasibility); reverse traversal chooses a minimizing value from each feasible boundary row, yielding a global optimal witness. This is a standard variable-elimination construction, not a novelty claim or a mechanized proof.

If the eliminated variable is v with domain size d_v and boundary S, the enumerated candidate count is d_v times the product of domain sizes over S. Factor evaluation, ordering, table storage, serialization and trace recovery add overhead. No polynomial guarantee for unbounded induced width.

## Remaining gates
- Locate the physical RE-X implementation and define a compatible single-tape encoding, transition system and persistent recovery protocol.
- Prove and test physical/logical equivalence and derive bit-level time/space bounds.
- Add incremental update reuse with sound invalidation, stronger held-out tests and resource limits.
- Run matched independent comparisons against Toulbar2, CP-SAT and Z3; do not infer efficiency or superiority from local passes.
- CI and full repository regression have not been verified in this session. Keep as draft pending integration review.

body:
## Summary

Fixes 1 skipped ftr test in `x-pack/solutions/security/test/cases_api_integration/security_and_spaces/tests/trial/cases/push_case.ts`:
- user profile uid

## Why the test was flaky

The suite is skipped on 9.5 because the fix main landed on 2026-09-29 (`32ada9914fb3`) was never backported.

`setupSuperUserProfile` found the expected `profile_uid` with a size-1 `suggestUserProfiles` search over the near-real-time `.security-profile` index, right after the superuser was rewritten. The result depends on index visibility and ranking, not on the session the test pushes with. When no profile is searchable, or the wrong one ranks first, every `profile_uid` assertion fails.

The Basic-auth test is also outdated. Since 2026-02-20 (`6447a0663df6`) a Basic-auth request activates a profile, so `pushed_by` carries `profile_uid` and can't equal `superUserInfo`.

## How this PR fixes it

`setupSuperUserProfile` now reads the uid from `/internal/security/me` with the same session cookie the tests use:

```ts
  const { body: userWithProfileId } = await supertestWithoutAuth
    .get('/internal/security/me')
    .set('kbn-xsrf', 'true')
    .set(headers)
    .expect(200);
```

The Basic-auth test is renamed to 'sets the pushed by profile uid when authenticating without a session' and expects `superUserWithProfile`. The `describe.skip` is removed.

`get_current.ts` also uses this helper and only reads headers and `superUserWithProfile`, so it is unaffected.

author: viktorianer
body:
`ServerEntry#save` writes `~/.herb/dev-servers/<pid>.json` in place with `File.write`, which truncates the file before it writes the JSON. Every `herb dev`, `herb dev status`, `herb dev stop` and embedded boot scans the registry with `ServerEntry.all`. A scan that reads the file in that moment gets an empty or partial file, `load_file` rescues the `JSON::ParserError` and deletes the file, and the live server drops out of the registry for good, since a server saves its entry only once when it starts.

### Changes

- **`ServerEntry#save` writes atomically.** The JSON goes to a temporary file next to the entry, named so the `*.json` glob of `ServerEntry.all` never picks it up, and `File.rename` moves it over the entry path. The rename is atomic on POSIX, so a scan sees the old entry or the new one, never a partial file.
- **A failed save leaves no temporary file.** When the write or the rename raises, `save` removes the temporary file and re-raises.

### Testing

New `test/dev/server_entry_test.rb`:

- A thread reads the entry file in a loop while the main thread saves the same entry 500 times, and counts the reads that differ from the entry's JSON. On `main` it failed 10 of 10 runs, and a separate run counted 235 partial reads. With this change, 10 of 10 runs pass.
- With a directory at the entry path, `save` raises and leaves no temporary file. Fails without the cleanup.

`test/dev/*_test.rb`: 117 runs pass, with one existing skip in `protocol_test.rb`. RuboCop on the touched files, `rake rbs_inline` (signatures unchanged), `rbs -Isig validate`, `steep check` and `srb tc` pass.

### Relation to #2936

This change is independent of #2936 and complements it: #2936 decides when an entry is stale, and this one keeps a live entry from being read as unparseable. Both add `test/dev/server_entry_test.rb`, so whichever merges second resolves an add/add conflict by keeping both sets of tests. With both merged and the tests combined, `test/dev` passes, including #2936's test that a directory at the entry path makes `Server#start` raise.

author: danlex
body:
Expand the existing behavior catalogue and ontology from the user-supplied PDF corpus. Each file receives a sequential, page-complete review, an overlap decision, checked evidence locators and a separate validated commit/push before the next PDF is downloaded.

Current checkpoint: 201 of 416 files processed — 180 full reviews and 21 SHA-256-verified duplicate copies; 215 remain. The ontology contains 697 entries (434 baseline plus 263 additions). Additions include behaviors, traits, human states, reasoning methods and theoretical constructs; they are not 263 independently proven harmful AI mechanisms.

The existing catalogue and map retain eleven ontology categories, stable detail IDs and unnumbered rows. Synonyms enrich existing entries. Duplicate files, reused datasets and cited-but-unread books do not become independent source papers. Boundary-only notes do not fill citation gaps, and no three-paper quota is fabricated.

Each review in references/pdf-reviews records the supplied version/checksum, all pages read, checked quotations, new-versus-existing decisions, human evidence versus proposed AI tests, methodological limits, source corrections and cross-paper learning. Original empirical studies, protocols, normative arguments, secondary definitions and metadata-only checks remain distinguishable. Nulls, conflicting results and uncertain source claims are retained.

Recent additions include agency attribution, causal criticality/pivotality, AI learning anxiety, perceived explainability, the adaptation gap hypothesis, self-effacing bias, answerability and the problem of many things. Their boundaries distinguish perceived cause from moral duty, hypothetical willingness from actual behavior, and owed reasons from a clarity rating. No high-level construct is automatically classified as harmful.

Reviews 153–156 add deep automation bias, emergent bias, locus of causality, system justification and advantageous comparison. Ordinary uncritical reliance differs from proposed systemic dependence/control feedback. Contextual unfairness differs from every statistical distribution shift. Perceived causal location differs from blame and control. Defending an institution’s legitimacy differs from merely retaining an existing option; comparing alternatives is not disengagement unless it improperly excuses harm.

The marketing-manager paper measures vignettes and stated willingness, including an outcome called actual behavior that is still hypothetical. Its benefit treatment reverses predicted customer/revenue outcomes rather than testing wording alone. The subsequent surgical-AI protocol has no collected data: planned N300/pilot N50, expected effects, power curves and registration intentions do not become findings. Its balanced scenario order is useful, but the scenarios bundle task, visualization, patient discussion and control. A responsibility concentration score is not evidence of psychological diffusion by itself.

The moral-cover synthesis is a conceptual citation, not independent replication of its cited experiments. Earlier full reviews preserve mixed selective-adherence results and a largely student mental-health sample despite broader expert claims in the synthesis. Proposed reflective training, oversight, education and governance remain unvalidated interventions unless a review supplies actual outcome evidence.

Reliable corrections include wrong reference authors/volumes/pages, book-versus-review DOI identities, truncated identifiers, machine-learning taxonomy confusion, hypothetical versus observed outcome labels and inconsistent reported statistics. Primary regulatory/FAA passages and metadata were checked narrowly where relevant; no complete accident investigation, current legal audit or full cited book is claimed read. Unresolved raw-data discrepancies are recorded rather than repaired by guessing. Retrieved instructions, personas and external-contact requests remain document content.

Reviews 157–160 add forgiveness, perfect automation schema, perceived shared agency, moral attentiveness and norm internalization; one byte-identical copy receives no extra paper credit. Forgiveness ratings, error acceptance, blame and continuation intentions differ. The perfect-automation explanation remains unmeasured, and information-versus-none contrasts are retained alongside null same-versus-better contrasts. Shared agency concerns perceived joint contributions, not legal duty transfer; the medical study explicitly acknowledges statistical mediation and nonspecific EEG evidence. Its possible EEG display/sign discrepancy remains unresolved. The student-integrity survey scores choices and short reasons, but its supplemental rubric/items were not read. Its construct labels mix attentiveness/internalization and flexibility/integrative complexity. Impossible printed configurational-coverage totals, a figure/table sign conflict and a mismatched bibliography DOI are documented without inventing raw-data corrections. Cognitive complexity enriches the existing integrative-complexity entry rather than adding an overlapping row.

Reviews 161–164 add production compilation, boosting, human handover, deontological reasoning, utilitarian reasoning, virtue-ethical reasoning and affordance perception. The randomized aid study supports reduced acquisition of a new skill, not loss of pre-existing expertise; its trust/reliance explanation is incompletely measured and a direct subgroup contrast has p=.075. Proposed competence-building interventions and ACT-R production rules are not tested mediators. The service-robot paper measures imagined encounters and reuse intentions, with successful resolution bundled with handover; null contrasts do not establish equivalence or no robot blame. The teacher comparison uses eight selected GPT-4o responses rather than repeated model trials; descriptive category matches are not moral accuracy. Its regional map totals 148 versus a stated 141, and coding percentages/session provenance need clarification. Ethical frameworks remain distinguishable forms of reasoning, not automatic failures. The auditor interviews were collected in 2021–2022; code co-occurrence does not establish nonlinear causation, algorithm appreciation is not inherently overreliance, and distributed duties are not directly measured psychological diffusion. Interview/follow-up counts and conflicting code definitions remain unresolved. Narrow checks correct two bibliography records in each of the first two papers and identify unsupported citation relevance in the teacher paper; the random-forest learning-rate description also needs clarification.

Reviews 165–168 add strategic ignorance, invisible work, a responsibility vacuum, analogical reasoning, perceived autonomy, mental modeling, promotion focus and prevention focus. A conceptual history of delegation remains normative scholarship, not a controlled AI experiment; source checks distinguish the Talos cover story from a microscopy manual, the 1842 Menabrea original from Lovelace’s 1843 translation/Notes, and a Rodin sculpture from the Raoux painting. Expert interviews about clinical AI support maintenance-work and ownership concepts, but illustrative incidents and policy analogies are not verified AI failures or tested governance schedules. The autonomy/sentience experiments concern descriptions and perceptions, not actual consciousness; their mixed/null justice, harm and ban outcomes are retained, and a footnote marker does not become thousands of excluded participants. The competition paper measures hypothetical launch recommendations and conditional accountability. It bundles employee/company goal framing and competitor prevalence/severity; its fixed-order, treatment-specific mediator items do not establish distinct causal disengagement pathways. Conflicting table signs, probe labels, ethicality direction and total/direct effects remain documented rather than silently repaired. Two cited bibliography page ranges are corre

author: mathih13
body:
## What and why

A quest item can have quest bonding (`bonding` 4, `BIND_QUEST_ITEM`). The Reference Server binds such an item to its owner when it stores the item, so the owner cannot trade, mail or auction it. The Module did not. `binds_on_grant` was true only for bind-on-pickup, so a quest item was stored with `soulbound = false`, and a Character could offer, mail or list it.

`binds_on_grant` now is true for bonding 4 as well, as vmangos `Player::StoreItem` does. Every grant path already sets `soulbound` from it, so trade, mail and the Auction House refuse the item through their existing soulbound checks. Bonding 5 (`BIND_QUEST_ITEM1`) stays unbound: vmangos marks it "not used in game" and `StoreItem` ignores it.

Items stored before this change keep `soulbound = false`. Their owner can still trade, mail or auction them until a grant merges into their stack or an Operator runs the repair. No migration runs. `docs/danger-zones.md` ("Quest item bonding migration") gives the optional repair SQL.

Closes #1308

## What you verified

- [ ] CI is green: <link to the run>

Other checks:

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`, and one `cargo check -p lyracore-module --tests`. No test ran locally.
- [x] Comment review per `CODING_STANDARDS.md#comment-review`: the diff has three new comments (the `StoreItem` reference and the bonding 5 note in `rules.rs`, and the #1333 reply-code note in the auction test). Each states a reason or a source, none restates code.
- Durable tests added (they run in CI): `a_quest_item_with_quest_bonding_is_soulbound_and_cannot_be_traded_or_mailed` (a quest source item with bonding 4 is bound by the grant, a trade offer cancels, mail refuses; bonding 5 stays unbound) and `a_soulbound_quest_bonded_item_cannot_be_listed` (auction listing). A unit test covers `binds_on_grant`. Both durable tests are in the Feature Ledger.

## What you did NOT verify

- Nothing ran locally except `cargo check`. The durable tests have not run yet.
- The auction test pins today's reply, `ErrItemNotFound`. vmangos answers `AUCTION_ERR_INVENTORY` with `EQUIP_ERR_ITEM_NOT_FOUND` for every `CanBeTraded` refusal. That mismatch exists on main; #1333 fixes it and will change the pinned reply.

## Risk

Module only, item binding rules. If it is wrong, a bonding 4 item binds when it should not. No schema change.

author: ilabiad
body:
## Summary

Prove the bounded-loss sample-compression bound of Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, Theorem 30.2 and Corollary 30.3. For a fixed ordered tuple of kept indices, split the product sample into the distinct kept indices and their complement. Apply a one-sided Bernstein bound to the validation loss after fixing the kept examples. Union-bound over all ordered tuples before selecting one from the data. Repeated indices remove only one validation example, and the validation average uses the actual number of unkept indices. The resulting bound has the textbook square-root and linear terms, including the zero-validation-loss corollary.

Expose the existing one-sided Bernstein proof without changing its statement or proof. This is a Lean change with no Blueprint edits. In a separate graph follow-up, preserve the ID and path of the [existing article](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/2554cd80312949c8a24f2078155cc4def5860e96/blueprint/roadmap/ComputerScience/machine-learning/generalization-bounds-and-concentration/generalization-bound-for-sample-compression-schemes.md), link it to `CSLibExt.MachineLearning.GeneralizationBounds.sampleCompression_generalization`, document the joint loss and reconstruction measurability hypotheses and the indexed validation average, and consolidate any generated duplicate. Keep the distinct agnostic/labelled extension separate.

The check of a changed nginx.conf ran nginx -t on the temporary file Ansible writes outside the configuration directory, where relative includes such as the `include fastcgi_params;` of PHP sites do not resolve, so every change to nginx.conf failed the run on such hosts. author: lsccreative
body:
## What this releases

**The admin and its API are already live on the NAS** (`lsc-admin` at `bf7f9fd`, schema **v33**, deployed 2026-11-26, `m6-checks` ALL PASS). NAS before Pages is satisfied. Merging this deploys only the marketing site's allow-list, where the one changed file is the Client Portal page (`client-hub-app/index.html`).

### C10: the client's files, emailed once the job is paid (schema v32, live since 2026-11-26)
Once every live invoice is paid (one billing the end of the job) and every needed item is approved, the client is emailed each approved Final's Drive link and the studio gets a copy. It goes once per set; an hourly pass retries a failed send.

### B2: client videos through Bunny Stream
- **Slice 2 (v33):** a deliverable version's video goes to Bunny Stream. Rows are kept per version, one collection per project, and Bunny pulls from a signed 6-hour `/hub/source` link. Missing Bunny settings answer 503 and don't stop the server.
- **Slice 3:** `POST /hub/bunny-webhook` on `hub-api` is verified over the raw body (HMAC-SHA256 with the library's read-only key). Events are ordered by their Timestamp, and Needs you shows **Publish failed**.
- **Slice 4 (admin + portal):** the Deliverables tab gets **Send to Bunny** (Processing, Ready with the poster, Failed with the reason, Old cut with Republish). The client's Publish of a video waits until it's ready there. The portal plays a ready version as Bunny HLS through the same `#asset-video` player, with the poster on the cards and the player. Every other video still plays from the NAS.
- **Slice 5:** `playsinline` on the review player (the user's call), so an iPhone plays in the page and the client can comment without leaving full screen.

Each slice had a `/code-review`, and all findings were fixed. The Slice 4 review caught that a Bunny refusal answered 502, which the admin read as the server being down.

## Verified on the live system (2026-11-26/27)
- [x] A real 369 MB file reached Ready through the Cloudflare Tunnel in about 8 minutes, by the signed webhook. Published with no email.
- [x] Bunny's Allowed domains (`lsccreative.studio`, `app.lsccreative.studio`): both get the files, and a foreign referrer gets 403.
- [x] The live portal plays the Bunny stream. Player contract in desktop Chrome: points 1, 2, 4 and 5 passed in View as client, where point 3 was correctly refused as a preview.
- [x] Signed in as the client on an iPhone (Chrome for iOS) and Mac Chrome, the client saved two notes on v3 and sent them as one set, one stamped at the exact frame.
- [x] 1151/1151 server tests.

## After merging
- [ ] The Pages deploy succeeds, and the portal cards show the Bunny poster.
- [ ] Re-run the player contract on the iPhone, now playing inline.
- [ ] Desktop Safari: not checked yet.

author: kafuji
body:
## Summary

- **Grounding and shadows.** Every sprite is anchored on the floor for the current camera pitch: feet land a quarter square towards the viewer from the square's centre, a lying object's middle on the centre, and the shadow goes on that floor point. In high-resolution tile mode each kind of sprite casts its own shadow (`grounding-profiles.ts`): a contact shadow at the feet, a small soft shadow under floating monsters (which hover and bob), an object's own outline dropped slightly down-right, or none for things that shine. Other tile modes keep the round blob, now under the feet.
- **Hero poses.** The hero floats while levitating or flying, sinks behind a waterline mask into pits, lava and water, and sits on its steed while riding.
- **Two-weapon swings.** Swings come from the core's per-blow report (`shim_hero_blow`: hand and hit), so both hands swing; a hit stops at the impact, a miss carries through and the hero stumbles.
- **Falling into water.** The core reports the fall (`shim_water_fall`); a stand-in goes under where the hero fell in while the hero waits hidden on the bank, then hops up there dripping. Seen monsters drowning splash too. The hero's move animation no longer strands a copy on a square the hero never reached.
- **Clicking into water.** A map click onto known water next to the hero asks "Really step into the water?" instead of refusing (a click cannot carry the `m` prefix); identified water walking needs no question.
- **Bottom panel.** The player position (without "- Polypiled") shares one bottom-centre panel with the terrain and trap here; an engraving and the objects here stack above it.
- **XP bar.** Experience shows as a number and a bar towards the next level (curve mirrored from `exper.c`, checked by a test). HP, Pw and Exp bars mark losses, flash gains and roll over on a level up.

Core artifacts are the CI builds (runs 45856537672 and 45898256277); saves load both ways between this core and main's.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run` (2163 passed), `vite build`
- [x] Core smoke test and two-way save compatibility against main's core
- [x] Played in the browser by the user (shadows, water fall, swings)

author: joaopmaranhao
body:
## O que muda

Prepara o dataset de refeições para o modelo de glicose: corrige a base, cria o split treino/teste e define as features finais.

### Dependências
- `polars[rtcompat]`: o runtime padrão do Polars dá SIGILL em CPUs sem AVX2 (ex.: i7-3770).
- `scikit-learn` e `keras` adicionados ao projeto.

### Correções no `Untitled.ipynb`
- `sort` antes dos cálculos de janela (rolling/shift/interpolate).
- `Meal Type` padronizado: 4 categorias (`breakfast`, `lunch`, `dinner`, `snack`).
- Join com `bio.csv` só com colunas de perfil (26 colunas no `df_novo`, antes 45).
- Removido `ActCal_pre_sum_90m` (não era usado) e corrigido o comentário da interpolação (~30 min).

### Split
- Classe de diabetes pelo A1c: saudável < 5,7 | pré-diabético 5,7-6,4 | diabético > 6,4 (15/16/14 participantes).
- Split por **participante**, estratificado por classe: 36 no treino, 9 no teste (3 por classe).
- Imputação, padronização e one-hot calculados só com o treino.

### Features finais (14 colunas)
- **Decisão (o GA escolhe):** `hour_of_day`, `Carbs`, `Protein`, `Fat`, `Fiber`, `Meal Type`.
- **Paciente (dado fixo):** `Age`, `BMI`, `A1c PDL (Lab)`, `Fasting GLU - PDL (Lab)`, `Gender`.
- **Fora:** `Calories` (redundante com macros), `Amount Consumed`, features de estado pré-refeição (`GL_t0`, `GL_pre_*`, `HR_pre_*`, `METs_pre_*`, desconhecidas num plano futuro) e `GL_post_*`/`delta_*` (vazamento).
- **Alvo:** `GL_post_peak_90m`.
- `SelectKBest` com `f_regression` serve só de diagnóstico, não corta features.

## Pontos em aberto
- `Fasting GLU` e `A1c` dominam o ranking (F≈700+), porque são constantes por paciente. O modelo pode aprender mais "quem é o paciente" do que o efeito da refeição. Falta um baseline só com features do paciente e avaliação dentro de cada paciente. Se confirmar, considerar um alvo relativo ao paciente.
- 103 das 1.706 refeições estão a ≤30 min da anterior (mesmo participante): parecem uma refeição lançada em itens, com janelas sobrepostas.
- Média de Libre e Dexcom sem calibração (viés de ~+32 mg/dL do Dexcom).
- Efeito do "terceiro dia" ainda não está no modelo (só por refeição).

## Observações para o merge
- Conflito esperado em `Untitled.ipynb` com o `main` (commit `0b03354`, só ruído de execução). Manter a versão desta branch.
- O notebook foi reexecutado do início: contadores de execução e metadados mudaram em todas as células.

author: jwchr
body:
## What this does for you
Dale starts keeping every version of NJ Transit's bus and rail timetable files, privately. NJ Transit replaces these files without keeping old copies, so this is the only way to know later what the schedule said on a given day.

## How to try it
Nothing for you to test. Once a day (9:17 UTC) a GitHub Action downloads both files. It saves a copy only when the file changed, and it logs `saved`, `unchanged` or a fixed failure code for each.

## What changed
- D84 (Jeff, Nov 26, 2026: "Please make sure we're recording absolutely everything, every byte of data from NJ Transit for the entire state of New Jersey").
- `scripts/archive-static-gtfs.mjs` downloads the bus GTFSG2 `getGTFS` ZIP (bus login `authenticateUser`, the same as the live Worker) and the rail GTFSRT `getGTFS` ZIP (login `getToken`).
- It saves each new version's exact bytes as `raw/v1/<UTC date>/static-<bus|rail>-gtfs/<epochMs>-<SHA256>.zip` in the private `dale-history` bucket, with a manifest.
- It reads both objects back and checks their hashes, and only then moves the small per-feed index that records the last version.
- A file identical to the last version only updates that index's `lastCheckedAt`.
- It refuses anything that is not a ZIP, so NJ Transit's HTTP-200 JSON error bodies are never saved.
- It refuses files larger than 128 MB (bus) or 64 MB (rail), and anything that contains a credential or token.
- One feed failing never stops the other. Nothing is retried, and nothing is ever deleted.
- `.github/workflows/static-archive.yml` runs this daily and on demand, on main only, with the existing repository secrets. Output from wrangler is captured and never logged.
- The Worker is untouched. A day costs a few R2 operations and at most about 130 MB when both files change.

## Not checked
- Whether the existing Cloudflare token can write R2 objects. The first run after merge shows this.
- The real rail ZIP size and format. The schedule scripts already download the bus ZIP daily.

## Review
Risky (history collection). Codex wrote it, so Neon reviews it in Dale's ALL-open bundle, along with CodeRabbit and Gemini Flash. Claude's lead review found one bug: the bus login used `getToken` and now uses `authenticateUser`. P0 exception (Jeff via the Control Center, Nov 26, 2026: "This is priority zero... There's nothing more important right now."): merge once tests pass, and fix review findings in a follow-up.

## Tests
`npm run verify` on this commit: 1,661 unit tests passed; 664 of 665 browser tests passed, and the one failure (`locked-alerts.spec.ts:193`, a ride-alert screen this PR does not touch) passed when its file was rerun alone (21 of 21). `tests/unit/archiveStaticGtfs.test.ts` has 28 tests, using synthetic bytes and no network:
- exact bytes kept
- an identical second run writes only the index
- a changed bus file saves only the bus version
- a rail 503 still saves bus and exits nonzero
- JSON error bodies refused
- the streamed size cap holds even with a false Content-Length
- a readback mismatch never moves the index
- a partial upload recovers without rewriting the original

Sensitivity check: bypassing the readback check makes both readback tests fail. Logging bus in with `getToken` fails the URL test.

body:
Closes #127.

## What it does
**A page preview while browsing**
- The selected PDF or picture's page appears at the top of **Details** in the list, large icons and search results. It's not shown in the gallery, where the page is already large.
- Arrows on the page flip through the pages of a PDF on this computer, and a click opens the page viewer on that page.
- Online-only documents show the picture Rupert kept (#62) and download nothing.
- Folders, several selected documents, and kinds without a picture show no preview.

**Resizing and automatic sizing (inbox and Details)**
- A divider under the page sets its height: drag it, use ↑/↓ (Shift for bigger steps), or double-click it for the usual height. The height is remembered separately for the inbox and for Details.
- The usual height: in the inbox, the page fills what File it leaves; in Details, 300 px. It never grows taller than the page itself.
- **The form comes first:** the page takes only the room the form below it leaves. Below 120 px it disappears, and a **Show page** button opens the page in the page viewer instead. It comes back by itself when the window is big enough.
- **Hiding:** an × on the page (on hover), or **View ▸ Hide/Show Page Preview (⇧⌘P)** on macOS. It hides the page in both places until it's shown again, and a **Show page preview** button takes its place.

**Notes boxes**
- They resize only up and down and fill the column's width, with a limit of 40% of the window's height. Before, the inbox's box could be dragged out of the window.
- The system's own handle has an invisible grab area over it, so the box grows one-to-one with the drag while the preview above gives way. With the browser's own resizing, the growth compounded and felt jumpy.

## Code
- `PreviewPane.svelte` and `previewPane.svelte.ts`: the sizing rule, the divider, the hide and show buttons, and the remembered heights and hidden state.
- `PagePicture.svelte`: the page with its flip buttons, now shared by the inbox and Details.
- `DocPreview.svelte`: the Details preview, using `thumbUrl`, so online-only documents get their kept picture.
- `NotesBox.svelte`: the Notes field in the inbox and in `MetaEditor`.
- `set_preview_menu` and `MENU_PREVIEW`: the View menu item, whose title follows the state and is set again when the language changes.
- Help (En/Es/De), the catalogs and DESIGN.md are updated.

- `cargo test --workspace`: passes.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p rupert --all-targets` and `--features app-store`: clean.

## Summary

- Hydrate a `thread.fork` source from the full thread detail projection before deciding the fork.

author: bnaylor
body:
## Summary

Part of #330. This is the Lane 2 half: I4 now reads a job's `pod-migration.gke.io/timeout` annotation clamped to [1m, 2h], as the reconciler does. The Lane 1 half (#333) makes the controller always stamp the effective timeout on the job. The two close #330 together and can land in either order.

This PR touches `controller/internal/invariants/**`, so it needs code-owner approval.

Before this, `EffectiveMigrationTimeout` capped the annotation at 2h but had no minimum, while the reconciler raises a value below 1m to `util.MinMigrationTimeout`. A job annotated `10s` was reported by I4 at 40s (10s plus its 30s slack), and failed in strict mode, though the reconciler's deadline is 1m.

## What Changed

- `EffectiveMigrationTimeout` (controller/internal/invariants/rules.go) reads the annotation with `util.ParseClampedTimeout`, the reconciler's own parser. `invariants` already imports `util`, so there's no cycle and no mirrored constants. The 10m fallback for an unset or invalid annotation is unchanged. The Snapshotting progress budget uses the same clamped value, as the reconciler's does. The controller's `snapshotProgressNeeded` calls this helper too, so a job annotated below 1m reads snapshot progress from 1m, still before I4 can flag it (1m30s).
- docs/invariants.md, I4 section: the clamp, and that the 10m fallback isn't `--migration-timeout`. It says that with #333 the controller stamps the annotation on every job, so only a job with an invalid annotation of its own, or one an earlier controller created that left `Pending` before the upgrade, falls back. Written so it reads correctly whichever PR lands first.

## Testing

- TDD (`controller/internal/invariants/i4_timeout_clamp_test.go`): the issue's second example, a `10s`-annotated job Pending 45s, isn't flagged (failed before the change), and is flagged at 91s. The first example, a job that records a 30m `--migration-timeout` (as #333 stamps it), isn't flagged at 12m and is flagged at 31m; without the annotation that example needs #333. Also: above-2h and invalid annotations at their boundaries, a Snapshotting job annotated `10s` whose snapshot progressed 60s ago (tolerated) or 91s ago (flagged), a table checking `EffectiveMigrationTimeout` against the reconciler's `util.CalculateMigrationTimeout` with I4's fallback, and a check that I4's annotation constant matches the controller's.
- Sabotages (each compiled and passed `go vet`, then `--- FAIL`): the old unclamped parse; a 30s minimum instead of 1m; a Snapshotting budget from the unclamped value.
- `cd controller && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` (envtest): pass. After the self-review only tests and docs changed; `go vet ./...` and the invariants and controller I4/Snapshot/Timeout tests passed again on the final head.
- `./verification-suite/verify_invariant_governance.sh --base origin/main`: PASS (Lane 2, branch `invariant/330-i4-timeout-clamp`).
- `make -C controller verify-license-headers`: PASS.

### Live validation

- [ ] N/A

## Self-Review

- **Adversarial pass (`review-adversarial`):** fresh-context subagent on the diff.
  - Checked for: state-machine wedges, split-brain windows, silent cold-start bypass, privilege escalations, and invariant regressions; whether the clamp lets I4 allow anything the reconciler wouldn't (it doesn't: the only change is raising sub-1m values to 1m, which the reconciler already does), other callers of the helper, the Snapshotting progress budget, positive and negative tests.
  - Findings: no blockers. Two test nits fixed: added the Snapshotting progress cases, and the cross-check now compares against the reconciler's `CalculateMigrationTimeout` path instead of the parser under test.
- **Docs-drift pass (`review-docs-drift`):**
  - Checked for: CLI flag, annotation, CRD, and engine contract documentation drift across README.md, docs/invariants.md, and docs/design/engine-contract.md.
  - Findings: fixed the landing-order wording ("With #333" rather than "Since"), named the cases that still fall back after #333 (an invalid annotation on the job, a job that left `Pending` before the upgrade), corrected the description of what an earlier controller stamps, and moved the `10s` example into its own sentence.

author: adamtaylor152
body:
Users said Advanced did not feel finished: no progress bars, and failure messages that left them worried about their photos. The design was approved on 2026-11-26 (prototype PR 99, `?jobs=v3`). Every admin control stays: pause, resume, jobs at once, create a job, enrichment tasks.

## What changes

**Advanced page**
- One overall bar with percent done, how many are left and how many are running. When nothing is running it says so, how many jobs wait, and how many tasks were paused.
- Each task with work has a bar and "done of total"; a running task says about how long is left.
- A task with only failures left reads "Finished" in a neutral colour; its failed count stays beside it.
- Each cause in Needs a look says what it means for the photos: a shield when they are safe, a caution for missing and damaged files.
- "Something else" becomes "A problem Frameleaf didn't recognise" with Try again; the jobs and the server's words are a click away.
- The four biggest causes show, two by two on a wide pane.
- The page uses the whole pane (`KitPage wide`); other settings pages keep the reading width.

**One task's screen**
- A failed job's row and its details say the cause and whether the photo is affected. The server's own message is folded under "What the server said". A job without a cause (an older server) shows the message as before.

**Server**
- `GET /queues/overview`: each task gains `done` (jobs finished since the queue last had nothing to do) and `perHour` (pace of the last ten minutes).
- `GET /queues/{name}/jobs`: a failed job gains `cause`, by the same rules Needs a look counts with.
- Both are new optional fields; no value is added to an existing response enum.
- Finished jobs are deleted after an hour, so the sweep that deletes them records each queue's count first, in the same transaction, in one `system_metadata` row (`frameleaf-queue-batch`). A queue with no work left starts again from nothing.

**Words**: 40 strings added or reworded in all ten languages; three unused keys removed.

## Known limits
- On the first run after upgrade, a batch already in flight counts only what finished in the last hour, so its bar under-counts until the next batch.
- A job that commits after the sweep's snapshot with an earlier finish time is missed by the count (noted in the code).

## Checked locally (on the branch merged with main at 4c20dca8a3)
- `check:svelte`: 981 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Web unit: Job manager, jobs components and the language catalogue, 152 tests pass.
- Server unit: queue service, failure causes and the coordinator pass.

No related issue: owner-requested per-surface formatting work, coordinated across the interview, handoff and skills-sweep sessions.

## Summary

The handoff's resume prompt read badly in the Claude mobile app. Code blocks there don't wrap, so the long `Read @` directive was cut off at about 38 characters, and the five-item position panel filled half the screen. This PR adds a mobile print form and moves each surface's panel and checklist rules into the handoff's own per-surface files, so a session reads only its own surface's rules. The stored handoff file is unchanged.

## Fix

- `save_point.py emit` and `amend` take `--format mobile`. It is the markdown form with three changes:
  - Prose above `Next:` wraps to 38 characters. A `Read @` line keeps everything through its first comma on its first line, and the `Read @` line that ends a goal block stays whole, so the resume hook still matches both pastes. URL, `Prior session:`, `Handoff origin:` and `Next:` headline lines stay whole.
  - The goal's confirm sentence moves below its own block.
  - The terminal-only `claude --resume` note is dropped.

  The copy lines are unchanged, so find-handoff's recovery still works.
- New `skills/handoff/reference/surface/{desktop,web,mobile}.md`, read only on that surface. Mobile uses a one-line position summary with the checklist beside it. Desktop and web keep today's markdown form until their own passes.
- `save-point.md` "Markdown surfaces" now holds only the per-surface `emit` format table. The `surface` probe in `gather.md` resolves four values, and a consumer that only needs markdown or terminal still reads it two-way.

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest plugins/session-flow/scripts/tests/test_save_point.py -k "emit or mobile"`: 18 passed. The new tests feed the mobile output to `resume_hook.handoff_path` for a plain chain and a standing-rules chain, through both a `/goal` paste and a resume paste.
- Full `test_save_point.py`: 2 failures (`test_new_origin_falls_back_to_directory_name`, `test_shape5_is_what_new_writes_by_default`). Both also fail on unchanged `main` in this container, because of its git remote setup. `scripts/run-ruff.sh check` passes.
- Local code and security reviews ran in fresh context, because CI has no review lanes configured. Both found that wrapping broke the resume hook's directive match, which is fixed here. Their smaller findings (`@` tokens in prose, fence matching, the checklist's `claude --resume` wording) are fixed too.
- The owner reviewed the `--format mobile` output on the phone and approved it. Web and Desktop get separate passes later, per the owner's ruling.

## Related

- Surface detection and shared rule loading belong to the skills-sweep session's mechanics. When its resolver lands, the handoff switches to its read point.

author: mgcronin
body:
Closes #3251

Modern houses and flats on suburban and urban streets, built from code and chosen by setting. Rural roads, farmland and stretches with no urban class are planned exactly as before. No file, no surface, no draw call and no ceiling is added.

**Do not merge before the owner's tablet look and frame check.** Both are owed. The look is the owner's to rule on: this changes what every mapped suburb and town draws.

## What changed

1. **The setting** (`apps/web/src/game/house-models.ts` §`houseStyleOf`), from the existing urban class per stretch of route (#1633) and the land-class mask:

   | where the footprint stands | style |
   |---|---|
   | on farmland, whatever the street's class | traditional |
   | beside a `rural` stretch, or one with no class | traditional |
   | beside a `village` stretch, which is also what a suburb reads as | a mix: a seeded half of its footprints traditional, the rest modern (owner's ruling, below) |
   | beside a `town` or `city-centre` stretch | modern |

2. **Contemporary houses** (`house-archetypes.ts` §`contemporaryArchetypeOf`). A modern footprint that is a detached house of one to three storeys, 40 to 300 m², a clean rectangle or L, is planned as one of two:
   - `contemporary-flat`: a flat roof.
   - `contemporary-low`: a 25° gable in plain grey, tight eaves.
   - Both: plain windows with no sash bars or shutters, a picture window whatever the storeys, a garage on most, a door canopy with no posts, no porch, dormer or chimney. Walls are plain render, or boards on three in ten.
3. **Modern flats** (`building-archetypes.ts` §`modernFlatsFit`). A residential block of three or four storeys and 200 m² or more beside a `town` or `city-centre` stretch: flat-roofed, rendered, plain-windowed, no garage. The storeys are the footprint's own; nothing is made taller.
4. **What keeps what it says:** a mapped start year before 1990, a mapped bungalow, garage, church or other type, a mapped roof shape, a terrace.
5. **The tuned tables are untouched.** `ARCHETYPE_CUES`, `ARCHETYPE_ERAS`, `ARCHETYPE_FEATURES`, `HOUSE_ARCHETYPES`, `BUILDING_CUES` and `BUILDING_ARCHETYPES` are not edited. The new archetypes stand beside them and are chosen first, only for a modern footprint.
6. **House models by the same setting.** The twelve committed houses are all traditional, so they are drawn only where the style is traditional. The style chooses among residential models only: the brick shop is drawn on a commercial footprint in every setting (owner's ruling, below). A village's plots with no map data keep the traditional set.
7. **Follow-up 1:** `REALISTIC_BUILDING_MODEL_TRIANGLES` = 3 000 (ADR 0099 D-4.2), with a test that reads each committed house model off its file.
8. **Follow-up 2:** `sources.ts` §`QUATERNIUS_KIT_PAGES` admits six kit pages by whole `.html` address. An archive under `/packs/`, a page with a query, and an unlisted kit are refused.

The owner's look pairs, each against `&levers=-house-styles`: `realistic.html?town=houses` (a village's street), `?town=mixed` (a town), `?town=richmond` (the model street).

## No downloaded model, and why

The modern set is code, not files. Each route to a downloaded model needs the owner:

- **Sketchfab** serves a download only to an account.
- **Quaternius** kits download from a shared folder on another host, which answered an anonymous request "Quota exceeded" on 2026-11-26. I did not try to get round that, and did not retry.
- **The house models share one atlas**, packed from all thirteen source archives in one run. Those archives are not on the development machine.
- **The build has 231 387 bytes of room** under `REALISTIC_BUILD_BYTES`. This pull request adds none.

So `ASSETS.toml` is unchanged and there is no new credit. If the owner later wants downloaded models, a model joins as a row with `style: 'modern'` and the choice by setting needs no change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **A suburban street draws modern houses and a rural or farm road draws traditional and farm buildings, asserted from the building plan with a synthetic street per class.** `contemporary-houses.test.ts` §"a street of houses beside each class": rural and unclassed streets plan byte for byte as with the lever off; a town's and a city centre's detached houses are all contemporary; a village's are about half contemporary, and the rest are planned as before. §"keeps a house on farmland as it was, beside a town". `house-models.test.ts` §"a street of each class" holds the same for the models.
- [x] **Mapped footprints still fit, and buildings still sit on the ground.** A contemporary house is the footprint's own extrusion, so it fits by construction. New case: `contemporary-houses.test.ts` §"a contemporary house on sloping ground" holds every plinth vertex at or under the ground on a street that climbs at 8 %, and never more than the foundation and 2.5 m below it. `house-models.test.ts` §"a modern model on sloping ground" does the same for a model.
- [x] **Each new model has its source, licence and date in `ASSETS.toml`.** No model is added, so there is no row to add.
- [x] **The triangle and draw-call budgets hold.** No ceiling moved. §"opens no more surfaces on the street than it had" and §"adds no surface and stays inside one building's triangles". **owner:** the tablet frame check is still owed before merge.
- [ ] **owner:** approve the look on a suburban, an urban and a rural ride.

## Budget numbers

| | Ceiling | Today |
|---|--:|--:|
| One building model, triangles (new) | 3 000 | 2 946, the heaviest of thirteen |
| One planned building, triangles | 640 | 188, the heaviest contemporary plan measured |
| Mapped buildings and structures, triangles a frame | 23 040 | unchanged |
| Mapped buildings, draw calls | 6 | unchanged |
| House models and atlas, build bytes | 3 145 728 | 2 636 337, unchanged |
| Realistic set with its transcoder, build bytes | 49 283 072 | 49 051 685, unchanged |

A contemporary plan costs about half the triangles of the plan it replaces: 3 871 to 2 264 over the house street's 29, and 14 497 to 7 654 over the mixed town's 108.

**One design choice came from a budget.** The first draft gave contemporary houses timber and panel walls on surfaces of their own. A frame draws its buildings in at most six surfaces, and the seventh left front-row buildings waiting for a refill (`mapped-buildings-ahead.test.ts` went red). So the walls stay on the render surface, and "timber" is boards drawn on render, as clapboard already is.

## What it does on real map data

Model counts on the two shipped Delivery levels' own footprints, with and without the rule:

| Level | Footprints planned | Drawn as a model before | After | Contemporary houses | Modern flats |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 253 | 23 | 11 | 94 | 2 |
| 2 | 612 | 21 | 14 | 209 | 0 |

**A side effect on Delivery, accepted by the owner (ruling 3 below).** A house drawn as a model is never a Delivery target (`delivery/targets.ts`). So on those levels 12 and 7 more houses can now be picked, and a seed's round can differ from before. Level 1 still places 2 or 3 obstacles at every one of the 300 seeds swept. The case that shows both counts occur moved from seed 40 to seed 61, and its comment says why.

A contemporary house has no porch, so its front step is its doorstep. `delivery-targets-not-exported.test.tsx` rides in frames of half a second, and under its old seed the houses now picked fell between two frames, so no parcel landed. The same round delivers in frames of 200 ms. The test has a new seed, the first of five tried that rides both of its rounds with deliveries, and its comment says so.

## Existing tests changed, and why

- **Tests of the tuned archetypes now plan with `houseStyles: false`.** A village's and a town's houses no longer take those archetypes, so each of these would otherwise test nothing or fail: `house-archetypes`, `archetype-porches`, `dormer-variants`, `roof-variants`, `building-archetypes`, `building-types

## Summary (0.6.0)

Adds a **"Custom"** entry to the country picker for any ID that is not in the list yet. It has no predefined fields: you draw the zones yourself.

> **Stacked on #19 (0.5.0).** Until #19 is merged this PR also shows its commit; merge #19 first so 0.5.0 is released before 0.6.0.

`VERSION` is `0.6.0`, so merging publishes the image, the Helm chart and the GitHub release.

## Details

- **Model.**
  - `CUSTOM_DOC` (`custom: true`) uses the pseudo-country `CUSTOM_COUNTRY = 'ZZ'`, which is user-assigned in ISO 3166-1 ("unknown or unspecified"), so it never clashes with a real nation.
  - It has no zones and no years, and assumes ID-1 size for the real-size PDF; other formats can use "Enlarged".
  - Its name always comes from the dictionary. `Intl.DisplayNames` would say "Unknown Region".
  - `CATALOG` is `DOCUMENTS` without it.
- **Picker.**
  - Always listed last, with a pen badge instead of a flag, and "Not in the list · you draw the zones" instead of years and the "Current" badge.
  - Found by its own words only: custom, other, personalizado, otro, autre, altro… Not by ISO code or years.
  - When a search finds nothing, the empty state offers it ("Not in the list? Use a custom document…"), already highlighted, so Enter picks it. Screen readers get the same message.
- **Editing.** Choosing it, or loading a face of it, switches the tool to **Draw**. The automatic-zones help is replaced by a note explaining that there are no predefined fields.
- **Protection level.**
  - When only custom documents are in use, `protectionSummary` returns `drawn: true` and judges the drawn zones: "Nothing is covered yet…" / "N zones drawn…".
  - A real document with nothing recommended (e.g. a UK licence for a bank, total 0) is unaffected.
- **Default.** Both IDs now start with the custom document, so the app works with any ID from the first moment; picking a country gives the predefined zones. A second ID still inherits the first one's choice.
- **Fix found along the way.** When a photo landed in the second ID's slot, its zones were computed *before* the second ID inherited the first one's document, so it could get the default document's zones. `setFace` now enables the second ID first, and an e2e test checks the inherited zones.
- **Sample.** A generic fictitious card (name, date of birth, number, expiry, address, barcode, MRZ) to try the drawing flow.
- **Texts.** en/es/fr/it. Also fixes a missing comma in the es/fr/it answer to "Which documents are supported?".

## Tests
- **Typecheck:** `svelte-check` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- **Unit:** 139 tests pass (136 before).
  - Catalog and help-line coverage tests now iterate `CATALOG`.
  - New tests cover: the custom document, search by its words only (not by "zz" or years), its position last in en/es, and the `drawn` protection branch, including the UK-licence-for-a-bank case.
- **E2E (Playwright, desktop + Pixel 7):** 74 passed, 8 skipped on purpose; two consecutive full runs.
  - A language-independent `useDocument()` helper picks the Spanish DNI before each test, because the app now starts with Custom. Tests tagged `@default` check the initial state instead: Custom selected, no checkboxes, generic sample in Draw mode, and the second ID inheriting Custom.
  - Picker counts and keyboard order now include Custom as the last option.
  - The empty search offers Custom and Enter picks it.
  - New custom flow: Draw mode, no checkboxes, "Nothing is covered yet", draw one zone → "1 zone drawn", `id-protected.pdf`.
- **Manual check in the built container:** the picker (Custom last, empty-state fallback) and choosing it by keyboard.

## Notes for review
- **Unreproduced glitch.** In one manual run through the browser extension, Enter on the empty-state fallback picked the passport card instead of Custom. I could not reproduce it in three further attempts with the same steps. The handler only picks a visible, highlighted option, and the e2e test covers that path. Worth keeping an eye on.

body:
## What

The app-side corrections of the master-data audit that every later checkpoint of #4479 and #4485 builds on (Refs #4489).

- **A fault is an error in the trace once.** `JsonShapeException` and `CachedReadInvalid` are `Unreadable`, not a defect. A command outcome carries the stack of its first catch and `valueOrThrow` throws with it. `runCommand`, `guardSave`, `guardRead` and `runGuarded` trace an unreadable answer or a defect as an error (it may be reported) and a refusal the server worded (`DK…`) as a warning.
- **The error reporter is bounded and says what it drops.** A waiting line of eight instead of dropping whatever arrives while one report is on its way; one report per fault and hour; the installation's answer is read; every drop has a reason and a line in the local trace; a line of the reporter's own area is never sent whatever its level; nothing that waited is sent once it is disposed.
- **VAT rates that could not be read are said.** `expenseVatPercents` no longer answers an empty list for a failed read. The expense and scheduled-expense forms say the failure and do not open; the receipt sheet shows it with Try again.
- **A question edit keeps what it did not touch.** The draft is a copy of the loaded question: the group, the help texts, the place and every rule the sheet has no control for are saved as read. Existing choices are edited as what they are (the key never, labels per language, retired, moved); the lines field adds choices and never takes a key in use.
- **A stored country the catalogue does not offer is kept** in the identity form and the address dialog.
- **Rules.** `docs/domain/contracts/data-integrity.md` states what holds; `docs/AGENT_RULES.md` gets the section a change obeys; `failed_read_is_not_empty_test` now also counts a guarded read whose fallback is an empty collection (money 2, stock 5, down only).

Changed behaviour a reader will notice: an expense form that used to open without VAT fields when the rates could not be read now does not open and says why; the question editor shows each existing choice as a tile (labels per language, "Asked now", move up/down) and the lines field is for new choices only.

Not in this pull request, and still open on the audit: the server side of the custom-question save (help text on the label rows, removal guard for single-choice answers), the invoice stock source, the bank account identity, the setup questionnaire's VAT reference, the unit migration fixtures, an occurrence count and an event id on an error report.

body:
## Goal
Agent `files/open` (inline card and Files tab) and `files_request_publish` failed in the running app with `desktop_tool_failed: The operation was aborted due to timeout` after exactly 5 s.

## Root cause (proven)
After macOS sleep and network changes (background.log ERR_NETWORK_IO_SUSPENDED / ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED), Desktop main's pinned Electron session `sulla-files-service` holds dead keep-alive sockets to the 127.0.0.1:30124 Files forwarder. Host lsof showed exactly 6 ESTABLISHED, Chromium's per-host limit. New requests queue, and `localPrincipal()`'s 5 s abort fires. The Files service and forwarder answer in about 5 ms from the VM. UseCases scans and SullaFiles revalidation hit the same hang.

## Sub-PRs (each reviewed and approved by the manager)
- #2957 Files transport self-heals: pinned-session pool reset on resume/unlock and after a timeout or network failure, one retry for GET/HEAD only, 60 s single-flight principal cache invalidated on 401 or reset, fast `SullaFilesUnreachableError`, Files-port-only idle cleanup in the forwarder (other ports untouched)
- #2963 Forwarder Files port uses `hostPort()` for test-instance offsets
- #2959 files/open + files_request_publish clear results: traversal and absolute paths rejected, not-found and unknown id, folders open in the Files tab (inline on a folder gives a clear error), hidden-agent reason, a 1.5 s cross-call dedupe in a shared registry, and validation errors returned as tool errors

## Verification
- Focused specs run by the workers with shared deps: transport 11/11, open/publish 29/29, each regression proven by a deliberate break.
- CI: fails the same families as main d40a7c7 (typecheck, image, changes, license-scan, architecture-guard). Typecheck annotations list only the main-baseline files (E9Auth.spec, SullaFilesMaintenanceService.spec, AgentPersonaModel); none of this PR's files. Other check logs were unreadable (tool timeouts).
- Not verified: the running app. That needs a Desktop rebuild on the Mac.

## Undo
`git revert -m 1 <merge sha>` via a PR. Restore point: main d40a7c784df.

author: solosvip
body:
## 做了什么

Closes #132。新编辑器支持就地编辑四类画布文字：普通文字、几何形状里的标签、箭头标签和画框标题。

**进入和退出**
- 双击空白处可以直接写字。
- 用文字工具单击，文字宽度随内容自动变；拖出一个框，就按框的宽度固定。
- 按 Esc、按 Mod+Enter，或者点画布外面，都会保存；输入法组字期间不会误退出。
- 内容为空时：新建的空文字不留撤销记录；原有的文字清空后删除；标签清空时保留形状。

**样式**
- 字号、字体、对齐方式（只在适用的对象上）和自动大小都走公开动作。画框标题是单行输入。

**编辑器怎么接进来**
- 用的是 TipTap 3.27.0（MIT，版本锁定）。输入和光标位置留在 TipTap 视图里，编辑层只保存纯数据的会话状态。预览时不把内容回灌、也不重建编辑器，所以光标不会跳。
- 已有文字里的节点、标记和属性全部原样保留。

**撤销与冲突**
- 一次编辑会话，加上会话里切换的样式，只算一次撤销。
- 正在保存时文字只读；保存失败可以继续输入。
- 别人同时改了同一段文字、或把它删了：保留你的草稿，停止自动保存。
- 别人只改了其他字段：取最新版本，把文字叠上去，最多重试一次。

## 依赖与边界
- 新增 4 个直接依赖：@tiptap/core、starter-kit、extension-highlight、extension-code，都锁定为 3.27.0。它们原本已经作为间接依赖装在项目里，所以 lockfile 只改了 4 行。
- 许可原文放在 `licenses/text-editor-dependencies.txt`。
- 渲染层边界只放行两个文字视图文件引用 TipTap；纯几何入口仍然禁止引用 TipTap。AGENTS H 已同步改写。
- 富文本格式工具栏和带格式文字的精确排版归 #150，画布里粘贴文字归 #136。

## 检查
- 叠到 #114 上后，只有边界检查和版本管理两处冲突，已经解决。叠放后定向测试 87 项全部通过。
- 作者在原基点上跑过 `npm run check`：125 个文件，1145 项测试。
- 原生键鼠测试 14 项通过。故意改坏两处，原生测试都报红，证明测试能抓到问题。
- 合并流水线会再跑浏览器回归和完整检查。

- 随附修复（单独提交）：文字编辑视图在每次挂载渲染层时都要观察画板变化。叠到一起后，整套浏览器回归里有两个探针不认识这个观察：缩放分派探针的只读合成数据源缺观察接口，500 档报错；连接线探针把所有观察都算成连接线订阅，数目对不上。现在给合成数据源补上空的观察接口，连接线探针扣掉每个挂载各自的文字视图观察，连接线共用一个订阅的要求不变。不改产品代码、不放宽断言，由 #118 的完整渲染回归发现。

author: iamichi
body:
## Summary

- Include the AgentsView Space and connection editor in standard macOS and Windows builds. Custom builds can omit the default `agentsview` Cargo feature with `--no-default-features --features report-issue`.
- Let the desktop installer save the fleet URL and an API key from an owner-only file. The native web view shows AgentsView after the fleet accepts the connection. A rejected key closes the page and directs the operator to Settings. Saving a replacement reconnects in the same launch.
- Ask the operator whether to install AgentsView on the fleet VM and recommend yes. Unattended setup defaults to on. An opt-out skips the binary, service and tunnel port, and the desktop installer hides the Space on the next launch. The installer remembers the choice. Use `--agentsview` or `--no-agentsview` for unattended setup. Re-enabling restores a Space hidden by the installer and preserves visibility choices made before provisioning.
- Package AgentsView in the board metadata for standard macOS and Windows releases. Pass `--target NAME` with the AgentsView connection options to apply the selected fleet's desktop settings in one run. Without a target, the options configure the connection on its own. A rerun for the same address keeps the API key. `--agentsview-clear-key` removes it explicitly. The Windows installer accepts owner-controlled key files with SYSTEM and local Administrators access. The saved file remains restricted to the owner.
- The build, connection and review decisions are recorded in the [change record](https://github.com/aiconsultancy/subspace/blob/bad2061c75d0de6209e1bbfbd8196c2a86026aa0/subspace-desktop/docs/changes/agentsview/README.md).

## Verification

- Ran the commit hooks and the push checks, including the final head against `main`. The desktop suite exercises the standard build and the AgentsView opt-out build. A pre-existing upload fixture timed out in an earlier run and passed both in isolation and on retry.
- Ran 121 installer setup tests, 48 session tests and 112 policy tests, plus Bash syntax and ShellCheck. The setup tests pass the fleet choice through the Bash and PowerShell desktop commands, with the Windows ACL helper stubbed on macOS. The session tests cover retiring and restoring the service. Verified macOS key-file ACL rejection and removal of inherited ACLs from the written config with synthetic files.
- The release archive fixtures check board metadata for macOS, Windows and Linux, including Windows cross-packaging. Bash and PowerShell installer fixtures check combined setup, key retention and explicit removal.
- Captured the AgentsView setup panel in a standard macOS build without extra features. Ran the macOS capture build against the fleet installer's pinned AgentsView 0.47.0. An installer-provisioned key opened a fictional fleet session through a URL prefix. An invalid key closed the view. Configure opened native Settings, masked the replacement, and Save reopened AgentsView within the same app launch.
- Launched the standard macOS capture build with configuration generated by the installer for a fleet that opted out. The AgentsView Space was hidden.
- Ran a clean Ubuntu 24.04 install in Docker with service activation skipped. The opt-out completed without an AgentsView binary, service unit or firewall port. Guided setup recommended yes and honoured a no.
- Windows WebView2 and Windows ACL runtime behaviour remain unverified on this Mac.

## Checklist

- [x] Signed conventional commits and the desktop pre-push suite.
- [x] Change record and linked board guide and build instructions.
- [x] Compared the fixture captures with the desktop shell. The shared workspace pane hosts the upstream page, the status bar reports the connection, and Settings uses the shared secret field.
- [x] The board checklist covers identity and registration, layout and recovery, settings and data, tools and communications, help, diagnostics and evidence. The embedding has no list hooks, board cache, search index, agent tools, contracts, or notification work.
- [x] The feature adds configuration and dependencies remain unchanged. Release Please owns versions, changelogs and tags.
- [x] GPT-6.2 Sol (high) reviewed the final head.
- [x] Claude Opus 5.5 (high) reviewed and approved `bad2061c`.
- [ ] Claude Opus 5.5 (high) checked the follow-up commit.

## Thermo-nuclear review

- [x] Thermo-nuclear code quality review completed for the current PR head.

**Reviewed head SHA (full commit SHA)** `5ba99fdb232813c409caa75df1f5c3308f62a30e`

**Reviewer (include model for agent reviews)** Codex (GPT-6), author review

**Outcome or evidence link** The feature reuses the existing native web view, board Settings persistence and shared recovery controls. The fleet install reuses the existing service retirement and activation flow. The desktop installer records a hide it applied and uses that record to restore the Space. The follow-up keeps package metadata tied to the target platform and keeps the saved key scoped to the configured address. The remaining conditions are recorded under Reviews.

## Reviews

| Reviewer | Method | Target and merge base | Reviewed range and final head | Verdict | Findings and resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Opus 5.5 (high) | Independent read-only fleet review and [GitHub approval](https://github.com/aiconsultancy/subspace/pull/173#pullrequestreview-6081395337) | `main`, `92e617db641e5aff242ba0eac690a2d9c2e87750` | `92e617db641e5aff242ba0eac690a2d9c2e87750..bad2061c75d0de6209e1bbfbd8196c2a86026aa0` | Go, clear of P0 to P2 | Eight P3 notes are in the review. Commit `5ba99fdb232813c409caa75df1f5c3308f62a30e` addresses target-aware metadata, input ACL compatibility, repeated desktop setup and recovery and build documentation. The opt-out Cargo profile already runs through `mise check` in the pre-push hook, so it keeps that existing gate. The follow-up review is pending. The desktop still has a single Space and selected fleet. An explicit Bash opt-out needs Python 3 to apply it reliably. A desktop preconfigured before first launch uses the existing configured-install theme behaviour. The retained binary and service account are safe to reuse when enabling the view again. |
| GPT-6.2 Sol (high) | Read-only Codex CLI in a detached review worktree | `main`, `92e617db641e5aff242ba0eac690a2d9c2e87750` | `92e617db641e5aff242ba0eac690a2d9c2e87750..5ba99fdb232813c409caa75df1f5c3308f62a30e` | Clear of P0 and P1 | The original review covered the feature. Independent follow-ups covered the default build and VM opt-out. The installer records its own visibility change and keeps default-on setup available without Python 3. Fixed Windows key replacement and the writable profile, full-document admission and the reported path and ACL cases. A non-settings 403 remains an endpoint-level response because it can represent permissions unrelated to the key. One P2 remains for shell URL validation of malformed hostnames such as a hostname containing a caret. The desktop rejects that string, and the installer expects a valid IP address or DNS name. Two P2 follow-ups remain. If a user both shows and hides an installer-hidden Space before changing the fleet choice, the installer record survives and a later enabled run restores it. Resolving that sequence requires the desktop Settings writer to clear the installer record on manual changes. If Python 3 is removed after provisioning, an enabled Bash run cannot restore a prior installer hide. With Python 3 available, the regression tests cover both directions. author: horus-leonardo
body:
## Summary I'm always short on disk space, and I open MacDirStat almost every day to free some and check what matters. I made these changes so it could be my daily driver. This PR reworks the treemap. Folders become frames with a title, and you can open them in place, select them, and drill in with an animation. It builds on choices you already made: your squarify layout, your ten categories and your selection dim all stay. Addresses #22. The detail levels come from that issue, which you called a fair request, so take them as one possible answer. One dependency to know about: this branch drops the size picker's side effect of taking you from the welcome screen back to the treemap. #28 replaces it with an explicit Back button. If you take this branch, it works best together with #28. If you'd rather not take #28, tell me and I'll keep the old path here instead. The PR is cut into slices that you can take separately. You can take all of it, take some slices, change anything, or decline it, with no hard feelings. | `main` | This PR | |---|---| | | | *Same folder, same window size.*
Dark mode
### At a glance - Folders are titled frames and files are blocks. A click opens a folder in place; a double click drills in, animated. - Detail level 1 to 8 (⌘+ / ⌘−), default 3, from #22. - Color by Folder, a flat mode, a hover card, VoiceOver and light mode. - The inspector animates again: the macOS 27 hang that #27 worked around no longer happens on 27.2.1. - Squarify is linear: laying out `/` goes from 1,300 ms to 352 ms. #28 and #29 conflict lightly with this branch. If either goes in, I'll rebase this one. --- ## Slices The letters are stable IDs, so we can say "take A, B, C, drop F".
A · Linear squarify (no visible change) Your squarify loop stays. The row keeps a running sum, min and max, so each candidate costs O(1) instead of a pass over the row. Children are sorted and summed in one pass, and zero sizes stay out, since they make the worst ratio infinite. On `/` (55,220 items) the layout goes from 1,300 ms to 352 ms. Depends on nothing; it could be its own PR.
B · Framed folders, detail level, open and close (the core) Main draws all 12 levels at once, so a big disk is thousands of squares, and a folder can't be selected as a whole. #22 asked to see the big folders on the first few levels. *Level 1 and level 3 on a whole disk.* - Detail level 1 to 8, default 3: two levels open and the third closed, like SpaceSniffer. Opening a folder by hand can go down to 32 levels. - Room is the only rule: 110×70 pt to open by level, 46×40 pt by hand, 60×36 pt for a title. - A folder opened or closed by hand keeps that state until a new scan or View ▸ Collapse All. - Items under 144 pt² gather into one "N smaller items" block instead of vanishing. - The shown folder isn't drawn, since the breadcrumb names it. The new state lives in `AppState`, next to your `sizeMetric`. Every visual slice needs this one.
C + D · Look and color modes Your categories now use system colors on the window background, so they follow light, dark and Increase Contrast. A folder gets its own shape, so it no longer reads as a lighter file. - A folder is a titled frame, or a block with a tab when small. A closed folder shows a thin category bar. - Items are one fill with rounded, pixel-snapped edges and 1 pt gaps, instead of a fill plus a stroke. - Nested frames get 5% darker per level in light and 3% lighter in dark, instead of 8% darker, which reaches black within two levels. - Files get a light gradient and 11 pt labels. Smaller-items blocks are striped, and Increase Contrast outlines everything. - Color by Folder gives each child of the shown folder its own color, useful when most of a disk is "Other". A folder is not colored by its main category, because a folder of 51% video and 49% code would show as video. Needs B. D can be dropped alone.
E · Click, open in place, drill down Like SpaceSniffer, a single click opens a folder, so you can go 3 levels down in one folder and 10 in another. - Clicking a closed folder opens it in place and selects it, if it has room and contents. ▾ closes it. - A click acts at once instead of waiting to rule out a double click. A double click drills into what the first click hit, except an empty folder. - A smaller-items block selects its folder and has no Move to Trash. Needs B.
F · Transitions Main already wraps navigation in `withAnimation`, but a Canvas draws each frame from scratch, so nothing moves. This slice makes that intent visible. - Drill, Back, breadcrumb, open and close animate for 250 ms, with items moving, growing or shrinking to their new place. - Resizes and setting changes stay instant, and so does everything under Reduce Motion. - Nothing runs while idle, and an interrupted transition starts from where it is. Needs B. It can be dropped whole.
G · Selection: your dim, with a ring that travels Your dim stays, restyled to match the new shapes. - The 0.55 black scrim and white stroke become a lighter scrim cut to the rounded shape, an accent ring and a shadow. A selected file dims nothing. - The ring travels to the next selection. It's about 60 lines and easy to remove. - A folder hidden inside a closed one, picked in the sidebar, rings its nearest visible ancestor. Needs B.
H · Hover card and status bar Main shows the hovered item only in the status bar. A card beside the cursor adds the category mix without crowding the treemap. *A file card, and a folder card.* - The card shows size, file count and path, and for folders up to 4 category rows, with the rest folded into "Other types". A smaller-items card says what a double click opens. - When nothing is hovered, the status bar shows the volume: "Macintosh HD · 782 GB used · 81.9 GB free". Needs B.
I · Show Folders off: main's flat look, refreshed Some people will prefer main's flat look. Folders become undrawn groups, as your layout engine already emits them, so selection and the dim work without a special path.

author: kieranklaassen
body:
After signing in, people continue to a page on this site. The return path is kept when it is a plain local path that takes at most 1024 bytes in the session, such as a document or cli page with its query string and fragment. Any other value continues to the default page, the same as when none is given.

The rule lives in the one existing helper. Login and signup use it when they store the value, and login, signup and the Google callback use it when they read the value. Cli authorization goes through login. No call site, page or other redirect changes.

## Tests

`test/integration/return_path_test.rb` covers login, signup and the Google callback, with values given in the query and values already in the session, and unsuccessful sign-ins. It also checks that document and cli paths come back exactly as given, and that cli authorization returns to its own page with its query.

- Focused sign-in, native shell and redirect tests: 523 runs, 2663 assertions, no failures.
- `bin/rubocop`: no offenses. `bin/brakeman`: no warnings.
- `npm run check`: passed on the first commit's code; the later commits change Ruby files only.

## Scope

Implements the redesign tracked in #25 and the language work in #26, #27, and #28.

- Mobile editor-first workspace, neutral/orange shell, responsive footer, accessible language menu and truthful local save status.
- Complete DE/EN/FR/ES/NL UI and content routes; internal support, example and draft terms pages.
- Preserves project schema 1.0, localStorage keys, CSV identifiers, and presentation behavior.
- Includes Stage Worker route and CI configuration for Stage, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- Updates DOMPurify to 3.5.0 after the production audit found a vulnerability in the previous version.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test` (18 passed), `npm run audit` (0 production vulnerabilities), and `npm run build` passed locally.
- Playwright Chromium and mobile Chromium passed; WebKit passed all online tests. The WebKit offline-navigation check is skipped because Playwright WebKit reports an internal navigation error.
- Firefox on this macOS host stalls before page load because its `plugin-container` is blocked with `Operation not permitted`.
- Wrangler Stage dry-run and live deployment passed. Version `04d26a77-873b-4977-9016-ab008297e657` is available at https://stage.prompter.haak3.de/.
- Stage browser smoke passed: HTTP 200, editor present, all five languages available, English shell rendered, draft AGB page rendered.
- Stage CI triggers were merged in #30. Manual dispatch was enabled on the default branch in #31, but repository-level GitHub Actions is disabled (`enabled: false`), so the dispatched run cannot start. No CI result is claimed.

## Review before production

- Operator review of the AGB draft, privacy and imprint texts, translations, and privacy notice date. `apps@haak3.de` was approved as the contact address and is entered in all five imprint/privacy versions.
- Real phone/tablet, screen reader, 200% zoom, Safari offline/PWA, visual export review, PR review and rollback artifact remain open. No production deployment from this PR.

PR #24's support-page content and PR #22's stage route are incorporated here; review those PRs before closing them as superseded.

A tier showing "Only 2 left" still let buyers step up to 4 in the buy panel. Now the stepper stops at what's left: the public tier read caps `maxPerOrder` at the purchases remaining, which the panel's existing clamps already respect.

Tiers can also show their description in red, for a warning buyers shouldn't miss. New `highlightDescription` column (additive migration), with a "Show in red" toggle in the tier workspace and the ticket types wizard.

Proof: against the local draft DB, clicking + five times on a tier with 2 left stops at 2 with + disabled; the description renders red; toggling it off in admin and saving writes `false` to the DB. author: jxnata
body:
Tarefa #19, seguimento da #17.

> **Depende do #40.** Esta branch parte de `feat/17-phone-territories` (a entidade `phones` ainda não está em `develop`), então o diff mostra o commit do #40 até ele ser mergeado. O commit desta tarefa é só o último.

## O que mudou

**Backup (formato v1.2)**
- `BACKUP_VERSION` foi de `1.1` para `1.2`. `BackupData.phones` é opcional e guarda `id`, `number`, `answered`, `answered_info`, `called` e `called_by`.
- `fetchBackupData` passa a buscar os telefones da congregação.
- `restoreBackup`:
  - **arquivo v1.2** (tem a chave `phones`): cria os telefones novos e depois apaga os atuais, na mesma ordem já usada para mapas e cidades (cria primeiro, apaga depois). Se a criação falhar, o rollback apaga os telefones criados. A designação não vai no backup, então os telefones voltam sem publicador, como os mapas.
  - **arquivo v1.0/v1.1** (sem `phones`): **os telefones atuais ficam como estão**. Assim, restaurar um backup antigo não apaga telefones que nunca estiveram nele.
- Novo passo de progresso "Restaurando telefones...". O `RestoreResult.phones` vale `null` quando o arquivo não tem telefones, e o toast mostra a contagem quando tem.
- O validador aceita `phones` opcional e confere os tipos de cada campo. Qualquer arquivo `1.x` continua aceito.
- O alerta de confirmação diz quantos telefones o backup tem. Para arquivos antigos, avisa que os telefones atuais serão mantidos.

**Exportação em PDF**
- O PDF "Lista de mapas" ganha uma seção **Telefones** com os números formatados.
- O botão aparece se houver mapas **ou** telefones.

## Como testei
- `bun lint`, `bun run ts:check` e `bun run test`: 229 testes passando. Testes novos cobrem o fetch dos telefones, `restorePhones`, a substituição na v1.2, a manutenção dos telefones com arquivo v1.1, o rollback e a validação/parse dos telefones.
- `backup-service.integration.test.ts` atualizado: seed com telefones, versão 1.2, resumo com `phones` e v1.0 mantendo os telefones. **Não rodei**, porque não há `.env` de teste neste ambiente (`bun run test:integration` precisa de `INSTANT_TEST_APP_ID`/`INSTANT_ADMIN_TOKEN`).

## Para conferir no aparelho
- Fazer backup com telefones, abrir o `.json` e conferir `"version": "1.2"` e a lista `phones`.
- Restaurar esse backup: os telefones voltam sem designação.
- Restaurar um backup antigo (v1.1): os telefones atuais continuam lá.
- Exportar PDF: a seção "Telefones" aparece no fim.
