author: lemonphase
body:
## What changes for the player

Nothing. For the next contributor: a new drill, serve, lesson, setting, graphics level, venue or section of config now has to say what holds it, in `tests/verification.map.json`, or `npm test` fails.

## Why

Slice 2 of the verification workflow. 18 of the 29 settings arrived in a month, with a drill, two serves, four venues and five graphics levels, and no check asked whether any run played them. Nobody could say, without reading everything, what a person still has to try before a release.

### What it adds

- **`tests/verification.map.json`**: 123 entries. For each drill, each drill played as each position, each serve, lesson, setting, graphics level and venue, and each section of config: the unit test files, trace runs and end-to-end checks that hold it, or `manual` with why no check can and what a person looks for. A `note` says what a reader should know about the checks named.
- **`tests/verification.map.test.ts`**, in `npm test`: it fails, with one sentence that says what to add and where, when
  - something that exists has no entry,
  - an entry is for something that no longer exists,
  - an entry names a unit test, a trace run, an end-to-end check or a feature file that is not there,
  - an entry names no check and gives no reason (a feature file is a recipe run by hand, not a check).
- The test file is the owner's (`.github/CODEOWNERS`). The data file is not, so a feature adds its own entry.
- A sentence each in `AGENTS.md` ("Docs that move with a change"), `docs/verification.md` and the README's list of tests.

### How the test reads what exists

From the code, not from a second list:

| What | Read from |
|---|---|
| Drills | `MODE_INFO` in the drill registry (`src/game/modes/mode`) |
| Positions, serves, settings, graphics levels, venues | `POSITIONS`, `SERVE_KINDS`, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, `GRAPHICS_LEVEL_IDS`, `VENUE_IDS`, imported from `src/config` as every other test imports them |
| Sections of config | Every export of `src/config` that is a table of values (not a list of ids, not a function): 35 today |
| Lessons | The game has no list of them, only the type `Lesson`. The test reads the type as it is written in `src/game/tutorial.ts` (`'spike' \| ServeKind` is the spike lesson and one for each serve), so a lesson added to the type fails `npm test` with the map's sentence |
| Trace runs | The text of `scripts/trace.mjs` (imported as text: the script plays the game when it is loaded, so it cannot be imported). The test cuts out `RUNS`, `LESSONS`, `KEY_RUNS` and the script's own `nameOf`, and works the names out with them: 40 runs. `scripts/trace.mjs` is not changed |
| End-to-end checks | The text of `scripts/e2e.mjs` the same way: its list of drill runs with its own line that names one (`serve_OH_call2`), and its phases (`keys`, `touch`, `probes`…). Not changed either |
| Unit test files, feature files | The folders, with `import.meta.glob` |

**The move of config into `src/config/`.** The test reads config through its one door and keys the map by export name. I wrote and filled the map on `main` at 298c73e, where config was one file. #156 merged while I worked. I rebased onto it and the same test with the same map passed with nothing changed (8 of 8), with config a folder of ten files.

### How the map was filled

By what plays or notices each thing, and I measured where reading would have been a guess. All in scratch clones, nothing committed:

- **Drills and positions**: the checks named are the ones that play that drill or that pair, by their own names (`spike/MB/good`, `spike_MB_call2`, `headlessGame('spike', 'MB')`). For a pair, each trace run is named beside how often the player's own athlete touches the ball in it, read from a recording (after the review: a run in which it never does is no check of the pair by itself).
- **Sections of config**, two sweeps on `main` at 298c73e:
  - every number of a section multiplied by 1.2, then `npm test`: the unit tests named are the files that went red (15 sections had none, and `VENUES` names `settings` by reading: it holds which venues have an open sky);
  - every number multiplied by 1.02, then `trace.mjs compare`: the trace run named is the first one the comparison showed to differ. For 10 sections it printed `same play`.
  - `BALL`, `ARENA` and `FX` stopped the app from starting when a count was no longer whole, so their trace measurement moved only the numbers that are not whole. `BALL` could not load the tests when all its numbers moved at once, so its unit measurement is eight parts added together.
- **Settings**: each default changed in turn (a switch flipped, a number scaled, a choice moved) and the comparison run again. 18 of 29 made a run differ, and that run is named. `unit` is by reading: a test of what the setting switches. That a stored value is valid is `tests/settings.test.ts` for every setting and is not repeated.
- **Serves, lessons, graphics levels, venues**: by reading the tests and the two scripts.

## The counts, from the map

| | Things | Unit test | Trace run | End-to-end | No check at all | Says `manual` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Drills | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| Drill and position | 35 | 10 | 12 | 12 | 21 | 21 |
| Serves | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 2 |
| Lessons | 4 | 4 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Settings | 29 | 16 | 18 | 5 | 7 | 12 |
| Graphics levels | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| Venues | 5 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 5 |
| Sections of config | 35 | 21 | 25 | 0 | 5 | 8 |
| **All** | **123** | **71** | **70** | **29** | **33** | **53** |

"No check at all" is an entry with only `manual`. "Says `manual`" also counts entries that name checks and still leave part to a person. Of the 123, **90 are held by at least one check and 33 by none**. (Before the review: 91 and 32. The Mini Rally as an opposite named a trace run in which the player never touches the ball, and is now one of the 33.)

### What still needs a person: every `manual` line

**Drill and position** (21)

- Played by nothing at all: free/OPP, free/MB, free/S, free/L, block/OH, block/OPP, block/S, block/L, receive/OH, receive/OPP, receive/MB, receive/S, setter/OH, setter/OPP, setter/MB, setter/L, serve/OPP, serve/MB, serve/S, serve/L, rally/OPP. A person plays a few reps of each.

**Serves** (2)

- `jumpFloat`, `jump` (part held): In the trace it is served only in its lesson, by scripted hands that are not good ones. How the serve feels with a real toss, run and swing is a person's.

**Settings** (12)

- `touchFov`: How wide the view is on a phone. Its stored value is validated (settings). Nothing draws a phone at another width: a person looks, on a phone.
- `invertY`: Looking up with the mouse pushed away. Nothing checks which way the view turns: a person moves the mouse.
- `womenNet` (part held): No run plays on the women's net: every run is on the men's. A person switches it, looks at the net and hits a ball that clears 2.24 m and not 2.43 m.
- `setArc`: The arc drawn over a set. No unit test draws it, and the trace played and drew the same with it off: a person looks in the Setter Drill with it on and with it off.
- `landingMarker`: The ring on the floor where the ball will land. No unit test draws it, and the trace played and drew the same with it off: a person looks in Free Play with it on and with it off.
- `replays` (part held): A replay watched to its end, and how it looks: the trace switches replays off in every run, and the end-to-end run only sees that a Perfect spike starts one.
- `volume`: Sound: nothing in CI can hear it. Its stored value is validated (settings). A person listens at 0, at the default and at 1.
- `firstPerson` (part held): What first person looks like, and aiming with the view: the end-to-end run takes screenshots of it and compares them with nothing.
- `keyHints`: The line of key hints at the foot of the screen. Nothing checks that it is shown: the trace played and showed the same with it on. A person switches it on and reads it.

author: ashlesh-t
body:
## Summary

When `storage.encrypt` is on and `keyring` + `cryptography` are installed but no keyring backend can be reached, CogniRepo said "graph.pkl is encrypted and could not be decrypted ... Install keyring + cryptography". It now says what is actually wrong: which cause it is, which backend was found, and what to do. The refusal to save is unchanged (it was right); only what it says, and one latent data-loss trap next to it, changed.

## Motivation

Fixes #283 (COG-21). Reproduced on `development` @ `007632a`.

The ticket's case: an encrypted repo run where the OS keychain is unreachable (SSH without a desktop session, a container, another user). `keyring` and `cryptography` are installed, so the advice to install them is wrong. Two more things were wrong with the old text:

- It named `graph.pkl` even when that file was plain (the graph was locked by the key lookup for the *journal*, not by anything encrypted).
- When `storage.encrypt` had been switched off over encrypted files (what #280 used to cause), the advice was still "install the packages"; the fix is to switch it back on.

Real run (`index-repo` on a repo whose config says `encrypt: true`, plain files on disk, `PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=keyring.backends.fail.Keyring`):

| | message |
|---|---|
| `development` | `No recommended backend was available. Install a recommended 3rd party backend package; or, install the keyrings.alt package ...` (keyring's own text, nothing about CogniRepo) |
| this branch | `there is no usable keyring backend here (keyring.backends.fail.Keyring), so the encryption key cannot be read. keyring and cryptography are installed; the key itself is kept in the OS keychain. Run where the keychain is reachable (...), or install a keyring backend (for example keyrings.alt) or set PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND.` |

## Changes

- [x] `core/security/encryption.py`: `KeyUnavailableError`, `explain_key_failure()` and the shared `is_unusable_backend()`. `get_or_create_key()` raises `KeyUnavailableError` (chained to the keyring error) instead of leaking keyring's raw text. Causes named: packages missing (the old text, unchanged), no usable backend (names it), keychain locked, a key that does not decrypt the data, `storage.encrypt` off over encrypted files.
- [x] `data/graph/knowledge_graph.py`: the graph stores why it locked (`_lock_reason`) and every place that warns or raises uses it (load, journal replay, `save()`, journalling, the rebase path, `incremental_base_status`). A missing key at journal-replay time is no longer reported as a damaged journal; real damage keeps its "could not be read" wording.
- [x] `interface/cli/install_probe.py`: imports `is_unusable_backend` instead of defining its own copy.
- [x] `tests/test_encryption_key_unavailable.py` (new, 20 tests), `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` (a table of the messages and the fix for each), `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Decisions to check (easy to drop)

1. **The `null` keyring backend now raises instead of minting a key.** `null.get_password()` returns `None` and `null.set_password()` drops the key, so `get_or_create_key()` returned a *different* key on every call (I checked: two calls, two keys). Anything encrypted under it could never be read again. `install_probe` already treats `null` as unusable. This is the one behaviour change that is not a message; it is the `if backend and ".backends.null." in backend` block in `get_or_create_key()` and its test.
2. **Removed `COGNIREPO_ENCRYPT_KEY` from `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.** It was documented as "Encryption key (overrides keychain)" but is read nowhere: it entered the docs in a sprint-7 docs commit and never existed in Python code, and no test mentions it. The key is read only from the OS keychain, so the answer to the ticket's "mention how to provide the key another way" is that there is none, and the docs now say so. If you want that override as a feature, it is a separate, security-sensitive change.
3. **The message suggests `keyrings.alt`**, as `install_probe` already did. I could not check here what `keyrings.alt` stores or where (it is not installed in my environment); worth confirming it fits the "key is never written to disk" claim before keeping the suggestion.

## Testing

```bash
pytest tests/test_encryption_key_unavailable.py       # 20 passed
pytest tests/ -p no:xdist -o addopts=""               # 3177 passed, 10 skipped, 1 failed (see below)
pylint --disable=C,R,import-error --fail-under=8.0 core/security/encryption.py data/graph/knowledge_graph.py interface/cli/install_probe.py tests/test_encryption_key_unavailable.py   # 9.99/10, same as the base, no new message
python scripts/check_no_stdout_pollution.py           # passed
```

- On the old code 15 of the 20 new tests fail (every message check, the new-graph save, the `null` backend, the helper). The 5 that pass before and after are the guards: nothing on disk is touched, missing packages still get the install hint, the lock clears when the key comes back, damage keeps its wording, a working keychain returns the same key.
- 607 tests (the 20 new ones included) across the graph, encryption, doctor, install-probe, safe-read, quarantine, prune and init suites pass.
- The one failure, `tests/test_embedding_memory.py::test_bulk_embedding_stays_within_the_memory_budget`, fails the same way on untouched `development` in my sandbox (same assertion, `tests/test_embedding_memory.py:47`; its subprocess cannot build the embedding model session: isolated `HOME`, no model cache). It is not related to this change.
- Tests use a real `keyring` with in-memory, `fail`, `null` and locked backends (not mocks of `get_password`), and a real plain `graph.pkl` plus journal for the case in the ticket.

## Not in this PR

- Other stores' wording: `core/config/safe_read.StoreUnreadableError(locked=True)` still says "install keyring/cryptography or restore the key". It has no cause to report, so it needs a different change.
- The graph stays locked when the key is unreachable even if the files on disk are plain. That is the refusal the ticket calls correct (saving needs the key to encrypt). Reading a plain journal without the key would show more data, and is a separate decision.

## Not verified

- The exact scenario from the ticket (`unshare -rn cognirepo setup`, no session bus). I used `PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=keyring.backends.fail.Keyring` for the real-process run and in-memory fakes in the tests.
- A real locked keychain (the locked case uses a fake backend that raises `KeyringLocked`), and the macOS and Windows backends. A backend counts as unusable only if its module is `keyring.backends.fail` or `.null`; any other backend is left to its own errors.

## Checklist

- [ ] All existing tests pass (`pytest tests/`): one environment-related failure, identical on `development` (see Testing)
- [x] New functionality has tests
- [x] SPDX header added to new `.py` files
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated if this is user-visible
- [ ] `cognirepo doctor` passes with exit 0: not run; this change does not touch doctor
- [x] No secrets or API keys in code or config

author: johnpetros
body:
## Objective

The complexity gate compared functions with a committed baseline, matched them by file, name and starting line, and looked only at each function's worst level. Moved code failed it, functions already over a limit grew freely, and regenerating the baseline accepted everything. The gate now judges each change against the target branch, with no baseline, covers the email templates and comments its findings on the pull request. It also adds `pnpm check:changed`, which runs the local checks on changed code only, following the local check scope in `documentation/tooling.md`.

Excluded: changing the limits in `.code-multivitals.json`, refactoring existing oversized functions, and failing on duplicated code, which did not fail the gate before either.

## Related issues

None

## PRD and Spec traceability

None. Direct request about repository tooling; no PRD requirement or Spec.

## Implementation

- **Checker** (`scripts/check-complexity.mjs`, rewritten): calls the CodeMultiVitals analyser instead of its CLI. It measures each changed production file at the merge base and in the change, follows git renames, pairs functions by name and closest measurements, and writes a table to the console and the job summary. It also writes a `findings` step output, and a failure report when it cannot measure a change. Options are `--scope`, `--base` (default `origin/main`), `--head` and `--output`; without `--head` it reads the working tree, including untracked files.
- **Comment** (`scripts/comment-complexity-report.mjs`, new): keeps one pull-request comment per workspace. It creates one only when there is something to report, updates an existing one on every run, and shortens reports over 60,000 characters.
- **Tests:** `scripts/tests/check-complexity.test.mjs` (rewritten, 16 tests) covers the metric rules, pairing, path selection, arguments and report files, with temporary git repositories for renames, the merge base and unreadable files. `scripts/tests/comment-complexity-report.test.mjs` (new, 5 tests) covers creating, skipping, updating and shortening comments.
- **Workflows:** the `Complexity` jobs of Core, Validation, Server and Web CI fetch depth 2, run both test files, pass `--base HEAD^1` and publish the comment with `actions/github-script`. The new `.github/workflows/email-package-ci.yml` (`Email CI`) runs the same job for `packages/email`.
- **Local command** (`scripts/check-changed.mjs`, new; `check:changed` in `package.json`): derives the checks from everything changed since the merge base with `origin/main`, including uncommitted and untracked files. It covers lint, complexity, types, architecture, script tests, test integrity, Vitest tests tied to the change with changed-lines coverage, changed Playwright files and mutation of changed use cases. Core and Web use `vitest related`; Server runs tests named after changed files, plus any given with `--tests`. `scripts/tests/check-changed.test.mjs` (new, 13 tests) covers the plan, results and options.
- **Coverage checker** (`scripts/check-changed-coverage.mjs`): the new `--working-tree` option measures uncommitted and untracked lines, with one added test. CI still compares two revisions.
- **Removed:** `.code-multivitals-baseline.json` and the `update:complexity-baseline` script.
- **Docs:** `documentation/tooling.md` (the new gate, the comment and the command) and one line of the implement-spec prompt.

## Business-rule changes

No product behavior or application authorization changes. In CI, the `Complexity` jobs of Validation and Email CI gain `pull-requests: write` to post the comment; Core, Server and Web CI already had it at workflow level. The comment step is skipped for pull requests from forks. The CI rules change as follows.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New function over an error limit | Fails | Fails |
| Existing metric goes over its error limit | Fails, unless the function was already at error on another metric | Fails |
| Cyclomatic, cognitive or nesting already over its limit grows | Passes | Fails |
| Length or Halstead volume already over its limit grows | Passes | Fails above 10% |
| New function at warning level, or a move from ok to warning | Fails | Listed, passes |
| Maintainability index | Counts toward warnings and errors | Not gated |
| Function above a limit moves to another line | Judged as new | Compared by name |
| Changed file the analyser cannot parse | Error printed, gate passes | Fails |
| Email templates in CI | Not checked | Checked |
| Running the gates locally | Each command and test file chosen by hand | `pnpm check:changed` chooses them from the changes, without coverage floors or whole suites; exits 1 on a failure and 2 on a skipped check |
| Changed-lines coverage of uncommitted work | Not measured | Measured with `--working-tree` |
| Complexity result on the pull request | Job log only | Job summary, plus one comment per workspace for blocking results, new warnings or an unmeasurable change; updated to `PASS` once fixed |

## Manual testing

Prerequisites: Node.js 22, `pnpm install`, `git fetch origin`.

1. Run `node --test scripts/tests/check-complexity.test.mjs scripts/tests/comment-complexity-report.test.mjs`. All 21 tests pass.
2. Run `pnpm check:complexity` on this branch. It reports 0 changed source files and `PASS`.
3. Run `pnpm check:complexity --base 2ded493a^1 --head 2ded493a` (the #74 merge). It exits 1 with six results across `NewSaleCart`, `useNewSalePage`, `OrdersFilters` and `useOrdersFilters`, and lists one new warning.
4. Add a function longer than 70 lines to a production file and run `pnpm check:complexity`. It fails and names the function. Remove the function and the run passes.
5. Move a file that holds an oversized function with `git mv` and run it again. It passes.

author: lukeaupiais
body:
## What

After the engine installs a workspace's JavaScript packages for scip-typescript, each declared package that ships no declarations (no `types`/`typings`, no `types` export condition, no `index.d.ts`) and has no `@types` package installed gets its DefinitelyTyped package. The TypeScript language server's automatic type acquisition does the same.

- The pinned `types-registry` 0.1.794, installed into the engine's cache through `tool_provisioning`, names which packages DefinitelyTyped has and the exact version tagged for the compiler scip-typescript runs (`ts6.0`, else `latest`).
- Those exact versions are installed with npm, scripts off, into a scratch prefix and moved into the copy's `node_modules` where nothing of that name is installed. The user's workspace is never touched.
- Each install records what was acquired under `types`. A failed acquisition makes the run `partial`, so its files carry `dependencies_unavailable`, the same as a failed install.

## Why

The compiler types a call into a package only from its declarations. Plain JavaScript packages such as `express` and `koa-router` ship none, so the index recorded no library symbol at their calls. Nothing downstream could tell `router.get('/x', handler)` from any other method call. This is the prerequisite for identifying JavaScript routes and clients by the type checker's answer rather than by rules over imports.

## Testing

- `tests/test_js_dependencies.py`: new tests for which packages count as untyped; for an untyped `file:` package getting its `@types` package from a local registry, with the call then resolving to the `@types` symbol; and for an unreachable types-registry making the install `partial` while indexing still completes. 20 passed. The dependency, provisioning and indexer tests: 80 passed, 7 skipped.
- Through `index_workspace` on dev corpora: node-express-boilerplate goes from 0 to 15 route calls resolved to `@types/express-serve-static-core`, koa-knex-realworld from 0 to 19 koa-router calls, and hackathon-starter acquires 24 packages (109 Express route calls resolved).

author: muhmi
body:
## Change

macOS GTK3 now always builds the same OpenGL pacing and doubling path as X11, with four backbuffers. Removed the configure switch, `USE_MACOS_PACING`, and its configure summary. Runtime gating remains VSync on and warp off, with doubling selected by the existing 2.2× display/emulated-rate rule. The present-stats tool is retained. Windows DirectX has no corresponding configure option, so this follows the fork's option-parity rule.

## VRR measurement

Laptop M5 Pro; Odyssey G70D, 3840×2160, Variable refresh already selected by the user. Read-only NSScreen query reports maximum 144 Hz and supported refresh intervals 6.945041–20.832875 ms. No display/system settings changed. Windowed, VSync on, same PAL scroll PRG as #2, CoreAudio 48 kHz / 0.67 ms fragments / 20 ms buffer.

Built unchanged origin/main `34c753c2b24c` and measured it before editing. Then built always-on pacing and measured three runs. A temporary control changed only `PACING_DOUBLE_MIN_RATIO` from 2.2 to 100.0, measured three more runs, then restored 2.2 and rebuilt. Control code is absent from the diff.

Each retained run lasts approximately 70 wall seconds, with the first 10 seconds skipped, leaving 60.1–60.3 seconds. Every config starts with `[Version]`, `ConfigVersion=3.10`, `[C64SC]`. PRG injection (`-autostartprgmode 1`) and autostart warp disabled avoid consuming the cycle limit during loading. Each retained log confirms `Autostart: Done.` and cycle-limit exit; exit code 1 is VICE's expected cycle-limit result.

All intervals below concern **new frames**. Latency is frame-completed → present-returned. Return means CPU-side `flushBuffer` + `glFinish`, not panel presentation.

| CSV run | Call p1 / p99 / sd (ms) | Return p1 / p99 / sd (ms) | Latency mean / p99 (ms) | Late / dropped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default-1 | 18.833 / 20.998 / 0.421 | 16.620 / 23.175 / 0.931 | 1.20 / 4.38 | 0 / 0 |
| default-2 | 18.909 / 20.933 / 0.439 | 16.542 / 23.194 / 0.989 | 1.21 / 4.48 | 0 / 0 |
| default-3 | 18.877 / 20.940 / 0.367 | 16.848 / 22.606 / 0.833 | 1.11 / 3.95 | 0 / 0 |
| paced-1 | 19.944 / 20.017 / 0.046 | 17.345 / 22.520 / 0.641 | 2.99 / 5.70 | 0 / 0 |
| paced-3 | 19.944 / 20.018 / 0.047 | 16.721 / 23.018 / 0.830 | 3.01 / 6.37 | 0 / 0 |
| paced-4 | 19.946 / 20.045 / 0.050 | 17.072 / 22.692 / 0.679 | 3.68 / 6.89 | 0 / 0 |
| nodouble-1 | 19.945 / 20.006 / 0.045 | 17.398 / 22.430 / 0.578 | 3.13 / 5.81 | 0 / 0 |
| nodouble-2 | 19.945 / 20.334 / 0.051 | 17.278 / 22.385 / 0.648 | 3.61 / 6.79 | 0 / 0 |
| nodouble-4 | 19.944 / 20.058 / 0.046 | 17.001 / 22.803 / 0.792 | 3.18 / 6.37 | 0 / 0 |

Late = new-frame return interval >1.5 PAL periods. The 144 Hz refresh equivalents below are interval / 6.944 ms, and bins round that ratio. They are **not physical refresh counts on VRR**; neither this API nor the CSV observes scanout.

| CSV run | Mean 144 Hz refresh equivalents per new frame | Rounded bins: 2 / 3 / 4 refresh equivalents | New / repeat presents |
|---|---|---|---|
| default-1 | 2.8735 | 71 / 2941 / 2 | 3015 / 0 |
| default-2 | 2.8734 | 80 / 2926 / 6 | 3013 / 0 |
| default-3 | 2.8734 | 53 / 2957 / 2 | 3013 / 0 |
| paced-1 | 2.8734 | 33 / 2979 / 1 | 3014 / 3015 |
| paced-3 | 2.8735 | 69 / 2944 / 1 | 3015 / 3016 |
| paced-4 | 2.8735 | 50 / 2970 / 0 | 3021 / 3021 |
| nodouble-1 | 2.8734 | 29 / 2988 / 0 | 3018 / 0 |
| nodouble-2 | 2.8736 | 31 / 2981 / 1 | 3014 / 0 |
| nodouble-4 | 2.8735 | 56 / 2957 / 1 | 3015 / 0 |

## Verdict

- **Pacing works at the call boundary:** call SD falls from 0.367–0.439 ms to 0.046–0.050 ms. Return SD falls from 0.833–0.989 ms to 0.641–0.830 ms. Mean latency rises from 1.11–1.21 ms to 2.99–3.68 ms. No late/dropped frames in any retained VRR run.
- **CPU return cadence is near 19.95 ms, not a two/three-refresh grid.** Paced mean new-frame return intervals are 19.954–19.955 ms. 87.1–90.1% fall within ±0.5 ms of 19.950 ms, versus 3.3–3.9% within ±0.5 ms of an integer multiple of 6.944 ms. This does not establish panel VRR operation: arrival mode also averages near 19.95 ms, and the historical fixed-144 Hz returns were not grid-locked either. NSOpenGL exposes no actual presentation timestamps.
- **Doubling has no demonstrated benefit here; observed return jitter is slightly worse, with overlapping ranges.** No-doubling return SD is 0.578–0.792 ms versus 0.641–0.830 ms with doubling. Latency ranges overlap (3.13–3.61 versus 2.99–3.68 ms). Doubling adds one repeat per new frame. Sequential runs confound background load and adaptive pacing history, so these data do not establish a causal scanout benefit or regression. Actual motion smoothness and panel low-framerate compensation were not measured.

### Fixed 144 Hz comparison

Recomputed from #2's retained `run-modal` CSVs using the same `--skip 10` analyzer. Those CSVs retain 50.3–50.5 s, despite the earlier description of 60 s. All three runs are included here, including the documented background-load outlier.

| Build | Call p1–p99 envelope (ms) | Call SD (ms) | Return SD (ms) | Mean latency (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed 144 Hz arrival | 18.87–20.96 | 0.308–0.453 | 0.704–1.017 | 1.04–1.17 |
| Fixed 144 Hz paced | 13.89–25.63 | 0.041–1.184 | 1.034–1.689 | 3.00–4.29 |

### Display-rate independence

No macOS pacing/present path examined makes emulated CPU/VIC/audio speed depend on display Hz. `opengl_pacing_schedule()` derives its nominal period from `vsync_get_refresh_frequency()` (machine rate), with completed-frame timing for drift/speed changes. NSScreen's display Hz is used only by `opengl_pacing_should_double()`. Repeats draw an existing texture; they do not advance emulated cycles. `vice_opengl_refresh_rect()` drops a video frame if the pool is exhausted rather than advancing emulation on a display clock, and the pacing wait occurs after releasing the canvas lock.

`vsync_set_machine_parameter()` sets machine cycles/frame and machine refresh; `vsync_do_end_of_line()` synchronizes emulated cycles with host/audio timing (`sound_flush()`). `statusbar_speed_widget_update()` reads emulated-rate metrics via `vsyncarch_get_metrics()`, not display rate. This is cycle-driven emulation with asynchronous presentation, consistent with display-independent fixed-step timing; no deltaTime multiplier is applied to emulated CPU/VIC execution.

Measured completed-frame rates are 50.113–50.114 Hz both in historical fixed-144 Hz and current Variable-refresh data, with identical nominal PAL 50.1245 Hz and 48 kHz CoreAudio configuration. Thus no display-dependent emulation-speed shift is visible. Status-bar pixels and audible audio were not independently captured, so exact status-bar/audio identity is not claimed from CSV timing alone. The scroll PRG is not an audio-content test.

## Verification and evidence

- `./autogen.sh && ./configure --enable-gtk3ui && make -j18`: passed before and after; final doubling threshold restored and rebuilt.
- `make check`: passed before and after. The default configure disables bundled lib tests; this is a build/check target, not automated pacing coverage. The actual changed path is exercised by the nine retained hardware runs, including the no-doubling counter-test. No redundant source-mirroring unit tests added.
- Configure help and all tracked files contain no removed option/macro. `git diff --check` passes. Builds have existing warnings (67 baseline, 64 paced); comparison finds no new warning text.
- `FORK-CHANGES.md` describes always-on behavior and both fixed/Variable results.

Evidence on Laptop: `~/agents/artifacts/work/evidence/vice-gsync/macos-vrr/20261126T210136-laptop-34c753c2b24c/`. Includes raw CSVs/logs/configs, `run.py`, `analyse.py`, `summary.json`, display query, build/check logs, and this report generator. Historical inputs remain under `~/agents/artifacts/work/evidence/vice-gsync/macos-pacing/run-modal/`.

Excluded attempts remain preserved: `baseline-1` consumed its emulated-cycle limit during warp; `baseline-vrr-*` used wall-time termination (one remained in au

body:
## Que cambia y por que

Fase 2 de `docs/PLAN-ESTILO-C.md`. Escaramuza y Campaña eran la tarjeta crema de antes, y se notaba al salir de Inicio. Se dibujaron tres formas de cada una en el lienzo, en la página [«Escaramuza y Campaña»](https://claude.ai/artifact/Hax2zKee8XFXvKV4WG8XfV), y el usuario eligió la **A de Escaramuza** («todo en la lista») y la **C de Campaña** («el camino de misiones»).

Las dos van como la pausa. A la izquierda, lo pequeño en oro, el título en grande y la lista de texto; a la derecha, en su ficha oscura, lo que se va a jugar. El velo de detrás oscurece hasta la ficha. En el móvil, la ficha va debajo.

- **Escaramuza**: Empezar, «Modo ◂ Normal ▸» con lo que da debajo, «Rival ◂ La IA ▸» y Atrás. En Personalizada, sus nueve opciones salen debajo del rival, más pequeñas y apartadas con una raya.
  - Cada valor se cambia con ← → o con ◂ ▸, y pulsar el nombre es un paso adelante.
  - A la derecha, el mapa, de qué es, su código (se puede escribir y avisa si no vale) y «Otro mapa» (R).
- **Campaña**: las misiones son un camino de puntos unidos por una raya, en oro lo ya andado.
  - Las hechas llevan ✓ en oro; las abiertas, su número en un aro dorado (más grande la elegida); las cerradas, un candado de píxeles.
  - Las cerradas salen apagadas, con «termina la anterior para abrirla». Las flechas las saltan y llegan a «Atrás».
  - Debajo de cada nombre va su objetivo y cómo está («hecha en 9 días»); arriba, «1 de 6 hechas».
  - La ficha de la elegida lleva su mapa, de qué va, el objetivo en oro, la mejor marca y «Jugar ▸».

Piezas:
- `MenuScreen.tsx` + `styles/menus/screen.css` (nuevas): la pantalla con su lista a la izquierda y su ficha a la derecha. Las usan las dos.
- `ChoiceEntry.tsx` (nueva): una entrada de `textlist.css` con su valor entre ◂ y ▸. No es un botón entero porque lleva dos dentro.
- `TextEntry`: `disabled?: boolean`, con el mismo nombre, doc y forma que la fase 4.
- `setupScreen.ts`: el modo se cambia como una opción más (`setupStep(id, delta)` en vez de `setupSet`). ← → cambian el valor de la entrada señalada.
- `campaignScreen.ts`: «Atrás» también se señala (`backSel`), y las flechas pasan solo por las misiones abiertas y «Atrás».
- Fuera lo que ya no se usaba: `.ng-code*`, `.ng-coderow*`, `.ng-groups` y `.cp-back`, y el texto `locked`. La tarjeta crema de «Crear sala» (En línea) sigue con sus `.newgame2`/`.ng-*`, que se quedan en `newgame.css`.

Docs:
- `PLAN-ESTILO-C.md`: la fase 2, hecha.
- `IDEAS.md` «Descartado»: Escaramuza B y C, y Campaña A y B, con el porqué.
- `ESTETICA.md`: cómo se ven, lo apagado y el valor con ◂ ▸.

### Al fusionar con la fase 4 y la fábrica

- `TextEntry.tsx` choca un poco con la fase 4, que además añade `icon`: quedarse con el de la fase 4.
- `base.css` (`--menu-off`, `--menu-off-note`) y el bloque `.text-entry.disabled` de `textlist.css` son idénticos a los de la fase 4.
- La sección de `ChoiceEntry` va al final de `textlist.css`.
- `screen.css` se importa en `hud.css` antes de `newgame.css`, no al final.

## Comprobado

- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `tests/aiGolden.test.ts` sin cambios, o actualizado a proposito porque cambian reglas o IA
- [x] CHANGELOG.md (si lo nota el jugador)
- [x] Navegador a 1280×800, 1366×640 y 390×844, con teclado y ratón (y toque en el móvil), sin errores en la consola:
  - Escaramuza: Normal, Rápida y Personalizada; ◂ ▸ con el ratón; un código malo da el aviso rojo; R da otro mapa. Empecé una escaramuza de verdad desde el escritorio y otra desde el móvil.
  - Campaña con la primera misión hecha: las flechas saltan las cerradas y llegan a «Atrás»; la hecha dice su mejor marca. Empecé «Cabeza de puente» de verdad con «Jugar».

author: nicolaerotaru
body:
## In parole semplici
Chi visita i negozi per proporre i servizi di SDG ha adesso una pagina tutta sua dentro MyCity. Incolla il link di Google Maps del negozio in cui sta per entrare, preme «Analizza» e riceve la scheda del cliente. La prima parte arriva in pochi secondi, la scheda intera in circa un minuto.

In MyCity «venditore» vuol già dire negozio. Per questo qui il ruolo si chiama **agente**.

Si diventa agente in un modo solo: col link che Nicola crea in Admin → Agenti. Non esiste nessun'altra porta.

## Cosa cambia per te
- **Admin → Agenti** (voce nuova nel menu): crei un link e lo copi. Il link si vede una volta sola. Vale per una persona e per 14 giorni. Puoi ritirarlo, sospendere un agente e riattivarlo. Niente si cancella.
- **L'agente apre il link** e crea il suo account MyCity con la registrazione normale. Conferma l'email, poi torna al link e preme «Attiva».
- **La pagina /agente**: una casella, il pulsante «Analizza», la scheda. Le schede restano legate al suo account, anche da un altro telefono.
- La proposta per il titolare non è qui: va nel preventivo.

## Cosa devi fare
1. Unire questa PR (va in produzione).
2. Applicare la migrazione 865. Se avevi una copia vecchia, usa questa versione.
3. Su Vercel, progetto mycity, mettere la variabile `N8N_SCHEDA_SEGRETO`. Il valore è nel file mandato in chat.
4. Creare il primo link in Admin → Agenti e provarlo da un telefono. Non aprirlo da admin: la pagina è già tua.

## Cosa non ho verificato
- **Con il database vero non ho provato niente:** la migrazione non è ancora applicata. Ho provato con un database ricostruito dalle migrazioni e con risposte simulate.
- **Con un vero agente non ho provato** la catena intera: link, registrazione, conferma email, «Attiva», scheda. Ho provato ogni pezzo da solo. La pagina del link l'ho aperta in Chromium.
- **Un punto resta aperto:** le schede di un agente restano in n8n dopo la cancellazione del suo account. È registrato tra i difetti del sito, con la correzione proposta.

---

## Dettagli tecnici
- **Migrazione 865**:
  - `inviti_agente`: nel database solo l'impronta sha256 del codice, mai il codice.
  - `agenti`: ON DELETE CASCADE verso auth.users.
  - `usa_invito_agente`: un posto in meno, in modo atomico.
  - `restituisci_invito_agente`: mai sotto il numero di agenti già entrati con quel link.
  - Accesso: RLS attiva e niente permessi ad anon e authenticated.
- **Link**: `/invito-agente#<codice>`. Il frammento non va al server, quindi non finisce nei log, in PostHog o nel Referer. La pagina lo tiene in localStorage per 24 ore e pulisce la barra. Le rotte `/api/invito-agente/stato` e `/api/invito-agente/attiva` ricevono il codice nel corpo.
- **Nessuna rotta del link crea account**: c'è una prova che le esegue tutte. «Attiva» mette a verbale il consenso (`consent_log` + `tos_accepted_at`) se manca la versione in vigore. Un agente sospeso resta sospeso. Freno per IP, per utente e per link.
- **Scheda**: `lib/agenti/*`. La prima scheda la costruisce il sito: lettura del link Maps solo dai redirect, OpenStreetMap per indirizzo e concorrenti, misura del sito con guardia SSRF. Poi l'AD completa la scheda attraverso i flussi n8n 14, 14b e 14c («Chiedi all'AD», piano Max, nessuna API a pagamento). I prezzi vengono da `lib/agenzia/preventivo`. C'è una prova di contratto col nodo vero del flusso 14.
- **Privacy**: `agenti` è nell'elenco delle tabelle personali (`lib/account/cancellazione.ts`) e nello scarico dei dati.
- **Collaudo**: tre giri indipendenti. Il terzo ha trovato 1 difetto grave e 8 minori; tutti chiusi tranne quello di n8n.
- **Prove**:
  - typecheck ed eslint puliti;
  - vitest 13.226 su 13.226;
  - harness SQL tutto verde: 237 migrazioni, 14 controlli nella prova nuova;

author: benjamingriff
body:
The last katsu import through the MCP couldn't be used. Every field had agent notes in it, steps did five things at once, three mains were crammed into one version, steps linked to the wrong ingredients, and made-up nutrition was marked `from_source`. The guidance sat in server instructions that some clients drop, and the server accepted anything.

Now the server checks what agents write. Errors refuse the write, and warnings come back with the saved result. The guidance agents need sits in the tool descriptions, where every client sees it.

## What changed

- **Server-side checks** (`apps/api/src/recipe-check.ts`, MCP only, so REST is unchanged):
  - Refused: notes that are agent reasoning, unlinked lines, steps that cross-reference other steps, two waits with one timer, imperial units, prep text inside `raw_text`, leftover base ingredients in a swapped version, and kcal that don't match the macros.
  - Warned: odd spoon fractions, step amounts above the line's amount, long steps, named-but-unlinked ingredients, and timers covering two waits or a "per side" cook. Timer design is still open, so these don't refuse.
- **Per-line nutrition estimates.** Agents estimate each line, and the server sums them into the batch. Whole-batch guesses are gone, and so are `agent_estimate` totals typed in by hand.
- **`for_meals`.** A version can say who it's for (people × slot × dates). The server sums those slot targets and refuses a batch more than 10% off the kcal, giving the scale factor and protein-aware advice. It also checks protein per portion.
- **Guide and workflow in tool descriptions.** `create_recipe` carries the recipe guide. The server instructions give a 6-step flow per dish: catalog and targets → recipe → a version per alternative → fix warnings → read back with `get_recipe` → reply.
- **Compact write results**: ids, counts, kcal, protein, warnings and what to do next, instead of echoing the whole recipe.
- **`delete_recipe`** (refused while a service uses it), so test rounds and bad imports can be cleared.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - `raw_text` for measured lines is built from the fields.
  - `update_recipe_version` merges partial changes.
  - The `based_on_version_id` error lists the valid ids.
  - "chillies" now matches "chilli".
  - Schema descriptions are tightened.

## How it was tested

I ran 14 rounds of the same three imports through a local lab API, which logged every call:

- Wagamama katsu as chicken and pumpkin versions: air-fried, sauce blended instead of sieved, lighter, with rice and salad.
- RecipeTin massaman made with only a stick blender, plus a high-protein version.
- BBC jambalaya without Cajun seasoning, for two plus a lunch.

Cheaper models did the imports. A council of four judges (Opus, Sonnet, GPT Sol, GPT Astra) scored the recipes and the MCP flow out of 10, leaving out retrieval problems. After each round I changed the MCP and had a Sol review check it.

Scores are written recipe / MCP flow. Rounds r4, r7 and r14 had no council.

| Round | Test models | Opus | Sonnet | Sol | Astra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | Haiku / Luna | 7 / 4 | 6.5 / 5 | 7 / 6 | 7 / 6 |
| r2 | Haiku / Luna | 6.5 / 4 | 7 / 5 | 7 / 5 | 7 / 5 |
| r3 | Haiku / Luna | 7 / 4 | 7 / 4 | 7 / 5.5 | 7 / 5 |
| r5 | Haiku / Luna | 7 / 3 | 7 / 3 | 7 / 4 | 8 / 4 |
| r6 | Haiku / Luna | 6 / 4 | 6 / 4 | 7 / 5 | 7 / 5 |
| r8 | Haiku / Luna | 5 / 4 | 5 / 4 | 6 / 5 | 5 / 5.5 |
| r9 | Sonnet / GPT-6 Astra | 7 / 6 | 8 / 6 | 7 / 8 | 7 / 8 |
| r10 | Sonnet / GPT-6 Astra | 7 / 6 | 8 / 7 | 7 / 8 | 7.5 / 8.5 |
| r11 | Sonnet / GPT-6 Astra | 7.5 / 7 | 7 / 6 | 7 / 7.5 | 7 / 8 |
| r12 | Sonnet / GPT-6 Astra | 7 / 6 | 8 / 6 | 7 / 8 | 8 / 8 |
| r13 | Sonnet / GPT-6 Astra | 8 / 7 | 8 / 6 | 7 / 8 | 8.5 / 6.5 |

The target was 9 from every judge, and no round got there.

- With Haiku and Luna the scores stayed flat. Most of their failures were incomplete runs, not bad recipes.
- After the models were raised to Sonnet and GPT-6 Astra, the recipes settled at 7–8.5.
- The remaining gap is cooking judgement (rice timing, pan size for small batches) and estimates nudged to pass the checks. Server rules can't fix much more of either.

The rounds stopped there. The r14 Sonnet recipes were replayed onto the live account.

**Sol loop:** about 14 rounds, and none ended in a full APPROVE. I fixed most findings. I declined two:

- S7, a delete race between check and delete, which isn't worth the complexity for one household.
- S50, refusing a fixed-size "High protein" version without `for_meals`. The user may have fixed the amounts on purpose.

The last completed review (r13) asked for changes, which are fixed in c164f7c, 7d98556 and 5ae1b9a. The r14 review didn't run because of a usage limit.

Checks: typecheck, lint, format:check, 25 API tests, 11 core tests, and `smoke-mcp` against the lab API all pass.

## Cleanup after the rounds

Over the rounds, the council pulled the design towards the three test dishes. The last commit (9c8a514) takes that back out:

- **Guide.** I took out cooking tips that only fit the test dishes, such as stick-blender liquid, light coconut milk, 75 g of rice a person and "about a quarter more" protein. It went from 1,460 to 830 words.
- **Timers.** The timer checks now warn instead of refusing.
- **Side steps.** The check on steps that only cook a side is gone.
- **"High protein" label.** It no longer changes what gets checked.
- **`for_meals`.** It's accepted in one place only.

Re-running all 182 logged lab writes, only those refusals stop firing (52 in total, 36 of them the two-waits check), and there are no new refusals.

## Follow-ups

- The app shows `0.125 tsp` and should show `⅛ tsp`. The same goes for other quantities (`format.ts`).
- Count lines don't pluralise ("2 egg").
- The recipe screen labels notes "Agent note" (`apps/mobile/app/recipe/[id].tsx`).
- Aisles can't be edited through the tools.
- Prod has no people yet, and `for_meals` needs people to size versions.
- Per-line estimates aren't stored, so there is nothing to cross-check them against later, and nudged estimates can't be caught.
- Timer design (several waits in one step, per-side timers) still needs deciding.
- Possible further steps: `versions[]` on `create_recipe`, slimming the uuid-heavy schemas, and a smaller catalog in `list_ingredients`.

Merging deploys the API to Railway after CI, and no mobile Release is needed. The old archived katsu import stays in prod until `delete_recipe` is live.

Created with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code). Test imports were run by Claude Haiku, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT Luna and GPT-6 Astra. Judging was done by Opus, Sonnet, GPT Sol and GPT Astra, and code review by GPT Sol.

author: jimsimon
body:
## Problem

A thread that had been idle for about two months failed every turn on Claude models with:

```
no provider is currently able to run auto/claude-fable-5-2; tried 1 route(s).
Last error from claude-code/claude-fable-5-2: backend error: backend protocol error:
No conversation found with session ID: <id>
```

Claude Code prunes idle conversation transcripts on its own retention schedule. Trouve stored the vendor session id in `backend_sessions`, never removed it, and passed it to `--resume` on every later turn. Once the transcript was gone the thread could not run on any Claude model again, because the row is keyed per `(thread, backend)`. On automatic models the rejection was also recorded as a route failure.

## Fix

- **Adapter:** the Claude adapter reports this rejection as a new `BackendError::SessionNotFound`, only for turns that actually resumed a session.
- **Store:** `clear_backend_session` removes the row only if it still holds the reported id.
- **Engine:** both turn paths forget the stale id and rerun the same attempt once as a fresh session, with the full history digest from trouve's own transcript.
  - Automatic routes (`run_backend_route`): the rerun is the same attempt, not a failover, so route health and thread affinity are untouched.
  - Pinned backends (`run_backend_turn`): the rerun reuses the continuation mechanism and does not store the prompt or publish admission a second time.

The rerun only happens when the vendor did no work (no text, no tool activity), and at most once per attempt.

## Not covered

- Only the Claude adapter classifies the error. Codex and Cursor would need their own detection to use the same engine recovery.
- A `SessionNotFound` returned from `run_turn` itself (rather than from the stream) is handled on the automatic path only; Claude reports it in the stream.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p trouve-agents -p trouve-core` passes.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all` are clean.
- New tests: a stub-CLI adapter test, a classifier unit test, a store test, and engine tests for the automatic and pinned paths.
- Not exercised against the real Claude CLI: the error-result shape in the stub is an assumption; the classifier matches on the message text seen in the failed turns.

body:
Two fixes for the website, from feedback on the theme lab and the Lens Apps grid.

## 1. Accent picks now visibly repaint the demo desk
Before this change, picking an accent changed only the music progress bar, because the real surfaces use `--lens-accent` sparingly and the lab desk opened with no window focused.

- **Picker:** the accents are now a radio group of named colours: Snow, Iris, Sky, Mint, Amber, Tangerine, Coral and Violet, plus **Theme's own**. The picked colour gets a ring and a check, and its name and hex show under the dots. The arrow keys move between colours.
- **Desk:** `docs/site/css/lab-accent.css` is linked into every real surface on the lab desk. It paints these in the accent:
  - the dock's running marks and icon hover
  - the selected tab and selected or pressed items
  - switches that are on, and primary buttons (text colour picked for contrast)
  - icon-button and window-button hover
  - focus rings, and the browser's one box
- **Focus border:** the lab opens with the music window active, and that window wears Lens's focus border in the accent. The dock's focused mark is full width.
- **Motion:** `--lens-accent` (in the frames) and `--lx-accent` (on the page) are registered with `@property`, so a pick eases over `--lens-dur-slower` / `--lens-ease-out`. A short wash also crosses the desk. With reduced motion there is no ease and no wash.
- **Drag onto the desk:** the cursor becomes a grabbing hand. The desk gets an outline as the drop target and a "Drop to paint the desk Coral" label, which lights up in that colour when the pointer is over the desk.
- **Other lab controls:** the theme cards, All themes, Shuffle and Download already changed something obvious, so they are unchanged.
- **New check in `tools/site/check.mjs`:** clicking each accent must turn four desk elements into that exact colour: the dock's running marks, the music window's primary button, the browser's space dot and the focus border. The accent must also be marked checked and its name shown. A separate check confirms "Theme's own" can be picked again.

The layer only shows colours the surfaces already take from `--lens-accent`, at full strength. It is site-only and changes nothing in the app.

## 2. Lens Apps cards: real screenshots and credits
- **Card layout:** a 16:10 screenshot sits on top in a rounded matte frame, lazy-loaded with width and height set. Below it:
  - name and one-line description
  - **by <maker>**, linked to the repo
  - licence
  - "Screenshot: <project>, <licence>", small and muted
  - **Get**
- **Grid:** 3 columns on desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 on phone.
- **Footer note:** names, screenshots and trademarks belong to each project, and Lens isn't affiliated with any of them.
- **`tools/site/app-thumbs.mjs`:** makes `docs/media/apps/<id>.webp` (640×400, 9–30 KB each, 208 KB in total) from pinned commits. It fetches with a shallow tree-less git fetch, the same way as `fetch-app-media.mjs`; `gh api` is scoped away from third-party repos in this environment.
- **Catalogue (`catalog/apps/catalog.json`):** gains `author` and `thumb` (`{src, site}` or `null`), added to the schema, `types.ts` and `validate.ts`, so the in-app store can reuse them.
  - `repo` is now set to the GitHub repo for WordCraft, DeckCraft and GridCraft. It was `null`; their media is already pinned there.
  - Install behaviour is unchanged.
- **Test in `apps.test.ts`:** every thumb is pinned to a commit, its file exists, and it is 60 KB or less.

| App | Screenshot source (repo @ pinned commit : path) |
|---|---|
| ArtCraft | storytold/github-media @22a2737 : `character-posing.webp` (linked from ArtCraft's README) |
| WordCraft | storytold/wordcraft @c369c3a : `docs/images/hero.png` |
| DeckCraft | storytold/deckcraft @7fbdc08 : `docs/images/editor.png` |

**No screenshot, so these keep the Lens-drawn tile:**
- **OBS Studio:** its repo has no app screenshot. The metainfo points to obsproject.com, which can't be reached from here.
- **Krita:** the KDE/krita mirror holds only icons, splash art and donation banners. Its screenshots are on cdn.kde.org.
- **Blender:** the GitHub mirror's screenshot test renders are Git LFS pointers. The README image is on code.blender.org.

GitHub social previews (opengraph.githubassets.com) couldn't be fetched either.

## 3. The home page opens on the Dock widget (later feedback)
- **Hero desk hidden:** the big demo desk is off via a flag, `HERO_DESK = false` in `tools/site/pages.mjs`. Its code moved unchanged to `docs/site/js/hero.js`, which loads only when the desk is on the page.
- **"Magic Dock + Top Dock":** the page now starts with the real top bar and dock, live, in one matte frame.
  - You can pick any of the nine styles, any of four edges, or an accent. Each pick changes the real dock in place, with its own transition.
  - `js/desk.js` can now place the dock's frame on any edge.

  2. The cursor opens Lens Browser from the dock and types the search into it.
  3. The booking step shows the real "Needs your OK" card.
  - An action trail beside the desk marks each step done. With reduced motion everything stays still.
- **Captions:** every exhibit now has a solid matte strip with the step number and label, then one sentence at 17 px.
- **Order:** Dock widget → Lens Browser → Magic Mouse → Themes → Agentic desktop → Lens Apps (with the thumbnails) → the rest.
- **Exhibit behaviour:** an exhibit starts its first step only once it is on screen, and the loops wait while a desk window is being dragged.
- **Where apps open:** Lens Apps' "Get" and the small apps now open on the Theme lab's desk. The Guide works without the hero desk.
- **`tools/site/check.mjs`:**
  - The desk checks (drag, resize, snap, minimise and restore, right-click, Command, Quick Settings, every dock icon, the Settings pop-out) now drive the Theme lab's desk.
  - New checks:
    - the hero desk is hidden, and the sections come in the right order
    - the widget shows the real top bar and dock: Taskbar, Left and Top change the real dock, and an accent paints its marks
    - each Magic Mouse and agentic step shows its real surface
    - captions are at least 16 px on a solid strip

## Checks
`node tools/site/check.mjs` passes locally ("no problems"):
- Page weight on the home page: 809 KB first load and 1,544 KB with everything loaded. The budgets are 1.2 MB and 2.2 MB.
- Desk drag at 4× CPU throttle: the median frame is 16.7 ms and the longest task is 140 ms. The budget is 200 ms.
- Layout shift: 0.008.

`bun test src/__tests__/apps.test.ts` passes. axe-core isn't installed locally, so C

author: ikimyonsoo
body:
Driver and evaluation fixes from the first real CARC drives (CARLA 0.9.16, `-nullrhi`), plus a small edge-case scenario set. All 95 tests pass.

## Results

Test set: `use-pyotter/make_scenarios.py`. One new route (Town10 spawn 35 → 2), 4 worlds (baseline, icy, bright-sun, mixed with seeds 7 / 42 / 1227), × 3 drivers = 18 runs.

| | First 18-run batch (items 1–6 only) | After items 7–9 |
|---|---|---|
| Collisions while moving | 1 (seed 7 cautious, 13 km/h) | **0** |
| Runs keeping every requirement | 16 / 18 | **14 / 18** on the stricter 300 s set, with no remaining failure caused by the driver (see Open questions) |
| Worst `min_gap` / `min_gap_ahead` | −2.40 m / −4.45 m | **−0.72 m / −0.94 m** |
| `braking` | 100% | 100% (least margin +1.30 m/s²) |

## Changes

### Evaluation (`driver.py`, `config.yaml` → `driver.evaluation`)
1. **A contact counts as a collision only while the car moves** (`least_impact_speed_mps: 0.5`). `no_collision` is now `always((collision >= 0.5) -> (speed_mps <= 0.5))`, in m/s. Scripted walkers walk into a stopped car; that isn't the driver's collision.
2. **Gap rules apply only while the car moves** (`moving_above_mps: 0.5`). A walker coming up to a stopped car is not a gap the driver left.
3. **Gaps capped at 60 m** (`gap_cap_m`) so "no road user" (the 1000 m placeholder) reads as "at least the clear-weather sight" and no longer dominates margins. The charts use the same trace (`Driver.trace`).

### Driver (`carla_runner.py`, `controller.py`, `driver_model.py`)
4. **Anticipation**: the driver predicts where each visible pedestrian walks over `anticipation_s` (3 s) and brakes for the nearest one that will be in its path. The recorded `gap_ahead_m` is unchanged.
5. **Walkers are created off the road** (`walk_m: 12.25`, `start_off_m: 6.0`, outside the path half-width), so the driver sees them walk in. Seed 1227 had a walker created inside the path 8.9 m ahead.
6. **The car waits while a walker is within `min_gap_m` (2 m) of its body**, now or within `walker_lookahead_s` (1 s), from any side, and drives on once clear. Walker behaviour is unchanged; an earlier "walkers yield" attempt was reverted.
7. **Speed-for-sight cap** (`drive_within_sight: true`): the car drives no faster than it can stop `min_gap_m` short of a road user appearing at the edge of its sight, braking at its planned deceleration. Clear sight leaves the 30 km/h limit unchanged; 8 m of sight gives about 17 km/h; 5 m (thickest fog) about 5–7 km/h. `false` turns it off for before/after comparisons.
8. **Self-correcting brake**: CARLA's brake is much weaker than our linear pedal model at part pedal (pedal 0.55 gave 3.4 m/s² when 6 was asked). `SpeedControl` now adds pedal while the measured deceleration falls short of what was asked (`brake_trim_gain`, `brake_trim_clip_mps2`) and drops it when braking ends. This fixed the last real driver failure (seed 42 risk-aware: −0.43 m → +1.08 m).

### Scenarios
9. `use-pyotter/make_scenarios.py` writes the 18 one-change scenarios. Duration is 300 s, because with the sight cap the foggy drives take 150–200 s.

## Open questions for @nathanaday

The 4 remaining failures are not driving mistakes. They need a decision on the spec:

**A. Sight shorter than the rule (3 breaches, −0.39 to −0.94 m on `min_gap_ahead`).** In the thickest fog the driver sees 5 m (`min_detection_range_m`), the same as `min_gap_ahead_m`. A walker stepping in at the edge of sight is already inside 5 m; the car (crawling at about 5 km/h) stops within 0.2 s, about 4.3 m away. Should the rule:
  1. stay at 5 m, and count these as failures,
  2. become `min(5 m, sight)`, or
  3. flag them separately as unavoidable?

**B. Walkers created beside the car (2 breaches, about −0.6 m on `min_gap`).** At seed 7, 172.4 s, a walker is created about 1.3 m from the car's body (the gap jumps from 14.6 m to 1.3 m in one tick); the car stops at once. Should we flag such pop-ups as unavoidable when scoring, and how do we define that? My proposal: the walker first appears closer than the stopping distance at 6 m/s² from the current speed.

## Notes
- Repeat runs of the same scenario file differ: small timing changes move walker encounters. Report failure rates over repeats, not single verdicts.
- Single-tick acceleration spikes of −15 to −27 m/s² come from physics, not the controller. The sustained 0.5 s rule ignores them; a hard-brake count would need smoothing.
- #12 (world forecasts) touches the same `reach_m` line in `CarlaRun._step`, a trivial merge. Its `build.duration_s` should be 300 for the same reason as item 9.

author: echobob
body:
## Why

Outreach runs as two-week experiments, measured by positive replies and calls booked, and each target needs to tie back to its cycle, hook and result. Outreach state lives on Person today, but nothing in the CRM groups People into a cycle. The shape was decided on 2026-11-21: a Cycle object related to Person, with an Opportunity opened only on a positive reply, so the "apps open Opportunities for posted leads" rule stands unchanged. This is slice 1, the object in crm. The frontdesk writer that enrolls People and links the Opportunity is a separate card.

## What changed

Net source lines vs main: +215 (tests excluded). Why: one new object with nine fields (122 lines, most of it the field declarations Twenty requires), two reverse relation fields on Person and Opportunity (26 each, the same shape as `opportunity-waiting-on.field.ts`), a reverse field on Brand, its identifiers, and a two-value verdict list. It adds new code and replaces nothing.

- `twenty-app/src/objects/outreach-cycle.object.ts`: the **Outreach cycle** object, following `brand.object.ts`. It has `audience`, `hook` and `ask` (TEXT), `brand` (MANY_TO_ONE to Brand, cleared when the Brand is deleted), `startDate` and `endDate` (DATE), and `verdict` (SELECT, Keep or Kill, empty until decided). It also has two ONE_TO_MANY relations:
  - `people`: **Enrolled people**, to Person.
  - `opportunities`: **Replies and calls booked**, to Opportunity.
- `twenty-app/src/fields/person-outreach-cycle.field.ts` and `opportunity-outreach-cycle.field.ts`: the reverse sides, `Person.outreachCycle` and `Opportunity.outreachCycle`. Both are MANY_TO_ONE and are cleared when the cycle is deleted. Twenty relations are declared on both objects, as crm#28 did for Waiting-on.
- `brand.object.ts`: `outreachCycles`, the reverse of the cycle's `brand`.
- `universal-identifiers.ts`: a new block for the cycle object after the Brand block. The Brand and Opportunity reverse ids go in `BRAND_FIELDS` and `OPPORTUNITY_FIELDS`, the same placement as crm#28.
- `packages/client/src/lead-record.ts` (and its index export): `OUTREACH_CYCLE_VERDICTS`, so the field and any writer share one list of values, as with every other select.

**How a call booked is marked.** The app has no "call booked" field. It marks a booked call by stage: Engaged (stored as `MEETING`, `LEAD_STAGES.ENGAGED`) means the conversation is under way. A cycle's calls booked are therefore its Opportunities at Engaged or later. The cycle's Opportunities list shows each one's stage. I added no second marker that would need its own writer.

## What deliberately did NOT change

- No writer. Frontdesk enrolling People in a cycle and linking the Opportunity it opens on a positive reply is the follow-up card.
- No views and no column on the Outreach Person view. Twenty's default record page lists both relations on the cycle.
- No app-role change. The app's own logic functions never read or write cycles.
- No client package version bump. Only the option list is exported, as crm#28 did with `WAITING_ON_CHANNELS`.

## Proof

author: rishenko
body:
## What this is

One lookup command for every session and blind reader (Kevin 2026-11-26: "I want everybody to do lookups the same way repeatedly"; "efficient, quick, doesn't use a lot of resources, but is automated via code to retrieve").

`npm run reign-pages -- <uuid> [<uuid> ...] [--from FILE] [--full]` prints, for each committed reign, three pages from the local dump, each with its title, Wikidata QID and dump revision, then infobox and lead (`--full`: the whole page):
- **person:** the reign's own source page. The first source that isn't a list page, because offices events cite their list page first.
- **realm:** the page of the row's Wikidata item (`Track.ids.wikidata`).
- **office:** the first link in the person's infobox office fields (succession, title, office, office1…).

It's plain code and local only: the committed timelines, `wp_dump`, and the Wikidata item table. No model, no network. A page the dump doesn't hold prints "no page", and a missing QID prints "none"; nothing is guessed. Lookups are cached in `~/data/reign-pages-cache.jsonl` (one line per dump + title). `$TIMELINES_REPO` points it at another checkout, such as a blind reader's frozen copy.

No stage, no data, no schema change. The reign-to-person match is already stored once, as each reign's first source (page + revision).

## Files

- `pipelines/common/reign_pages.py` (the command) and `pipelines/common/test_reign_pages.py`. 5 tests: infobox and lead split, office link, person source skipping list pages, cache round trip, and one that reads the dump, skipped where the dump is absent (CI).
- `package.json` gains `reign-pages`; one line each in `docs/development.md` and `pipelines/README.md`.

author: gtanczyk
body:
## Why

[`Publish games snapshot #45888792390`](https://github.com/gamedevpl/www.gamedev.pl/actions/runs/45888792390) failed after ~15 minutes of baking on two unrelated games (`checker-champ`, `tower-defence`) with:

```
FAIL checker-champ: fetch failed
FAIL tower-defence: fetch failed
```

`createGcsSnapshotStore`'s `writeObject` uploads thousands of objects per publish (`games/*.json`, media originals, WebP/resized variants, videos) with raw `fetchImpl` and no retry, so a single transient socket reset (`UND_ERR_SOCKET` / `ECONNRESET`) or transient GCS `429`/`5xx` response aborts the entire snapshot publish. Because `publishSnapshot` only logs `error.message`, Node's `TypeError: fetch failed` also hid `error.cause` and which object failed.

## What changed

- Added `apps/api/src/catalog/snapshot-write-retry.ts` (`retrySnapshotWrite`, `describeTransportError`):
  - Retries idempotent GCS snapshot writes up to 4 times with exponential backoff + jitter (and honors `Retry-After` up to `maxDelayMs`) on transient transport errors and HTTP `408`, `429`, `5xx`.
  - Leaves non-retryable HTTP statuses (`400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `412`) and `AbortError` untouched without retrying.
  - Cancels retryable response bodies before sleeping so connections are returned cleanly.
  - Wraps exhausted transport errors with the object name and `error.cause` code/message (e.g. `fetch failed (UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)`).
- Wired `writeObject` in `apps/api/src/catalog/game-snapshot.ts` through `retrySnapshotWrite` (including `authHeaders()` inside the retry callback so a transient token fetch error or boundary refresh is retried too).
- Registered `'snapshot-write-retry': 'catalog'` in `eslint-rules/module-boundary-map.mjs`.
- Added unit + `createGcsSnapshotStore` integration tests in `apps/api/src/catalog/snapshot-write-retry.test.ts`.

## Verification

- `npm run type-check`
- `npm run lint` (including `comment-prose`, `module-size`, `module-boundary`, `firestore-*-cost`, etc.)
- `npx --workspace apps/api vitest run src/catalog/snapshot-write-retry.test.ts src/catalog/game-snapshot.test.ts src/catalog/game-snapshot-publish.test.ts src/game-snapshot-serve.test.ts`
- `npm run test:rules`
- `npm run build`

author: vincentkoc
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Commands such as `openclaw infer model run` load channel and web capability code while selecting model credentials. A short-lived CLI process pays for those imports even when it only uses a model provider.

## User Impact

Model, image, video and media commands can select model credentials independently of channel and web discovery. They use the same configured credential paths, including custom request headers, proxy TLS and request TLS. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model credential paths are a fixed list. Model-only callers now import that list through a small module which creates a fresh set for each caller. Commands that combine model and other credentials reuse the same list and keep their existing discovery behavior.

## Evidence

- With the same pinned esbuild compiler and Node 24 target, the model command's emitted dynamic import selected a target module with 18 direct static imports on the parent and zero on this change. This measures the compiled module in isolation. Packaged startup time remains unmeasured.
- Compared the candidate getter with the parent definition at runtime. All 13 IDs matched in order, and clearing one returned set left the next call intact.
- Added a regression test that throws if model target selection imports channel, web fetch or web search discovery. The test verifies the full set after mutating the prior result.
- At `7067ab1f3251`, PR-shaped CI selected the import regression and all selected Node test jobs passed. Its mock-factory guard flagged five test factories and the packaged build job was skipped. The dependency check also reported unused symbols outside this change. [Initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45913760861)
- The test-only correction at `5729b04b9faa` uses the real getter in model config tests, documents four intentional mock boundaries and removes two old mock allowances. The repository's mock-factory scanner reproduced five new findings on the published parent and zero on the correction for the affected mocks. Formatting and whitespace checks passed. The full mock-factory ratchet passed on the corrected head. The five focused suites passed all 152 tests.
- The corrected head passed `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` on Linux with Node 24.22.1. The Testbox command exited zero and the one-shot lease stopped after completion. An optional probe of the final packaged dependency graph did not follow the generated re-export, so there is no measured package-byte or startup-time delta. [Testbox workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45918285003)
- In the separately compiled test-worker distribution, the real model command selected a re-export and its implementation. The entire static dependency closure was two files totaling 982 bytes. Importing that compiled entry returned 13 independent targets.
- Local autoreview covered the full staged range from `eb0faf79a5be` through the contents of `5729b04b9faa` at priorities P0–P3, with zero actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its installation could not resolve TypeScript.

author: meepleai-app
body:
Refs #4780. È il primo pezzo della PR 2 decisa nel corpo della issue (il ciclo di vita): l'annullamento. Gli altri due pezzi seguono in PR loro, per tenerle piccole:
- l'avviso sulla live conclusa con la serata ancora aperta;
- i ranghi.

## Il difetto

Una serata si poteva annullare mentre una sua partita era in corso. La partita dal vivo e il `GameSession` correlato tenevano il posto di quota finché qualcuno non li terminava, dalla serata ormai annullata che nessuno apre più. Il link della serata, poi, poteva passare a `Skipped` solo da `Pending`.

## La correzione

Decisione dell'utente del 2026-11-25: l'annullamento è rifiutato con un 409 («termina prima la partita»), e la UI lo dice.

- **`CancelGameNightCommandHandler`** rifiuta con `ConflictException("game_night_has_live_game", …)` quando una partita della serata è **avviata e non conclusa**, cioè `InProgress` o `Paused`. Interpretazione mia, scritta qui:
  - «in corso» è ciò che tiene la quota;
  - una partita creata e mai avviata (`Created`), o conclusa, non blocca nulla.
- **Lo stato del link non basta:** la pausa riporta il link a `Pending` (`PauseSessionCommandHandler`), quindi si legge la partita dal vivo collegata a ogni seduta (`ILiveSessionRepository.GetByTrackingSessionIdAsync`, una lettura per seduta, al più cinque).
- **Una serata già annullata non viene interrogata:** il ritentativo resta il no-op che era e svuota comunque le pagine in cache (#4856).
- **Client:** `GameNightDetailView` riconosce il codice (`GAME_NIGHT_HAS_LIVE_GAME_CODE` in `gameNightsClient`) e mostra «C’è una partita in corso: terminala prima di annullare la serata.» invece dell'errore generico. Le stringhe sono in `it.json` ed `en.json`.

## Prove

**`CancelGameNightCommandHandlerTests`:**
- `InProgress` e `Paused`: 409 con il codice, serata non annullata, nessun salvataggio;
- `Created`, `Completed` e nessuna partita dal vivo: la serata si annulla;
- serata già annullata con una partita in corso: nessuna lettura delle partite, nessun errore.

**`GameNightDetailView.cancelBlocked.test.tsx`:** il messaggio dedicato con il codice, quello generico con un altro 409.

**Mutanti, tutti uccisi, con 0 errori di build:**
- il controllo del server disattivato: rossi i due casi `InProgress` e `Paused`;
- il codice ignorato dal client: rosso il test del messaggio.

**In locale:** 30 test del gestore verdi, più `ConflictErrorCodeStyleArchitectureTests` per lo stile del codice; 74 test Vitest verdi (il nuovo e quelli dei file di lingua).

**Non provato nel browser.**

body:
## 概要

- 日本語のイベント概要、両キーノート、検索できるセッション一覧、製品発表を GitHub Pages で提供します。
- 公式カタログ掲載の全 1,426 セッション（1,588 枠、うちオンデマンド 835 枠）と、Book of News の全 59 発表項目を収録しました。参加条件付きのラボ 49 件も公開メタデータのみ収録し、制限付きの資料や字幕・動画の転載は含めていません。
- 同じ JSON から HTML と AI の入口 `llms.txt` を生成します。更新は出典と差分を確認する手動 PR 方式です。

## セッション別の詳細と録画要約

- 公開 1,426 セッションすべてに公式コード名の `session/{code}.html` と `data/sessions/{code}.json` を生成し、HTML からそのセッションの JSON に移動できます。
- `data/sessions.json` はカタログ兼索引で、確認済み ID と状態別件数を収録。個別 JSON にメタデータ、録画の確認状況、要約をまとめ、一括要約 JSON は廃止しました。編集用は `data/session-notes/{code}.json` が唯一の要約ソースです。
- オンデマンド案内のある全 831 セッションに日本語要約を追加しました（最新バッチで 62 件追加）。話の要点、アップデート、事例・デモ、Tips に録画の時刻を付けました。各時刻前後の字幕に基づく要約で、全編視聴を示しません。公開録画の案内がない 595 件は、公式メタデータのみ掲載し、録画内容を推測していません。
- 827 件は公式イベント録画の字幕、4 件は照合済みの Microsoft Events の YouTube 文字起こしが出典です。YouTube を参照した 4 件は時刻が YouTube 版を指し、詳細ページから該当箇所へ移動できます。音声認識や録画のダウンロードは行っていません。

## 公式 YouTube と Ignite タグ付き更新

- Microsoft の公式チャンネルと Ignite 2026 プレイリストで、セッションコードとタイトル等を確認できた 673 件を対応付けました。録画の紐づけと内容の確認は別で表示します。
- Azure Updates の `Microsoft Ignite` タグかつ 2026 年公開の 202 投稿を公式フィードと照合して掲載しました。Book of News の 59 発表とは出典・提供状況を区別できます。
- 根拠の確認できた 240 セッションを関連アップデートにリンクし、更新ページからも参照できます。セッション内の発表と補足資料を区別します。

## Fluent 2 と追加した出典

- Fluent 2 に沿って、概要、セッション一覧・詳細、製品発表のヘッダー、カード、検索、状態表示を更新しました。ライト・ダークとデスクトップ・モバイルに対応します。
- 公式プレーヤーと字幕トラックを 831 セッションすべてで照合し、825 件にチャプター開始時刻があります。録画情報の確認と内容の要約は別です。最新バッチで追加した 62 件について、イベント版字幕 235 箇所、YouTube の文字起こし 14 箇所を確認しました。
- Azure Updates の 202 件すべてに日本語概要を追加。限定プレビューと、原題・フィードの提供段階が実質的に食い違う 4 件を別表示します。206 セッションから公式技術記事へ移動でき、参照元の更新も示します。

## レビューと検証

- 公式カタログの全 1,426 コードと 1,588 枠を照合しました。参加条件付きの 179 枠も、未ログインで公式詳細ページのタイトル・コード・枠 ID を確認しました。Book of News の全発表 ID も照合済みです。
- Python テスト 15 件、静的ビルド、JavaScript の構文確認が通過しました。既存 30 件の要約を変更せずに分割し、追加 18 件の 70 箇所を公式字幕の時刻と照合しました。
- 全個別 JSON、確認状況の整合、HTML と `llms.txt` の導線、旧一括要約の非公開を確認しました。ラバーダックの指摘を踏まえ、録画の対応付けと確認範囲を明示しています。
- Pages の公開元は GitHub Actions に設定済みです。初回の本番デプロイは `main` へのマージ後に実行されます。

<!-- copilot-pr-assessment:v1 -->

author: kingchenc
body:
Maven Central now counts every organization's monthly release size and count, and the family reached the limit on 2026-11-26. This bundle covers Maven Central's usage and throttling, a release page that no longer waits on Maven Central, the PyPI upload and draft pull requests without CI; CHANGELOG.md records all of it under [Unreleased].

**Keep the native libraries out of the sources jar.** The release workflow stages every platform's native library into `src/main/resources/native/` before the deploy, and `maven-source-plugin` packed them into the sources jar a second time. `excludeResources` stops that. Measured on wickra-impact 0.2.2 with the six published natives staged as CI stages them:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `-sources.jar` | 3,609,322 B (25 entries) | 7,313 B (12 entries) |
| `.jar` | 3,612,548 B | 3,612,676 B (unchanged, every native still in it) |
| one release on Central | ~7.3 MB | ~3.7 MB |

**Retry Maven Central throttling, skip r-universe in link checks.**

- `bindings/java/.mvn/maven.config`: the resolver retries 429 and 5xx eight times, backing off up to five minutes and honouring `Retry-After`, instead of the default three. Both property spellings (resolver 1.9 `aether.connector.*`, 2.x `aether.transport.*`). Verified that `mvn -f bindings/java` from the repository root, as CI calls it, picks the file up.
- `lychee.toml`: r-universe's HTML pages sit behind a Cloudflare challenge that answers 403 to every non-browser client (44 "broken links" across the org were all this). Excluded like crates.io and npmjs; r-universe's API is not challenged. Transient failures retry four times, 30 s apart.
- `release.yml`: the "already on Maven Central" pre-check ran `version=$(mvn ...)`. Maven prints its errors on stdout, so a failure there left an empty log; it now prints Maven's output before failing.

**Publish to PyPI with PyPA's action instead of `maturin upload`.** maturin deprecated its `upload` and `publish` commands (PyO3/maturin#2334) and will drop them; every release run already carries the warning. maturin keeps building every wheel; the upload moves to `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` (v1.14.3, pinned by commit) with the same token, the same `dist/` files and versions already on PyPI skipped. Its PEP 740 attestations need Trusted Publishing rather than a token, so they are off; the release's own provenance attestation is unaffected.

**The GitHub Release page no longer waits on Maven Central.** On 2026-11-26 Central refused twelve releases over its monthly limit after crates.io, PyPI, npm, NuGet and Go had all published them, and because `github-release` needed `java-publish`, none of those twelve got a release page. Now `github-release` and `attestations` no longer need `java-publish` (and no jar is staged onto the page; it lives on Central), and a new `attest-jar` job attests the jar after the deploy without attaching anything to the release. Re-running a refused Maven job later therefore never touches the published, immutable page. `actionlint` and `zizmor` are clean on the result.

**Draft pull requests start no CI.** Every workflow that runs on `pull_request` lists its activity types with `ready_for_review` added, and every job carries `if: ${{ !github.event.pull_request.draft }}` (combined with an `if:` it already had, e.g. `ci-ok`'s `always()`). A draft costs no runner time; marking it ready starts the full run. Push, schedule and dispatch runs are unchanged: they carry no pull request, and the condition is true.

body:
## What changed

- **Officer admin tools** (`src/app/admin/`, `src/services/admin.ts`, migration `20261121030256_officer_admin_tools.sql`): officers can create, edit and delete events and links, see attendance, check members in by hand, and upload flyers. Flyers are converted to WebP under 500 KB. Members can no longer promote themselves to officer.
- **Check-in codes hidden from members** (migration `20261126193102_hide_event_checkin_codes.sql`): the events select policy is `using (true)` and the app used to select `*`, so every phone received every event's 6-digit `checkin_code`. Anyone could read it and check in without attending. Members and anon can now select every events column except `checkin_code`. Officers read it through `get_event_checkin_code()`, and `check_in` (security definer) still validates against it. `getEvents`/`getEvent` now select explicit columns.
- **Check-in Google form sync**: app check-ins also submit the SASE Google check-in form.
- **App Store review prompt** after a successful check-in.
- **Verify screen**: pasting a one-time code works, and the screen stays above the keyboard.
- Event hero flyer uses `cachePolicy="memory-disk"`, so the hero and the full-screen viewer share the decoded image.

## ⚠️ Rollout order (please read)

Installed app builds load events with `select('*')`. Once the check-in-code migration is applied, Postgres refuses that query and **events stop loading on old builds**.

1. Publish this JS as an EAS Update for runtime `1.2.0`, then wait for adoption.
2. Only after that, push the migrations to production.

Builds on older runtimes will show no events until they update from the store.

## Notes for reviewers

- Column grants on `events` are explicit. A new column added to `events` stays hidden from the app until it's added to the grant in the new migration.
- `get_event_checkin_code` depends on `is_officer()` from the officer migration, so the two must ship together.
- Members also can't filter or sort by `checkin_code`, so the code can't be guessed with repeated filtered queries. `check_in` itself still has no attempt limit (unchanged by this PR).

## Testing

- `supabase test db`: 131 pgTAP tests pass, including the new `event_checkin_code_privacy.test.sql`.
- `npm test`: 583 tests pass. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` are clean.
- End-to-end against the local stack as member, officer and anon, using the app's own query strings. Checked: events list and detail, points, admin list, and officer insert/update/delete. Direct reads of the code, filtering or sorting by it, and `select('*')` are all refused for members.
