- Unproven message states get no extra press; timeouts and verifiers are unchanged.

Tests: with the old code the new acknowledgement test fails (three taps instead of four); the unproven-message guard passes before and after. author: maxgb23
body:
Closes #593

`pnpm import` writes `pnpm-lock.yaml`; which versions it records is pnpm's answer, not the foreign pin. Measured on pnpm 12.3.4, three shapes, each twice:

| Foreign lockfile | Range | Recorded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `package-lock.json` v3 pinning `4.17.20` | `^4.17.21` | **`4.18.1`** |
| the same beside a `pnpm-lock.yaml` recording `4.17.21` | `^4.17.21` | **`4.18.1`** |
| berry `yarn.lock` pinning `4.17.20` | `^4.17.21` | **`4.18.1`** |

`4.18.1` is a version lodash never published, and the value is synthesised from the range: 6 ms (35 ms for the yarn shape), `--offline` in the same 6 ms, and the store carries no `metadata/` directory.

The caveat printed under step 3 said "only the import carries its versions" — the line a human relies on before step 4 deletes their `package-lock.json`. It now names the comparison instead:

```
   pnpm-lock.yaml is present; even after the import, the versions it records are pnpm's to decide, so compare them with package-lock.json before step 4 removes it
```

And the `--from` refusal lost its "not `package-lock.json`" construction:

```
funky-secure: --from npm names a manager this repository does not hold: there is no foreign lockfile here, and --from npm needs package-lock.json
reason: run migrate --apply without --from, so the detected manager decides
```

Exit `2` unchanged (a flag value, not a refusal), and the remediation sequence `pnpm import && funky-secure migrate --from npm --apply` is untouched — it is spec-mandated and it is right.

## Verification

- RED: `node --test tests/migrate.test.js` → `pass 25 / fail 3`, with the three sentences quoted as actual vs expected.
- GREEN: `28 / 28`.
- Differential against `219608c` (`git archive` into a scratch dir), three fixtures, both binaries: stdout differs on exactly the intended line and nothing else; stderr byte-identical except the one refusal line.
- Suite: 1033 tests, 1032 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip.
- No golden carries either sentence, so the generator was not run.

The spec text that asserted the same claim is corrected in #595, which lands first in review order — `docs/spec/` decides, the code follows.

author: nikhilchoudhari9916
body:
## What and why

Ask refused "What does furosemide do?" whenever the papers named a medicine without saying why it is taken, because ADR-0046 turned every outside source off. The FDA label tool already existed and was tested, but Ask had it switched off.

This adds [ADR-0048](docs/decisions/0048-fda-label-for-plain-purpose-questions.md) (supersedes ADR-0046 only where it says the label is never evidence) and a graph step written in plain code for a plain purpose question about **one confirmed medicine** ("What does X do?", "What is X for?", "Why am I taking X?", "What is it for?" after a question that named X):

- **The papers win.** If the original medicine-list row states a purpose, it is shown as original words and nothing is looked up.
- Otherwise the label's **indications and usage only** (never dosage or warnings) is shown word for word under "General information from the FDA drug label, in its own words", tagged "From the drug label", followed by "The label may list several uses. It does not say which one is yours, so please ask your care team or your pharmacist."
- Only layout is removed from the label text (heading, numbering, "( 1.1 )" references, markup characters), and a long section is cut at a sentence end (about 450 characters). It is never rewritten.
- Only the medicine's names go to openFDA, never patient text. If the lookup fails or has no usage section, the reply says so and points to a person.
- The model writes none of the reply. New setting `fda_label_lookup` (default on); tests keep it off.

Not changed: the safety gate, the validators, prompts, the model's tool list, or any other question.

## How I tested it

- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass.
- Full offline suite: **1,222 passed** (32 new, in `tests/qa/test_label_purpose.py`): which questions count, trimming and markup-stripping of the label text, the papers winning, the fallback when there is no label, the Tier 2 care-team line, the endpoint end to end with a fake FDA service (only the medicine's names are sent, the model does only the three safety readings), a service that is down, a medicine that is not the patient's never being looked up, an emergency still getting only the 911 text, and the on/off switch.
- Live, real backend and the real openFDA service (synthetic Patient 1; the model was used only for the three safety readings): "What does furosemide do", "What is Lasix for?" and "What is metoprolol for?" each returned the general-information reply with a "From the drug label" tag in 1 to 3 seconds.

## Notes for review

- Like the fixed list answers in ADR-0047, this reply is composed by code, so the output validators do not run on it. Its safety rests on the fixed wording, the confirmed-medicine limit, the verbatim label text and the tests.
- The lookup can make up to four short requests (5 seconds each) and has no hard total deadline of its own. That belongs with the cost and concurrency work (security review F6).
- "What is my water pill for?" is unchanged: matching a lay term to a medicine needs a mapping the team has not decided on.
- Vinaya wrote ADR-0046, so please look at the ADR before approving.

## Safety review (`aftercare-safety-review`)

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tier 1 recall | PASS: the gate is the first graph step and the new step is reachable only after it; `test_an_emergency_still_gets_only_the_fixed_911_words`; `app/safety/` is untouched. The live Tier 1 eval was not re-run. |
| 2 | Tier 1 message unchanged | PASS: no diff to `app/safety/messages.py`. |
| 3 | Classifier error or timeout is Tier 2 | PASS: classifier code is untouched and its tests pass. |
| 4 | Gate and validators cannot be skipped by an agent | PASS with a noted exception: the gate precedes the new step, and no agent can call it. The validators do not run on this code-composed reply (same as ADR-0047); recorded in ADR-0048. |
| 5 | No tool writes patient data | PASS: only the read-only `search_fda_label` and `read_original_medicine_entries` tools are used; none was added. |
| 6 | Guardrails | PASS with a note: at most 2 tool calls and no model call. The label lookup has a 5 s limit per request but no total deadline (see notes). |
| 7 | Unconfirmed items never used | PASS: confirmed profile only; `test_a_medicine_that_is_not_the_patients_is_never_looked_up`. |
| 8 | Schedules and dates by code | N/A: not touched. |
| 9 | Validators still reject | PASS: `app/qa/validators.py` is untouched and its tests pass. |
| 10 | No over-escalation regression | N/A: gate, router and prompts are unchanged; the live eval was not re-run. |

## Checklist

- [x] Small and focused: one task, no unrelated changes
- [x] Tests added or updated, and `pytest` passes locally
- [x] `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass (pre-commit ran)
- [x] No real patient data, no `.env`, no `storage/` or database files
- [x] No patient text written to logs
- [x] Only `app/llm.py` calls the Anthropic SDK; no model IDs outside `app/config.py`
- [x] No new dependency
- [x] Changes a project decision: new ADR-0048, ADR-0046's status line and `CLAUDE.md` updated

author: roquerodrigo
body:
## Summary

Adds a way to open the release pull request even when the notes find nothing that matters to those who use the project, for instance after changes confined to CI or to development dependencies.

- **Action:** new `force` input (default `"false"`).
- **Reusable workflow:** new `force` boolean input, passed on to the action.
- **Command line:** new `--force` option.
- **Library:** new `force` option of `ReleaseAutopilot`.

## Behaviour

- The model is told that the release was asked for, and must return at least one entry. When nothing reaches the users, that entry says the release brings internal maintenance. Notes without entries are rejected and written again, within the usual three attempts.
- The pull request records `forced` in its hidden state, so later runs keep it forced and never close it for lack of relevant changes, until it is merged or closed.
- The fingerprint of a forced pull request differs from that of a regular one, so forcing a release whose pull request is already open with current notes rewrites it once as forced. Fingerprints of regular pull requests are unchanged.
- A release still needs a conventional commit since the last tag to take a version from.

## Usage

The README now shows a `workflow_dispatch` trigger with a `force` input, so a release can be forced from the Actions tab with **Run workflow**. This repository's own release workflow gains the same trigger.

## Verification

- `npx eslint` and `npm test` (type check, tests and coverage) pass, with new tests for the use case, the prompt, the action and the command line.
- `actionlint` and `zizmor` report no findings.

author: bvdaakster
body:
## Problem
`retryFailedEmails` matched nothing in the default flow. An email only becomes `failed` once `attempts >= retryAttempts`, but the query asked for `failed` emails with `attempts < retryAttempts`.

## Design
Since #166, failed sends that still have attempts left are retried automatically. That leaves `retryFailedEmails` as the manual "try these again" action:
- It selects up to 20 `failed` emails, whatever their attempt count, once `retryDelay` has passed since their last attempt. Oldest `lastAttemptAt` comes first, so a backlog larger than 20 rotates instead of starving.
- Each email gets **one more attempt**, still through the atomic `failed -> processing` claim. If that attempt fails, the email stays `failed` and no retry job is queued. `attempts` is not reset, so it keeps the total count.
- I chose this over "reset attempts and start a new automatic retry round" because `processAllEmails` calls `retryFailedEmails`. With a reset, a host running `processAllEmails` on a cron would get a full burst of `retryAttempts` sends per cycle for every permanently failing email. With this design it is one attempt per `retryDelay`. I documented this in the `processAllEmails` JSDoc.
- `retryDelay: 0` is honoured here too.

README API row and JSDoc updated.

## Tests
- Unit (`MailingService.retry.test.ts`): the selection query (no `attempts` clause, sort, limit, delay), an exhausted email being claimed from `failed` and sent, and a failed extra attempt staying `failed` with `attempts: 4` and no job. The query test fails on main.
- Integration (`dev/int.spec.ts`): a `failed` email with `attempts: 3` (= `retryAttempts`) becomes `sent` after `retryFailedEmails(payload)`. Fails on main (stays `failed`).

Local: readme peer check, lint (0 errors), typecheck, test (304), test:int (9).

author: arantespp
body:
Task: https://flow.ttoss.dev/app/tasks/task_c27yde77p3 (settles it).

A workflow state declares an optional `max_tasks` (positive integer). An entry into a state already holding that many open tasks answers `409 TASK_STATE_FULL` (`meta.state`, `meta.max_tasks`) and the task stays where it was.

- `lib/tasksStateCapacity.ts` is the one check: counts open tasks of the workflow in the state (every version), excluding the entering task; inside a transaction it first takes a per-workflow advisory lock (`workflowStateCapacity`), so two entries racing for the last slot cannot both pass.
- Entries: transitions (in `transitionRefusal`, so the write, the approval resolution and `GET /tasks/{id}/transitions` answer the same), creates (now one transaction with the history row), migrations that change state.
- `TASK_STATE_FULL` joins the rejection codes of `on_complete` routing (`tasks.automation_rejected`) and approval resolution (`tasks.approval_failed`).
- Validation: `max_tasks` must be a positive integer, refused on a terminal state (`WORKFLOW_VALIDATION_FAILED`).
- `tests/harness/stateCapacityChokepoint.test.mjs` fails when a new site writes a task's state without the check.
- `lib/tasks.ts` passed the 400-line ceiling, so the update path moved to `lib/tasksUpdate.ts` (re-exported; the route imports it directly so the `x-raises` scan still reaches `TASK_PAYLOAD_INVALID`).

Fix shape: changes one rule path (`transitionRefusal`) and adds one check module; no code path removed.

**Closing validation.** `merged` here, then `api` on naturali after the bump: https://flow.ttoss.dev/app/tasks/task_ac5s8pe8cn, blocked by `Bump naturali to soat (next)`.

**Checks run locally:** `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm eslint`, `pnpm run test:harness` (474 pass), `pnpm run docs-lint`, `pnpm declare-error-codes`, `generate-error-hints`.
**Left to CI:** `pnpm test` (incl. the new `rest/taskStateCapacity.test.ts`) — no Docker here and the local Postgres has pgvector 0.6 (< 0.8 floor); smoke tests — no Docker.

**Reversal:** revert this commit; `max_tasks` is a key inside the JSONB `states`, no migration.

## Decisions

- Q: Which version's limit applies when tasks are pinned to versions? A: the entering task's pinned version, counted across every version. Test: consistency with pinning — every other state property (`on_enter`, `stalled_after`, `terminal`) is read from the pinned version. Checked `taskWorkflowDefinition.ts`.
- Q: A migration that would overfill a state? A: a migration mapping a task to another state is refused with `TASK_STATE_FULL`; a task kept in its state keeps its slot, even over a lowered limit (the state then refuses entries until it drains). Test: brief allows refused or documented; documented in `workflows.md` § State capacity and tested.
- Q: `max_tasks` on a terminal state? A: refused (`FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED`): a terminal state holds no open task, so the limit could never apply. Test: fail closed on what nothing reads.
- Q: Approval-gated transitions into a full state? A: parking defers the capacity check to resolution, like the guard; a full state at approval clears the gate and emits `tasks.approval_failed`. Test: consistency with the guard rule.
- Q: Lock granularity? A: per workflow, only taken when the target state declares `max_tasks`. Test: smallest lock that covers the count; no contention for workflows without limits.

Noted, not changed: the `x-raises` scanner does not follow re-exports from `lib/tasks.ts`, so `transitionTask`/`migrateTask` declare neither `TASK_GUARD_REJECTED` nor `TASK_STATE_FULL`: https://flow.ttoss.dev/app/tasks/task_sctnxb573n.

author: kozlvign
body:
## Problem

LearnHarness could use Claude and ChatGPT plans, but not a Google Antigravity plan. The goal was to use Google's models (and the partner models a plan includes) with the learner's own Google account, the way T3 Code does.

## What it does

**Settings → Providers → Subscriptions → Antigravity** (row after Claude) runs the account's models through Google's official, unmodified `agy acp` (Agent Client Protocol). LearnHarness never reads or stores Google tokens. Full write-up: `docs/antigravity.md`.

- **Runtime:** install, update or remove Google's runtime from its update manifest. The download must be Google's file for this platform and match its SHA-512, and it's activated whole. An agy already on the computer is used too (`LH_ANTIGRAVITY_PATH`, the installer's folder, `PATH`). agy 1.5.1+ is required.
- **Sign-in:** Google sign-in in a profile only LearnHarness uses, with `agy acp --login`: open Google's link, then paste the code. Sign-out goes through agy itself. There's an *Allow background use* switch, and the connection never falls back to an API key.
- **Models:** every model on the account except Orchestrator. Thinking levels map 1:1 to agy's, and context windows come from agy. Cost shows as "Antigravity", with no dollar amount.
- **Bridge:** one agy process per conversation, running a LearnHarness agent with no built-in tools (`tools: []`) and LearnHarness's prompt appended. LearnHarness's tools are served from a loopback MCP endpoint per session, and the permission gate refuses anything else.
- **Session behavior:** held tool calls, so a posed question waits for the learner's answer. Model and thinking-level switches apply in place. Prompt or tool changes resume the session, and replay happens when the history changed.
- **Images and usage:** images travel both ways. Usage is split across responses so per-turn totals add up.
- **Shutdown:** clean shutdown shared with the Claude connection (`src/agent/graceful-shutdown.ts`).

### Differences from the approved plan (found by testing against the real agy 1.5.18)

- **MCP config location:** the MCP server is written into the profile's `config/mcp_config.json`, not a per-session workspace config. Workspace servers load only after the first prompt starts, so turn 1 had no tools. Servers passed over ACP ignore `timeoutSeconds` and are cut off after 3 minutes. The profile config honors `timeoutSeconds: -1`: a 200 s held call got the real answer. agy reads that file once, during `authenticate`, so processes start one at a time.
- **System prompt:** sent via `_meta.antigravity.systemPrompt.append` with a fixed `agent.md`, so the prober → teacher hand-off resumes the same session. A 90 KB prompt arrived whole.
- **Workspace:** one shared empty workspace instead of one per session.

## Tests

- **New offline tests:** 22 in `tests/antigravity-bridge.test.ts`, with a scripted agy that runs as a real child process and calls the real MCP endpoint, and 4 in `tests/antigravity-connection-ui.test.tsx`. All pass.
- **Updated tests:** `tests/subscription-connection-ui.test.tsx` and `tests/render-settings.test.tsx` now expect 5 subscription rows.
- **Full suite (Windows):** every failure on the branch also fails on unchanged `main`; those are known environment failures (CRLF, symlinks, signals, network sentinels).
- **Static checks and build:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` with no errors, `npm run build` passes, and `node scripts/fork/i18n/check.mjs` reports every text with a pt-BR entry (75 added).
- **Live, against agy 1.5.18 with a Google AI Pro account (temporary test profile, signed out and deleted afterwards):**
  - model probe (about 4 s);
  - tool call → held quiz → learner answer delivered in the same session;
  - prompt change → resume in a new process;
  - images, cancel, long prompt;
  - managed download of 1.5.18 from Google (53 s, checksum verified);
  - sign-out.
- **Not covered:** GitHub Actions are off on this fork, so the PR has no CI checks. macOS and Linux runtime installs (tar.gz) are covered only by the offline extraction test.

author: williampring
body:
## Why

The UI's **Enable Auto-Sync** toggle does not work on a generated Application, and it never will. The ApplicationSet controller owns every Application it generates (via `ownerReference`) *and* watches them — so the UI write is itself the event that triggers the reconcile that overwrites it. Sub-second, no error. It looks like a bug and isn't.

So auto-sync gets granted where the Application is actually defined: the generator.

## What

**Auto-sync for four apps** — `searxng`, `kavita`, `suwayomi`, `immich-public-proxy`. All stateless or trivially re-creatable. Added through `templatePatch` in `kubernetes/bootstrap/apps.yaml`:

- `automated: {}` — **no `selfHeal`**, so a hotfix applied by hand in a 2am incident stays applied
- **no `prune`** — nothing gets deleted without a human
- Renovate still never automerges, so **the PR remains the gate**. Merging an image bump deploys it; opening one does not.

Two independent `if`s, deliberately not `if/else` — an app needing both flags would silently get one. And a merge patch *replaces* lists, so `syncOptions` has to restate `CreateNamespace=true`; that's commented in place.

Everything else stays manual, including anything that migrates a database.

## The cleanup that came with it

Review turned up real rot, not just style:

| | |
|---|---|
| `templates/app/kustomization.yaml` | Taught `generators:` for the ExternalSecret. Banned by CLAUDE.md **and** wrong — kustomize expects a generator plugin config there, not a manifest. All 7 real ExternalSecrets use `resources:`. This is the file new apps get copied from. |
| `argocd-notifications-cm.yaml` | Named "KSOPS decrypt" as a likely sync failure, in a push that lands on a phone. KSOPS was retired Nov 2026. Now says "missing OpenBao key", which is the actual cause today. |
| `argocd-cm.yaml` | Referenced by nothing — the kustomization patches `argocd-cm-patch.yaml`. Deleted. |
| `docs/platform/argocd.md` | Listed two files that don't exist (`ingress.yaml`, `repo-server-ksops-patch.yaml`), omitted two that do. |
| `Homelab` | A tracked zero-byte file from a shell typo. |
| `.gitignore` | `.claude/` was ignored only in `.git/info/exclude` — local-only, does not survive a clone. **This repo is public and that directory has held real secret files.** |
| `docs/apps/calibre.md` | Did not exist. Written to the `wealthfolio.md` shape. |

Comments were trimmed throughout: kept where they record a *why* that cost an outage, cut where they restate what the YAML already says.

## Checks

- `make conventions` → `CONVENTIONS OK` (7 warnings, all pre-existing)
- `make lint` → warnings only, all pre-existing
- `make validate` not run locally (no `helm` on this machine) — leaving that to CI

## Note

Disjoint from #(the Homepage PR) — no shared files, either order merges clean.

author: beomseogkim
body:
Fixes #438. Refs #400.

## Problem
A member whose session runs on a linked device has no publish state on the home, so `who`, `ask` and `reply` fall back to `linkedMemberWake`. While the device held its stream, that function returned `no_route`, so a member whose native wake worked was reported as `not woken: no notice route` and its sender was told to wake it by hand.

## Decision (after two review rounds)
The home cannot prove a linked member's current local route. Only the device checks its socket or managed server, and a past successful wake is not current reach. So the home does not claim a notice for a linked member, and it reports a distinct, display-only outcome instead.

## Change
- `linkedMemberWake`: with the stream open, a binding that is live and not in do-not-disturb, whose linked launch passes `linkWakeRouteEligible`, returns `Wake{Wake: "device"}`.
  - `held`, `device_offline` and `no_route` (no launch the home could wake) are unchanged.
- `messageWakeOf`:
  - A device wake keeps `device` for a message the device could offer (`pendingPublishItem`, not announced, not submitted).
  - Other messages, such as a note, read as `kind` ("this message starts no turn"), as for a local notice route.
  - A request that a linked wake may have submitted reads as submitted, before the member's current state.
- CLI: a send says `the linked device will try to wake it` and `who` says `its linked device will try to wake it`. `NeedsManualWake` is false, so there is no "tell your user" line.
- Unchanged:
  - Resume: `CanResume` is false for a device wake.
  - Telemetry: `recordWakes` audits a device wake as `none`, so `send.wake.*` keys and counts are as before.
  - The scheduler and the refusal fence: display only.
- Docs: `docs/adapters.md` lists `device` among the JSON wake values.

## Tests
- Domain:
  - `TestLinkWakeOfflineUsesTheCurrentProvenStream`:
    - device while connected, also across a stream change;
    - `no_route` in do-not-disturb;
    - `device_offline` once closed;
    - `no_route` for an unverified launch.
  - `TestLinkWakeReportsTheDeviceForAConnectedMember`:
    - the ask's recipient is `device` with no manual-wake line;
    - `send_wake` is audited as `none`;
    - no resume;
    - a note reads as `kind`;
    - `held` while dispatching;
    - notice once a linked wake submitted it.
  - Mutations fail these tests: the device return, the do-not-disturb check, the pending check, the note's `kind`, the history check, the resume guard and the audit mapping.
- CLI: the wake text table includes `device` for send, waiting and who.
- e2e: `TestSpokeLinkWakesClaudeThroughNativeInbox` checks that `who` reports `wake: device` for the linked receiver and that the ask's recipient is `device` with no "tell your user". The wake is then delivered as before.

## Checks
- `go test ./internal/domain`, `go test ./internal/cli`
- `go test -tags e2e,testvendorhome -count=2 -run 'TestSpokeLinkWakes|TestSpokeLinkCodex|TestSendWake' ./test/e2e/`

No hook path changes.

author: sunbininfokim-yeon
body:
Before: The Brazil cards said only "엘니뇨 유사 연도 반영 −4.3%" and the backtest gain. Nothing said the 2027 shift rests on about 2.8 seasons because sowing Niño3.4 (+2.59°C) is warmer than anything on record.

After: Under the shift line the card lists the analog years with how each came in (e.g. 1998(+4%)·2016(−10%)·2024(−12%)), the effective number of seasons, and, when Niño3.4 is outside the record, a note that the value leans on the warmest few years and that the one past beyond-record case came in worse than the shift said.

The point itself is not shrunk. `brazil/enso_shrink_check.py` tested pulling the shift toward zero by n_eff/(n_eff+k) and halving it beyond the record. Every variant lowers backtest skill where the shift is on (MT soy +5.1% to +4.1% at k=2, MT corn +9.5% to +7.3%). The only past season beyond its own record (India east rice 2015) was −19% against a −6% shift, so shrinking would have been further off.

How: new check script and its JSON; `renderEnsoBasis` in app.js (v=164) reads the `effective_seasons`, `beyond_record` and `analogs` fields the forecasts already publish.

author: abolsen
body:
Rebuilds the embeddable gateway (`./gateway`) in the shape of the MCP server template, and adds the everyday sales work in the team's own Apollo data. The MCP server's own tools are unchanged.

**Multi-tenant embedding**
- `createApolloGateway({ apiKey, fetchImpl?, timeoutMs?, policy? })`: explicit key, never read from the environment; fixed address `https://api.apollo.io`; no `APOLLO_*` variable is read.
- Key admission (`admitsKey`, fixed corpus generated by `scripts/fixed-corpus.mjs`) and the sink check on every output (tool list, results, audit records, construction errors), with fixed fallbacks.
- Host policy per instance (`enableWrites`, `disabledTools`, `audit`), every call in its own scope (AsyncLocalStorage).
- `apolloToolCatalog`: deeply frozen, with risk level, `broad` (none) and the Apollo requests each tool may make. The client refuses a request its tool did not declare.
- Errors are our own text by HTTP status; error results carry `failure` metadata (status, request id from a header in id form, method, path template). Apollo's body is never read on an error.
- Redirects are never followed; answers over 10 MB or not JSON are refused.

**Tools**
- Reads: `check_connection`, `search_contacts`, `get_contact`, `search_accounts`, `get_account`, `search_deals`, `get_deal`, `search_tasks`, `search_sequences`, `list_users`, `list_email_accounts`, `list_stages`; `credit_usage` now also returns the remaining credits.
- Writes: `create_contact`, `update_contact`, `set_contact_stage`, `set_contact_owner`, `create_account`, `update_account`, `set_account_owner`, `create_deal`, `update_deal`, `create_task`, `complete_task`, `add_contacts_to_sequence` (without Apollo's enrollment overrides).
- No deletion, merging, users, settings or custom-field definitions. CRM answers are projected onto allowlists (a mailbox's sending credentials never leave).
- The gateway drops phone reveals and `webhook_result`: a reveal needs a public webhook that receives personal data outside the host.

Endpoints, methods and parameters follow docs.apollo.io (read 2026-11-27).

**Tests:** catalog, policy, declared requests per tool, projections, failure metadata, sink check with spliced keys, fixed corpus. `npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` pass locally (173 tests).

author: krilliac
body:
## Summary
- llama.cpp throws `std::runtime_error` from `llama_sampler_accept`/`llama_sampler_apply` when replayed text violates a (lazy) grammar. The backend was compiled with `/EHsc`, which lets MSVC assume `extern "C"` functions never throw and drop the surrounding `catch`, so the exception hit a `noexcept` frame and called `std::terminate` ("Terminate handler called").
- `sonder_backend_llamacpp` is now built with `/EHs /EHc-` (MSVC and clang-cl only, this target only). The `/EH` letters are last-wins per letter, so `/EHc-` is what turns the assumption off.
- Every grammar `llama_sampler_apply` goes through a new `TryApplyGrammar`, matching the existing `TryAcceptGrammar`; failures become `kDecodeFailed` / `LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL` per request.
- Stochastic-rejection verification stops after a failed grammar accept, so it never reaches the uncatchable `GGML_ASSERT(!stacks.empty())`.
- Adds the vocab-only regression test (ctest 322).

## Testing
- RED: test 322 crashes with "Terminate handler called" under `/EHsc` and also under `/EHsc /EHs` (the catch is still dropped).
- GREEN: after a cache-clean rebuild (0 foreign sccache deps), `ctest -R "sonder\.llamacpp"` reports 100 passed and 1 skipped (the integration test needs weights) out of 101.
- An independent read-only review found no blocking issues. Follow-ups that were raised and are not covered here: the generation-path error message still says "grammar deadlock", and the GGML_ABORT/ASSERT paths (EOG with a non-empty stack, trigger type range) still need input validation.

body:
A busca e os contadores agora cruzam a árvore do recorte com seus artigos salvos, antes da paginação. O Modo conferência recebe o recorte, filtra no servidor e não oferece marca global de conferência dentro do modal recortado. ## Summary

Calcs breakdowns: rows both builds share now line up, and hovering a row highlights its pair on the other side.

```diff
 <Breakdowns a b>
+  pairs = markSources(a, b)          # one pairing drives both sides
+  hot: [yourRow, theirRow]           # set on row hover, cleared on leave
   <Side who="a" …>

+    <tr class="hot"> when it's the hovered row or its pair
   <Side who="b" …>
+    rows sorted: paired first (in *your* order), one-sided last
```

`markSources` now returns `at` (the paired row's index on the other side) for `same` / `changed` marks.

- **Before:** The two breakdown tables listed sources in Path of Building's order. Matching rows (e.g. Bone Offering +26 vs +28) could sit at different heights, so you had to scan both lists to pair them.

## Problem

A book dropped into the Book Dock showed **Series # 3** with an empty **Series** field before any fetched metadata was applied. #126 stopped fetched metadata from doing this, but the number here came from the file. Calibre writes `calibre:series_index` on every book, and `opf-parser` reads it even when there is no `calibre:series` or `belongs-to-collection`. PDF (XMP), FB2, comics and audio tags can do the same.

## Changes

- `MetadataExtractionService.extract`, which every format goes through for library scans, re-extraction and the Book Dock, now drops `seriesIndex` when the extracted data has no series name (`lib/series-index-guard.ts`).
- `mergeRegexMetadata` applies the same rule after combining the file and filename-rule values. A rule that captures both a name and a number still keeps both.
- Book Dock finalize (`normalizeFinalizeMetadata`) saves no `seriesIndex` without a series name. This covers files already read before this fix, whose stored metadata still holds the lone number, and numbers typed by hand.
- Book Dock editor shows "Add a series name, or this number will not be saved." under Series # when there is a number but no name.

## Tests

- New: `series-index-guard.test.ts`, extraction tests across EPUB, PDF, FB2, CBZ and M4B, a regex merge test, a finalize test and a `BookDockFileSheet` spec.
- Ran: server `src/modules/book-dock` and `src/modules/metadata` (3512 passed), client `BookDockFileSheet.spec.ts` (29 passed). Client `pnpm lint:check`, vue-tsc, server tsc (build config), eslint and prettier are clean.

author: diegosouzapw
body:
## What

Opt-in fallback port for the desktop app, behind `ELECTRON_LOCAL_PORT_FALLBACK_ENABLED` (default `false`, restart required, read from the environment by the main process).

When the default port 20128 is taken, the packaged app in local graphical mode tries 20129–20133, in order. Only a bind confirmed by the active child over its private IPC channel, followed by a health check on that same port, publishes the URL, tray, IPC and recipes. A foreign service answering 200 on 20128 never opens a window. An explicit `PORT` / `OMNIROUTE_PORT`, split ports, remote, dev or headless mode keep the current behavior. If every candidate is taken, or the bind fails for another reason (`EACCES`), the app shows an error and exits without opening a window. Restarts and the tray port picker reuse the confirmed port. A packaged server that does not report its bind keeps the search off.

## How

- `electron/lib/localServerStartup.js`: eligibility, IPC event validation (exact type, integer port in range, bounded code, per-spawn token) and the port search. Added to `build.files`.
- `scripts/dev/standalone-server-ws.mjs`: reports `listening` / `EADDRINUSE` on the private IPC channel when the per-spawn token is present.
- `electron/main.js`: confirmed-bind gate before readiness, tray and URL.
- `OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDED_BIND_TOKEN` is an internal per-spawn handshake value, listed (with a comment) in the env-doc-sync ignore list.

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/electron-local-port-fallback.test.ts` (38 tests), including real child processes with a really occupied port and a real IPC channel.
- Sibling `tests/unit/electron-*.test.ts` green; flag-count tests 138 → 139.
- Gates run locally: eslint, `typecheck:core`, `check:build-typecheck`, `check:boundary`, `check:cycles`, `check:complexity-ratchets`, `check:test-tla-order`, `check:file-size`, `check:pr-derived-paths` / `check:docs-sync` / `check:docs-all` (pr mode).
- Not run: the packaged Electron build. Worth a manual check that the helper ships and that the launcher uses the effective port with 20128 taken.

Docs: `docs/guides/ELECTRON_GUIDE.md`, `docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md`, `docs/reference/FEATURE_FLAGS.md`, `.env.example`.

author: charlesarnal
body:
Draw one latent class `Θ`, then draw `n ≥ 1` observations from that class's product law. Write `m(Θ)` and `v(Θ)` for the component mean and variance, and `B` for the sample mean. The joint covariance of `m(Θ)` and `B` is `Var(m(Θ))`. The variance of `B` is `Var(m(Θ)) + E[v(Θ)] / n`: only the within-class contribution is divided by `n`.

The component moments are computed from the component laws, including when a class has zero probability under the mixing law. The proof does not divide by a class mass or assume that the observations are independent after mixing. It does not assert optimality of a predictor or identify it with a posterior mean.

Source: [*Bühlmann Model*](https://home.cc.umanitoba.ca/~farhadi/ACT4630Winter2017/Buhlmann.pdf), ACT 4630, University of Manitoba, Winter 2017. Page 1 defines the two variance components. Pages 3–4 derive the vanishing residual cross term and residual second moment, including equation (4). The two identities proved here are their consequences for the finite joint model.

Tasks: af_224f371f65cc85e84cb5624c

Graph: af_224f371f65cc85e84cb5624c new

Place: MathlibExt/Probability/FiniteMixtureMoments -> Economics/actuarial-mathematics | Bühlmann moments in a finite mixture

Validation: both named modules built, both sources passed direct Lean checks with warnings as errors, and the compiled import and axiom checks passed. In a mixture of a constant-zero and a fair Bernoulli component, the sample-mean variance is `3/16` at `n = 1` and `1/8` at `n = 2`. Redrawing the class for each observation would instead give `3/32` at `n = 2`.

- Add a regression test proving an expired social budget skips network work but still finalizes/persists the partial pass.

## Safety
- Does not alter candidate scores, Elite thresholds, Telegram publication gates, RPC proof requirements, or memory limits.
- Scanner retries immediately after the background task releases its lock.

author: crown-3
body:
## 요약

CI의 iOS E2E가 실패하는 원인은 러너의 메모리 부족이었다. 앱 코드나 시나리오의 문제가 아니었다. 메모리가 7GB인 arm64 러너(`macos-26`)에서는 iOS 26 시뮬레이터, 호스트 세션, Maestro가 쓰는 메모리가 실제 메모리보다 컸다. 그래서 호스트가 실행 파일을 디스크에서 계속 다시 읽었고, 시뮬레이터가 새 프로세스를 하나 띄우는 데 수십 초에서 몇 분이 걸렸다. 이 PR은 iOS 작업을 메모리가 14GB인 `macos-15-intel`로 옮긴다.

관련: #734

## 원인

`development` HEAD(8d83125)와 계측용 커밋으로 iOS core를 수동으로 8번 실행했다. 8번 모두 실패했다. 4번은 Maestro 드라이버가 120초 안에 시작되지 않았고(`IOSDriverTimeoutException`), 4번은 시나리오 1~3이 모두 실패했다.

| 측정 항목 (arm64 `macos-26`) | 값 |
|---|---|
| 남은 메모리 | 시나리오 실행 내내 60~90MB |
| 메모리 사용 (footprint 합계) | 호스트 3.4~4.3GB(약 600개 프로세스), 시뮬레이터 4.0~6.0GB(230~270개 프로세스) |
| 압축기가 들고 있는 데이터 | 5.5~8.2GB |
| 파일 캐시 | 0.6~1.4GB |
| 디스크 페이지 읽기 | 10초당 최대 400MB, swap 최대 660MB |
| 프로세스 실행 대기 (시뮬레이터 로그) | `SafariViewService` 28초, `WebKit.Networking` 177초, 위젯 확장 최대 320초 |

#734에 적힌 증상은 모두 이 지연에서 나온다. 01 시나리오는 `SafariViewService`가 늦게 떠서 "Continue" 알림을 20초 안에 찾지 못했다. 02 시나리오는 `WebKit.Networking`이 177초 동안 시작되지 않아서, Maestro 드라이버가 웹 뷰의 화면 계층을 기다리다가 종료되었다. 03 시나리오는 드라이버가 끊긴 상태에서 시작했다. CPU는 병목이 아니었다. 3코어 가운데 평균 1.4코어만 썼다.

시뮬레이터를 첫 부팅 뒤에 한 번 더 부팅하면 시뮬레이터 메모리가 4.0~4.3GB에서 2.1~2.2GB로 줄었다. 하지만 남은 메모리는 여전히 60MB 수준이었고, 드라이버도 여전히 시작 시간을 넘겼다. 그래서 이 방법은 넣지 않았다.

## 변경 내용

- `e2e.yml`: iOS 작업을 `macos-15-intel`(4코어, 14GB)에서 실행한다. 이 이미지의 기본 Xcode는 16이라 Firebase Swift 패키지를 해석하지 못하므로, 설치된 Xcode 26 가운데 가장 최신 버전을 선택한다. 기기와 OS 이미지가 바뀌었으므로 `E2E_ENVIRONMENT`를 올렸다.
- `e2e.yml`: Step Summary의 마지막 줄에 호스트 메모리와 swap 사용량을 남긴다. 이번에는 원인을 찾으려고 시뮬레이터 로그를 직접 뒤져야 했다. swap 사용량이 보이면 같은 원인을 바로 의심할 수 있다.
- `run.sh`: Maestro 드라이버의 시작 제한 시간을 120초에서 300초로 늘린다. Intel 러너에서 측정한 두 번의 시작 가운데 한 번이 116초 걸렸기 때문이다.
- `.maestro/README.md`: CI 절에 러너를 바꾼 이유를 적었다.

## 대안과 한계

- `macos-15-intel`은 GitHub가 마지막으로 제공하는 Intel 이미지이고, 2027년 가을에 종료된다. 그 전에 메모리가 더 큰 arm64 러너로 옮겨야 한다.
- `macos-26-xlarge` 같은 larger runner는 메모리가 충분하지만, 공개 저장소에서도 사용량만큼 비용이 청구된다. 그래서 무료인 Intel 러너를 골랐다.
- Intel 러너에서는 iOS 시뮬레이터 런타임이 26.2까지만 설치되어 있다(arm64는 26.5).

## 검증

upstream은 모든 브랜치 생성을 규칙으로 막고 있다. 그래서 워크플로를 바꾼 실험은 fork(crown-3/ziggle-flutter)에서 실행했다. fork에는 IdP 테스트 계정 secret이 없으므로, 로그인 직전까지 진행하는 탐침 시나리오를 따로 만들었다. 탐침은 앱 실행, 로그인 버튼 누르기, "Continue" 알림, IdP 화면 표시까지 확인하므로 느렸던 경로를 모두 지난다. 같은 탐침을 두 러너에서 2번씩 실행했다.

| 항목 | arm64 `macos-26` | Intel `macos-15-intel` |
|---|---|---|
| 파일 캐시 | 0.6~1.4GB | 5.9~6.6GB |
| 로그인 버튼 → "Continue" 알림 | 1초, 4분 53초 | 7초, 2초 |
| 탐침 소요 시간 | 142초, 595초 | 167초, 126초 |
| 드라이버 시작 | 31초, 86초 | 34초, 116초 |

**아직 하지 않은 검증:** 바뀐 워크플로로 실제 core 시나리오(1~3)를 Intel 러너에서 실행하지 않았다. 이 검증에는 테스트 계정 secret이 필요하다. 지금은 `E2E_GATE`가 `false`이므로, 이 PR을 병합해도 내부 배포는 영향을 받지 않는다. 병합한 뒤에 아래 순서로 #734의 완료 기준을 확인한다.

- [ ] `E2E (Maestro)`를 `platform=ios`, `suite=core`로 여러 번 수동 실행해서 연속으로 통과하는지 확인한다. 같은 커밋에서 통과한 시나리오는 캐시 때문에 다시 실행되지 않으므로, 실행을 동시에 시작하거나 커밋마다 한 번씩 실행한다.
- [ ] Step Summary의 swap 사용량이 0인지 확인한다.
- [ ] 결과를 확인한 뒤 `E2E_GATE`를 `true`로 되돌린다.

author: calebn
body:
Part of #4660

## What a host hits today

When online sharing isn't set up, the Invite sheet's Record guest link is a local address (`http://127.0.0.1:8080/rec/...`). Copy link copies it and nothing says it will not open for a guest on another network. The server already knows: the room mint carries an online-sharing warning, but the web shows it once, as an error line after Create record links, and loses it on every later visit to the sheet and on the Home Record command. Review and Listen links already show an "Only on this network" hint; Record links never did.

## What this changes

- Each Record room card in the Invite sheet shows a standing note when its links are local-only: "Online sharing isn't set up on this computer, so only people on this network can open these links." When online sharing is set up but not running, it says "Online sharing is off, so only people on this network can open these links." Both link to the existing online sharing guide.
- Copy link still copies, with the same toast. The note is attached to the Copy buttons' accessible description only when it is shown.
- The decision uses the same reach signal Review links already use (`reachOf`), checked per row, so closed or missing links show no note. Review and Listen groups are untouched.
- CLI parity: creating a record room from the CLI now prints the online sharing warning once (one line per distinct warning code) before the guest URLs. MCP and HTTP already returned it.
- Reuses the existing `.inv-note` style and the existing guide link. No new CSS, component, token or setting.

## Proof

Vitest for the logic and the card (positive and negative cases, Review/Listen leak check, still-copies, describedby), a CLI test (one warning, none when sharing is set up), and `e2e/record-links-reach.spec.ts` at laptop and iPhone touch (real server reports not set up; online and off states via `/api/tunnel/status`). On the old code 25 of 50 Vitest tests in the Invite folder, the new CLI test and 6 of 8 e2e tests fail. A Storybook story (`RecordLinksLocalOnly`) was added and the Storybook build passes. Before/after screenshots: `audits/ui-proof-4660d/`.

## Not done, and why

- **The local link points at a port the app does not serve.** With nothing set up, the share origin falls back to a relay default of `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, even though the app is served elsewhere. That default also affects Review links, so it is not changed here; logged on #4660.
- "127.0.0.1" only opens on this computer, not on this network. The note says "this network", like the existing Review globe popover. Both should be reworded together later.
- There is no in-app setting for online sharing (it is configured outside the app), so the note's only path is the guide link. A settings screen would be a separate feature.
- The story-sweep browser run was not executed; the new story is covered by the Storybook build and by equivalent Vitest and e2e assertions.

author: freddiehaddad
body:
After an in-place edit (e.g. `~`), a line kept `ML_LINE_INPLACE` set even though `with_ml_get_buf_mut_slice` had already recomputed its exact length. Each subsequent access rescanned the line for a NUL, so searching or redrawing `hlsearch` matches on a long edited line became quadratic.

This clears the flag once the length is exact (including the empty-line path) and keeps `ML_LINE_DIRTY` set, so write-back behavior is unchanged.

On a 1.2 MB single-line JSON buffer after `~`, release builds, median of four interleaved rounds:

| | Backward search | `hlsearch` redraw |
|---|---|---|
| Windows, before | 2291.9 ms | 1847.1 ms |
| Windows, after | 1.2 ms | 7.8 ms |
| Linux, before | 1930.2 ms | 968.3 ms |
| Linux, after | 1.2 ms | 7.6 ms |

Unedited identical content was already ~1.2 ms, and search time now scales linearly with line length.

Adds memline assertions for the flag transitions (including an embedded NUL and an empty line) and a functional test that searches backward after `~`. The memline assertion fails on the previous code.

Unzip and copy PNGs into `Assets/Game/Art/Depot/ProductionCandidates`, run the Unity Editor import and review menus, inspect alpha/framing/scale on devices, then commit the reviewed PNG plus generated `.meta` files to this feature branch. This task was filed from bounded Code scanning evidence collected on the engine-private host boundary. It does not require agent-side GitHub access.

author: qte77
body:
## Summary

Finishes #79. The release flow moves to the `qte77/.github` reusables, all pinned to the v0.1.2 tag commit (`@aeef158f…  # v0.1.2`). This follows gha-ai-changelog#54, including the fixes from its tier-3 review.

- **`bump-and-release.yml`:** now a thin caller of `bump-version.yml`.
  - The file name is kept, since tests and the CHANGELOG refer to it.
  - Same `bump_type` input, and `bump_my_version_pin: "1.8.1"`, the release the inline step used.
  - The bumped files still come from `[tool.bumpversion]`: pyproject, the `action.yaml` version comment, the CHANGELOG block and the README badge.
- **`tag-release.yml` (new):** on a push to `main` that touches `pyproject.toml`, three jobs run:
  1. `tag` calls `tag-release.yml`, which creates an annotated `vX.Y.Z`.
  2. `publish` calls `publish-release.yml` with that tag.
  3. `move-floating-major-tag` first checks the tag matches `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`, then moves `v<major>` to the commit the tag points at.
- **`publish-release.yml` (new):** a dispatch-only re-publish of a named tag. A `validate` job accepts only `vX.Y.Z`, reading the input through `env:`. This matters because immutable releases are on, and a Release published on a floating tag would freeze it. After publishing, it moves `v<major>` the same way.
- **Serialized runs:** both release workflows share the concurrency group `release-tags`, without cancel-in-progress. None of the reusables defines a concurrency group, so the name can't clash. GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so a third queued run cancels the one that is pending.
- **Removed:** `.github/scripts/delete_branch_pr_tag.sh` and `tests/unit/test_cleanup.bats`. The old bump workflow was the script's only caller, and it deleted the release tag on failure, which burns the version for good (qte77/.github#23).
- **Tests (RED first):** `tests/unit/test_infra_files.bats` now checks that:
  - the three callers use the reusables at a full SHA;
  - both move jobs carry the `vX.Y.Z` guard;
  - the tag-deleting script is gone.
  These three tests failed before the change.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** one Changed line and one Removed line.

## Behaviour changes

- **When the tag, Release and floating tag happen:** the inline workflow created `vX.Y.Z` on the bump-branch commit, published the Release and moved `v0` at dispatch time, before the bump PR was reviewed or merged. Now all three happen after the merge, on the merged commit.
- **Squash subject:** this repo's `squash_merge_commit_title` is `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE`, so the one-commit bump PR lands as "Bump version: X -> Y", the same subject the inline commit had. The PR title becomes `chore(release): bump X → Y`; it was `PR bump-N-main [skip ci bump]`, and nothing reads the hint.
- **Signing:** the bump commit is signed through `createCommitOnBranch`. The inline Git Data API commit was unsigned.
- **Release notes:** from the `## [X.Y.Z]` CHANGELOG block, with generated notes as the fallback; inline always used `--generate-notes`.
- **Annotated tags:** the release tag is now annotated; inline made a lightweight ref.

## Fail-or-pass differences

- **CHANGELOG search:** the CHANGELOG entry in `[tool.bumpversion]` is a regex `^---$`, and that line occurs exactly once in CHANGELOG.md. The README badge (`badge/version-0.5.0-blue`) and the `action.yaml` comment (`# version: 0.5.0`) also occur once each. These are unchanged from before, since the config is not edited.
- **On failure:** the callee closes the bump PR and deletes the bump branch, but never deletes a tag; the inline cleanup deleted the tag too. On a re-run with the same run number, the callee force-resets the bump branch to the base head.
- **Shared callee issue:** qte77/.github#79 applies here as well. Don't re-run an old failed bump run; dispatch a new one.

## Not changed, for the owner

- **Stale `v1`:** README and `docs/usage.md` tell consumers `uses: …@v1`, but `v1` points at `d6fc672` (2026-03-24, #22). The releases are 0.x, and the old workflow moved `v0`, which is at v0.5.0, as this one will. Re-pointing the docs to `@v0` or retiring `v1` is a separate decision.

## Checks

- `make validate`: shellcheck lint plus 119 bats tests passed.
- `actionlint` on all workflows: clean.
- `zizmor --offline` on the three changed workflows: no findings.
- `markdownlint-cli2` on CHANGELOG.md with the shared qte77/.github config: 0 errors.

Closes #79

author: kaikei-e
body:
## Summary

Adds an external probe of the certificate each mTLS listener actually presents, plus alerts that fire when the presented certificate is about to expire or the handshake fails. The existing alerts only watch what each workload reports about the certificate on disk, so a listener that keeps serving a stale certificate from memory was invisible until peers started failing. Decision record: `docs/ADR/001034.md` (accepted).

## What changes

- **Prober**: one new `blackbox-exporter` container (`prom/blackbox-exporter:v0.28.0`, non-root, read-only, no capabilities, no host port). It holds no key and no client identity, and verifies the presented chain against the public trust bundle.
- **Scrape jobs**: `tls-handshake` (12 listeners), `tls-handshake-canary` (the CA's own listener, same module and trust bundle), and `blackbox-exporter` (self metrics).
- **Alerts** (`observability/prometheus/rules/tls-handshake-alerts.yml`, all `stack: mtls`):
  - page: `TlsHandshakeCertExpirySoon`, `TlsHandshakeListenerFailing`
  - ticket: `TlsHandshakeCanaryFailing`, `TlsHandshakeCertDivergesFromReported`, `TlsHandshakeProberDown`, `TlsHandshakeProbeScrapeFailing`, `TlsHandshakeProbeFleetIncomplete`, `TlsHandshakeProbeNoExpiry`, `TlsHandshakeReportedCertMissing`
- **Coverage contract** (`scripts/tests/test-tls-handshake-probe.py`): every compose service with a TLS listener must be a probe target or an explicit exclusion; the listener's certificate path must equal the enrolled certificate path; the env var names must be the ones the listener source actually reads.
- **Admin availability tile**: the three new scrape jobs are added to the job matcher in `alt-backend` (the scrape-config parity test requires it). Their rows show whether Prometheus could scrape the prober, not whether a listener completed a handshake.
- **CI**: the observability workflow now also runs when one of the ten listener source files changes.
- **Runbooks**: alert triage rows in `pki-agent-recovery.md`; enable order and post-deploy checks in `observability-config-reload.md` (sections 2.4 and 2.5).
- **Operational-surface budget**: the new container is recorded as a time-boxed exception; the frozen caps are not raised.

## Design notes

- The listener page is aggregated and suppressed while the canary fails, so a broken prober or trust bundle produces a ticket instead of twelve pages.
- Page expressions use short windows (`last_over_time` / `max_over_time`) so a single flapping scrape does not reset the `for` clock.
- The expiry page requires the on-disk certificate to have at least four hours left, so it does not duplicate the existing on-disk expiry page.

## Verification

- `./scripts/observability-validate.sh` passes: `promtool check config`, `check rules`, `test rules`, the config audit, and 128 contract tests.
- `./scripts/lint/run.sh` passes for `observability`, `compose`, `repo`, `scripts`, and `alt-backend/app`.
- `go test ./orchestrator/gateway/admin_metrics_gateway/...` passes.
- `docdag validate`, `docdag validate --immutable-since origin/main`, `docdag lint --strict`, and `alt-harness adr-gate --base origin/main` pass.
- Probe behaviour against an expired leaf was measured in an isolated throwaway environment: `probe_success` is 0 and no `probe_ssl_*` series is emitted.

## Not verified

- Nothing here has run against a live stack. That the canary probe succeeds against the real CA listener is inferred from the configuration, not measured.
- The ticket-severity divergence and missing-series conditions are instantaneous and can reset on a flapping scrape; this is listed in the ADR's tradeoffs.

## After deploy

The prober may not be started automatically. Follow `docs/runbooks/observability-config-reload.md` section 2.4 to start it and confirm all 13 probes succeed before reloading Prometheus, then run the section 2.5 checks within 24 hours.

author: isaacgarcia110606-arch
body:
## Summary
Adds the persistence needed to accept orders from a second entry point without
duplicates. Each order now records **where it came from** (`source`) and, for
external channels, the **external order ID**. The database guarantees that the
same external order cannot be stored twice for the same source.

## Changes
- **`src/store/models.py`**
  - `Order.source`: `VARCHAR(20)`, defaults to `"storefront"` (ORM default and
    `server_default`), so the existing checkout needs no change.
  - `Order.external_order_id`: `VARCHAR(80)`, nullable. Storefront orders
    leave it `NULL`.
  - Unique index `uq_orders_source_external_order_id` on
    `(source, external_order_id)`. SQLite allows many `NULL`s in a unique
    index, so storefront orders never collide with each other.
- **`src/store/db.py`**
  - `_ensure_order_fulfillment_column` becomes `_upgrade_orders_table`: one
    ordered table of added columns (`fulfillment_method`, `source`,
    `external_order_id`) applied with `ALTER TABLE` only when missing.
  - Creates the unique index with `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, because
    SQLite cannot add constraints via `ALTER TABLE`. It uses the same name
    `create_all` uses, so new and upgraded databases end up with the same schema.
  - Safe to re-run on every app start.

## Why a unique index and not only an application-level check
A "look up, then insert" check alone is not enough if the same external order
arrives twice at the same time: both requests can pass the lookup. The unique
index makes the database the final guard. The application can catch
`IntegrityError` and return the order that already exists.

## Tests (`tests/test_order_persistence.py`, 13 new)
- New orders default to `storefront` with no external ID; a real storefront
  checkout persists `storefront`.
- Several storefront orders with `NULL` external IDs coexist.
- `(marketplace, MKT-1001)` twice raises `IntegrityError` and only one row remains.
- The same external ID under a different source is allowed.
- New databases have the unique index on the expected columns.
- Databases with the M1 and M2 schemas get both columns and the index; old
  orders are kept and become `storefront`.
- Migrated databases enforce uniqueness, and the migration can be re-run.
- Uniqueness still holds after an app restart on a file database.

## Not in this PR
The ordering service doesn't write these fields yet. Passing the origin through
`PlaceOrder` and returning the existing order on repeats comes next.

## Testing
- `pytest`: 81 passed locally. Existing tests unchanged.

## AI use
Coded with claude, checked and reviewed locally

author: simcity400
body:
## Problem

When a dashboard page is paused shortly before a gap in a recording, read-ahead crosses the gap where live cells disappear and then return. Each return re-registered the panel's live-cell follow, calling `Playhead::seed_paused_query()` unconditionally and dropping/re-adding the panel's columns, resetting the paused playhead in an endless loop. In addition, a paused cross-piece table join (or a stalled-lane join in a gap) could spin indefinitely because `land_joins()` rejected joins prepared past the paused hour and `publish_reset()` recorded gap endpoints past `piece.last`.

## Fix

- **`crates/playhead/src/playhead.rs`**:
  - Made `Stepper` the single owner of paused resets via one `seed_paused: bool` field (no new locks). Added `Playhead::redeclare_seeding(reader, tables, seed_paused)` (`redeclare` delegates with `false`) and routed `Playhead::seed_paused_query()` through `control.seed_paused = true`.
  - Added `Stepper::reset_paused()` (resets when `seed_paused && newest > head`, or when an active join is unlandable across pieces or behind `piece.last` in a gap) next to `Stepper::hold_for_paused_seed()` (holds forward read-ahead in `build()` after same-hour catch-up while a seeded join can still land at `head`).
  - Clamped `publish_reset()`'s `slot.ended(...)` to `pieces[self.piece].last` and added `Stepper::piece_at(hour)` so join deliveries at gap hours preserve `step.gap() == true`.
- **`crates/dashboard-follow/src/follow.rs` & `host.rs`**:
  - Replaced `product_lanes` with `retain_product_lanes(id, read)` (monotonic merge per shown panel id, skipping `redeclare` when unchanged) and `clear_product_lanes(id)` (invoked on `ProductReads::remove`, so replacing a panel's request on the same id replaces its retained lanes and `unpanel` clears them).
  - Retained both `StepProduct` (`read.lanes` + `cell_lanes`) and `Shown` (`cell_lanes`) lanes while shown.
  - Threaded explicit `seed_paused: bool` into `StepProduct::read_at` / `PanelJob::read_one` / `Follow::follow_cells`: `PanelRead::Seed`, `pending_seed`, and `step.reset()` pass `true`; read-ahead steps and `PanelRead::CatchUp` pass `false`.

## Callers of `seed_paused_query` and playhead redeclaration

- `crates/dashboard-follow/src/host.rs` (`PlayheadHost::new_with_budget`): previously the only production caller of `seed_paused_query()`; now calls `playhead.redeclare_seeding(reader, tables, joining)` atomically under `clock -> control`.
- `crates/viewer/src/embedded.rs` (`FollowPlayheads::open`): main dashboard and map viewer share a `playhead_host::Entry` via `open_clocked(..., Side::Follow)`; pop-out and export windows use `open_private(...)` or separate clocks. All route through `PlayheadHost::new_with_budget`.
- `crates/viewer-layer-core/src/playhead_host.rs`: the map viewer shares the same `Playhead` and calls `playhead.redeclare(self.reader, ...)` (`seed_paused = false`), never `seed_paused_query()`. Dashboard read-ahead no longer resets the shared playhead, and any paused cross-piece or stalled-lane gap join now resolves via `Stepper::reset_paused()`.
- `crates/playhead/src/playhead/tests.rs` (`a_paused_follow_builds_its_lead_and_seeds_a_new_query_at_the_paused_hour`): direct test of `Playhead::seed_paused_query()`, now routed through `control.seed_paused = true`.

## Verification

- Ported regression test `paused_reset::paused_cells_dropping_across_a_gap_do_not_reset_the_playhead` failed on `main` (`b6509b3205`) and passes on HEAD.
- Boat `playhead` tests (6 passed in 0.03s): `a_paused_follow_builds_its_lead_and_seeds_a_new_query_at_the_paused_hour`, `paused_seed_redeclare_holds_read_ahead_until_join_lands_at_head`, `paused_cross_piece_join_seeks_once_and_covered_redeclare_does_not`, `paused_gap_seek_column_expansion_clears_join_without_stalling`, `paused_gap_entry_with_stalled_lane_clears_column_expansion_via_seek`, `paused_seed_hold_allows_stalled_slot_catch_up_at_head`.
- Boat `dashboard-follow` tests (8 passed in 0.15s): `host::a_retired_product_read_cannot_publish_its_seed`, `host::a_product_lane_redeclared_on_its_table_keeps_every_flag_it_asked_for`, and all 6 `paused_reset::*` tests (gap drop/return, catch-up across gap, panel request replacement & `unpanel`, `Shown` panel retention/replacement/clear, cross-piece join & shrink, external paused follow).
- Boat `clippy -p playhead -p dashboard-follow`: 0 warnings.
- `python tools/ci.py check`: passed (`citations`, `comments`, `dead-code`, `game-content`, `machine-paths`, `patterns`, `suppressions`).

Reviewed with Astra Loop: 4 rounds with gpt-6.2-astra on xhigh. Astra verdict: approved

body:
## What changed

- OPS-01 C1 plans both USB fault roles in each radio direction, with three default repetitions. It matches a saved interrupted transfer to a fresh known-data transfer.
- `nodes.py` records the first owned serial I/O failure. `radio_runs.py` links it to the interrupted run and records cleanup time. `ops_reconnect.py` verifies the continuously connected peer stopped, the selected node returned on a fresh connection, and the recovery archive matches the expected bytes.
- `ProcedureMatrix.tsx` accepts and displays the evidence pairs. See `docs/ops_matrix.md` for the capture procedure.

## How to check

Run `uv run --project testbed pytest -q testbed/tests/test_ops_usb_recovery.py`. Expect 12 planned default cases and four native fixture combinations covering each interruption role and direction. The wrong role must remain inconclusive, and missing evidence must block the case. The 88-test serial, artifact, audio, and radio regression passed. Dashboard build, formatting, browser and CLI previews also passed.

For bench validation record the physical unplug time, confirm the peer stops, and keep the other serial connection open. Reconnect and repeat the original request to produce the fresh-run evidence. Review all physical repetitions separately.

Refs #124

 "dwell_seconds": 5.000011, "overlap_ratio": 0.9999999999999996,

프레임으로 학습됐습니다. 리플레이에 --calibration을 필수로 만들어 막았습니다.

author: leolobato
body:
Hi @quer3q and @Dang3rZone, thanks for #131. With Kraken Mount on 127.0.0.1:10101, Playden installs and starts its games with no Kraken-specific code. Two things were left, both from Playden's side of #126:

## 1. `games/fakelib` for a title not listed yet

Dang3rZone asked whether Playden could call `games/fakelib` for its titles, so players don't turn the libraries off by hand. Playden now does, with `{mode: "disabled"}`, before the title's folder appears in `/data/homebrew`. That's the only point where it works for the first launch: once the folder is there, the next pass can build the title with the overlay.

**Before:** `set_overlay` answered `404 ENOENT` unless the title was already in the library, so that call always failed. The scan waits while Playden runs (Playden is a Kraken title itself), so the title was first built and started with the overlay.

**Now:** a valid title id that isn't in the library is still put in `overlay_off`, saved, and the answer has `"listed": false`. `overlay_off` is part of `inputs_key` and `cache::build` reads it, so the first build makes an empty `fakelib/`. The pkg refusal still applies when the source is known; an unlisted title that turns out to be a pkg keeps its overlay, as `cache::overlay_off` already decides. `/api/overlay/<TID>` still answers 404 for a title not in the library. `/api/v1/version` lists `fakelib_unlisted`.

## 2. Register again a title uninstalled outside Kraken Mount

**Before:** a title this run registered stays in the per-run `registered` set, and each pass only remounts it. When something else uninstalls it, it shows `installed: false` until Kraken Mount restarts. Playden does this on purpose for "Register again" (dropping a title's old download area): its title remover uninstalls the title and keeps the folder, expecting the mounter's next pass to register it in full. On v0.4.1 that pass never comes.

**Now:** for a title in the set, each pass stats its two staged files (`register::staged`: `/user/app/<TID>/sce_sys/param.json` and `/user/appmeta/<TID>/param.json`, which `is_registered` and `registered` now share). When either is gone, it logs `<TID>: no longer on the home screen; registering again`, takes the title out of the set, and the full register path runs. That's two stats per registered title per pass, not an app.db read. An app.db row deleted with both files left isn't seen. `/api/v1/version` lists `reregister_missing`.

`DESIGN.md` is updated for both (Flow, Web API).

## Checks

- `cargo check --offline --target x86_64-unknown-freebsd`: clean. `ps5/build.sh` builds `target/ps5/kraken-mount.elf`.
- Console, FW 13.60, Playden built from its PR branch, one GOG game (Flight of the Amazon Queen):

  | | v0.4.1 | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `games/fakelib` before the folder exists | `404` (`status 2`); first build with the overlay | `200`, `overlay off (not in the library yet)`; first build `fakelib: overlay off (overlay_off)`, the game starts from Home |
  | Register again (title remover, folder kept), then quit Playden | stays `installed: false`, `/user/app/<TID>` gone, never registered again | next pass: `no longer on the home screen; registering again`, back on Home |
  | Uninstall from Playden (`manual/remove`, title remover, folder moved away) | clean | clean |

- Not run on the console: a title deleted from Home by the system, and an unlisted title that turns out to be a pkg.

## Not handled here

- Kraken Mount still pauses while a homebrew title runs, Playden included, so a new game reaches Home only after the player quits Playden. ShadowMount+ 1.7beta6 stopped pausing for a running FAKE/LAPY title; Playden now polls while a game waits, so a Kraken Mount that did the same would put games on Home with Playden open. Left to you: Kraken's builds are heavier than SMP's scans.
- `games/fakelib` (and `/api/overlay`) for a title already listed changes `overlay_off`, but a launch overlays what the cache's `fakelib/` holds, which only a pass refreshes, so it applies after the next idle pass, not on the next launch as `applies_on_next_launch` says.
- `manual/remove` adds the folder to `exclude`, and `manual/add` of the same path takes it off again (`manual` in web.rs). A client that removes many titles over time leaves a long `exclude` list behind.

Commits:
- Let games/fakelib set a title not in the library yet
- Register again a title uninstalled outside Kraken Mount

body:
Part of SIG-259: SIG-262. This records in record 0023 the results of SIG-261's part 2 trials and SIG-262's part 3 trial, observed on 2026-11-26 (UTC). It changes `docs/decisions/0023-hosting-off-the-box.md`, `docs/how-fidant-works.md` and two phrases in `AGENTS.md`. No code changes, and nothing changes for visitors.

## What it records

- **Open questions.** The intro now says which questions are settled: 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 in full, and 1, 3 and 4 in part.
  - **1, the free plan:** the account qualifies, because the three plan subscriptions reached `CREATE_COMPLETE`. Compression and the plan's dashboards are still open.
  - **2, the CSP on the free plan:** answered. The function's CSP, HSTS, `referrer-policy` and `x-content-type-options` came back on pages, the 404, both receive pages and an asset.
  - **3, the load balancer:** the self-signed target is settled. The idle timer, the split `X-Forwarded-For` test, the group's egress and the replacement timing are still open.
  - **4, the service:** the rollback took about 11 minutes, with signaling down throughout. No two tasks overlapped, and no task ran for about 1 minute 45 seconds. The task runs without a NAT gateway. Also recorded: a commit tag can't be moved, and the release role can't turn on commands in the task.
  - **6, `/relay-secret/*`:** it is forwarded on the free plan.
  - **9, tmpfs:** `node` can write the mount, so the fallback is not needed.
- **Part 3's trial** gets a results bullet: every `curl` line, the two-browser direct transfer through the CDN, and the function test with the 128 cap, which passed on 2026-11-27. The highest utilisation was 40, for the backslashes. One input's utilisation varied by up to 16 between two runs, which the bullet records. The runs before that cap stay in the cap's bullet, which #185 wrote, and the results bullet points to it.
- **CloudFront's own 403 and 301** carry none of the three headers and no HSTS. This is now stated in 0023's Pages bullet and in `docs/how-fidant-works.md` line 415, which said only that the trial would observe it.
- **"Unused until the cutover"** is no longer true, because the trial used these places. In `docs/how-fidant-works.md` (10 places) and in `AGENTS.md`'s `FidantSignal` and `FidantPages` bullets, it now reads "serving no visitor until the cutover". The load balancer's trace row says only the maintainers' trial pages connect to it before then.
- **Consequences:** a server release now reads "about 2 minutes or more without signaling", up from "about a minute". The failed-release bullet gives the rollback's 11 minutes.

## What it leaves open, and why

- **That the task's master is the one in Secrets Manager** is not recorded as answered. `apps/server/src/relays.ts` makes a master when the file is missing, `apps/server/entrypoint.sh` writes the file only when `RELAY_MASTER` is set, and no AWS page read says ECS refuses to start a container whose secret it can't read. So a settled service looks the same either way. With a master of its own, every new task would make a new one, and relays would be cut off briefly after each release. Two ways to settle it are under Follow-ups.
- **"A merge will add the network, the load balancer, the secret and the service"** in part 2 stays as it is, as does line 11's list of what the present tense covers. `docs/decisions/README.md` says what a Proposed record says about code on `main` changes only in a pull request that changes that code. #174 left that line in "will", and #182 moved its own line when it changed its config. The same holds for part 3's "One merge will add the bucket" since #178. The next pull request that changes `apps/infra/src/signal.ts` or `apps/infra/src/pages.ts` should move them.
- **The 128 cap** is #185, which merged first. This branch then merged `main` and kept both sides of the four conflicts: 128 everywhere, "answered under open question 2", the observed 403 and 301 in 0023's Pages bullet and in `docs/how-fidant-works.md` line 415, and #185's trial bullet followed by this branch's results bullet.

## Steps for David

This touches `AGENTS.md`, so it needs a `maintainers` approval from the other developer, and I don't merge it myself. The Claude review asked for that change (see Review).

1. **Approve it once the Claude review has approved the current head**, and merge.
2. After the merge I mark SIG-262 Done.

## Checks

- `pnpm check` passes on the tree merged with `main` at 2ee6e22.
- The diff touches only these three files. It has no account ID, secret or local path. The distribution name holds no account ID, as `AGENTS.md` says.

## Review

One pass with a Code Reviewer lane and an AppSec lane, per David's go of 2026-11-27.
- **Code Reviewer** found one major: the record gave two downtime figures for a task swap, and "about 2 minutes" said more than the running count showed. Fixed: the overlap result now gives the 1 minute 45 seconds with no task running, and the Consequences line says "about 2 minutes or more". Its five minors are fixed. These were the tmpfs owner and mode, "uncached" from one miss, the variable versus the file it names, the 11 minutes holding only for an image that exits at once, and a note that the heads don't show which request the viewer-response event carries. Its seven nits are fixed. It agreed with both judgment calls above.
- **Claude review, second head (74ac1bd):** one major: the root `AGENTS.md` still called both stacks unused. Fixed in this head. Its nit ("It loaded" after two browsers) is fixed too.
- **Claude review, first head (0759a61):** one blocker. The trial used places that `docs/how-fidant-works.md`'s "Where traces are kept" called "unused until the cutover", and the load balancer's row said no page connects to it before then. Fixed in this head: every "unused until the cutover" there now reads "serving no visitor until the cutover", the load balancer's row says only the maintainers' trial pages connect to it before then, as on 2026-11-26, and 0023's "nobody uses it" for `sto.signal.fidant.se` reads "no visitor uses it". Its minor is fixed too: the results bullet and both trace tables say CloudFront's reports have not been read yet. The traces explorer's text in `apps/web` names none of these places, so it needs no change. Biome realigned the two tables.
- **AppSec** found no blocker or major. Its minor (the tmpfs owner and mode) and its three nits are fixed. It found no exposure in the missing headers: HSTS on a plain-HTTP 301 does nothing, and the 403 has no script and nothing to frame. It found nothing private disclosed, and it agreed with the reasoning about the master.

## Follow-ups

- **Settle the master's source**, before the cutover. Either make `apps/server/entrypoint.sh` exit with an error when `RELAY_MASTER` is unset, so a task without it never settles, or run one task with the command overridden to `test -e /run/sigill/relay-master && echo written || echo missing`.
- **Settle the tmpfs owner and mode** with one task whose command is `stat -c '%u %g %a' /run/sigill`. Its log line prints no secret.
- **`apps/infra/AGENTS.md`**: the tmpfs fact ("The first task settles it") still reads as pending. The ECR fact leaves open whether an immutable tag can be deleted, and the trial settled it: David deleted the `broken-trial` tag by hand.
- **The load balancer's trace row overstates "only"** (Claude review minor on 1b8bb75). `docs/how-fidant-works.md` says only the maintainers' trial pages connect to it before the cutover. `sto.signal.fidant.se` is in public DNS and answers anyone, so the row should say no visitor's page connects to it and that it answers anyone who reaches its name, such as the trial on 2026-11-26.
- **Three reviewer agents still say the trial will observe CloudFront's 403 and 301** (Claude review nit). `.claude/agents/api-tester.md`, `application-security-engineer.md` and `backend-architect.md` should say what was observed: none of the three headers and no HSTS. `.claude/**` needs a `maintainers` app

## A. Repo X-ray ranked a test fixture token as the top improvement

On `sindresorhus/ky`, improvement #1 was "Rotate or remove secret-like value in test/hooks.ts", citing line 4061: `newToken: 'refreshed-token-…'`.

**Cause.** The generic assignment rule flagged the value (it has enough entropy and a digit). The hotspot was marked `low` because it was in a test file, but the improver ranks from the evidence list, and that list carried no severity or confidence. So the model ranked "rotate a secret" first.

**Line number.** 4061 is correct. `test/hooks.ts` in ky has 8,063 lines, and lines are counted per file. A test now pins this.

**Fix.**
- `secrets.ts`: every finding gets a `confidence`. Findings in test, fixture, example, mock and spec paths (`isFixturePath`) are `low`. Values that look like placeholders (`isPlaceholderValue`: placeholder words, dictionary words plus digits, provider formats that are low entropy or contain `EXAMPLE`/`test`/`xxxx`) are also `low`. Real-looking provider tokens in production paths stay `high`.
- `hotspots.ts`: low-confidence findings are merged into one `low` hotspot, "Test fixture tokens, verify not real (N values in M files)", listed last. `rankableHotspots` keeps it out of the improver's evidence.
- `draft.ts`: as a backstop in code, a `security` improvement about secrets whose files are all fixture paths is dropped, and a `critic.flagged` event says so.
- The ky gate-run test in `draft.test.ts` used to keep that improvement. It now expects it to be dropped.

**Tests.** `secrets.test.ts` covers placeholder and real values, fixture and production paths, and line 4061 counted within one file. `hotspots.test.ts` checks that a fixture token in `test/` and a placeholder in `src/` end up in the minor hotspot, that AWS and GitHub token formats in `src/` stay high and come first, that the fixture tokens are absent from the evidence, and that the improver backstop works.

## B. An off-topic custom-goal brief scored 100%

The goal "Which open-source licences does the Python Software Foundation use, and why?" produced a brief about GitHub repo counts and stars, and still showed 100% citation accuracy.

**Cause.** The critic only checks that each claim is entailed by its cited quotes. Nothing checked whether the brief answers the goal.

**Fix.**
- New prompt `packages/runtime/prompts/goal-coverage.v1.md` (`goal-coverage@1`, status active, with intent in the header). It runs on the `fast` role and its output is parsed by `GoalCoverageOutputSchema` with one repair attempt (`callStructured`). It returns `answered`, `partly` or `not_answered`, the missing aspects and a reason. If the grader fails, the result is "unchecked". It never guesses.
- `deepen_research` grades the first draft. If the draft is not answered, the missing aspects become the first thin sections and reference searches, and at least one research round runs. This stays within the existing `deepRounds: 2` and the time budget. The critic step has no web capability, so the research happens in deepen, which does.
- `critic` grades the final brief again if it changed (after a redraft or claim removals). The result goes into `CriticReport.goalCoverage`, `verification.goalCoverage`, the step and run summaries (`citation accuracy 100% (…); goal coverage: not answered (missing: …)`), and a `critic.flagged` event (warn for not answered, info for partly or unchecked).
- UI: a "Goal coverage" metric next to "Citation accuracy" in the run top bar, and a verdict line with the reason and missing aspects in the goal panel.
- Evals: a soft `goal_answered` check and a `goalCoverage` metric in the custom-goal grader. The goal adapter and evolve targets record the prompt version.

**Tests.** `goal-coverage.test.ts` uses the scripted provider. It checks the fast role, the versioned prompt, repair, the honest failure, verdict spellings, the caps and the `formatAccuracy` line. `custom-goal/run.test.ts` runs end to end over a fixture web with a scripted model: an answered goal, a not-answered goal (research targets the missing aspect first, `researched: true`, warn flag, summary line) and a grader failure (unchecked flag). The evals grader test covers an off-topic brief with 100% citations. `run-view.test.ts` covers the top-bar metric.
